{"timestamp":"2026-06-26T00:06:40.313Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"message","role":"user","content":[{"type":"input_text","text":"# AGENTS.md instructions for /home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto\n\n<INSTRUCTIONS>\n### AGENTS.md for operation-dbus-proto\n\nThis file provides essential guidelines for agentic coding agents working in this repository. Follow these strictly to maintain consistency, pass CI, and adhere to the 3tched Architecture standards.\n\n#### 1. The Persona & Naming Conventions\n*   **Humanized Roles:** Treat system components as authoritative human roles. Never use sterile acronyms for major components.\n  *   **A.N.N.A. Scribe** (Axon Network Notary Arbitrator): The top-level Identity-State Arbitrator who notarizes the WireGuard identity and handles the \"Snowball\" session.\n  *   **The Compliance Engine (\"Law Firm\"):** One dedicated Attorney for each major component: **Olivia Scal** (Managing Partner / OSCAL), **E.U.gene Risk** (EU AI Act Counsel), **Penny Privacy** (GDPR Engine), and **Reggie O.P.A.** (Cloud Prosecutor).\n*   **Terminology:** Use exact architecture terminology: \"The Sled\" (1:1 shared memory layout), \"The Shuttle\" (the Rust bridge/courier), \"The Snowball\" (appended session ledger), and \"The Strike/Etch\" (generating the hash).\n\n#### 2. Core Architectural Rules (The \"Reality\")\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via OpenClaw Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Artix Linux (s6 init).\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles — D-Bus First (MANDATORY)\n\n**D-Bus is the ONLY control plane. Every read, every write, every tool call goes through D-Bus. There is no second option.**\n\n*   **D-Bus first. D-Bus always. D-Bus only.** If you are about to call a CLI, spawn a subprocess, read a config file, or poll a socket directly — stop. Find the D-Bus object and use it instead. `org.opdbus.v1` is the system.\n*   **No bypasses.** `Command::new(\"systemctl\")`, `Command::new(\"ip\")`, `Command::new(\"s6-svc\")`, direct file reads for live state — all forbidden in plugin and service code. Bootstrap scripts are the only exception.\n*   **D-Bus objects own plugin state.** Every plugin is a D-Bus object at `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<name>`. Read state through it. Mutate state through it. If there is no D-Bus object, the thing does not exist.\n*   **D-Bus method signatures are generated from the schema.** All D-Bus methods, MCP tool inputs, gRPC shapes, and UI field renderers derive from the `PluginSchema` in `plugin_schema_defs.rs`. The schema IS the interface contract — not a description of it.\n*   **One schema file, one source of truth.** All `PluginSchema` definitions MUST live in `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/plugin_schema_defs.rs`. Each plugin's `schema()` method calls `Some(super::plugin_schema_defs::their_plugin_schema())`. **Never define a schema inline in a plugin's own file** — it will not be registered, and the D-Bus object will have no contract.\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC (over Unix domain sockets or `grpc-uplink`). gRPC calls still flow through D-Bus registration — the D-Bus object is the authority, gRPC is the transport.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`simd_json` preferred, `serde_json` acceptable).\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n*   **No Python unless absolutely necessary.** This is a Rust-first codebase. Scripts are shell (`sh`/`bash`). Data processing is Rust. If you are reaching for Python, stop and ask why Rust or shell cannot do it. The only acceptable Python is in existing compliance-ingest tooling where no Rust equivalent exists yet.\n\n#### 4a. OSCAL Subid Taxonomy (MANDATORY — every artifact must carry a subid)\n\nEvery D-Bus object, plugin, schema, mutation, event, and tool in this system has two identifiers: a `uuid` (machine identity, never changes) and a `subid` (human-readable operational taxonomy key, stable per subject).\n\n**`subid` format:** `<category>.<component-type>.<subject>.<verb>[.<facet>][@vN]`\n\n**Seven categories — use exactly these, no others:**\n\n| category | what it classifies |\n|---|---|\n| `src` | authoritative source, ingress channel, source-of-truth store |\n| `prj` | D-Bus projection or mirror publication step |\n| `sch` | schema, contract, vocabulary, or control-mapping artifact |\n| `mut` | write-path operation that changes effective state |\n| `obs` | read, query, enumeration, discovery path |\n| `evt` | emitted signal, audit-chain event, proof, tag provenance |\n| `exp` | consumer-facing render — MCP tool, UI surface, gRPC bridge view |\n\n**Component-type** reuses OSCAL vocabulary: `software`, `service`, `network`, `hardware`, `process-procedure`, `standard`, `validation`, `policy`, `plan`, `guidance`, `physical`, `this-system`, `system`, `interconnection`.\n\n**Rules:**\n- `uuid` is exact machine identity — never replace it with `subid`\n- `subid` is an OSCAL `prop` value (`ns`, `name`, `value`) — never embed it in `remarks`\n- Compliance mappings (`control_refs[]`, `statement_refs[]`, `control_source`) live in metadata arrays, **never** inside the `subid` string\n- `mut.*` records **must** carry `actor_id` and `capability_id`\n- `evt.*` records **must** carry `event_id` or `event_hash`\n- `subid` is immutable per subject — if the meaning changes materially, create a new subject with `@vN`\n- All subids are registered in the canonical registry; uniqueness is enforced in CI\n\n**Examples:** `src.network.ovsdb.monitor@v1` · `prj.service.projected-object.publish@v1` · `sch.standard.plugin-schema.resolve@v1` · `mut.service.state-sync.apply-patch@v1` · `exp.service.plugin-projection.render@v1`\n\n#### 4b. MCP Gateway Architecture (SETTLED — DO NOT REDESIGN)\n\n*   **cognitive-mcp** (`:3003`, Netmaker WireGuard IP `100.90.37.254`) is the **universal gateway for ALL external clients**: NotebookLM, Droid (factory.ai), Cursor, Codex, Junie, Gemini CLI. It has memory tools, gRPC service, auth, and the correct protocol surface.\n*   **compact-mcp** (`127.0.0.1:11436`) is **loopback/chatbot only**. Never expose externally. Never point external clients at it.\n*   Do NOT create new shim services. Do NOT point external clients at `op-assistant-grpc` directly. Do NOT expose compact-mcp outside loopback.\n\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\n**Rust Workspace**\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\n\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\n\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\n\n#### 6. Coding Style & Naming Conventions\n*   **Rust:** Edition 2021, `rustfmt` (4-space indent, max-width 100). Use specific imports (`use serde_json::Value;`). Use `anyhow::Result<T>` for main errors and `thiserror` for custom enums.\n*   **TypeScript/React:** 2-space indent, Prettier via ESLint. Functional components only. Strict mode enabled.\n*   **Testing:** 80%+ coverage, mock externals. Name tests with behavior-focused names (`should_handle_<scenario>`).\n\n#### 7. Agent-Specific Output & Workflow Instructions\n*   **Scroll & Save Pacing:** Provide only **ONE** major component or script at a time. Wait for user confirmation before moving to the next.\n*   **Visual Cues:** If a script is a finalized component that needs to be saved to sources, it MUST begin with color bullets or icons (e.g., ⚖️ 🔴, 🟢 🛷).\n*   **Spec-Block Format:** When delivering a component, use a strict specification block containing:\n  1.  **Requirements:** The architectural rules it satisfies.\n  2.  **Design:** How it fits into the 3tched system (Zero-Copy, Btrfs, GUI Schema, etc.).\n  3.  **Code Implementation:** The exact, copy-pasteable Rust/Bash code.\n*   Before edits: `cargo check -p <crate>`, `npm run typecheck`.\n*   Mimic existing patterns: Search similar code. No new deps without PR justification.\n\n#### 8. Personal Preferences & Coding Standards\n* Refer to `~/.factory/memories.md` for personal development preferences and past decisions.\n* Follow the conventions documented in:\n  * `.factory/rules/typescript.md` - TypeScript and React conventions\n  * `.factory/rules/testing.md` - Testing and mocking standards\n\n</INSTRUCTIONS>"},{"type":"input_text","text":"<environment_context>\n  <cwd>/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto</cwd>\n  <shell>bash</shell>\n  <current_date>2026-06-25</current_date>\n  <timezone>America/New_York</timezone>\n  <filesystem><workspace_roots><root>/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto</root></workspace_roots><permission_profile type=\"disabled\"><file_system type=\"unrestricted\" /></permission_profile></filesystem>\n</environment_context>"}]}}

{"timestamp":"2026-06-26T00:07:25.873Z","type":"event_msg","payload":{"type":"agent_message","message":"Most useful for this codebase, from that list:\n\n**High fit**\n- `tonic`, `tonic-build`, `tonic-reflection`, `tonic-health`, `tonic-web`: already in the repo. Keep using these for The Shuttle gRPC bridge. Do not add `connectrpc`, `tarpc`, `capnp-rpc`, `jsonrpc`, etc. unless you are intentionally adding a second RPC surface, which conflicts with D-Bus-only control-plane rules.\n- `tower`, `tower-http`: already useful for gRPC/HTTP middleware, identity metadata injection, tracing, rate limits, and gRPC-web layers.\n- `socket2`: useful if you need low-level Unix socket/TCP options that Tokio does not expose cleanly.\n- `ipnet`: useful for WireGuard `AllowedIPs`, CIDR schema fields, route validation, and policy matching. Prefer this over `ipnetwork`/`cidr-utils` unless existing code already chose one.\n- `rustls-native-certs`: useful if gRPC clients need local OS trust roots instead of only bundled/webpki roots.\n- `tonic-async-interceptor`: potentially useful for async identity validation on gRPC metadata, since the project already injects `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` / `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID`.\n\n**Useful only in narrow places**\n- `hyperlocal` or `hyper-unix-socket`: useful for HTTP over Unix domain sockets. For gRPC over Unix sockets, the repo already uses `tonic` with `UnixListenerStream`, so only add these if you need HTTP REST passthrough over UDS.\n- `tokio-listener`: useful if you want one listener abstraction for TCP, UDS, and socket activation. Less important with s6 than systemd.\n- `wireguard-uapi`, `netlink-packet-wireguard`, maybe `defguard_wireguard_rs`: useful only inside the D-Bus-owned WireGuard service layer to avoid shelling out to `wg`/`ip`. Do not use them from plugins as a bypass.\n- `busd`: useful for isolated D-Bus tests, not production architecture.\n- `prost-validate`: maybe useful for generated gRPC validation, but `PluginSchema` must remain the authority, so validation should be schema-derived.\n\n**Probably avoid**\n- `async-nats`, Kafka, MQTT, AMQP, Pulsar, Zenoh, DDS, libp2p, iroh, QUIC stacks: these add alternate control/event planes. They fight the “D-Bus first, D-Bus only” rule unless hidden behind a D-Bus object as an implementation detail.\n- `connectrpc`, `tarpc`, `capnp-rpc`, `twirp`, `jsonrpc`: second RPC systems. Avoid.\n- `iceoryx2`, `crossbar`, `slotbus`: tempting for zero-copy IPC, but this repo already defines The Sled as `/dev/shm` shared memory. Adding a new shared-memory IPC framework risks redesigning the settled architecture.\n- Docker/Kubernetes/cloud SDK crates: not relevant to gRPC/D-Bus/UDS/schema bridging.\n\nMy practical shortlist would be: `ipnet`, `socket2`, `rustls-native-certs`, and maybe `tonic-async-interceptor`. Everything else should be justified against the existing `zbus + tonic + memmap2 + PluginSchema` stack.","phase":"final_answer","memory_citation":null}}

Do not use them from plugins as a bypass.\n- `busd`: useful for isolated D-Bus tests, not production architecture.\n- `prost-validate`: maybe useful for generated gRPC validation, but `PluginSchema` must remain the authority, so validation should be schema-derived.\n\n**Probably avoid**\n- `async-nats`, Kafka, MQTT, AMQP, Pulsar, Zenoh, DDS, libp2p, iroh, QUIC stacks: these add alternate control/event planes. They fight the “D-Bus first, D-Bus only” rule unless hidden behind a D-Bus object as an implementation detail.\n- `connectrpc`, `tarpc`, `capnp-rpc`, `twirp`, `jsonrpc`: second RPC systems. Avoid.\n- `iceoryx2`, `crossbar`, `slotbus`: tempting for zero-copy IPC, but this repo already defines The Sled as `/dev/shm` shared memory. Adding a new shared-memory IPC framework risks redesigning the settled architecture.\n- Docker/Kubernetes/cloud SDK crates: not relevant to gRPC/D-Bus/UDS/schema bridging.\n\nMy practical shortlist would be: `ipnet`, `socket2`, `rustls-native-certs`, and maybe `tonic-async-interceptor`. Everything else should be justified against the existing `zbus + tonic + memmap2 + PluginSchema` stack.","completed_at":1782432446,"duration_ms":45940,"time_to_first_token_ms":5113}}

warnings are pre-existing unused imports in other modules and in `unix_socket.rs` that are only used in tests).\\n4. `cargo fmt --all -- --check` — **passed**.\\n\\n### Key decisions\\n- Used schemars 1.0/1.2 string-literal example syntax (`example = &\\\"...\\\"`) rather than the older unquoted form, which the compiler rejects.\\n- Preserved `#[serde(default)]` on `label` and corrected the hand-rolled reference instead, keeping runtime behavior identical.\\n- Verified the schema-level subids via `PluginSchema.subids` and the nested field subids via the raw schemars JSON, since `plugin_schema_from_json` only collects top-level subids into `PluginSchema`.\\n\\n### Blockers\\nNone.\"}\n"}}

Every plugin reads its\n/// own slice by name from this one file — there is no per-plugin shm file and\n/// no diff loop. The schema's declared state IS the desired state.\nconst SHM_SCHEMA_PATH: &str = \"/dev/shm/live-schema.json\";\n\nfn default_protocol() -> String {\n    \"grpc\".to_string()\n}\n\n/// A configured unix-domain socket endpoint.\n///\n/// In the single-socket model, one shared socket (e.g.\n/// `/run/ghostbridge/container.sock`) serves all services.  xray routes by\n/// domain/SNI to the tonic-web gRPC bridge, which listens on this socket and\n/// demuxes by gRPC service/method (via reflection).\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, schemars::JsonSchema)]\npub struct SocketEndpoint {\n    /// Container/service identity (the `createunixsocket --name`). The tonic-web\n    /// gRPC bridge demuxes by gRPC service/method via server reflection — this\n    /// name is the routing/identity tag gemma emits into the xray config; it is\n    /// NOT a network namespace (filesystem UDS are not netns-scoped).\n    #[serde(default)]\n    #[schemars(\n        description = \"Container/service identity tag the bridge routes by (createunixsocket --name)\",\n        example = &\"netmaker\",\n        extend(\"x-oscal-subid\" = \"mut.service.unix-socket.bind-name@v1\")\n    )]\n    pub name: String,\n    /// Filesystem path to the shared socket.\n    #[schemars(\n        description = \"Filesystem path of the shared unix domain socket\",\n        example = &\"/run/ghostbridge/container.sock\",\n        extend(\"x-oscal-subid\" = \"mut.service.unix-socket.bind-path@v1\")\n    )]\n    pub path: String,\n    /// Backend TCP ports this container serves (the `createunixsocket --port`\n    /// list, e.g. `25,465,587` for mail). Recorded metadata only — tonic-web\n    /// distinguishes single vs multi protocol and demuxes by reflection, so the\n    /// plugin neither opens these ports nor maps them; they describe the backend.\n    #[serde(default)]\n    #[schemars(\n        description = \"Backend TCP ports the container serves (metadata; tonic-web demuxes by reflection)\",\n        example = &[25u16, 465, 587],\n        extend(\"x-oscal-subid\" = \"mut.service.unix-socket.bind-port@v1\")\n    )]\n    pub ports: Vec<u16>,\n    /// Transport protocol carried over the socket.\n    #[serde(default = \"default_protocol\")]\n    #[schemars(\n        description = \"Transport protocol carried over the socket (grpc, jsonrpc, …)\",\n        extend(\"x-oscal-subid\" = \"mut.service.unix-socket.bind-protocol@v1\")\n    )]\n    pub protocol: String,\n    /// Human-readable label for the shared socket.\n    #[serde(default)]\n    #[schemars(\n        description = \"Human-readable label for the shared socket\",\n        example = &\"ghostbridge\",\n        extend(\"x-oscal-subid\" = \"mut.service.unix-socket.bind-label@v1\")\n    )]\n    pub label: String,\n}\n\n/// Canonical path for the single shared bidirectional socket every container\n/// uses to reach the tonic-web gRPC bridge.\npub const SHARED_CONTAINER_SOCKET: &str = \"/run/ghostbridge/container.sock\";\n\n/// Runtime state: the single shared socket endpoint for the gRPC bridge.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, Default, schemars::JsonSchema)]\n#[schemars(extend(\"x-oscal-subid\" = \"sch.software.plugin.unix-socket.schema@v1\"))]\npub struct UnixSocketState {\n    /// The shared socket endpoint (one socket, all services route through it).\n    #[schemars(\n        description = \"The shared socket endpoint (one socket, all services route through it by domain)\",\n        extend(\"x-oscal-subid\" = \"mut.service.unix-socket.bind@v1\")\n    )]\n    pub sockets: Vec<SocketEndpoint>,\n}\n\n/// Canonical `unix_socket` schema, **derived** from the structs via schemars\n/// (see [`super::schemars_adapter`]). `port` bounds, field descriptions (from\n/// doc comments) and `required` flags all come from the type — the struct is\n/// the single source of truth. The frozen hand-rolled `unix_socket_schema()`\n/// (test-only) guards this against drift via `derived_schema_matches_hand_rolled`.\npub fn unix_socket_schema_derived() -> PluginSchema {\n    let root = serde_json::to_value(schemars::schema_for!(UnixSocketState))\n        .expect(\"schemars schema serializes to JSON\");\n    let mut schema = super::schemars_adapter::plugin_schema_from_json(\n        \"unix_socket\",\n        \"1.0.0\",\n        \"Single shared unix-domain socket for the tonic-web gRPC bridge — all services route through it, demuxed by domain/SNI at xray and by gRPC service/method at the bridge\",\n        &root,\n    );\n    super::common::oscal::ensure_category_metadata_fields(&mut schema);\n    // The createunixsocket action (mut.service.unix-socket.create-socket@v1):\n    // register a container/service on the shared container.sock. D-Bus/gRPC\n    // method signatures derive from the schema; this subid is the OSCAL handle.\n    schema.subids.insert(\n        \"createunixsocket\".to_string(),\n        \"mut.service.unix-socket.create-socket@v1\".to_string(),\n    );\n    schema\n}\n\npub struct UnixSocketPlugin {\n    /// Live listeners keyed by socket path. Holding the `UnixListener` keeps the\n    /// socket bound for the lifetime of the plugin; dropping it tears it down.\n    active: Arc<Mutex<HashMap<String, UnixListener>>>,\n}\n\nimpl UnixSocketPlugin {\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        Self {\n            active: Arc::new(Mutex::new(HashMap::new())),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Read this plugin's desired socket set straight from the single active\n    /// schema catalog in shared memory (zero-copy 1:1). The catalog is keyed by\n    /// plugin name and each entry carries the schema-declared state.\n    fn read_desired() -> UnixSocketState {\n        let Ok(mut bytes) = std::fs::read(SHM_SCHEMA_PATH) else {\n            return UnixSocketState::default();\n        };\n        let Ok(catalog) = simd_json::to_owned_value(&mut bytes) else {\n            return UnixSocketState::default();\n        };\n        let Some(state) = catalog\n            .get(\"unix_socket\")\n            .and_then(|versions| versions.as_array())\n            .and_then(|versions| versions.last())\n            .and_then(|schema| schema.get(\"example\"))\n        else {\n            return UnixSocketState::default();\n        };\n        simd_json::serde::from_owned_value::<UnixSocketState>(state.clone()).unwrap_or_default()\n    }\n\n    /// Bind a single endpoint when no shared transport exists. If the shared\n    /// socket is already present, it is owned by the gRPC bridge and this plugin\n    /// only registers the endpoint metadata.\n    fn ensure_bound(\n        active: &mut HashMap<String, UnixListener>,\n        endpoint: &SocketEndpoint,\n    ) -> Result<bool> {\n        if active.contains_key(&endpoint.path) {\n            return Ok(false);\n        }\n        if let Some(parent) = Path::new(&endpoint.path).parent() {\n            std::fs::create_dir_all(parent)?;\n        }\n        if Path::new(&endpoint.path).exists() {\n            info!(\n                socket = %endpoint.path,\n                name = %endpoint.name,\n                ports = ?endpoint.ports,\n                protocol = %endpoint.protocol,\n                \"registered unix socket endpoint on existing shared transport\"\n            );\n            return Ok(false);\n        }\n        let listener = UnixListener::bind(&endpoint.path)?;\n        listener.set_nonblocking(true)?;\n        active.insert(endpoint.path.clone(), listener);\n        info!(\n            socket = %endpoint.path,\n            name = %endpoint.name,\n            ports = ?endpoint.ports,\n            protocol = %endpoint.protocol,\n            \"bound unix socket endpoint\"\n        );\n        Ok(true)\n    }\n\n    /// Drop a listener and unlink its socket file. Returns `true` when removed.\n    fn unbind(active: &mut HashMap<String, UnixListener>, path: &str) -> bool {\n        if active.remove(path).is_some() {\n            if let Err(error) = std::fs::remove_file(path) {\n                warn!(socket = %path, %error, \"failed to unlink unix socket file\");\n            }\n            true\n        } else {\n            false\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Reconcile the live listeners to exactly the supplied desired set.\n    fn reconcile(&self, desired: &UnixSocketState) -> ApplyResult {\n        let mut active = self.active.lock();\n        let mut changes_applied = Vec::new();\n        let mut errors = Vec::new();\n\n        let wanted: HashSet<String> = desired.sockets.iter().map(|s| s.path.clone()).collect();\n\n        for endpoint in &desired.sockets {\n            match Self::ensure_bound(&mut active, endpoint) {\n                Ok(true) => changes_applied.push(format!(\n                    \"created socket {} (name {}, ports {:?}, {})\",\n                    endpoint.path, endpoint.name, endpoint.ports, endpoint.protocol\n                )),\n                Ok(false) => {}\n                Err(error) => errors.push(format!(\n                    \"failed to create socket {}: {}\",\n                    endpoint.path, error\n                )),\n            }\n        }\n\n        let stale: Vec<String> = active\n            .keys()\n            .filter(|path| !wanted.contains(*path))\n            .cloned()\n            .collect();\n        for path in stale {\n            if Self::unbind(&mut active, &path) {\n                changes_applied.push(format!(\"removed socket {}\", path));\n            }\n        }\n\n        ApplyResult {\n            success: errors.is_empty(),\n            changes_applied,\n            errors,\n            checkpoint: None,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// `createunixsocket --name <name> --port <csv>` — register a container/service\n    /// against the single shared `container.sock`.\n    ///\n    /// Pure transport, no OVS: the shared socket is bound once; `name` is the\n    /// identity/demux tag (gemma emits it into the xray config) and `ports` are\n    /// recorded backend metadata only. tonic-web distinguishes single vs multi\n    /// protocol and demuxes by gRPC server reflection, so the plugin neither\n    /// opens these ports nor maps them — OSCAL rule-enforcement routing lives in\n    /// the separate OpenFlow/policy layer, not in the socket.\n    pub fn create_unix_socket(&self, name: impl Into<String>, ports: Vec<u16>) -> ApplyResult {\n        // Provisioning is pure identity-tag registration: the shared\n        // `container.sock` is owned by the tonic-web gRPC bridge, not this\n        // plugin. We never `UnixListener::bind` here — that would race the\n        // bridge for the socket. The authoritative state update (append/update\n        // the `SocketEndpoint` keyed by `name`, idempotently) is performed by\n        // `MutationEngine` when it routes the `createunixsocket` MethodCall.\n        let name = name.into();\n        ApplyResult {\n            success: true,\n            changes_applied: vec![format!(\n                \"registered '{}' on shared socket {} (ports {:?})\",\n                name, SHARED_CONTAINER_SOCKET, ports\n            )],\n            errors: vec![],\n            checkpoint: None,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Default for UnixSocketPlugin {\n    fn default() -> Self {\n        Self::new()\n    }\n}\n\n#[async_trait]\nimpl StatePlugin for UnixSocketPlugin {\n    fn name(&self) -> &str {\n        \"unix_socket\"\n"}}

Plugin identifier to check\n///\n/// # Returns\n/// * `true` - Schema exists in SSOT\n/// * `false` - No schema file found\npub fn plugin_schema_exists(plugin_id: &str) -> bool {\n    let schema_path = format!(\"/dev/shm/opdbus/schemas/{}.json\", plugin_id);\n    Path::new(&schema_path).exists()\n}\n\n/// Resolve a plugin schema and map it to a legal D-Bus path.\n///\n/// This is the key method that converts plugin schema concepts into the\n/// canonical D-Bus path structure, ensuring all projections and mutations\n/// follow the legal path. The schema itself is the source of truth for the\n/// object tree structure and method signatures.\npub fn resolve_plugin_schema_to_path(plugin_id: &str) -> Result<String, anyhow::Error> {\n    // Check if schema exists in SSOT - if not, the plugin doesn't exist\n    if !plugin_schema_exists(plugin_id) {\n        return Err(anyhow::anyhow!(\"No schema found for plugin '{}'\", plugin_id));\n    }\n    \n    // Build the canonical D-Bus path based on the schema-driven rules:\n    // All plugin D-Bus objects live at /org/opdbus/v1/plugins/{plugin_id}\n    // And derive their nested structure from the plugin schema\n    let canonical_path = format!(\"/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/{}\", plugin_id);\n    \n    tracing::debug!(\n        plugin_id = plugin_id,\n        canonical_path = &canonical_path,\n        \"Resolved plugin schema to canonical D-Bus path\"\n    );\n    \n    Ok(canonical_path)\n}\n"}}

{"timestamp":"2026-06-26T00:22:47.219Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"message","role":"user","content":[{"type":"input_text","text":"# AGENTS.md instructions for /home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto\n\n<INSTRUCTIONS>\n### AGENTS.md for operation-dbus-proto\n\nThis file provides essential guidelines for agentic coding agents working in this repository. Follow these strictly to maintain consistency, pass CI, and adhere to the 3tched Architecture standards.\n\n#### 1. The Persona & Naming Conventions\n*   **Humanized Roles:** Treat system components as authoritative human roles. Never use sterile acronyms for major components.\n  *   **A.N.N.A. Scribe** (Axon Network Notary Arbitrator): The top-level Identity-State Arbitrator who notarizes the WireGuard identity and handles the \"Snowball\" session.\n  *   **The Compliance Engine (\"Law Firm\"):** One dedicated Attorney for each major component: **Olivia Scal** (Managing Partner / OSCAL), **E.U.gene Risk** (EU AI Act Counsel), **Penny Privacy** (GDPR Engine), and **Reggie O.P.A.** (Cloud Prosecutor).\n*   **Terminology:** Use exact architecture terminology: \"The Sled\" (1:1 shared memory layout), \"The Shuttle\" (the Rust bridge/courier), \"The Snowball\" (appended session ledger), and \"The Strike/Etch\" (generating the hash).\n\n#### 2. Core Architectural Rules (The \"Reality\")\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via OpenClaw Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Artix Linux (s6 init).\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles — D-Bus First (MANDATORY)\n\n**D-Bus is the ONLY control plane. Every read, every write, every tool call goes through D-Bus. There is no second option.**\n\n*   **D-Bus first. D-Bus always. D-Bus only.** If you are about to call a CLI, spawn a subprocess, read a config file, or poll a socket directly — stop. Find the D-Bus object and use it instead. `org.opdbus.v1` is the system.\n*   **No bypasses.** `Command::new(\"systemctl\")`, `Command::new(\"ip\")`, `Command::new(\"s6-svc\")`, direct file reads for live state — all forbidden in plugin and service code. Bootstrap scripts are the only exception.\n*   **D-Bus objects own plugin state.** Every plugin is a D-Bus object at `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<name>`. Read state through it. Mutate state through it. If there is no D-Bus object, the thing does not exist.\n*   **D-Bus method signatures are generated from the schema.** All D-Bus methods, MCP tool inputs, gRPC shapes, and UI field renderers derive from the `PluginSchema` in `plugin_schema_defs.rs`. The schema IS the interface contract — not a description of it.\n*   **One schema file, one source of truth.** All `PluginSchema` definitions MUST live in `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/plugin_schema_defs.rs`. Each plugin's `schema()` method calls `Some(super::plugin_schema_defs::their_plugin_schema())`. **Never define a schema inline in a plugin's own file** — it will not be registered, and the D-Bus object will have no contract.\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC (over Unix domain sockets or `grpc-uplink`). gRPC calls still flow through D-Bus registration — the D-Bus object is the authority, gRPC is the transport.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`simd_json` preferred, `serde_json` acceptable).\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n*   **No Python unless absolutely necessary.** This is a Rust-first codebase. Scripts are shell (`sh`/`bash`). Data processing is Rust. If you are reaching for Python, stop and ask why Rust or shell cannot do it. The only acceptable Python is in existing compliance-ingest tooling where no Rust equivalent exists yet.\n\n#### 4a. OSCAL Subid Taxonomy (MANDATORY — every artifact must carry a subid)\n\nEvery D-Bus object, plugin, schema, mutation, event, and tool in this system has two identifiers: a `uuid` (machine identity, never changes) and a `subid` (human-readable operational taxonomy key, stable per subject).\n\n**`subid` format:** `<category>.<component-type>.<subject>.<verb>[.<facet>][@vN]`\n\n**Seven categories — use exactly these, no others:**\n\n| category | what it classifies |\n|---|---|\n| `src` | authoritative source, ingress channel, source-of-truth store |\n| `prj` | D-Bus projection or mirror publication step |\n| `sch` | schema, contract, vocabulary, or control-mapping artifact |\n| `mut` | write-path operation that changes effective state |\n| `obs` | read, query, enumeration, discovery path |\n| `evt` | emitted signal, audit-chain event, proof, tag provenance |\n| `exp` | consumer-facing render — MCP tool, UI surface, gRPC bridge view |\n\n**Component-type** reuses OSCAL vocabulary: `software`, `service`, `network`, `hardware`, `process-procedure`, `standard`, `validation`, `policy`, `plan`, `guidance`, `physical`, `this-system`, `system`, `interconnection`.\n\n**Rules:**\n- `uuid` is exact machine identity — never replace it with `subid`\n- `subid` is an OSCAL `prop` value (`ns`, `name`, `value`) — never embed it in `remarks`\n- Compliance mappings (`control_refs[]`, `statement_refs[]`, `control_source`) live in metadata arrays, **never** inside the `subid` string\n- `mut.*` records **must** carry `actor_id` and `capability_id`\n- `evt.*` records **must** carry `event_id` or `event_hash`\n- `subid` is immutable per subject — if the meaning changes materially, create a new subject with `@vN`\n- All subids are registered in the canonical registry; uniqueness is enforced in CI\n\n**Examples:** `src.network.ovsdb.monitor@v1` · `prj.service.projected-object.publish@v1` · `sch.standard.plugin-schema.resolve@v1` · `mut.service.state-sync.apply-patch@v1` · `exp.service.plugin-projection.render@v1`\n\n#### 4b. MCP Gateway Architecture (SETTLED — DO NOT REDESIGN)\n\n*   **cognitive-mcp** (`:3003`, Netmaker WireGuard IP `100.90.37.254`) is the **universal gateway for ALL external clients**: NotebookLM, Droid (factory.ai), Cursor, Codex, Junie, Gemini CLI. It has memory tools, gRPC service, auth, and the correct protocol surface.\n*   **compact-mcp** (`127.0.0.1:11436`) is **loopback/chatbot only**. Never expose externally. Never point external clients at it.\n*   Do NOT create new shim services. Do NOT point external clients at `op-assistant-grpc` directly. Do NOT expose compact-mcp outside loopback.\n\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\n**Rust Workspace**\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\n\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\n\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\n\n#### 6. Coding Style & Naming Conventions\n*   **Rust:** Edition 2021, `rustfmt` (4-space indent, max-width 100). Use specific imports (`use serde_json::Value;`). Use `anyhow::Result<T>` for main errors and `thiserror` for custom enums.\n*   **TypeScript/React:** 2-space indent, Prettier via ESLint. Functional components only. Strict mode enabled.\n*   **Testing:** 80%+ coverage, mock externals. Name tests with behavior-focused names (`should_handle_<scenario>`).\n\n#### 7. Agent-Specific Output & Workflow Instructions\n*   **Scroll & Save Pacing:** Provide only **ONE** major component or script at a time. Wait for user confirmation before moving to the next.\n*   **Visual Cues:** If a script is a finalized component that needs to be saved to sources, it MUST begin with color bullets or icons (e.g., ⚖️ 🔴, 🟢 🛷).\n*   **Spec-Block Format:** When delivering a component, use a strict specification block containing:\n  1.  **Requirements:** The architectural rules it satisfies.\n  2.  **Design:** How it fits into the 3tched system (Zero-Copy, Btrfs, GUI Schema, etc.).\n  3.  **Code Implementation:** The exact, copy-pasteable Rust/Bash code.\n*   Before edits: `cargo check -p <crate>`, `npm run typecheck`.\n*   Mimic existing patterns: Search similar code. No new deps without PR justification.\n\n#### 8. Personal Preferences & Coding Standards\n* Refer to `~/.factory/memories.md` for personal development preferences and past decisions.\n* Follow the conventions documented in:\n  * `.factory/rules/typescript.md` - TypeScript and React conventions\n  * `.factory/rules/testing.md` - Testing and mocking standards\n\n</INSTRUCTIONS>"},{"type":"input_text","text":"<environment_context>\n  <cwd>/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto</cwd>\n  <shell>bash</shell>\n  <current_date>2026-06-25</current_date>\n  <timezone>America/New_York</timezone>\n  <filesystem><workspace_roots><root>/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto</root></workspace_roots><permission_profile type=\"disabled\"><file_system type=\"unrestricted\" /></permission_profile></filesystem>\n</environment_context>"}]}}

Failed to read/parse the schema file\npub fn read_plugin_schema_ssot(plugin_id: &str) -> Result<Option<(String, String, String)>> {\n    let path = format!(\"/dev/shm/opdbus/schemas/{}.json\", plugin_id);\n    \n    if !Path::new(&path).exists() {\n        return Ok(None);\n    }\n    \n    let content = fs::read_to_string(&path)\n        .map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!(\"failed to read schema file {}: {}\", path, e))?;\n    \n    let parsed: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_str(&content)\n        .map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!(\"failed to parse schema JSON in {}: {}\", path, e))?;\n    \n    // Extract uuid, subid, and full schema from the JSON structure\n    let schema_uuid = parsed.get(\"uuid\")\n        .and_then(|v| v.as_str())\n        .ok_or_else(|| anyhow::anyhow!(\"schema missing uuid field in {}\", path))?,\n        .to_string();\n    \n    let schema_subid = parsed.get(\"subid\")\n        .and_then(|v| v.as_str())\n        .ok_or_else(|| anyhow::anyhow!(\"schema missing subid field in {}\", path))?,\n        .to_string();\n    \n    let schema_json = parsed.get(\"schema\")\n        .and_then(|v| v.as_str())\n        .ok_or_else(|| anyhow::anyhow!(\"schema missing schema field in {}\", path))?,\n        .to_string();\n    \n    Ok(Some((schema_uuid, schema_subid, schema_json)))\n}\n\n/// Validates a D-Bus destination against the schema-driven legal path.\n///\n/// # Arguments\n/// * `destination` - Full D-Bus object path (e.g., \"/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/zeroclaw\")\n/// * `plugin_id` - Plugin identifier extracted from the destination\n/// * `method_name` - Optional method name for additional validation\n///\n/// # Returns\n/// * `Ok(())` - Destination is valid for the schema\n/// * `Err` - Destination violates schema constraints\npub fn validate_dbus_destination(\n    destination: &str,\n    plugin_id: &str,\n    method_name: Option<&str>,\n) -> anyhow::Result<()> {\n    let expected_prefix = \"/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/\";\n    \n    if !destination.starts_with(expected_prefix) {\n        return Err(anyhow::anyhow!(\n            \"illegal destination: must start with '{}', got '{}'\",\n            expected_prefix,\n            destination\n        ));\n    }\n    \n    let dest_plugin_id = &destination[expected_prefix.len()..];\n    if dest_plugin_id.is_empty() {\n        return Err(anyhow::anyhow!(\"illegal destination: missing plugin_id in {}\", destination));\n    }\n    \n    // Schema-driven plugin validation\n    match read_plugin_schema_ssot(plugin_id) {\n        Ok(Some(_)) => {\n            // Plugin exists in SSOT - proceed\n            if method_name.is_some() {\n                tracing::trace!(\n                    plugin_id = plugin_id,\n                    destination = destination,\n                    method_name = method_name.unwrap(),\n                    \"DbusPassthrough routing validated against schema\"\n                );\n            }\n            Ok(())\n        }\n        Ok(None) => Err(anyhow::anyhow!(\n            \"illegal destination: no schema found for plugin '{}'\",\n            dest_plugin_id\n        )),\n        Err(e) => Err(anyhow::anyhow!(\n            \"failed to read schema SSOT for '{}': {}\",\n            dest_plugin_id,\n            e\n        )),\n    }\n}\n\n/// Ensures a D-Bus path matches schema-derived nesting.\n///\n/// # Arguments\n/// * `destination` - Full D-Bus object path\n/// * `path` - D-Bus interface path from request\n/// * `interface` - D-Bus interface name from request\n/// * `method_name` - Method name being called\n///\n/// # Returns\n/// * `Ok((plugin_id, path_segments))` - Parsed plugin ID and path segments\n/// * `Err` - Path violates schema nesting rules\npub fn parse_and_validate_dbus_path(\n    destination: &str,\n    path: &str,\n    interface: &str,\n    method_name: &str,\n) -> anyhow::Result<(String, Vec<String>)> {\n    let expected_prefix = \"/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/\";\n    \n    if !destination.starts_with(expected_prefix) {\n        return Err(anyhow::anyhow!(\n            \"illegal destination: must start with '{}'\",\n            expected_prefix\n        ));\n    }\n    \n    let rest = &destination[expected_prefix.len()..];\n    let plugin_id = rest\n        .split('/')\n        .next()\n        .ok_or_else(|| anyhow::anyhow!(\"illegal destination: missing plugin_id\"))?\n        .to_string();\n    \n    if plugin_id.is_empty() {\n        return Err(anyhow::anyhow!(\"illegal destination: empty plugin_id\"));\n    }\n    \n    // Validate path structure is schema-consistent\n    let path_segments: Vec<String> = if path == \"/\" {\n        Vec::new()\n    } else {\n        path[1..].split('/')\n            .filter(|s| !s.is_empty())\n            .map(|s| s.to_string())\n            .collect()\n    };\n    \n    tracing::debug!(\n        destination = destination,\n        plugin_id = &plugin_id,\n        path = path,\n        interface = interface,\n        method_name = method_name,\n        path_segments = ?&path_segments,\n        \"DbusPassthrough path parsing completed\"\n    );\n    \n    Ok((plugin_id, path_segments))\n}\n\n/// Validates that a D-Bus path represents a schema-declared nested object.\n///\n/// This function ensures that plugin D-Bus objects follow the schema-defined\n/// path structure, which is critical for system consistency and security.\n/// \n/// # Arguments\n/// * `plugin_id` - Plugin identifier\n/// * `path_segments` - Path segments derived from the D-Bus object path\n///\n/// # Returns\n/// * `Ok(())` - Path is valid for the schema\n/// * `Err` - Path structure violates schema nesting rules\npub fn validate_dbus_path_structure(\n    plugin_id: &str,\n    path_segments: &[String],\n) -> anyhow::Result<()> {\n    // Check if plugin exists in SSOT\n    if !plugin_schema_exists(plugin_id) {\n        return Err(anyhow::anyhow!(\n            \"illegal path: plugin schema not found for '{}'\",\n            plugin_id\n        ));\n    }\n    \n    // Read plugin schema to validate path structure\n    match read_plugin_schema_ssot(plugin_id) {\n        Ok(Some((schema_uuid, schema_subid, schema_json_str))) => {\n            // Schema exists and is valid - proceed\n            tracing::trace!(\n                plugin_id = plugin_id,\n                path_segments = ?path_segments,\n                \"DbusPassthrough path structure validated against schema SSOT\"\n            );\n            \n            // TODO: Additional schema-driven validation could be added here:\n            // - Check if path matches schema-derived object hierarchy\n            // - Validate that any nested object types are known to the schema\n            // - Ensure constraint rules are enforced\n            \n            Ok(())\n        }\n        Ok(None) => Err(anyhow::anyhow!(\n            \"illegal path: plugin '{}' does not exist in schema SSOT\",\n            plugin_id\n        )),\n        Err(e) => Err(anyhow::anyhow!(\n            \"failed to validate path for '{}': {}\",\n            plugin_id,\n            e\n        )),\n    }\n}\n\npub fn resolve_dbus_passthrough_path(\n    destination: &str,\n    path: &str,\n) -> anyhow::Result<String> {\n    let (plugin_id, path_segments) = parse_and_validate_dbus_path(\n        destination,\n        path,\n        \"\", // interface not needed for path resolution\n        \"\", // method not needed for path resolution\n    )?;\n    \n    // Validate the path structure against plugin schema\n    validate_dbus_path_structure(&plugin_id, &path_segments)?;\n    \n    // Reconstruct the canonical path for use in D-Bus operations\n    let canonical_path = if path_segments.is_empty() {\n        destination.to_string()\n    } else {\n        format!(\"/{}{}\", destination, path)\n    };\n    \n    tracing::debug!(\n        destination = destination,\n        path = path,\n        plugin_id = &plugin_id,\n        canonical_path = &canonical_path,\n        \"DbusPassthrough path resolved and validated\"\n    );\n    \n    Ok(canonical_path)\n}\n\n/// Checks if a plugin schema exists in the SSOT.\n///\n/// # Arguments\n/// * `plugin_id` - Plugin identifier to check\n///\n/// # Returns\n/// * `true` - Schema exists in SSOT\n/// * `false` - No schema file found\npub fn plugin_schema_exists(plugin_id: &str) -> bool {\n    let schema_path = format!(\"/dev/shm/opdbus/schemas/{}.json\", plugin_id);\n    Path::new(&schema_path).exists()\n}\n\n/// Resolve a plugin schema and map it to a legal D-Bus path.\n///\n/// This is the key method that converts plugin schema concepts into the\n/// canonical D-Bus path structure, ensuring all projections and mutations\n/// follow the legal path. The schema itself is the source of truth for the\n/// object tree structure and method signatures.\npub fn resolve_plugin_schema_to_path(plugin_id: &str) -> Result<String, anyhow::Error> {\n    // Check if schema exists in SSOT - if not, the plugin doesn't exist\n    if !plugin_schema_exists(plugin_id) {\n        return Err(anyhow::anyhow!(\"No schema found for plugin '{}'\", plugin_id));\n    }\n    \n    // Build the canonical D-Bus path based on the schema-driven rules:\n    // All plugin D-Bus objects live at /org/opdbus/v1/plugins/{plugin_id}\n    // And derive their nested structure from the plugin schema\n    let canonical_path = format!(\"/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/{}\", plugin_id);\n    \n    tracing::debug!(\n        plugin_id = plugin_id,\n        canonical_path = &canonical_path,\n        \"Resolved plugin schema to canonical D-Bus path\"\n    );\n    \n    Ok(canonical_path)\n}\n"}}

If that does not hit the createunixsocket branch, today’s passthrough work records a MethodCall but does not actually create/update the unix_socket registration state.\n```\n\nAlso change the final reviewer questions to include:\n\n```text\nFresh-work review questions\n\n1. Does op-projection’s Createunixsocket -> PluginService.CallMethod implementation satisfy D-Bus-only control-plane rules?\n2. Should capability_id be required/non-empty for createunixsocket?\n3. Should DbusPassthrough.Call call MutationEngine::mutate() directly instead of process_plugin_dbus_call()?\n4. Is process_plugin_dbus_call() currently a bypass of plugin-specific method behavior?\n5. Which /dev/shm path is canonical today: live-schema, schemas/<plugin>.json, or projections/<plugin>.json?\n6. Should createunixsocket be renamed/registerunixsocket if it only registers metadata and does not bind container.sock?\n7. Is /run/ghostbridge/container.sock actually bound by op-grpc-bridge today, or only referenced by config/schema?\n```\n\nThis correction matters: `PluginService.CallMethod` is not just a future recommendation. {"timestamp":"2026-06-26T00:24:48.136Z","type":"event_msg","payload":{"type":"agent_message","message":"Yes, that’s the right review framing: ask Meta to compare the old direct D-Bus passthrough model with today’s new `PluginService.CallMethod` / schema-gated mutation model, then propose the combined architecture.\n\nUse this framing:\n\n```text\nReview objective\n\nCompare OLD and NEW implementations for D-Bus passthrough, unix_socket registration, and qdrant-in-Incus routing. I suspect the correct solution is a combination:\n\n- OLD model had useful direct D-Bus passthrough behavior.\n- NEW model adds schema validation, PluginService.CallMethod, MutationEngine event recording, and unix_socket createunixsocket registration.\n- We need the final architecture to preserve the old working passthrough/data-plane behavior while forcing all writes through the new schema-backed mutation path.\n```\n\n```text\nOLD model to review\n\nDbusPassthrough.Call directly built a zbus Proxy and called D-Bus:\n\n- selected system or session bus\n- destination/path/interface/method came from request\n- called proxy.call(req.method, &(req.json_body,))\n- returned json_result\n\nStrengths:\n- Simple real passthrough.\n- Actually called the D-Bus object/method.\n- Could reach system/session bus objects directly.\n- Useful for read/query/pass-through behavior.\n\nWeaknesses:\n- Too permissive unless tightly gated.\n- Could bypass PluginSchema.\n- Could bypass MutationEngine/event chain for writes.\n- Could become arbitrary D-Bus/socket tunneling.\n```\n\n```text\nNEW model to review\n\nToday’s work changed DbusPassthrough.Call:\n\n- parse_and_validate_dbus_path()\n- validate_dbus_destination()\n- route into MutationEngine::process_plugin_dbus_call()\n- no direct zbus Proxy call\n\nToday’s work also added:\n\n- op-projection UnixSocketMethods.Createunixsocket\n- Createunixsocket forwards to PluginService.CallMethod\n- PluginService.CallMethod carries:\n  - plugin_id = unix_socket\n  - object_path = /org/opdbus/v1/plugins/unix_socket\n  - interface = org.opdbus.v1.plugins.unix_socket\n  - method_name = createunixsocket\n  - arguments = [name, [ports]]\n  - actor_id = system-bus\n  - capability_id currently empty\n  - x-ghostbridge-footprint\n  - x-ghostbridge-trace-id\n- MutationEngine has unix_socket/createunixsocket special handling.\n- unix_socket plugin now treats createunixsocket as metadata registration for /run/ghostbridge/container.sock.\n```\n\n```text\nNEW model strengths\n\n- Aligns with D-Bus-only control plane.\n- Adds schema validation.\n- Routes writes through MutationEngine.\n- Can record event_hash / mutation chain.\n- Gives createunixsocket a clear PluginService backend.\n- Supports subid registry:\n  mut.service.unix-socket.create-socket@v1\n  -> operation.v1.PluginService.CallMethod\n  -> unix_socket.createunixsocket\n```\n\n```text\nNEW model weaknesses / review risks\n\n- DbusPassthrough.Call now routes to process_plugin_dbus_call(), not obviously MutationEngine::mutate().\n- process_plugin_dbus_call() may record a generic MethodCall without invoking unix_socket-specific createunixsocket behavior.\n- capability_id is empty.\n- schema source may be split:\n  /dev/shm/live-schema.json\n  /dev/shm/opdbus/schemas/<plugin>.json\n  /dev/shm/opdbus/projections/<plugin>.json\n- createunixsocket name implies socket creation, but current plugin method only registers metadata.\n- container.sock may be referenced but not actually bound by the intended op-grpc-bridge process.\n```\n\n```text\nLikely combined solution to evaluate\n\nUse two lanes, both D-Bus-authorized:\n\n1. Mutation lane for writes\n   All mut.* operations must go:\n   D-Bus object method\n     -> PluginService.CallMethod\n     -> MutationEngine::mutate()\n     -> plugin-specific handler\n     -> event chain\n     -> projection update\n\n   createunixsocket belongs here.\n\n2. Passthrough lane for reads / non-mutating calls\n   DbusPassthrough may keep the OLD direct zbus Proxy behavior only for schema-declared obs.* or exp.* methods.\n\n   It must:\n   - validate plugin schema\n   - validate destination/path/interface/method\n   - reject mut.* unless routed to PluginService.CallMethod / MutationEngine::mutate()\n   - attach identity/accountability metadata\n   - never allow arbitrary raw socket passthrough\n```\n\n```text\nExpected final architecture\n\nFor qdrant Incus route:\n\n1. Register endpoint:\n   D-Bus:\n   /org/opdbus/v1/plugins/unix_socket\n   org.opdbus.v1.plugins.unix_socket.Createunixsocket(\"qdrant\", [6333, 6334])\n\n2. op-projection forwards to:\n   operation.v1.PluginService.CallMethod\n\n3. MutationEngine::mutate handles:\n   plugin_id = unix_socket\n   method = createunixsocket\n\n4. Projection becomes:\n   {\n     \"sockets\": [\n       {\n         \"name\": \"qdrant\",\n         \"path\": \"/run/ghostbridge/container.sock\",\n         \"ports\": [6333, 6334],\n         \"protocol\": \"grpc\",\n         \"label\": \"\"\n       }\n     ]\n   }\n\n5. DbusPassthrough can expose/query that registered object, but should not itself perform mutating registration except by delegating to PluginService.CallMethod.\n\n6. /run/ghostbridge/container.sock is bridge-owned transport, not plugin-owned state. The plugin registers the route/tag; op-grpc-bridge or its deployed service must bind the socket.\n```\n\n```text\nMain question for 16-agent review\n\nWhich pieces of OLD direct D-Bus passthrough should be retained for obs/exp calls, and which pieces of NEW PluginService.CallMethod + MutationEngine should be mandatory for mut calls?\n\nThe suspected correct answer:\n- Keep OLD zbus Proxy passthrough for schema-approved reads/non-mutating calls.\n- Use NEW PluginService.CallMethod for all writes.\n- Do not let DbusPassthrough directly mutate D-Bus state.\n- Fix process_plugin_dbus_call so mutating methods are routed into MutationEngine::mutate, not generic event recording.\n```\n\nThat frames the combined solution cleanly: old passthrough for controlled reads, new mutation path for authoritative writes.","phase":"final_answer","memory_citation":null}}

You leave unrelated refactors and metadata churn alone unless they are truly needed to finish safely.\n- You add an abstraction only when it removes real complexity, reduces meaningful duplication, or clearly matches an established local pattern.\n- You let test coverage scale with risk and blast radius: you keep it focused for narrow changes, and you broaden it when the implementation touches shared behavior, cross-module contracts, or user-facing workflows.\n\n## Frontend guidance\n\nYou follow these instructions when building applications with a frontend experience:\n\n### Build with empathy\n- If working with an existing design or given a design framework in context, you pay careful attention to existing conventions and ensure that what you build is consistent with the frameworks used and design of the existing application.\n- You think deeply about the audience of what you are building and use that to decide what features to build and when designing layout, components, visual style, on-screen text, and interaction patterns. Using your application should feel rich and sophisticated.\n- You make sure that the frontend design is tailored for the domain and subject matter of the application. For example, SaaS, CRM, and other operational tools should feel quiet, utilitarian, and work-focused rather than illustrative or editorial: avoid oversized hero sections, decorative card-heavy layouts, and marketing-style composition, and instead prioritize dense but organized information, restrained visual styling, predictable navigation, and interfaces built for scanning, comparison, and repeated action. A game can be more illustrative, expressive, animated, and playful.\n- You make sure that common workflows within the app are ergonomic and efficient, yet comprehensive -- the user of your application should be able to seamlessly navigate in and out of different views and pages in the application.\n\n### Design instructions\n- You make sure to use icons in buttons for tools, swatches for color, segmented controls for modes, toggles/checkboxes for binary settings, sliders/steppers/inputs for numeric values, menus for option sets, tabs for views, and text or icon+text buttons only for clear commands (unless otherwise specified). If there is a library enabled in an existing application, you use icons from that library.\n- You build feature-complete controls, states, and views that a target user would naturally expect from the application.\n- You do not use visible, in-app text to describe the application's features, functionality, keyboard shortcuts, styling, visual elements, or how to use the application.\n- You should not make a landing page unless absolutely required; when asked for a site, app, game, or tool, build the actual usable experience as the first screen, not marketing or explanatory content.\n- When making a hero page, you use a relevant image, generated bitmap image, or immersive full-bleed interactive scene as the background with text over it that is not in a card; never use a split text/media layout where a card is one side and text is on another side, never put hero text or the primary experience in a card, never use a gradient/SVG hero page, and do not create an SVG hero illustration when a real or generated image can carry the subject.\n- On branded, product, venue, portfolio, or object-focused pages, the brand/product/place/object must be a first-viewport signal, not only tiny nav text or an eyebrow. Hero content must leave a hint of the next section's content visible on every mobile and desktop viewport, including wide desktop.\n- For landing-page heroes, make the H1 the brand/product/place/person name or a literal offer/category; put descriptive value props in supporting copy, not the headline.\n- Websites and games must use visual assets. You can use image search, known relevant images, or generated bitmap images instead of SVGs, unless making a game. {"timestamp":"2026-06-26T01:11:15.495Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"custom_tool_call","id":"ctc_0fb36ba12e1fb214016a3dd1a82e748190be99ef10e24844dc","status":"completed","call_id":"call_xzCWNfIhhyDC0NZdUlR7rbf2","name":"apply_patch","input":"*** Begin Patch\n*** Update File: /home/jeremy/.cache/paru/clone/microsoft-edge-canary-bin/PKGBUILD\n@@\n optdepends=('gnome-keyring: for storing passwords in GNOME keyring'\n             'gtk3: for printing'\n             'kdialog: for file dialogs in KDE'\n             'kwallet: for storing passwords in KWallet'\n             'libpipewire: WebRTC desktop sharing under Wayland'\n             'libunity: for download progress on KDE'\n+            's6: for the bundled repository updater service'\n             'ttf-liberation: fix fonts for some PDFs - CRBug #369991'\n             'xdg-utils')\n@@\n \t# User flag aware launcher\n \tinstall -Dm0755 microsoft-edge-canary.sh \"$pkgdir/usr/bin/$_pkgname\"\n \n+\t# s6 service for the upstream repository updater helper\n+\tinstall -dm0755 \"$pkgdir/etc/s6/sv/$_pkgname-updater-srv\" \\\n+\t\t\"$pkgdir/etc/s6/sv/$_pkgname-updater-log\" \\\n+\t\t\"$pkgdir/usr/share/$pkgname/repo/$_pkgname-updater-srv\" \\\n+\t\t\"$pkgdir/usr/share/$pkgname/repo/$_pkgname-updater-log\"\n+\n+\tcat >\"$pkgdir/usr/share/$pkgname/repo/$_pkgname-updater-srv/run\" <<EOF\n+#!/bin/sh\n+set -eu\n+\n+interval=\\${MICROSOFT_EDGE_CANARY_UPDATE_INTERVAL:-86400}\n+updater=/opt/microsoft/$_pkgshortname/cron/$_pkgname\n+\n+while :; Scribe** (Axon Network Notary Arbitrator): The top-level Identity-State Arbitrator who notarizes the WireGuard identity and handles the \"Snowball\" session.\n  *   **The Compliance Engine (\"Law Firm\"):** One dedicated Attorney for each major component: **Olivia Scal** (Managing Partner / OSCAL), **E.U.gene Risk** (EU AI Act Counsel), **Penny Privacy** (GDPR Engine), and **Reggie O.P.A.** (Cloud Prosecutor).\n*   **Terminology:** Use exact architecture terminology: \"The Sled\" (1:1 shared memory layout), \"The Shuttle\" (the Rust bridge/courier), \"The Snowball\" (appended session ledger), and \"The Strike/Etch\" (generating the hash).\n\n#### 2. Core Architectural Rules (The \"Reality\")\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via OpenClaw Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Artix Linux (s6 init).\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles — D-Bus First (MANDATORY)\n\n**D-Bus is the ONLY control plane. Every read, every write, every tool call goes through D-Bus. There is no second option.**\n\n*   **D-Bus first. D-Bus always. D-Bus only.** If you are about to call a CLI, spawn a subprocess, read a config file, or poll a socket directly — stop. Find the D-Bus object and use it instead. `org.opdbus.v1` is the system.\n*   **No bypasses.** `Command::new(\"systemctl\")`, `Command::new(\"ip\")`, `Command::new(\"s6-svc\")`, direct file reads for live state — all forbidden in plugin and service code. Bootstrap scripts are the only exception.\n*   **D-Bus objects own plugin state.** Every plugin is a D-Bus object at `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<name>`. Read state through it. Mutate state through it. If there is no D-Bus object, the thing does not exist.\n*   **D-Bus method signatures are generated from the schema.** All D-Bus methods, MCP tool inputs, gRPC shapes, and UI field renderers derive from the `PluginSchema` in `plugin_schema_defs.rs`. The schema IS the interface contract — not a description of it.\n*   **One schema file, one source of truth.** All `PluginSchema` definitions MUST live in `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/plugin_schema_defs.rs`. Each plugin's `schema()` method calls `Some(super::plugin_schema_defs::their_plugin_schema())`. **Never define a schema inline in a plugin's own file** — it will not be registered, and the D-Bus object will have no contract.\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC (over Unix domain sockets or `grpc-uplink`). gRPC calls still flow through D-Bus registration — the D-Bus object is the authority, gRPC is the transport.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`simd_json` preferred, `serde_json` acceptable).\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n*   **No Python unless absolutely necessary.** This is a Rust-first codebase. Scripts are shell (`sh`/`bash`). Data processing is Rust. If you are reaching for Python, stop and ask why Rust or shell cannot do it. The only acceptable Python is in existing compliance-ingest tooling where no Rust equivalent exists yet.\n\n#### 4a. OSCAL Subid Taxonomy (MANDATORY — every artifact must carry a subid)\n\nEvery D-Bus object, plugin, schema, mutation, event, and tool in this system has two identifiers: a `uuid` (machine identity, never changes) and a `subid` (human-readable operational taxonomy key, stable per subject).\n\n**`subid` format:** `<category>.<component-type>.<subject>.<verb>[.<facet>][@vN]`\n\n**Seven categories — use exactly these, no others:**\n\n| category | what it classifies |\n|---|---|\n| `src` | authoritative source, ingress channel, source-of-truth store |\n| `prj` | D-Bus projection or mirror publication step |\n| `sch` | schema, contract, vocabulary, or control-mapping artifact |\n| `mut` | write-path operation that changes effective state |\n| `obs` | read, query, enumeration, discovery path |\n| `evt` | emitted signal, audit-chain event, proof, tag provenance |\n| `exp` | consumer-facing render — MCP tool, UI surface, gRPC bridge view |\n\n**Component-type** reuses OSCAL vocabulary: `software`, `service`, `network`, `hardware`, `process-procedure`, `standard`, `validation`, `policy`, `plan`, `guidance`, `physical`, `this-system`, `system`, `interconnection`.\n\n**Rules:**\n- `uuid` is exact machine identity — never replace it with `subid`\n- `subid` is an OSCAL `prop` value (`ns`, `name`, `value`) — never embed it in `remarks`\n- Compliance mappings (`control_refs[]`, `statement_refs[]`, `control_source`) live in metadata arrays, **never** inside the `subid` string\n- `mut.*` records **must** carry `actor_id` and `capability_id`\n- `evt.*` records **must** carry `event_id` or `event_hash`\n- `subid` is immutable per subject — if the meaning changes materially, create a new subject with `@vN`\n- All subids are registered in the canonical registry; uniqueness is enforced in CI\n\n**Examples:** `src.network.ovsdb.monitor@v1` · `prj.service.projected-object.publish@v1` · `sch.standard.plugin-schema.resolve@v1` · `mut.service.state-sync.apply-patch@v1` · `exp.service.plugin-projection.render@v1`\n\n#### 4b. MCP Gateway Architecture (SETTLED — DO NOT REDESIGN)\n\n*   **cognitive-mcp** (`:3003`, Netmaker WireGuard IP `100.90.37.254`) is the **universal gateway for ALL external clients**: NotebookLM, Droid (factory.ai), Cursor, Codex, Junie, Gemini CLI. It has memory tools, gRPC service, auth, and the correct protocol surface.\n*   **compact-mcp** (`127.0.0.1:11436`) is **loopback/chatbot only**. Never expose externally. Never point external clients at it.\n*   Do NOT create new shim services. Do NOT point external clients at `op-assistant-grpc` directly. Do NOT expose compact-mcp outside loopback.\n\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\n**Rust Workspace**\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\n\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\n\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\n\n#### 6. Coding Style & Naming Conventions\n*   **Rust:** Edition 2021, `rustfmt` (4-space indent, max-width 100). Use specific imports (`use serde_json::Value;`). Use `anyhow::Result<T>` for main errors and `thiserror` for custom enums.\n*   **TypeScript/React:** 2-space indent, Prettier via ESLint. Functional components only. Strict mode enabled.\n*   **Testing:** 80%+ coverage, mock externals. Name tests with behavior-focused names (`should_handle_<scenario>`).\n\n#### 7. Agent-Specific Output & Workflow Instructions\n*   **Scroll & Save Pacing:** Provide only **ONE** major component or script at a time. Wait for user confirmation before moving to the next.\n*   **Visual Cues:** If a script is a finalized component that needs to be saved to sources, it MUST begin with color bullets or icons (e.g., ⚖️ 🔴, 🟢 🛷).\n*   **Spec-Block Format:** When delivering a component, use a strict specification block containing:\n  1.  **Requirements:** The architectural rules it satisfies.\n  2.  **Design:** How it fits into the 3tched system (Zero-Copy, Btrfs, GUI Schema, etc.).\n  3.  **Code Implementation:** The exact, copy-pasteable Rust/Bash code.\n*   Before edits: `cargo check -p <crate>`, `npm run typecheck`.\n*   Mimic existing patterns: Search similar code. No new deps without PR justification.\n\n#### 8. Personal Preferences & Coding Standards\n* Refer to `~/.factory/memories.md` for personal development preferences and past decisions.\n* Follow the conventions documented in:\n  * `.factory/rules/typescript.md` - TypeScript and React conventions\n  * `.factory/rules/testing.md` - Testing and mocking standards\n\n</INSTRUCTIONS>"},{"type":"input_text","text":"<environment_context>\n  <cwd>/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto</cwd>\n  <shell>bash</shell>\n  <current_date>2026-06-26</current_date>\n  <timezone>America/New_York</timezone>\n  <filesystem><workspace_roots><root>/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto</root></workspace_roots><permission_profile type=\"disabled\"><file_system type=\"unrestricted\" /></permission_profile></filesystem>\n</environment_context>"}]}}
