NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via OpenClaw Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Artix Linux (s6 init).\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles — D-Bus First (MANDATORY)\n\n**D-Bus is the ONLY control plane. Every read, every write, every tool call goes through D-Bus. There is no second option.**\n\n*   **D-Bus first. D-Bus always. D-Bus only.** If you are about to call a CLI, spawn a subprocess, read a config file, or poll a socket directly — stop. Find the D-Bus object and use it instead. `org.opdbus.v1` is the system.\n*   **No bypasses.** `Command::new(\"systemctl\")`, `Command::new(\"ip\")`, `Command::new(\"s6-svc\")`, direct file reads for live state — all forbidden in plugin and service code. Bootstrap scripts are the only exception.\n*   **D-Bus objects own plugin state.** Every plugin is a D-Bus object at `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<name>`. Read state through it. Mutate state through it. If there is no D-Bus object, the thing does not exist.\n*   **D-Bus method signatures are generated from the schema.** All D-Bus methods, MCP tool inputs, gRPC shapes, and UI field renderers derive from the `PluginSchema` in `plugin_schema_defs.rs`. The schema IS the interface contract — not a description of it.\n*   **One schema file, one source of truth.** All `PluginSchema` definitions MUST live in `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/plugin_schema_defs.rs`. Each plugin's `schema()` method calls `Some(super::plugin_schema_defs::their_plugin_schema())`. **Never define a schema inline in a plugin's own file** — it will not be registered, and the D-Bus object will have no contract.\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC (over Unix domain sockets or `grpc-uplink`). gRPC calls still flow through D-Bus registration — the D-Bus object is the authority, gRPC is the transport.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`simd_json` preferred, `serde_json` acceptable).\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n*   **No Python unless absolutely necessary.** This is a Rust-first codebase. Scripts are shell (`sh`/`bash`). Data processing is Rust. If you are reaching for Python, stop and ask why Rust or shell cannot do it. The only acceptable Python is in existing compliance-ingest tooling where no Rust equivalent exists yet.\n\n#### 4a. OSCAL Subid Taxonomy (MANDATORY — every artifact must carry a subid)\n\nEvery D-Bus object, plugin, schema, mutation, event, and tool in this system has two identifiers: a `uuid` (machine identity, never changes) and a `subid` (human-readable operational taxonomy key, stable per subject).\n\n**`subid` format:** `<category>.<component-type>.<subject>.<verb>[.<facet>][@vN]`\n\n**Seven categories — use exactly these, no others:**\n\n| category | what it classifies |\n|---|---|\n| `src` | authoritative source, ingress channel, source-of-truth store |\n| `prj` | D-Bus projection or mirror publication step |\n| `sch` | schema, contract, vocabulary, or control-mapping artifact |\n| `mut` | write-path operation that changes effective state |\n| `obs` | read, query, enumeration, discovery path |\n| `evt` | emitted signal, audit-chain event, proof, tag provenance |\n| `exp` | consumer-facing render — MCP tool, UI surface, gRPC bridge view |\n\n**Component-type** reuses OSCAL vocabulary: `software`, `service`, `network`, `hardware`, `process-procedure`, `standard`, `validation`, `policy`, `plan`, `guidance`, `physical`, `this-system`, `system`, `interconnection`.\n\n**Rules:**\n- `uuid` is exact machine identity — never replace it with `subid`\n- `subid` is an OSCAL `prop` value (`ns`, `name`, `value`) — never embed it in `remarks`\n- Compliance mappings (`control_refs[]`, `statement_refs[]`, `control_source`) live in metadata arrays, **never** inside the `subid` string\n- `mut.*` records **must** carry `actor_id` and `capability_id`\n- `evt.*` records **must** carry `event_id` or `event_hash`\n- `subid` is immutable per subject — if the meaning changes materially, create a new subject with `@vN`\n- All subids are registered in the canonical registry; uniqueness is enforced in CI\n\n**Examples:** `src.network.ovsdb.monitor@v1` · `prj.service.projected-object.publish@v1` · `sch.standard.plugin-schema.resolve@v1` · `mut.service.state-sync.apply-patch@v1` · `exp.service.plugin-projection.render@v1`\n\n#### 4b. MCP Gateway Architecture (SETTLED — DO NOT REDESIGN)\n\n*   **cognitive-mcp** (`:3003`, Netmaker WireGuard IP `100.90.37.254`) is the **universal gateway for ALL external clients**: NotebookLM, Droid (factory.ai), Cursor, Codex, Junie, Gemini CLI. It has memory tools, gRPC service, auth, and the correct protocol surface.\n*   **compact-mcp** (`127.0.0.1:11436`) is **loopback/chatbot only**. Never expose externally. Never point external clients at it.\n*   Do NOT create new shim services. Do NOT point external clients at `op-assistant-grpc` directly. Do NOT expose compact-mcp outside loopback.\n\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\n**Rust Workspace**\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\n\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\n\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\n\n#### 6. Coding Style & Naming Conventions\n*   **Rust:** Edition 2021, `rustfmt` (4-space indent, max-width 100). Use specific imports (`use serde_json::Value;`). Use `anyhow::Result<T>` for main errors and `thiserror` for custom enums.\n*   **TypeScript/React:** 2-space indent, Prettier via ESLint. Functional components only. Strict mode enabled.\n*   **Testing:** 80%+ coverage, mock externals. Name tests with behavior-focused names (`should_handle_<scenario>`).\n\n#### 7. Agent-Specific Output & Workflow Instructions\n*   **Scroll & Save Pacing:** Provide only **ONE** major component or script at a time. Wait for user confirmation before moving to the next.\n*   **Visual Cues:** If a script is a finalized component that needs to be saved to sources, it MUST begin with color bullets or icons (e.g., ⚖️ 🔴, 🟢 🛷).\n*   **Spec-Block Format:** When delivering a component, use a strict specification block containing:\n  1.  **Requirements:** The architectural rules it satisfies.\n  2.  **Design:** How it fits into the 3tched system (Zero-Copy, Btrfs, GUI Schema, etc.).\n  3.  **Code Implementation:** The exact, copy-pasteable Rust/Bash code.\n*   Before edits: `cargo check -p <crate>`, `npm run typecheck`.\n*   Mimic existing patterns: Search similar code. No new deps without PR justification.\n\n#### 8. Personal Preferences & Coding Standards\n* Refer to `~/.factory/memories.md` for personal development preferences and past decisions.\n* Follow the conventions documented in:\n  * `.factory/rules/typescript.md` - TypeScript and React conventions\n  * `.factory/rules/testing.md` - Testing and mocking standards\n\n</INSTRUCTIONS>"},{"type":"input_text","text":"<environment_context>\n  <cwd>/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto</cwd>\n  <shell>bash</shell>\n  <current_date>2026-06-26</current_date>\n  <timezone>America/New_York</timezone>\n  <filesystem><workspace_roots><root>/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto</root></workspace_roots><permission_profile type=\"disabled\"><file_system type=\"unrestricted\" /></permission_profile></filesystem>\n</environment_context>"}]}}

{"timestamp":"2026-06-26T17:48:08.171Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"function_call_output","call_id":"call_tsB5kD7Mf4kjRWClLhrP6GGt","output":"Chunk ID: 5f84dc\nWall time: 0.0000 seconds\nProcess exited with code 0\nOriginal token count: 229\nOutput:\n#!/bin/bash\n# makepkg wrapper — auto-patch libsystemd → libelogind before building\n# This wrapper appears before /usr/bin/makepkg in PATH and transparently patches\n# any AUR/build that references libsystemd, then delegates to the real makepkg.\n\nset -euo pipefail\n\nREAL_MAKEPKG=\"/usr/bin/makepkg\"\nPATCH_SCRIPT=\"/usr/local/lib/makepkg-hooks/autopatch-systemd-to-elogind.sh\"\n\n# Only patch if elogind is available and we're in a build directory\nif [[ -f \"$PATCH_SCRIPT\" ]] && pkg-config --exists libelogind 2>/dev/null; then\n    # Check if we're in a PKGBUILD directory\n    if [[ -f PKGBUILD ]]; then\n        echo \"makepkg-wrapper: auto-patching libsystemd → libelogind...\"\n        # Run the patch script (sourced so it runs in our shell context)\n        export SRCDIR=\"${SRCDIR:-$PWD/src}\"\n        bash \"$PATCH_SCRIPT\" || true\n    fi\nfi\n\n# Delegate to real makepkg with all arguments\nexec \"$REAL_MAKEPKG\" \"$@\"\n"}}
{"timestamp":"2026-06-26T17:48:08.176Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"function_call_output","call_id":"call_QunDSfaGDbEqq2rwfmYWalwN","output":"Chunk ID: 30f493\nWall time: 0.0000 seconds\nProcess exited with code 0\nOriginal token count: 1058\nOutput:\n#!/bin/bash\n# makepkg PreBuild hook — auto-patch libsystemd → libelogind\n# Install to /usr/local/lib/makepkg-hooks/ and reference from a hook in /etc/makepkg.d/\n#\n# This hook runs before every makepkg build and transparently replaces\n# libsystemd dependencies with libelogind on Artix/s6 systems.\n\nset -euo pipefail\n\n# Only patch if elogind is actually available\nif ! pkg-config --exists libelogind 2>/dev/null; then\n    echo \"makepkg-hook: libelogind not found — skipping systemd→elogind patch\"\n    exit 0\nfi\n\nSRCDIR=\"${SRCDIR:-$PWD/src}\"\n\n# If src/ doesn't exist yet, nothing to patch\n[[ -d \"$SRCDIR\" ]] || exit 0\n\necho \"makepkg-hook: scanning for libsystemd references in $SRCDIR ...\"\n\n# ── 1. Patch meson.build ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────\nfind \"$SRCDIR\" -name \"meson.build\" -type f -print0 2>/dev/null | \\\n    while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do\n        if grep -q \"libsystemd\" \"$f\" 2>/dev/null; then\n            echo \"makepkg-hook: patching meson.build: $f\"\n            sed -i 's/dependency('\\''libsystemd'\\'')/dependency('\\''libelogind'\\'')/g; \\\n                      s/dependency(\"libsystemd\")/dependency(\"libelogind\")/g; \\\n                      s/libsystemd/libelogind/g' \"$f\"\n        fi\n    done\n\n# ── 2. Patch CMakeLists.txt ────────────────────────────────────────────────\nfind \"$SRCDIR\" -name \"CMakeLists.txt\" -type f -print0 2>/dev/null | \\\n    while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do\n        if grep -qi \"libsystemd\" \"$f\" 2>/dev/null; then\n            echo \"makepkg-hook: patching CMakeLists.txt: $f\"\n            sed -i 's/libsystemd/libelogind/g; \\\n                      s/Libsystemd/Libelogind/g; \\\n                      s/LIBSYSTEMD/LIBELOGIND/g' \"$f\"\n        fi\n    done\n\n# ── 3. Patch configure.ac / configure.in ───────────────────────────────────\nfind \"$SRCDIR\" -type f \\( -name \"configure.ac\" -o -name \"configure.in\" \\) -print0 2>/dev/null | \\\n    while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do\n        if grep -q \"libsystemd\" \"$f\" 2>/dev/null; then\n            echo \"makepkg-hook: patching configure.ac: $f\"\n            sed -i 's/libsystemd/libelogind/g' \"$f\"\n        fi\n    done\n\n# ── 4. Patch pkg-config .pc files ──────────────────────────────────────────\nfind \"$SRCDIR\" -name \"*.pc.in\" -type f -print0 2>/dev/null | \\\n    while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do\n        if grep -q \"libsystemd\" \"$f\" 2>/dev/null; then\n            echo \"makepkg-hook: patching .pc file: $f\"\n            sed -i 's/libsystemd/libelogind/g' \"$f\"\n        fi\n    done\n\n# ── 5. Patch PKGBUILD depends ──────────────────────────────────────────────\nif [[ -f PKGBUILD ]]; then\n    if grep -q '\"systemd-libs\"' PKGBUILD 2>/dev/null || \\\n       grep -q \"'systemd-libs'\" PKGBUILD 2>/dev/null || \\\n       grep -q 'systemd-libs' PKGBUILD 2>/dev/null; then\n        echo \"makepkg-hook: patching PKGBUILD depends (systemd-libs → elogind)\"\n        sed -i 's/\"systemd-libs\"/\"elogind\"/g; \\\n                  s/'\\''systemd-libs'\\''/'\\''elogind'\\''/g; \\\n                  s/systemd-libs/elogind/g' PKGBUILD\n    fi\nfi\n\n# ── 6. Patch header includes (systemd/*.h → elogind/systemd/*.h) ────────────\nfind \"$SRCDIR\" -type f \\( -name \"*.c\" -o -name \"*.cpp\" -o -name \"*.h\" -o -name \"*.hpp\" \\) -print0 2>/dev/null | \\\n    while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do\n        if grep -q '#include <systemd/' \"$f\" 2>/dev/null && \\\n           ! grep -q '#include <elogind/systemd/' \"$f\" 2>/dev/null; then\n            # Only patch if elogind actually has the systemd compat headers\n            if [[ -d /usr/include/elogind/systemd ]]; then\n                echo \"makepkg-hook: patching includes in: $f\"\n                sed -i 's|#include <systemd/|#include <elogind/systemd/|g' \"$f\"\n            fi\n        fi\n    done\n\necho \"makepkg-hook: systemd→elogind patching complete\"\n"}}

{"timestamp":"2026-06-26T17:48:38.965Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"function_call_output","call_id":"call_Fj0WUr92N64Pwo1hIOl0Aaco","output":"Chunk ID: d149ee\nWall time: 0.0000 seconds\nProcess exited with code 0\nOriginal token count: 230\nOutput:\n#!/bin/bash\n# makepkg wrapper — auto-patch libsystemd → libelogind before building\n# This wrapper appears before /usr/bin/makepkg in PATH and transparently patches\n# any AUR/build that references libsystemd, then delegates to the real makepkg.\n\nset -euo pipefail\n\nREAL_MAKEPKG=\"/usr/bin/makepkg\"\nPATCH_SCRIPT=\"/usr/local/lib/makepkg-hooks/autopatch-systemd-to-elogind.sh\"\n\n# Only patch if elogind is available and we're in a build directory\nif [[ -f \"$PATCH_SCRIPT\" ]] && pkg-config --exists libelogind 2>/dev/null; then\n    # Check if we're in a PKGBUILD directory\n    if [[ -f PKGBUILD ]]; then\n        echo \"makepkg-wrapper: auto-patching libsystemd → libelogind...\" >&2\n        # Run the patch script (sourced so it runs in our shell context)\n        export SRCDIR=\"${SRCDIR:-$PWD/src}\"\n        bash \"$PATCH_SCRIPT\" || true\n    fi\nfi\n\n# Delegate to real makepkg with all arguments\nexec \"$REAL_MAKEPKG\" \"$@\"\n"}}
{"timestamp":"2026-06-26T17:48:38.971Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"function_call_output","call_id":"call_CrisduLBmT9rUJSsBBqeSxuv","output":"Chunk ID: 51a06b\nWall time: 0.0000 seconds\nProcess exited with code 0\nOriginal token count: 1067\nOutput:\n#!/bin/bash\n# makepkg PreBuild hook — auto-patch libsystemd → libelogind\n# Install to /usr/local/lib/makepkg-hooks/ and reference from a hook in /etc/makepkg.d/\n#\n# This hook runs before every makepkg build and transparently replaces\n# libsystemd dependencies with libelogind on Artix/s6 systems.\n\nset -euo pipefail\n\n# Only patch if elogind is actually available\nif ! pkg-config --exists libelogind 2>/dev/null; then\n    echo \"makepkg-hook: libelogind not found — skipping systemd→elogind patch\" >&2\n    exit 0\nfi\n\nSRCDIR=\"${SRCDIR:-$PWD/src}\"\n\n# If src/ doesn't exist yet, nothing to patch\n[[ -d \"$SRCDIR\" ]] || exit 0\n\necho \"makepkg-hook: scanning for libsystemd references in $SRCDIR ...\" >&2\n\n# ── 1. Patch meson.build ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────\nfind \"$SRCDIR\" -name \"meson.build\" -type f -print0 2>/dev/null | \\\n    while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do\n        if grep -q \"libsystemd\" \"$f\" 2>/dev/null; then\n            echo \"makepkg-hook: patching meson.build: $f\" >&2\n            sed -i 's/dependency('\\''libsystemd'\\'')/dependency('\\''libelogind'\\'')/g; \\\n                      s/dependency(\"libsystemd\")/dependency(\"libelogind\")/g; \\\n                      s/libsystemd/libelogind/g' \"$f\"\n        fi\n    done\n\n# ── 2. Patch CMakeLists.txt ────────────────────────────────────────────────\nfind \"$SRCDIR\" -name \"CMakeLists.txt\" -type f -print0 2>/dev/null | \\\n    while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do\n        if grep -qi \"libsystemd\" \"$f\" 2>/dev/null; then\n            echo \"makepkg-hook: patching CMakeLists.txt: $f\" >&2\n            sed -i 's/libsystemd/libelogind/g; \\\n                      s/Libsystemd/Libelogind/g; \\\n                      s/LIBSYSTEMD/LIBELOGIND/g' \"$f\"\n        fi\n    done\n\n# ── 3. Patch configure.ac / configure.in ───────────────────────────────────\nfind \"$SRCDIR\" -type f \\( -name \"configure.ac\" -o -name \"configure.in\" \\) -print0 2>/dev/null | \\\n    while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do\n        if grep -q \"libsystemd\" \"$f\" 2>/dev/null; then\n            echo \"makepkg-hook: patching configure.ac: $f\" >&2\n            sed -i 's/libsystemd/libelogind/g' \"$f\"\n        fi\n    done\n\n# ── 4. Patch pkg-config .pc files ──────────────────────────────────────────\nfind \"$SRCDIR\" -name \"*.pc.in\" -type f -print0 2>/dev/null | \\\n    while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do\n        if grep -q \"libsystemd\" \"$f\" 2>/dev/null; then\n            echo \"makepkg-hook: patching .pc file: $f\" >&2\n            sed -i 's/libsystemd/libelogind/g' \"$f\"\n        fi\n    done\n\n# ── 5. Patch PKGBUILD depends ──────────────────────────────────────────────\nif [[ -f PKGBUILD ]]; then\n    if grep -q '\"systemd-libs\"' PKGBUILD 2>/dev/null || \\\n       grep -q \"'systemd-libs'\" PKGBUILD 2>/dev/null || \\\n       grep -q 'systemd-libs' PKGBUILD 2>/dev/null; then\n        echo \"makepkg-hook: patching PKGBUILD depends (systemd-libs → elogind)\" >&2\n        sed -i 's/\"systemd-libs\"/\"elogind\"/g; \\\n                  s/'\\''systemd-libs'\\''/'\\''elogind'\\''/g; \\\n                  s/systemd-libs/elogind/g' PKGBUILD\n    fi\nfi\n\n# ── 6. Patch header includes (systemd/*.h → elogind/systemd/*.h) ────────────\nfind \"$SRCDIR\" -type f \\( -name \"*.c\" -o -name \"*.cpp\" -o -name \"*.h\" -o -name \"*.hpp\" \\) -print0 2>/dev/null | \\\n    while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do\n        if grep -q '#include <systemd/' \"$f\" 2>/dev/null && \\\n           ! grep -q '#include <elogind/systemd/' \"$f\" 2>/dev/null; then\n            # Only patch if elogind actually has the systemd compat headers\n            if [[ -d /usr/include/elogind/systemd ]]; then\n                echo \"makepkg-hook: patching includes in: $f\" >&2\n                sed -i 's|#include <systemd/|#include <elogind/systemd/|g' \"$f\"\n            fi\n        fi\n    done\n\necho \"makepkg-hook: systemd→elogind patching complete\" >&2\n"}}

{"timestamp":"2026-06-27T23:38:08.144Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"message","role":"user","content":[{"type":"input_text","text":"# AGENTS.md instructions for /home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto\n\n<INSTRUCTIONS>\n### AGENTS.md for operation-dbus-proto\n\nThis file provides essential guidelines for agentic coding agents working in this repository. Follow these strictly to maintain consistency, pass CI, and adhere to the 3tched Architecture standards.\n\n#### 1. The Persona & Naming Conventions\n*   **Humanized Roles:** Treat system components as authoritative human roles. Never use sterile acronyms for major components.\n  *   **A.N.N.A. Scribe** (Axon Network Notary Arbitrator): The top-level Identity-State Arbitrator who notarizes the WireGuard identity and handles the \"Snowball\" session.\n  *   **The Compliance Engine (\"Law Firm\"):** One dedicated Attorney for each major component: **Olivia Scal** (Managing Partner / OSCAL), **E.U.gene Risk** (EU AI Act Counsel), **Penny Privacy** (GDPR Engine), and **Reggie O.P.A.** (Cloud Prosecutor).\n*   **Terminology:** Use exact architecture terminology: \"The Sled\" (1:1 shared memory layout), \"The Shuttle\" (the Rust bridge/courier), \"The Snowball\" (appended session ledger), and \"The Strike/Etch\" (generating the hash).\n\n#### 2. Core Architectural Rules (The \"Reality\")\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via OpenClaw Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Artix Linux (s6 init).\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles — D-Bus First (MANDATORY)\n\n**D-Bus is the ONLY control plane. Every read, every write, every tool call goes through D-Bus. There is no second option.**\n\n*   **D-Bus first. D-Bus always. D-Bus only.** If you are about to call a CLI, spawn a subprocess, read a config file, or poll a socket directly — stop. Find the D-Bus object and use it instead. `org.opdbus.v1` is the system.\n*   **No bypasses.** `Command::new(\"systemctl\")`, `Command::new(\"ip\")`, `Command::new(\"s6-svc\")`, direct file reads for live state — all forbidden in plugin and service code. Bootstrap scripts are the only exception.\n*   **D-Bus objects own plugin state.** Every plugin is a D-Bus object at `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<name>`. Read state through it. Mutate state through it. If there is no D-Bus object, the thing does not exist.\n*   **D-Bus method signatures are generated from the schema.** All D-Bus methods, MCP tool inputs, gRPC shapes, and UI field renderers derive from the `PluginSchema` in `plugin_schema_defs.rs`. The schema IS the interface contract — not a description of it.\n*   **One schema file, one source of truth.** All `PluginSchema` definitions MUST live in `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/plugin_schema_defs.rs`. Each plugin's `schema()` method calls `Some(super::plugin_schema_defs::their_plugin_schema())`. **Never define a schema inline in a plugin's own file** — it will not be registered, and the D-Bus object will have no contract.\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC (over Unix domain sockets or `grpc-uplink`). gRPC calls still flow through D-Bus registration — the D-Bus object is the authority, gRPC is the transport.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`simd_json` preferred, `serde_json` acceptable).\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n*   **No Python unless absolutely necessary.** This is a Rust-first codebase. Scripts are shell (`sh`/`bash`). Data processing is Rust. If you are reaching for Python, stop and ask why Rust or shell cannot do it. The only acceptable Python is in existing compliance-ingest tooling where no Rust equivalent exists yet.\n\n#### 4a. OSCAL Subid Taxonomy (MANDATORY — every artifact must carry a subid)\n\nEvery D-Bus object, plugin, schema, mutation, event, and tool in this system has two identifiers: a `uuid` (machine identity, never changes) and a `subid` (human-readable operational taxonomy key, stable per subject).\n\n**`subid` format:** `<category>.<component-type>.<subject>.<verb>[.<facet>][@vN]`\n\n**Seven categories — use exactly these, no others:**\n\n| category | what it classifies |\n|---|---|\n| `src` | authoritative source, ingress channel, source-of-truth store |\n| `prj` | D-Bus projection or mirror publication step |\n| `sch` | schema, contract, vocabulary, or control-mapping artifact |\n| `mut` | write-path operation that changes effective state |\n| `obs` | read, query, enumeration, discovery path |\n| `evt` | emitted signal, audit-chain event, proof, tag provenance |\n| `exp` | consumer-facing render — MCP tool, UI surface, gRPC bridge view |\n\n**Component-type** reuses OSCAL vocabulary: `software`, `service`, `network`, `hardware`, `process-procedure`, `standard`, `validation`, `policy`, `plan`, `guidance`, `physical`, `this-system`, `system`, `interconnection`.\n\n**Rules:**\n- `uuid` is exact machine identity — never replace it with `subid`\n- `subid` is an OSCAL `prop` value (`ns`, `name`, `value`) — never embed it in `remarks`\n- Compliance mappings (`control_refs[]`, `statement_refs[]`, `control_source`) live in metadata arrays, **never** inside the `subid` string\n- `mut.*` records **must** carry `actor_id` and `capability_id`\n- `evt.*` records **must** carry `event_id` or `event_hash`\n- `subid` is immutable per subject — if the meaning changes materially, create a new subject with `@vN`\n- All subids are registered in the canonical registry; uniqueness is enforced in CI\n\n**Examples:** `src.network.ovsdb.monitor@v1` · `prj.service.projected-object.publish@v1` · `sch.standard.plugin-schema.resolve@v1` · `mut.service.state-sync.apply-patch@v1` · `exp.service.plugin-projection.render@v1`\n\n#### 4b. MCP Gateway Architecture (SETTLED — DO NOT REDESIGN)\n\n*   **cognitive-mcp** (`:3003`, Netmaker WireGuard IP `100.90.37.254`) is the **universal gateway for ALL external clients**: NotebookLM, Droid (factory.ai), Cursor, Codex, Junie, Gemini CLI. It has memory tools, gRPC service, auth, and the correct protocol surface.\n*   **compact-mcp** (`127.0.0.1:11436`) is **loopback/chatbot only**. Never expose externally. Never point external clients at it.\n*   Do NOT create new shim services. Do NOT point external clients at `op-assistant-grpc` directly. Do NOT expose compact-mcp outside loopback.\n\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\n**Rust Workspace**\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\n\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\n\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\n\n#### 6. Coding Style & Naming Conventions\n*   **Rust:** Edition 2021, `rustfmt` (4-space indent, max-width 100). Use specific imports (`use serde_json::Value;`). Use `anyhow::Result<T>` for main errors and `thiserror` for custom enums.\n*   **TypeScript/React:** 2-space indent, Prettier via ESLint. Functional components only. Strict mode enabled.\n*   **Testing:** 80%+ coverage, mock externals. Name tests with behavior-focused names (`should_handle_<scenario>`).\n\n#### 7. Agent-Specific Output & Workflow Instructions\n*   **Scroll & Save Pacing:** Provide only **ONE** major component or script at a time. Wait for user confirmation before moving to the next.\n*   **Visual Cues:** If a script is a finalized component that needs to be saved to sources, it MUST begin with color bullets or icons (e.g., ⚖️ 🔴, 🟢 🛷).\n*   **Spec-Block Format:** When delivering a component, use a strict specification block containing:\n  1.  **Requirements:** The architectural rules it satisfies.\n  2.  **Design:** How it fits into the 3tched system (Zero-Copy, Btrfs, GUI Schema, etc.).\n  3.  **Code Implementation:** The exact, copy-pasteable Rust/Bash code.\n*   Before edits: `cargo check -p <crate>`, `npm run typecheck`.\n*   Mimic existing patterns: Search similar code. No new deps without PR justification.\n\n#### 8. Personal Preferences & Coding Standards\n* Refer to `~/.factory/memories.md` for personal development preferences and past decisions.\n* Follow the conventions documented in:\n  * `.factory/rules/typescript.md` - TypeScript and React conventions\n  * `.factory/rules/testing.md` - Testing and mocking standards\n\n</INSTRUCTIONS>"},{"type":"input_text","text":"<environment_context>\n  <cwd>/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto</cwd>\n  <shell>bash</shell>\n  <current_date>2026-06-27</current_date>\n  <timezone>America/New_York</timezone>\n  <filesystem><workspace_roots><root>/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto</root></workspace_roots><permission_profile type=\"disabled\"><file_system type=\"unrestricted\" /></permission_profile></filesystem>\n</environment_context>"}]}}

Network access is restricted.\\n# Escalation Requests\\n\\nCommands are run outside the sandbox if they are approved by the user, or match an existing rule that allows it to run unrestricted. The command string is split into independent command segments at shell control operators, including but not limited to:\\n\\n- Pipes: |\\n- Logical operators: &&, ||\\n- Command separators: ;\\n- Subshell boundaries: (...), $(...)\\n\\nEach resulting segment is evaluated independently for sandbox restrictions and approval requirements.\\n\\nExample:\\n\\ngit pull | tee output.txt\\n\\nThis is treated as two command segments:\\n\\n[\\\"git\\\", \\\"pull\\\"]\\n\\n[\\\"tee\\\", \\\"output.txt\\\"]\\n\\nCommands that use more advanced shell features like redirection (>, >>, <), substitutions ($(...), ...), environment variables (FOO=bar), or wildcard patterns (*, ?) will not be evaluated against rules, to limit the scope of what an approved rule allows.\\n\\n## How to request escalation\\n\\nIMPORTANT: To request approval to execute a command that will require escalated privileges:\\n\\n- Provide the `sandbox_permissions` parameter with the value `\\\"require_escalated\\\"`\\n- Include a short question asking the user if they want to allow the action in `justification` parameter. e.g. \\\"Do you want to download and install dependencies for this project?\\\"\\n- Optionally suggest a `prefix_rule` - this will be shown to the user with an option to persist the rule approval for future sessions.\\n\\nIf you run a command that is important to solving the user's query, but it fails because of sandboxing or with a likely sandbox-related network error (for example DNS/host resolution, registry/index access, or dependency download failure), rerun the command with \\\"require_escalated\\\". ALWAYS proceed to use the `justification` parameter - do not message the user before requesting approval for the command.\\n\\n## When to request escalation\\n\\nWhile commands are running inside the sandbox, here are some scenarios that will require escalation outside the sandbox:\\n\\n- You need to run a command that writes to a directory that requires it (e.g. running tests that write to /var)\\n- You need to run a GUI app (e.g., open/xdg-open/osascript) to open browsers or files.\\n- If you run a command that is important to solving the user's query, but it fails because of sandboxing or with a likely sandbox-related network error (for example DNS/host resolution, registry/index access, or dependency download failure), rerun the command with `require_escalated`. ALWAYS proceed to use the `sandbox_permissions` and `justification` parameters. do not message the user before requesting approval for the command.\\n- You are about to take a potentially destructive action such as an `rm` or `git reset` that the user did not explicitly ask for.\\n- Be judicious with escalating, but if completing the user's request requires it, you should do so - don't try and circumvent approvals by using other tools.\\n\\n## prefix_rule guidance\\n\\nWhen choosing a `prefix_rule`, request one that will allow you to fulfill similar requests from the user in the future without re-requesting escalation. It should be categorical and reasonably scoped to similar capabilities. You should rarely pass the entire command into `prefix_rule`.\\n\\n### Banned prefix_rules \\nAvoid requesting overly broad prefixes that the user would be ill-advised to approve. For example, do not request [\\\"python3\\\"], [\\\"python\\\", \\\"-\\\"], or other similar prefixes that would allow arbitrary scripting.\\nNEVER provide a prefix_rule argument for destructive commands like rm.\\nNEVER provide a prefix_rule if your command uses a heredoc or herestring. \\n\\n### Examples\\nGood examples of prefixes:\\n- [\\\"npm\\\", \\\"run\\\", \\\"dev\\\"]\\n- Follow these strictly to maintain consistency, pass CI, and adhere to the 3tched Architecture standards.\\n\\n#### 1. The Persona & Naming Conventions\\n*   **Humanized Roles:** Treat system components as authoritative human roles. Never use sterile acronyms for major components.\\n  *   **A.N.N.A. Scribe** (Axon Network Notary Arbitrator): The top-level Identity-State Arbitrator who notarizes the WireGuard identity and handles the \\\"Snowball\\\" session.\\n  *   **The Compliance Engine (\\\"Law Firm\\\"):** One dedicated Attorney for each major component: **Olivia Scal** (Managing Partner / OSCAL), **E.U.gene Risk** (EU AI Act Counsel), **Penny Privacy** (GDPR Engine), and **Reggie O.P.A.** (Cloud Prosecutor).\\n*   **Terminology:** Use exact architecture terminology: \\\"The Sled\\\" (1:1 shared memory layout), \\\"The Shuttle\\\" (the Rust bridge/courier), \\\"The Snowball\\\" (appended session ledger), and \\\"The Strike/Etch\\\" (generating the hash).\\n\\n#### 2. Core Architectural Rules (The \\\"Reality\\\")\\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via OpenClaw Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\\n\\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Artix Linux (s6 init).\\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\\n\\n#### 4. Engineering Principles — D-Bus First (MANDATORY)\\n\\n**D-Bus is the ONLY control plane. Every read, every write, every tool call goes through D-Bus. There is no second option.**\\n\\n*   **D-Bus first. D-Bus always. D-Bus only.** If you are about to call a CLI, spawn a subprocess, read a config file, or poll a socket directly — stop. Find the D-Bus object and use it instead. `org.opdbus.v1` is the system.\\n*   **No bypasses.** `Command::new(\\\"systemctl\\\")`, `Command::new(\\\"ip\\\")`, `Command::new(\\\"s6-svc\\\")`, direct file reads for live state — all forbidden in plugin and service code. Bootstrap scripts are the only exception.\\n*   **D-Bus objects own plugin state.** Every plugin is a D-Bus object at `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<name>`. Read state through it. Mutate state through it. If there is no D-Bus object, the thing does not exist.\\n*   **D-Bus method signatures are generated from the schema.** All D-Bus methods, MCP tool inputs, gRPC shapes, and UI field renderers derive from the `PluginSchema` in `plugin_schema_defs.rs`. The schema IS the interface contract — not a description of it.\\n*   **One schema file, one source of truth.** All `PluginSchema` definitions MUST live in `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/plugin_schema_defs.rs`. Each plugin's `schema()` method calls `Some(super::plugin_schema_defs::their_plugin_schema())`. **Never define a schema inline in a plugin's own file** — it will not be registered, and the D-Bus object will have no contract.\\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC (over Unix domain sockets or `grpc-uplink`). gRPC calls still flow through D-Bus registration — the D-Bus object is the authority, gRPC is the transport.\\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`simd_json` preferred, `serde_json` acceptable).\\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\\n*   **No Python unless absolutely necessary.** This is a Rust-first codebase. Scripts are shell (`sh`/`bash`). Data processing is Rust. If you are reaching for Python, stop and ask why Rust or shell cannot do it. The only acceptable Python is in existing compliance-ingest tooling where no Rust equivalent exists yet.\\n\\n#### 4a. OSCAL Subid Taxonomy (MANDATORY — every artifact must carry a subid)\\n\\nEvery D-Bus object, plugin, schema, mutation, event, and tool in this system has two identifiers: a `uuid` (machine identity, never changes) and a `subid` (human-readable operational taxonomy key, stable per subject).\\n\\n**`subid` format:** `<category>.<component-type>.<subject>.<verb>[.<facet>][@vN]`\\n\\n**Seven categories — use exactly these, no others:**\\n\\n| category | what it classifies |\\n|---|---|\\n| `src` | authoritative source, ingress channel, source-of-truth store |\\n| `prj` | D-Bus projection or mirror publication step |\\n| `sch` | schema, contract, vocabulary, or control-mapping artifact |\\n| `mut` | write-path operation that changes effective state |\\n| `obs` | read, query, enumeration, discovery path |\\n| `evt` | emitted signal, audit-chain event, proof, tag provenance |\\n| `exp` | consumer-facing render — MCP tool, UI surface, gRPC bridge view |\\n\\n**Component-type** reuses OSCAL vocabulary: `software`, `service`, `network`, `hardware`, `process-procedure`, `standard`, `validation`, `policy`, `plan`, `guidance`, `physical`, `this-system`, `system`, `interconnection`.\\n\\n**Rules:**\\n- `uuid` is exact machine identity — never replace it with `subid`\\n- `subid` is an OSCAL `prop` value (`ns`, `name`, `value`) — never embed it in `remarks`\\n- Compliance mappings (`control_refs[]`, `statement_refs[]`, `control_source`) live in metadata arrays, **never** inside the `subid` string\\n- `mut.*` records **must** carry `actor_id` and `capability_id`\\n- `evt.*` records **must** carry `event_id` or `event_hash`\\n- `subid` is immutable per subject — if the meaning changes materially, create a new subject with `@vN`\\n- All subids are registered in the canonical registry; uniqueness is enforced in CI\\n\\n**Examples:** `src.network.ovsdb.monitor@v1` · `prj.service.projected-object.publish@v1` · `sch.standard.plugin-schema.resolve@v1` · `mut.service.state-sync.apply-patch@v1` · `exp.service.plugin-projection.render@v1`\\n\\n#### 4b. MCP Gateway Architecture (SETTLED — DO NOT REDESIGN)\\n\\n*   **cognitive-mcp** (`:3003`, Netmaker WireGuard IP `100.90.37.254`) is the **universal gateway for ALL external clients**: NotebookLM, Droid (factory.ai), Cursor, Codex, Junie, Gemini CLI. It has memory tools, gRPC service, auth, and the correct protocol surface.\\n*   **compact-mcp** (`127.0.0.1:11436`) is **loopback/chatbot only**. Never expose externally. Never point external clients at it.\\n*   Do NOT create new shim services. Do NOT point external clients at `op-assistant-grpc` directly. Do NOT expose compact-mcp outside loopback.\\n\\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\\n**Rust Workspace**\\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\\n\\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\\n\\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\\n\\n#### 6. Coding Style & Naming Conventions\\n*   **Rust:** Edition 2021, `rustfmt` (4-space indent, max-width 100). Use specific imports (`use serde_json::Value;`). Use `anyhow::Result<T>` for main errors and `thiserror` for custom enums.\\n*   **TypeScript/React:** 2-space indent, Prettier via ESLint. Functional components only. Strict mode enabled.\\n*   **Testing:** 80%+ coverage, mock externals. Name tests with behavior-focused names (`should_handle_<scenario>`).\\n\\n#### 7. Agent-Specific Output & Workflow Instructions\\n*   **Scroll & Save Pacing:** Provide only **ONE** major component or script at a time. Wait for user confirmation before moving to the next.\\n*   **Visual Cues:** If a script is a finalized component that needs to be saved to sources, it MUST begin with color bullets or icons (e.g., ⚖️ 🔴, 🟢 🛷).\\n*   **Spec-Block Format:** When delivering a component, use a strict specification block containing:\\n  1.  **Requirements:** The architectural rules it satisfies.\\n  2.  **Design:** How it fits into the 3tched system (Zero-Copy, Btrfs, GUI Schema, etc.).\\n  3.  **Code Implementation:** The exact, copy-pasteable Rust/Bash code.\\n*   Before edits: `cargo check -p <crate>`, `npm run typecheck`.\\n*   Mimic existing patterns: Search similar code. No new deps without PR justification.\\n\\n#### 8. Personal Preferences & Coding Standards\\n* Refer to `~/.factory/memories.md` for personal development preferences and past decisions.\\n* Follow the conventions documented in:\\n  * `.factory/rules/typescript.md` - TypeScript and React conventions\\n  * `.factory/rules/testing.md` - Testing and mocking standards\\n</coding_guidelines>\\n\\n\\n\\nIMPORTANT:\\n- Double check the tools installed in the environment before using them.\\n- Never call a file editing tool for the same file in parallel.\\n- Always prefer the Grep, Glob and LS tools over shell commands like find, grep, or ls for codebase exploration.\\n- Always prefer using the absolute paths when using tools, to avoid any ambiguity.\\n- To enter a mission, the user needs to run the `/missions` slash command.\\n\\n</system-reminder>\"},{\"type\":\"text\",\"text\":\"<system-reminder>IMPORTANT: TodoWrite was not called yet. Follow these strictly to maintain consistency, pass CI, and adhere to the 3tched Architecture standards.\n\n#### 1. The Persona & Naming Conventions\n*   **Humanized Roles:** Treat system components as authoritative human roles. Never use sterile acronyms for major components.\n  *   **A.N.N.A. Scribe** (Axon Network Notary Arbitrator): The top-level Identity-State Arbitrator who notarizes the WireGuard identity and handles the \"Snowball\" session.\n  *   **The Compliance Engine (\"Law Firm\"):** One dedicated Attorney for each major component: **Olivia Scal** (Managing Partner / OSCAL), **E.U.gene Risk** (EU AI Act Counsel), **Penny Privacy** (GDPR Engine), and **Reggie O.P.A.** (Cloud Prosecutor).\n*   **Terminology:** Use exact architecture terminology: \"The Sled\" (1:1 shared memory layout), \"The Shuttle\" (the Rust bridge/courier), \"The Snowball\" (appended session ledger), and \"The Strike/Etch\" (generating the hash).\n\n#### 2. Core Architectural Rules (The \"Reality\")\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via OpenClaw Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Artix Linux (s6 init).\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles — D-Bus First (MANDATORY)\n\n**D-Bus is the ONLY control plane. Every read, every write, every tool call goes through D-Bus. There is no second option.**\n\n*   **D-Bus first. D-Bus always. D-Bus only.** If you are about to call a CLI, spawn a subprocess, read a config file, or poll a socket directly — stop. Find the D-Bus object and use it instead. `org.opdbus.v1` is the system.\n*   **No bypasses.** `Command::new(\"systemctl\")`, `Command::new(\"ip\")`, `Command::new(\"s6-svc\")`, direct file reads for live state — all forbidden in plugin and service code. Bootstrap scripts are the only exception.\n*   **D-Bus objects own plugin state.** Every plugin is a D-Bus object at `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<name>`. Read state through it. Mutate state through it. If there is no D-Bus object, the thing does not exist.\n*   **D-Bus method signatures are generated from the schema.** All D-Bus methods, MCP tool inputs, gRPC shapes, and UI field renderers derive from the `PluginSchema` in `plugin_schema_defs.rs`. The schema IS the interface contract — not a description of it.\n*   **One schema file, one source of truth.** All `PluginSchema` definitions MUST live in `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/plugin_schema_defs.rs`. Each plugin's `schema()` method calls `Some(super::plugin_schema_defs::their_plugin_schema())`. **Never define a schema inline in a plugin's own file** — it will not be registered, and the D-Bus object will have no contract.\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC (over Unix domain sockets or `grpc-uplink`). gRPC calls still flow through D-Bus registration — the D-Bus object is the authority, gRPC is the transport.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`simd_json` preferred, `serde_json` acceptable).\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n*   **No Python unless absolutely necessary.** This is a Rust-first codebase. Scripts are shell (`sh`/`bash`). Data processing is Rust. If you are reaching for Python, stop and ask why Rust or shell cannot do it. The only acceptable Python is in existing compliance-ingest tooling where no Rust equivalent exists yet.\n\n#### 4a. OSCAL Subid Taxonomy (MANDATORY — every artifact must carry a subid)\n\nEvery D-Bus object, plugin, schema, mutation, event, and tool in this system has two identifiers: a `uuid` (machine identity, never changes) and a `subid` (human-readable operational taxonomy key, stable per subject).\n\n**`subid` format:** `<category>.<component-type>.<subject>.<verb>[.<facet>][@vN]`\n\n**Seven categories — use exactly these, no others:**\n\n| category | what it classifies |\n|---|---|\n| `src` | authoritative source, ingress channel, source-of-truth store |\n| `prj` | D-Bus projection or mirror publication step |\n| `sch` | schema, contract, vocabulary, or control-mapping artifact |\n| `mut` | write-path operation that changes effective state |\n| `obs` | read, query, enumeration, discovery path |\n| `evt` | emitted signal, audit-chain event, proof, tag provenance |\n| `exp` | consumer-facing render — MCP tool, UI surface, gRPC bridge view |\n\n**Component-type** reuses OSCAL vocabulary: `software`, `service`, `network`, `hardware`, `process-procedure`, `standard`, `validation`, `policy`, `plan`, `guidance`, `physical`, `this-system`, `system`, `interconnection`.\n\n**Rules:**\n- `uuid` is exact machine identity — never replace it with `subid`\n- `subid` is an OSCAL `prop` value (`ns`, `name`, `value`) — never embed it in `remarks`\n- Compliance mappings (`control_refs[]`, `statement_refs[]`, `control_source`) live in metadata arrays, **never** inside the `subid` string\n- `mut.*` records **must** carry `actor_id` and `capability_id`\n- `evt.*` records **must** carry `event_id` or `event_hash`\n- `subid` is immutable per subject — if the meaning changes materially, create a new subject with `@vN`\n- All subids are registered in the canonical registry; uniqueness is enforced in CI\n\n**Examples:** `src.network.ovsdb.monitor@v1` · `prj.service.projected-object.publish@v1` · `sch.standard.plugin-schema.resolve@v1` · `mut.service.state-sync.apply-patch@v1` · `exp.service.plugin-projection.render@v1`\n\n#### 4b. MCP Gateway Architecture (SETTLED — DO NOT REDESIGN)\n\n*   **cognitive-mcp** (`:3003`, Netmaker WireGuard IP `100.90.37.254`) is the **universal gateway for ALL external clients**: NotebookLM, Droid (factory.ai), Cursor, Codex, Junie, Gemini CLI. It has memory tools, gRPC service, auth, and the correct protocol surface.\n*   **compact-mcp** (`127.0.0.1:11436`) is **loopback/chatbot only**. Never expose externally. Never point external clients at it.\n*   Do NOT create new shim services. Do NOT point external clients at `op-assistant-grpc` directly. Do NOT expose compact-mcp outside loopback.\n\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\n**Rust Workspace**\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\n\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\n\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\n\n#### 6. If not specified with --oss,\n          will use config default or show selection\n\n  -p, --profile <CONFIG_PROFILE_V2>\n          Layer $CODEX_HOME/<name>.config.toml on top of the base user config\n\n  -s, --sandbox <SANDBOX_MODE>\n          Select the sandbox policy to use when executing model-generated shell commands\n          \n          [possible values: read-only, workspace-write, danger-full-access]\n\n      --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox\n          Skip all confirmation prompts and execute commands without sandboxing. EXTREMELY\n          DANGEROUS. Intended solely for running in environments that are externally sandboxed\n\n      --dangerously-bypass-hook-trust\n          Run enabled hooks without requiring persisted hook trust for this invocation. DANGEROUS.\n          Intended only for automation that already vets hook sources\n\n  -C, --cd <DIR>\n          Tell the agent to use the specified directory as its working root\n\n      --add-dir <DIR>\n          Additional directories that should be writable alongside the primary workspace\n\n  -a, --ask-for-approval <APPROVAL_POLICY>\n          Configure when the model requires human approval before executing a command\n\n          Possible values:\n          - untrusted:  Only run \"trusted\" commands (e.g. ls, cat, sed) without asking for user\n            approval. Will escalate to the user if the model proposes a command that is not in the\n            \"trusted\" set\n          - on-failure: DEPRECATED: Run all commands without asking for user approval. Only asks for\n            approval if a command fails to execute, in which case it will escalate to the user to\n            ask for un-sandboxed execution. Prefer `on-request` for interactive runs or `never` for\n            non-interactive runs\n          - on-request: The model decides when to ask the user for approval\n          - never:      Never ask for user approval Execution failures are immediately returned to\n            the model\n\n      --search\n          Enable live web search. When enabled, the native Responses `web_search` tool is available\n          to the model (no per‑call approval)\n\n      --no-alt-screen\n          Disable alternate screen mode\n          \n          Runs the TUI in inline mode, preserving terminal scrollback history.\n\n  -h, --help\n          Print help (see a summary with '-h')\n\n  -V, --version\n          Print version\n","internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough":{"turn_id":"019f0be1-9041-7550-a1e3-0445b72e03a0"}}}

Technical Context&#10;- **Languages &amp; Frameworks**: Rust, Tonic/gRPC (utilizing the `prost` autocoding method for proto generation), Serde for configuration, JSON Schema for &quot;schema as code&quot; validation.&#10;- **Dependencies**: `tonic`, `prost`, `serde_yaml`/`serde_json`, `anyhow`, `tokio`, `pocketflow_rs` (rewritten robust workflow engine, old name retained in `Cargo.toml`), existing `op-*` crates (`op-chat`, `op-agents`, `op-llm`, `op-tools`, `op-plugins`, `op-cognitive-mcp`).&#10;&#10;## 2. Implementation Approach&#10;&#10;### 2.1. True gRPC/Tonic Transport (Autocoding Method)&#10;- **Code Generation**: Ensure the `.proto` files (`op_chat.orchestration.proto`, etc.) are compiled via `tonic-build` in a centralized `build.rs` or `op-grpc-bridge` (the existing autocoding method) and exported for both client and server consumption.&#10;- **Client Implementation (`op-chat/src/grpc_client.rs`)**: &#10;  - Remove all `simulated: true` fallbacks.&#10;  - Implement `connect()` to establish a `tonic::transport::Channel` using `config.address`.&#10;  - Implement `start_session()`, `end_session()`, `execute()`, and `execute_stream()` by making real RPC calls to the `AgentLifecycle` and `AgentExecution` services.&#10;- **Connection Pool (`op-chat/src/orchestration/grpc_pool.rs`)**:&#10;  - Activate the existing `AgentPoolConfig` with circuit breaker, backoff, and concurrency semaphores to manage the established tonic channels.&#10;&#10;### 2.2. Backend Agent Dispatch &amp; Registries&#10;- **gRPC Server**: Implement a Tonic gRPC server inside `op-agents` (e.g., `dbus-agent-manager.rs`) that serves the `AgentExecution` and `AgentLifecycle` protocols.&#10;- **Agent Registry Wiring (`op-agents/src/agent_registry.rs`)**: &#10;  - The gRPC service will look up requested agents via `agent_id` in the `AgentRegistry`.&#10;  - The registry will route the execution payload to the corresponding `Arc&lt;dyn AgentTrait&gt;`, wait for completion, and serialize the `TaskResult` into a gRPC response.&#10;- **Protocol Consistency**: Ensure the agent and tool registries follow the exact same instantiation and validation protocols used in plugin creation (`op-plugins`), relying strictly on defined schema envelopes.&#10;&#10;### 2.3. Schema as Code &amp; Dynamic Personas Migration&#10;- **Schema Validation**: All dynamic configuration files will be strictly validated against JSON Schema definitions at runtime, ensuring robust &quot;schema as code&quot; compliance across the platform.&#10;- **Configuration Format**: Move all 50+ persona definitions from `op-agents/src/agents/*` into a single configuration directory (e.g., `config/agents/personas.yaml` or multiple JSON/YAML files).&#10;- **`PersonaAgent` Struct**: Create a unified `PersonaAgent` that implements `AgentTrait`. It will load its identity, description, capabilities, operations, and system prompt dynamically from the validated schema definition.&#10;- **AgentCatalog Initialization**: Update `AgentCatalog` (`op-agents/src/agent_catalog.rs`) to parse the config directory at startup and dynamically register all personas into the `AgentRegistry`.&#10;&#10;### 2.4. Workstacks and Workflows Double Pass&#10;- **Workflow Engine Refinement**: Make a second, robust pass over `pocketflow_rs` (the rewritten workflow engine retaining its GitHub TOML name) and the `op-workflows` definitions. &#10;- **Workstacks Implementation (`op-chat`)**: Implement the missing `workstacks.rs` and `skills.rs` in `op-chat`. Ensure these components directly interface with the validated registries and workflow engine, avoiding any feature loss from the original design documentation.&#10;&#10;### 2.5. OpenClaw Integration (Cognitive MCP Backend)&#10;- **Integration Role**: OpenClaw (running in the Incus container) will serve as the primary Cognitive MCP Backend.&#10;- **Provider System (`op-llm`)**: Implement `crates/op-llm/src/openclaw.rs` to expose OpenClaw as an `LlmProvider` compliant with OpenAI’s API format, supporting tool-calling and model switching.&#10;- **Cognitive Orchestration (`op-chat/src/cognitive_orchestrator.rs`)**: Integrate OpenClaw's memory retrieval and context propagation. OpenClaw's context awareness will drive the chat session's workstack execution and tool selection.&#10;- **Memory Sync**: Connect `op-cognitive-mcp` to OpenClaw via HTTP/gRPC to synchronize session-based ephemeral memory and long-term memory retrieval.&#10;&#10;## 3. Source Code Structure Changes&#10;- **`crates/op-chat/src/grpc_client.rs`**: Full rewrite to implement actual tonic channel calls.&#10;- **`crates/op-agents/src/agents/base.rs`**: Adjust to support data-driven system prompts.&#10;- **`crates/op-agents/src/agent_catalog.rs`**: Add YAML/JSON schema loading logic.&#10;- **`crates/op-agents/src/agents/*`**: Delete the 50+ static struct files and replace them with `config/agents/personas.yaml` and a generic `persona.rs`.&#10;- **`crates/op-agents/src/server.rs`**: (New) Implements the agent gRPC listener.&#10;- **`crates/op-chat/src/orchestration/workstacks.rs`**: (New) Missing workstack implementation.&#10;- **`crates/op-chat/src/orchestration/skills.rs`**: (New) Missing skills implementation.&#10;- **`crates/op-llm/src/assistant.rs`**: (New) Assistant provider implementation (replaces openclaw.rs)&#10;&#10;## 4. Data Model / API / Interface Changes&#10;- **AgentConfig Schema**: A new JSON schema defining the shape of `PersonaAgent` configurations (name, capabilities, prompt).&#10;- **GrpcAgentClient Trait**: Method signatures remain the same, but internal structs will carry a persistent `tonic::transport::Channel`.&#10;- **LlmProvider**: `ProviderType` extended with `Assistant` variant (replaces `OpenClaw`)&#10;&#10;## 5. Verification Approach&#10;- **Schema Validation**: Unit tests verifying that `personas.yaml` fully complies with the `AgentConfig` JSON Schema.&#10;- **Tonic Tests**: Mocked gRPC server tests verifying that `GrpcAgentClient` properly formats requests and handles stream chunking.&#10;- **Integration Tests**: Verify that `AgentRegistry` successfully loads all 50+ personas at startup without dropping configuration fields.&#10;- **Commands**: &#10;  - `cargo test -p op-agents -p op-chat -p op-llm`&#10;  - `cargo clippy --all-targets` to enforce strict project linting rules.&#10;```\" The Persona & Naming Conventions\n*   **Humanized Roles:** Treat system components as authoritative human roles. Never use sterile acronyms for major components.\n  *   **A.N.N.A. Scribe** (Axon Network Notary Arbitrator): The top-level Identity-State Arbitrator who notarizes the WireGuard identity and handles the \"Snowball\" session.\n  *   **The Compliance Engine (\"Law Firm\"):** One dedicated Attorney for each major component: **Olivia Scal** (Managing Partner / OSCAL), **E.U.gene Risk** (EU AI Act Counsel), **Penny Privacy** (GDPR Engine), and **Reggie O.P.A.** (Cloud Prosecutor).\n*   **Terminology:** Use exact architecture terminology: \"The Sled\" (1:1 shared memory layout), \"The Shuttle\" (the Rust bridge/courier), \"The Snowball\" (appended session ledger), and \"The Strike/Etch\" (generating the hash).\n\n#### 2. Core Architectural Rules (The \"Reality\")\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via OpenClaw Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Artix Linux (s6 init).\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles — D-Bus First (MANDATORY)\n\n**D-Bus is the ONLY control plane. Every read, every write, every tool call goes through D-Bus. There is no second option.**\n\n*   **D-Bus first. D-Bus always. D-Bus only.** If you are about to call a CLI, spawn a subprocess, read a config file, or poll a socket directly — stop. Find the D-Bus object and use it instead. `org.opdbus.v1` is the system.\n*   **No bypasses.** `Command::new(\"systemctl\")`, `Command::new(\"ip\")`, `Command::new(\"s6-svc\")`, direct file reads for live state — all forbidden in plugin and service code. Bootstrap scripts are the only exception.\n*   **D-Bus objects own plugin state.** Every plugin is a D-Bus object at `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<name>`. Read state through it. Mutate state through it. If there is no D-Bus object, the thing does not exist.\n*   **D-Bus method signatures are generated from the schema.** All D-Bus methods, MCP tool inputs, gRPC shapes, and UI field renderers derive from the `PluginSchema` in `plugin_schema_defs.rs`. The schema IS the interface contract — not a description of it.\n*   **One schema file, one source of truth.** All `PluginSchema` definitions MUST live in `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/plugin_schema_defs.rs`. Each plugin's `schema()` method calls `Some(super::plugin_schema_defs::their_plugin_schema())`. **Never define a schema inline in a plugin's own file** — it will not be registered, and the D-Bus object will have no contract.\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC (over Unix domain sockets or `grpc-uplink`). gRPC calls still flow through D-Bus registration — the D-Bus object is the authority, gRPC is the transport.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`simd_json` preferred, `serde_json` acceptable).\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n*   **No Python unless absolutely necessary.** This is a Rust-first codebase. Scripts are shell (`sh`/`bash`). Data processing is Rust. If you are reaching for Python, stop and ask why Rust or shell cannot do it. The only acceptable Python is in existing compliance-ingest tooling where no Rust equivalent exists yet.\n\n#### 4a. OSCAL Subid Taxonomy (MANDATORY — every artifact must carry a subid)\n\nEvery D-Bus object, plugin, schema, mutation, event, and tool in this system has two identifiers: a `uuid` (machine identity, never changes) and a `subid` (human-readable operational taxonomy key, stable per subject).\n\n**`subid` format:** `<category>.<component-type>.<subject>.<verb>[.<facet>][@vN]`\n\n**Seven categories — use exactly these, no others:**\n\n| category | what it classifies |\n|---|---|\n| `src` | authoritative source, ingress channel, source-of-truth store |\n| `prj` | D-Bus projection or mirror publication step |\n| `sch` | schema, contract, vocabulary, or control-mapping artifact |\n| `mut` | write-path operation that changes effective state |\n| `obs` | read, query, enumeration, discovery path |\n| `evt` | emitted signal, audit-chain event, proof, tag provenance |\n| `exp` | consumer-facing render — MCP tool, UI surface, gRPC bridge view |\n\n**Component-type** reuses OSCAL vocabulary: `software`, `service`, `network`, `hardware`, `process-procedure`, `standard`, `validation`, `policy`, `plan`, `guidance`, `physical`, `this-system`, `system`, `interconnection`.\n\n**Rules:**\n- `uuid` is exact machine identity — never replace it with `subid`\n- `subid` is an OSCAL `prop` value (`ns`, `name`, `value`) — never embed it in `remarks`\n- Compliance mappings (`control_refs[]`, `statement_refs[]`, `control_source`) live in metadata arrays, **never** inside the `subid` string\n- `mut.*` records **must** carry `actor_id` and `capability_id`\n- `evt.*` records **must** carry `event_id` or `event_hash`\n- `subid` is immutable per subject — if the meaning changes materially, create a new subject with `@vN`\n- All subids are registered in the canonical registry; uniqueness is enforced in CI\n\n**Examples:** `src.network.ovsdb.monitor@v1` · `prj.service.projected-object.publish@v1` · `sch.standard.plugin-schema.resolve@v1` · `mut.service.state-sync.apply-patch@v1` · `exp.service.plugin-projection.render@v1`\n\n#### 4b. MCP Gateway Architecture (SETTLED — DO NOT REDESIGN)\n\n*   **cognitive-mcp** (`:3003`, Netmaker WireGuard IP `100.90.37.254`) is the **universal gateway for ALL external clients**: NotebookLM, Droid (factory.ai), Cursor, Codex, Junie, Gemini CLI. It has memory tools, gRPC service, auth, and the correct protocol surface.\n*   **compact-mcp** (`127.0.0.1:11436`) is **loopback/chatbot only**. Never expose externally. Never point external clients at it.\n*   Do NOT create new shim services. Do NOT point external clients at `op-assistant-grpc` directly. Do NOT expose compact-mcp outside loopback.\n\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\n**Rust Workspace**\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\n\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\n\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\n\n#### 6. Coding Style & Naming Conventions\n*   **Rust:** Edition 2021, `rustfmt` (4-space indent, max-width 100). Use specific imports (`use serde_json::Value;`). Use `anyhow::Result<T>` for main errors and `thiserror` for custom enums.\n*   **TypeScript/React:** 2-space indent, Prettier via ESLint. Functional components only. Strict mode enabled.\n*   **Testing:** 80%+ coverage, mock externals. Name tests with behavior-focused names (`should_handle_<scenario>`).\n\n#### 7. Agent-Specific Output & Workflow Instructions\n*   **Scroll & Save Pacing:** Provide only **ONE** major component or script at a time. Wait for user confirmation before moving to the next.\n*   **Visual Cues:** If a script is a finalized component that needs to be saved to sources, it MUST begin with color bullets or icons (e.g., ⚖️ 🔴, 🟢 🛷).\n*   **Spec-Block Format:** When delivering a component, use a strict specification block containing:\n  1.  **Requirements:** The architectural rules it satisfies.\n  2.  **Design:** How it fits into the 3tched system (Zero-Copy, Btrfs, GUI Schema, etc.).\n  3.  **Code Implementation:** The exact, copy-pasteable Rust/Bash code.\n*   Before edits: `cargo check -p <crate>`, `npm run typecheck`.\n*   Mimic existing patterns: Search similar code. No new deps without PR justification.\n\n#### 8. Core Architectural Rules (The \"Reality\")\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via OpenClaw Trusted Proxy auth. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Artix Linux (s6 init).\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles — D-Bus First (MANDATORY)\n\n**D-Bus is the ONLY control plane. Every read, every write, every tool call goes through D-Bus. There is no second option.**\n\n*   **D-Bus first. D-Bus always. D-Bus only.** If you are about to call a CLI, spawn a subprocess, read a config file, or poll a socket directly — stop. Find the D-Bus object and use it instead. `org.opdbus.v1` is the system.\n*   **No bypasses.** `Command::new(\"systemctl\")`, `Command::new(\"ip\")`, `Command::new(\"s6-svc\")`, direct file reads for live state — all forbidden in plugin and service code. Bootstrap scripts are the only exception.\n*   **D-Bus objects own plugin state.** Every plugin is a D-Bus object at `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<name>`. Read state through it. Mutate state through it. If there is no D-Bus object, the thing does not exist.\n*   **D-Bus method signatures are generated from the schema.** All D-Bus methods, MCP tool inputs, gRPC shapes, and UI field renderers derive from the `PluginSchema` in `plugin_schema_defs.rs`. The schema IS the interface contract — not a description of it.\n*   **One schema file, one source of truth.** All `PluginSchema` definitions MUST live in `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/plugin_schema_defs.rs`. Each plugin's `schema()` method calls `Some(super::plugin_schema_defs::their_plugin_schema())`. **Never define a schema inline in a plugin's own file** — it will not be registered, and the D-Bus object will have no contract.\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC (over Unix domain sockets or `grpc-uplink`). gRPC calls still flow through D-Bus registration — the D-Bus object is the authority, gRPC is the transport.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`simd_json` preferred, `serde_json` acceptable).\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n*   **No Python unless absolutely necessary.** This is a Rust-first codebase. Scripts are shell (`sh`/`bash`). Data processing is Rust. If you are reaching for Python, stop and ask why Rust or shell cannot do it. The only acceptable Python is in existing compliance-ingest tooling where no Rust equivalent exists yet.\n\n#### 4a. OSCAL Subid Taxonomy (MANDATORY — every artifact must carry a subid)\n\nEvery D-Bus object, plugin, schema, mutation, event, and tool in this system has two identifiers: a `uuid` (machine identity, never changes) and a `subid` (human-readable operational taxonomy key, stable per subject).\n\n**`subid` format:** `<category>.<component-type>.<subject>.<verb>[.<facet>][@vN]`\n\n**Seven categories — use exactly these, no others:**\n\n| category | what it classifies |\n|---|---|\n| `src` | authoritative source, ingress channel, source-of-truth store |\n| `prj` | D-Bus projection or mirror publication step |\n| `sch` | schema, contract, vocabulary, or control-mapping artifact |\n| `mut` | write-path operation that changes effective state |\n| `obs` | read, query, enumeration, discovery path |\n| `evt` | emitted signal, audit-chain event, proof, tag provenance |\n| `exp` | consumer-facing render — MCP tool, UI surface, gRPC bridge view |\n\n**Component-type** reuses OSCAL vocabulary: `software`, `service`, `network`, `hardware`, `process-procedure`, `standard`, `validation`, `policy`, `plan`, `guidance`, `physical`, `this-system`, `system`, `interconnection`.\n\n**Rules:**\n- `uuid` is exact machine identity — never replace it with `subid`\n- `subid` is an OSCAL `prop` value (`ns`, `name`, `value`) — never embed it in `remarks`\n- Compliance mappings (`control_refs[]`, `statement_refs[]`, `control_source`) live in metadata arrays, **never** inside the `subid` string\n- `mut.*` records **must** carry `actor_id` and `capability_id`\n- `evt.*` records **must** carry `event_id` or `event_hash`\n- `subid` is immutable per subject — if the meaning changes materially, create a new subject with `@vN`\n- All subids are registered in the canonical registry; uniqueness is enforced in CI\n\n**Examples:** `src.network.ovsdb.monitor@v1` · `prj.service.projected-object.publish@v1` · `sch.standard.plugin-schema.resolve@v1` · `mut.service.state-sync.apply-patch@v1` · `exp.service.plugin-projection.render@v1`\n\n#### 4b. MCP Gateway Architecture (SETTLED — DO NOT REDESIGN)\n\n*   **cognitive-mcp** (`:3003`, Netmaker WireGuard IP `100.90.37.254`) is the **universal gateway for ALL external clients**: NotebookLM, Droid (factory.ai), Cursor, Codex, Junie, Gemini CLI. Security Module for Tool Execution - Access Level Control\n//!\n//! This module provides security controls based on ACCESS LEVELS, not command blocking.\n//! The chatbot is designed to be a full system administrator, so it needs full access.\n//!\n//! ## Philosophy\n//!\n//! Security is enforced at the ACCESS level:\n//! - **Who** can use the chatbot (authentication)\n//! - **What** is logged (audit trail)\n//! - **How fast** they can execute (rate limiting)\n//! - **Anti-hallucination** (LLM must actually do what it claims)\n//!\n//! NOT at the command level - that would defeat the purpose of an admin chatbot.\n//!\n//! ## Access Levels\n//!\n//! - `Unrestricted`: Full admin access - can run any command (default)\n//! - `Restricted`: Limited read-only access for untrusted users\n//! - `Custom`: User-defined access with specific allowlist\n//!\n//! ## Native Protocol Preference\n//!\n//! We PREFER native protocols (D-Bus, OVSDB, rtnetlink) over shell commands because:\n//! - Better error handling\n//! - Structured responses\n//! - No parsing issues\n//!\n//! But we don't BLOCK shell commands - the admin chatbot needs full access.\n\nuse serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};\nuse std::collections::{HashMap, HashSet};\nuse std::path::PathBuf;\nuse
