Follow these strictly to maintain consistency, pass CI, and adhere to the 3tched Architecture standards.\n\n#### 1. The Persona & Naming Conventions\n*   **Humanized Roles:** Treat system components as authoritative human roles. Never use sterile acronyms for major components.\n  *   **A.N.N.A. Scribe** (Axon Network Notary Arbitrator): The top-level Identity-State Arbitrator who notarizes the WireGuard identity and handles the \"Snowball\" session.\n  *   **The Compliance Engine (\"Law Firm\"):** One dedicated Attorney for each major component: **Olivia Scal** (Managing Partner / OSCAL), **E.U.gene Risk** (EU AI Act Counsel), **Penny Privacy** (GDPR Engine), and **Reggie O.P.A.** (Cloud Prosecutor).\n*   **Terminology:** Use exact architecture terminology: \"The Sled\" (1:1 shared memory layout), \"The Shuttle\" (the Rust bridge/courier), \"The Snowball\" (appended session ledger), and \"The Strike/Etch\" (generating the hash).\n\n#### 2. Core Architectural Rules (The \"Reality\")\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via OpenClaw Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Artix Linux (s6 init).\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles — D-Bus First (MANDATORY)\n\n**D-Bus is the ONLY control plane. Every read, every write, every tool call goes through D-Bus. There is no second option.**\n\n*   **D-Bus first. D-Bus always. D-Bus only.** If you are about to call a CLI, spawn a subprocess, read a config file, or poll a socket directly — stop. Find the D-Bus object and use it instead. `org.opdbus.v1` is the system.\n*   **No bypasses.** `Command::new(\"systemctl\")`, `Command::new(\"ip\")`, `Command::new(\"s6-svc\")`, direct file reads for live state — all forbidden in plugin and service code. Bootstrap scripts are the only exception.\n*   **D-Bus objects own plugin state.** Every plugin is a D-Bus object at `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<name>`. Read state through it. Mutate state through it. If there is no D-Bus object, the thing does not exist.\n*   **D-Bus method signatures are generated from the schema.** All D-Bus methods, MCP tool inputs, gRPC shapes, and UI field renderers derive from the `PluginSchema` in `plugin_schema_defs.rs`. The schema IS the interface contract — not a description of it.\n*   **One schema file, one source of truth.** All `PluginSchema` definitions MUST live in `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/plugin_schema_defs.rs`. Each plugin's `schema()` method calls `Some(super::plugin_schema_defs::their_plugin_schema())`. **Never define a schema inline in a plugin's own file** — it will not be registered, and the D-Bus object will have no contract.\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC (over Unix domain sockets or `grpc-uplink`). gRPC calls still flow through D-Bus registration — the D-Bus object is the authority, gRPC is the transport.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`simd_json` preferred, `serde_json` acceptable).\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n*   **No Python unless absolutely necessary.** This is a Rust-first codebase. Scripts are shell (`sh`/`bash`). Data processing is Rust. If you are reaching for Python, stop and ask why Rust or shell cannot do it. The only acceptable Python is in existing compliance-ingest tooling where no Rust equivalent exists yet.\n\n#### 4a. OSCAL Subid Taxonomy (MANDATORY — every artifact must carry a subid)\n\nEvery D-Bus object, plugin, schema, mutation, event, and tool in this system has two identifiers: a `uuid` (machine identity, never changes) and a `subid` (human-readable operational taxonomy key, stable per subject).\n\n**`subid` format:** `<category>.<component-type>.<subject>.<verb>[.<facet>][@vN]`\n\n**Seven categories — use exactly these, no others:**\n\n| category | what it classifies |\n|---|---|\n| `src` | authoritative source, ingress channel, source-of-truth store |\n| `prj` | D-Bus projection or mirror publication step |\n| `sch` | schema, contract, vocabulary, or control-mapping artifact |\n| `mut` | write-path operation that changes effective state |\n| `obs` | read, query, enumeration, discovery path |\n| `evt` | emitted signal, audit-chain event, proof, tag provenance |\n| `exp` | consumer-facing render — MCP tool, UI surface, gRPC bridge view |\n\n**Component-type** reuses OSCAL vocabulary: `software`, `service`, `network`, `hardware`, `process-procedure`, `standard`, `validation`, `policy`, `plan`, `guidance`, `physical`, `this-system`, `system`, `interconnection`.\n\n**Rules:**\n- `uuid` is exact machine identity — never replace it with `subid`\n- `subid` is an OSCAL `prop` value (`ns`, `name`, `value`) — never embed it in `remarks`\n- Compliance mappings (`control_refs[]`, `statement_refs[]`, `control_source`) live in metadata arrays, **never** inside the `subid` string\n- `mut.*` records **must** carry `actor_id` and `capability_id`\n- `evt.*` records **must** carry `event_id` or `event_hash`\n- `subid` is immutable per subject — if the meaning changes materially, create a new subject with `@vN`\n- All subids are registered in the canonical registry; uniqueness is enforced in CI\n\n**Examples:** `src.network.ovsdb.monitor@v1` · `prj.service.projected-object.publish@v1` · `sch.standard.plugin-schema.resolve@v1` · `mut.service.state-sync.apply-patch@v1` · `exp.service.plugin-projection.render@v1`\n\n#### 4b. MCP Gateway Architecture (SETTLED — DO NOT REDESIGN)\n\n*   **cognitive-mcp** (`:3003`, Netmaker WireGuard IP `100.90.37.254`) is the **universal gateway for ALL external clients**: NotebookLM, Droid (factory.ai), Cursor, Codex, Junie, Gemini CLI. It has memory tools, gRPC service, auth, and the correct protocol surface.\n*   **compact-mcp** (`127.0.0.1:11436`) is **loopback/chatbot only**. Never expose externally. Never point external clients at it.\n*   Do NOT create new shim services. Do NOT point external clients at `op-assistant-grpc` directly. Do NOT expose compact-mcp outside loopback.\n\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\n**Rust Workspace**\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\n\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\n\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\n\n#### 6. Coding Style & Naming Conventions\n*   **Rust:** Edition 2021, `rustfmt` (4-space indent, max-width 100). Use specific imports (`use serde_json::Value;`). Use `anyhow::Result<T>` for main errors and `thiserror` for custom enums.\n*   **TypeScript/React:** 2-space indent, Prettier via ESLint. Functional components only. Strict mode enabled.\n*   **Testing:** 80%+ coverage, mock externals. Name tests with behavior-focused names (`should_handle_<scenario>`).\n\n#### 7. Agent-Specific Output & Workflow Instructions\n*   **Scroll & Save Pacing:** Provide only **ONE** major component or script at a time. Wait for user confirmation before moving to the next.\n*   **Visual Cues:** If a script is a finalized component that needs to be saved to sources, it MUST begin with color bullets or icons (e.g., ⚖️ 🔴, 🟢 🛷).\n*   **Spec-Block Format:** When delivering a component, use a strict specification block containing:\n  1.  **Requirements:** The architectural rules it satisfies.\n  2.  **Design:** How it fits into the 3tched system (Zero-Copy, Btrfs, GUI Schema, etc.).\n  3.  **Code Implementation:** The exact, copy-pasteable Rust/Bash code.\n*   Before edits: `cargo check -p <crate>`, `npm run typecheck`.\n*   Mimic existing patterns: Search similar code. No new deps without PR justification.\n\n#### 8. Personal Preferences & Coding Standards\n* Refer to `~/.factory/memories.md` for personal development preferences and past decisions.\n* Follow the conventions documented in:\n  * {"timestamp":"2026-06-28T07:42:34.828Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"function_call_output","call_id":"call_cdhkLM2N1MugW9f2zy2S0zDR","output":"Chunk ID: 3ba12b\nWall time: 0.0000 seconds\nProcess exited with code 0\nOriginal token count: 1678\nOutput:\n---\nname: agent-orchestrator\ndescription: Meta-skill que orquestra todos os agentes do ecossistema. Scan automatico de skills, match por capacidades, coordenacao de workflows multi-skill e registry management.\nrisk: safe\nsource: community\ndate_added: '2026-03-06'\nauthor: renat\ntags:\n- orchestration\n- multi-agent\n- workflow\n- automation\ntools:\n- claude-code\n- antigravity\n- cursor\n- gemini-cli\n- codex-cli\n---\n\n# Agent Orchestrator\n\n## Overview\n\nMeta-skill que orquestra todos os agentes do ecossistema. Scan automatico de skills, match por capacidades, coordenacao de workflows multi-skill e registry management.\n\n## When to Use This Skill\n\n- When you need specialized assistance with this domain\n\n## Do Not Use This Skill When\n\n- The task is unrelated to agent orchestrator\n- A simpler, more specific tool can handle the request\n- The user needs general-purpose assistance without domain expertise\n\n## How It Works\n\nMeta-skill que funciona como camada central de decisao e coordenacao para todo\no ecossistema de skills. Faz varredura automatica, identifica agentes relevantes\ne orquestra multiplos skills para tarefas complexas.\n\n## Principio: Zero Intervencao Manual\n\n- **SEMPRE faz varredura** antes de processar qualquer solicitacao\n- Novas skills sao **auto-detectadas e incluidas** ao criar SKILL.md em qualquer subpasta\n- Skills removidas sao **auto-excluidas** do registry\n- Nenhum comando manual e necessario para registrar novas skills\n\n---\n\n## Workflow Obrigatorio (Toda Solicitacao)\n\nExecute estes passos ANTES de processar qualquer request do usuario.\nOs scripts usam paths relativos automaticamente - funciona de qualquer diretorio.\n\n## Passo 1: Auto-Discovery (Varredura)\n\n```bash\npython agent-orchestrator/scripts/scan_registry.py\n```\n\nUltra-rapido (<100ms) via cache de hashes MD5. So re-processa arquivos alterados.\nRetorna JSON com resumo de todos os skills encontrados.\n\n## Passo 2: Match De Skills\n\n```bash\npython agent-orchestrator/scripts/match_skills.py \"<solicitacao do usuario>\"\n```\n\nRetorna JSON com skills ranqueadas por relevancia. Interpretar o resultado:\n\n| Resultado              | Acao                                                    |\n|:-----------------------|:--------------------------------------------------------|\n| `matched: 0`          | Nenhum skill relevante. Operar normalmente sem skills.  |\n| `matched: 1`          | Um skill relevante. Carregar seu SKILL.md e seguir.     |\n| `matched: 2+`         | Multiplos skills. Executar Passo 3 (orquestracao).      |\n\n## Passo 3: Orquestracao (Se Matched >= 2)\n\n```bash\npython agent-orchestrator/scripts/orchestrate.py --skills skill1,skill2 --query \"<solicitacao>\"\n```\n\nRetorna plano de execucao com padrao, ordem dos steps e data flow entre skills.\n\n## Passo Rapido (Atalho)\n\nPara queries simples, os passos 1+2 podem ser combinados em sequencia:\n```bash\npython agent-orchestrator/scripts/scan_registry.py && python agent-orchestrator/scripts/match_skills.py \"<solicitacao>\"\n```\n\n---\n\n## Skill Registry\n\nO registry vive em:\n```\nagent-orchestrator/data/registry.json\n```\n\n## Locais De Busca\n\nO scanner procura SKILL.md em:\n1. `.claude/skills/*/` (skills registradas no Claude Code)\n2. `*/` (skills standalone no top-level)\n3. `*/*\\` (skills em subpastas, ate profundidade 3)\n\n## Metadata Por Skill\n\nCada entrada no registry contem:\n\n| Campo          | Descricao                                          |\n|:---------------|:---------------------------------------------------|\n| name           | Nome da skill (do frontmatter YAML)                |\n| description    | Descricao completa (triggers inclusos)             |\n| location       | Caminho absoluto do diretorio                      |\n| skill_md       | Caminho absoluto do SKILL.md                       |\n| registered     | Se esta em .claude/skills/ (true/false)            |\n| capabilities   | Tags de capacidade (auto-extraidas + explicitas)   |\n| triggers       | Keywords de ativacao extraidas da description      |\n| language       | Linguagem principal (python/nodejs/bash/none)      |\n| status         | active / incomplete / missing                      |\n\n## Comandos Do Registry\n\n```bash\n\n## Scan Rapido (Usa Cache De Hashes)\n\npython agent-orchestrator/scripts/scan_registry.py\n\n## Tabela De Status Detalhada\n\npython agent-orchestrator/scripts/scan_registry.py --status\n\n## Re-Scan Completo (Ignora Cache)\n\npython agent-orchestrator/scripts/scan_registry.py --force\n```\n\n---\n\n## Algoritmo De Matching\n\nPara cada solicitacao, o matcher pontua skills usando:\n\n| Criterio                     | Pontos | Exemplo                               |\n|:-----------------------------|:-------|:--------------------------------------|\n| Nome do skill na query       | +15    | \"use web-scraper\" -> web-scraper      |\n| Keyword trigger exata        | +10    | \"scrape\" -> web-scraper               |\n| Categoria de capacidade      | +5     | data-extraction -> web-scraper        |\n| Sobreposicao de palavras     | +1     | Palavras da query na description      |\n| Boost de projeto             | +20    | Skill atribuida ao projeto ativo      |\n\nThreshold minimo: 5 pontos. Skills abaixo disso sao ignoradas.\n\n## Match Com Projeto\n\n```bash\npython agent-orchestrator/scripts/match_skills.py --project meu-projeto \"query aqui\"\n```\n\nSkills atribuidas ao projeto recebem +20 de boost automatico.\n\n---\n\n## Padroes De Orquestracao\n\nQuando multiplos skills sao relevantes, o orchestrator classifica o padrao:\n\n## 1. Pipeline Sequencial\n\nSkills formam uma cadeia onde o output de uma alimenta a proxima.\n\n**Quando:** Mix de skills \"produtoras\" (data-extraction, government-data) e \"consumidoras\" (messaging, social-media).\n\n**Exemplo:** web-scraper coleta precos -> whatsapp-cloud-api envia alerta\n\n```\nuser_query -> web-scraper -> whatsapp-cloud-api -> result\n```\n\n## 2. Execucao Paralela\n\nSkills trabalham independentemente em aspectos diferentes da solicitacao.\n\n**Quando:** Todas as skills tem o mesmo papel (todas produtoras ou todas consumidoras).\n\n**Exemplo:** instagram publica post + whatsapp envia notificacao (ambos recebem o mesmo conteudo)\n\n```\nuser_query -> [instagram, whatsapp-cloud-api] -> aggregated_result\n```\n\n## 3. Primario + Suporte\n\nUma skill principal lidera; outras fornecem dados de apoio.\n\n**Quando:** Uma skill tem score muito superior as demais (>= 2x).\n\n**Exemplo:** whatsapp-cloud-api envia mensagem (primario) + web-scraper fornece dados (suporte)\n\n```\nuser_query -> whatsapp-cloud-api (primary) + web-scraper (support) -> result\n```\n\n## Detalhes Em `References/Orchestration-Patterns.Md`\n\n---\n\n## Gerenciamento De Projetos\n\nAtribuir skills a projetos permite boost de relevancia e contexto persistente.\n\n## Arquivo De Projetos\n\n```\n","internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough":{"turn_id":"019f0d2d-ffae-70b0-b5ff-f34730c91f43"}}}

`crates/op-workflows/src/orchestrator.rs:429` | No | Core performance metrics and cache hit rates are defined ad-hoc. |\ncrates/audits/op-workflows/18_18_Schema_OSCAL_Compliance.md:53:  The `Orchestrator` generates cache keys for intermediate step caching by serializing the input JSON and hashing it with SHA-256:\ncrates/audits/op-workflows/18_18_Schema_OSCAL_Compliance.md:62:  This leads to **cache key non-determinism**. Identical JSON payloads with multiple keys will periodically serialize with rearranged field orders, resulting in different SHA-256 hashes. This causes silent cache misses, cache pollution, and unpredictable execution latency. If caching is used for idempotency or critical state checks, this non-determinism can lead to split-brain states or re-execution of non-idempotent operations.\ncrates/audits/op-workflows/18_18_Schema_OSCAL_Compliance.md:77:  Or utilize `serde_json::to_string` with a sorted Map container when calculating cache hashes.\ncrates/audits/op-workflows/18_18_Schema_OSCAL_Compliance.md:151:  2. **SC-28 (Protection of Information at Rest)**: Restrict the cache lifetime of tool parameters and enforce an automatic cache eviction policy (e.g. strict TTL or in-memory encryption) to protect sensitive workflow inputs from unauthorized memory access. Document this in the OSCAL SSP.\ncrates/audits/op-cache/08_08_Performance_Allocation_And_Memory.md:1:# Product Security and Quality Audit: `op-cache`\ncrates/audits/op-cache/08_08_Performance_Allocation_And_Memory.md:5:This production security and quality audit evaluates the `op-cache` crate, which provides BTRFS-backed caching with NUMA optimization and agent orchestration. not directly initialize `memmap2` or standard `mmap` references within the provided crate files. However, the workspace leverages `cozo` with the `storage-sled` backend enabled (`Cargo.toml`). `sled` inherently memory-maps its database files. \ncrates/audits/op-cache/08_08_Performance_Allocation_And_Memory.md:145:1. **`tmpfs` Double-Caching**: Running a memory-mapped database on a RAM-backed filesystem (`tmpfs`) results in double-caching (data resides in the filesystem RAM allocation and again in the OS page cache/program memory map), significantly wasting physical RAM and increasing OOM crash likelihood.\ncrates/audits/op-cache/08_08_Performance_Allocation_And_Memory.md:152:| `cozo` Database / `sled` | `Cargo.toml` (Workspace dependency) | `sled` (Internal mmap) | **Medium**: Potential memory bloat on `tmpfs` mounts; initialization failures on hardened `noexec` mount points. |\ncrates/audits/op-cache/08_08_Performance_Allocation_And_Memory.md:153:| Cache Sizing | `crates/op-cache/src/btrfs_cache.rs:440` | Heap Allocation (Dynamic) | **Low**: Reads full contents of directory entries synchronously into memory vectors. |\ncrates/audits/op-cache/08_08_Performance_Allocation_And_Memory.md:154:| Embedding Vector Load | `crates/op-cache/src/btrfs_cache.rs:316` | Heap Allocation (Dynamic) | **Low**: `std::fs::read` fully allocates vector space matching vector database file size. |\ncrates/audits/op-cache/08_08_Performance_Allocation_And_Memory.md:155:| Workflow Cache Load | `crates/op-cache/src/workflow_cache.rs:147` | Heap Allocation (Dynamic) | **Low**: Dynamic buffer allocation on read. Potential heap fragmentation if cached steps are exceptionally large. |\ncrates/audits/op-cache/08_08_Performance_Allocation_And_Memory.md:156:| Workstack Cache Load | `crates/op-cache/src/workstack_cache.rs:125` | Heap Allocation (Dynamic) | **Low**: Dynamic buffer allocation proportional to step response size. |\ncrates/audits/op-cache/08_08_Performance_Allocation_And_Memory.md:163:* **Location**: `crates/op-cache/src/snapshot_manager.rs:47`\ncrates/audits/op-cache/08_08_Performance_Allocation_And_Memory.md:170:Because BTRFS cache snapshots contain highly sensitive security audits, proprietary source code analysis, and query traces, these directories must not be world-readable.\ncrates/audits/op-cache/08_08_Performance_Allocation_And_Memory.md:176:* **Location**: `crates/op-cache/src/pattern_tracker.rs:125` & `crates/op-cache/src/workflow_tracker.rs:136`\ncrates/audits/op-cache/08_08_Performance_Allocation_And_Memory.md:179:The SQLite database connection is protected via `Mutex<rusqlite::Connection>`. Under high concurrent requests through the gRPC server, multiple worker threads attempting to log agent execution paths will encounter serialized database locks. This forms a bottleneck at the SQLite connection mutex, negating the throughput benefits of the async scheduler.\ncrates/audits/op-cache/08_08_Performance_Allocation_And_Memory.md:182:Utilize a connection pool (e.g., `r2d2` or `sqlx` with sqlite) or leverage SQLite in WAL mode (`Write-Ahead Logging`) with thread-safe connection caching to permit concurrent reads and non-blocking writes.\ncrates/audits/op-cache/08_08_Performance_Allocation_And_Memory.md:185:* **Location**: `crates/op-cache/src/workflow_cache.rs:373` & `crates/op-cache/src/workstack_cache.rs:376`\ncrates/audits/op-cache/08_08_Performance_Allocation_And_Memory.md:188:Zstd decompression is performed directly on cached buffers using:\ncrates/audits/op-cache/08_08_Performance_Allocation_And_Memory.md:192:If an attacker manages to write a malformed payload or a highly-repetitive cache pattern to disk, decompression can expand a tiny file into gigabytes of memory, causing a Denial of Service (DoS) crash via Out-Of-Memory (OOM).\n","internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough":{"turn_id":"019f0d2d-ffae-70b0-b5ff-f34730c91f43"}}}

FieldType::Boolean\n    } else if value.as_i64().is_some() || value.as_u64().is_some() {\n        FieldType::Integer\n    } else if value.as_f64().is_some() {\n        FieldType::Float\n    } else if Shared-memory projection layer for the projected plugin tree.\n//!\n//! The projected plugin tree lives in tmpfs (`/dev/shm/opdbus/projections/`).\n//! The MutationEngine writes one file per plugin on every mutation (atomic\n//! temp+rename). The projection D-Bus server reads 1:1 from these files on\n//! every property access — zero-copy, memory-speed, no held cache.\n//!\n//! This module is the shared contract between the **writer** (op-grpc-bridge\n//! MutationEngine, the single write door) and the **reader** (op-projection\n//! D-Bus server). Both depend on op-core, so the path constants and I/O\n//! helpers live here.\n\nuse simd_json::prelude::*;\nuse std::fs;\nuse std::io::Write;\n\n/// Directory for per-plugin projection files (one JSON file per plugin).\npub const SHM_PROJECTION_DIR: &str = \"/dev/shm/opdbus/projections\";\n\n/// Manifest carrying the monotonic `generation` counter. Written LAST as the\n/// atomic commit point after each projection write. Consumers read it to\n/// detect staleness (compare generation before/after a read).\npub const SHM_PROJECTION_MANIFEST: &str = \"/dev/shm/opdbus/projections/.manifest.json\";\n\n/// Atomically publish `bytes` to a `/dev/shm` path via a sibling temp file +\n/// rename, so readers see either the old or new content, never a torn write.\npub fn atomic_write_shm(path: &str, bytes: &[u8]) -> anyhow::Result<()> {\n    let tmp = format!(\"{}.tmp\", path);\n    {\n        let mut file =\n            fs::File::create(&tmp).map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!(\"Cannot create {}: {}\", tmp, e))?;\n        file.write_all(bytes)\n            .map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!(\"Failed to write {}: {}\", tmp, e))?;\n        file.sync_all()\n            .map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!(\"Failed to sync {}: {}\", tmp, e))?;\n    }\n    fs::rename(&tmp, path)\n        .map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!(\"Failed to rename {} -> {}: {}\", tmp, path, e))?;\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n/// Sanitize a plugin id into a safe flat filename (no path separators or NUL).\nfn safe_filename(plugin_id: &str) -> String {\n    plugin_id\n        .chars()\n        .map(|c| {\n            if c == '/' || c == '\\\\' || c == '\\0' {\n                '_'\n            } else {\n                c\n            }\n        })\n        .collect()\n}\n\n/// File path for a specific plugin's projection.\npub fn projection_file_path(plugin_id: &str) -> String {\n    format!(\"{}/{}.json\", SHM_PROJECTION_DIR, safe_filename(plugin_id))\n}\n\n/// Write a plugin's full projected state to shm and bump the manifest\n/// generation.\n///\n/// Called by the MutationEngine on every mutation that changes a plugin's\n/// state. `json_bytes` is the JSON serialization of the plugin's current state\n/// (the mutation fold from `state_cache`).\npub fn write_projection(plugin_id: &str, json_bytes: &[u8]) -> anyhow::Result<()> {\n    fs::create_dir_all(SHM_PROJECTION_DIR).map_err(|e| {\n        anyhow::anyhow!(\"Cannot create projection dir {}: {}\", SHM_PROJECTION_DIR, e)\n    })?;\n\n    let path = projection_file_path(plugin_id);\n    atomic_write_shm(&path, json_bytes)?;\n\n    // Bump manifest generation (atomic commit point, written last).\n    let generation = read_manifest_generation().wrapping_add(1);\n    let manifest = format!(\"{{\\\"generation\\\":{}}}\", generation);\n    atomic_write_shm(SHM_PROJECTION_MANIFEST, manifest.as_bytes())?;\n\n    tracing::debug!(plugin_id, generation, \"Projection written to shm\");\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n/// Read the raw bytes of a plugin's projection from shm.\npub fn read_projection_bytes(plugin_id: &str) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {\n    fs::read(projection_file_path(plugin_id)).ok()\n}\n\n/// Read the current manifest `generation`, or 0 if no manifest exists yet.\npub fn read_manifest_generation() -> u64 {\n    let mut bytes = match fs::read(SHM_PROJECTION_MANIFEST) {\n        Ok(b) => b,\n        Err(_) => return 0,\n    };\n    let value = match simd_json::from_slice::<simd_json::OwnedValue>(&mut bytes) {\n        Ok(v) => v,\n        Err(_) => return 0,\n    };\n    match value.get(\"generation\") {\n        Some(g) => g.as_u64().unwrap_or(0),\n        None => 0,\n    }\n}\n\n/// List all plugin ids that currently have projection files in shm.\n///\n/// The manifest file (`.manifest.json`) is excluded. Plugin filenames are\n/// unsanitized back to their original form (the safe-filename transform is\n/// lossless for valid plugin ids).\npub fn list_projected_plugins() -> Vec<String> {\n    let mut plugins = Vec::new();\n    if let Ok(entries) = fs::read_dir(SHM_PROJECTION_DIR) {\n        for entry in entries.flatten() {\n            if let Some(name) = entry.file_name().to_str() {\n                if let Some(plugin) = name.strip_suffix(\".json\") {\n                    // Skip the manifest (`.manifest.json` → `.manifest`)\n                    if !plugin.starts_with('.') {\n                        plugins.push(plugin.to_string());\n                    }\n                }\n","internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough":{"turn_id":"019f0d2d-ffae-70b0-b5ff-f34730c91f43"}}}

To add a field, add it to the\n/// plugin state — never hand-write a field definition.\npub(crate) fn schema_from_state(\n    name: &str,\n    category: &str,\n    version: &str,\n    description: &str,\n    state: &Value,\n) -> PluginSchema {\n    use simd_json::prelude::*;\n\n    let mut builder = PluginSchema::builder(name)\n        .version(version)\n        .category(category)\n        .description(description);\n\n    if let Some(obj) = state.as_object() {\n        for (key, value) in obj.iter() {\n            builder = builder.field(&key.to_string(), field_from_value(value));\n        }\n    }\n\n    builder.example(state.clone()).build()\n}\n\n/// Infer a `FieldSchema` (type + example) from a live state value.\npub(crate) fn field_from_value(value: &Value) -> FieldSchema {\n    FieldSchema {\n        field_type: infer_field_type(value),\n        required: false,\n        description: String::new(),\n        default: None,\n        example: Some(value.clone()),\n        constraints: Vec::new(),\n        read_only: false,\n        read_only_when: None,\n    }\n}\n\n/// Infer a `FieldType` from a live state value, recursing into arrays/objects.\npub(crate) fn infer_field_type(value: &Value) -> FieldType {\n    use simd_json::prelude::*;\n\n    if value.is_null() {\n        FieldType::Any\n    } else if value.as_bool().is_some() {\n        FieldType::Boolean\n    } else if value.as_i64().is_some() || value.as_u64().is_some() {\n        FieldType::Integer\n    } else if value.as_f64().is_some() {\n        FieldType::Float\n","internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough":{"turn_id":"019f0d33-6b9e-7e52-920e-cc24848059df"}}}

Mirror Object D-Bus Interface\n\nuse serde_json::Value;\nuse zbus::interface;\n\n/// A generic D-Bus object representing a database row\npub struct MirrorObject {\n    data: Value,\n}\n\nimpl MirrorObject {\n    pub fn new(data: Value) -> Self {\n        Self { data }\n    }\n\n    pub fn update_data(&mut self, new_data: Value) -> bool {\n        if self.data == new_data {\n            return false;\n        }\n        tracing::debug!(\"Updating MirrorObject data\");\n        self.data = new_data;\n        true\n    }\n}\n\n#[interface(name = \"org.opdbus.ProjectedObjectV1\")]\nimpl MirrorObject {\n    /// Get the full JSON representation of the row\n    #[zbus(property)]\n    async fn json_data(&self) -> String {\n        serde_json::to_string(&self.data).unwrap_or_default()\n    }\n\n    /// Get a specific property value by key\n    async fn get_property(&self, key: String) -> String {\n        self.data\n            .get(&key)\n            .map(|v| serde_json::to_string(v).unwrap_or_default())\n            .unwrap_or_default()\n    }\n\n    /// Signal emitted when json_data changes\n    #[zbus(signal)]\n    pub async fn data_updated(\n        &self,\n        _ctxt: &zbus::object_server::SignalEmitter<'_>,\n    ) -> zbus::Result<()>;\n}\n","internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough":{"turn_id":"019f0d42-8feb-7e90-98e5-9bf27ed92d53"}}}

Shared between DbusMirror and the\n/// ObjectManagerInterface so writes are visible immediately to readers.\npub type ManagedObjectRegistry = Arc<DashMap<OwnedObjectPath, InterfaceMap>>;\n\n/// D-Bus path where the ObjectManager is registered.\npub const OBJECT_MANAGER_PATH: &str = \"/org/opdbus/v1\";\n\n/// Interface name exposed on every projected plugin object.\npub const PROJECTED_IFACE: &str Follow these strictly to maintain consistency, pass CI, and adhere to the 3tched Architecture standards.\n\n#### 1. The Persona & Naming Conventions\n*   **Humanized Roles:** Treat system components as authoritative human roles. Never use sterile acronyms for major components.\n  *   **A.N.N.A. Scribe** (Axon Network Notary Arbitrator): The top-level Identity-State Arbitrator who notarizes the WireGuard identity and handles the \"Snowball\" session.\n  *   **The Compliance Engine (\"Law Firm\"):** One dedicated Attorney for each major component: **Olivia Scal** (Managing Partner / OSCAL), **E.U.gene Risk** (EU AI Act Counsel), **Penny Privacy** (GDPR Engine), and **Reggie O.P.A.** (Cloud Prosecutor).\n*   **Terminology:** Use exact architecture terminology: \"The Sled\" (1:1 shared memory layout), \"The Shuttle\" (the Rust bridge/courier), \"The Snowball\" (appended session ledger), and \"The Strike/Etch\" (generating the hash).\n\n#### 2. Core Architectural Rules (The \"Reality\")\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via OpenClaw Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Artix Linux (s6 init).\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles — D-Bus First (MANDATORY)\n\n**D-Bus is the ONLY control plane. Every read, every write, every tool call goes through D-Bus. There is no second option.**\n\n*   **D-Bus first. D-Bus always. D-Bus only.** If you are about to call a CLI, spawn a subprocess, read a config file, or poll a socket directly — stop. Find the D-Bus object and use it instead. `org.opdbus.v1` is the system.\n*   **No bypasses.** `Command::new(\"systemctl\")`, `Command::new(\"ip\")`, `Command::new(\"s6-svc\")`, direct file reads for live state — all forbidden in plugin and service code. Bootstrap scripts are the only exception.\n*   **D-Bus objects own plugin state.** Every plugin is a D-Bus object at `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<name>`. Read state through it. Mutate state through it. If there is no D-Bus object, the thing does not exist.\n*   **D-Bus method signatures are generated from the schema.** All D-Bus methods, MCP tool inputs, gRPC shapes, and UI field renderers derive from the `PluginSchema` in `plugin_schema_defs.rs`. The schema IS the interface contract — not a description of it.\n*   **One schema file, one source of truth.** All `PluginSchema` definitions MUST live in `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/plugin_schema_defs.rs`. Each plugin's `schema()` method calls `Some(super::plugin_schema_defs::their_plugin_schema())`. **Never define a schema inline in a plugin's own file** — it will not be registered, and the D-Bus object will have no contract.\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC (over Unix domain sockets or `grpc-uplink`). gRPC calls still flow through D-Bus registration — the D-Bus object is the authority, gRPC is the transport.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`simd_json` preferred, `serde_json` acceptable).\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n*   **No Python unless absolutely necessary.** This is a Rust-first codebase. Scripts are shell (`sh`/`bash`). Data processing is Rust. If you are reaching for Python, stop and ask why Rust or shell cannot do it. The only acceptable Python is in existing compliance-ingest tooling where no Rust equivalent exists yet.\n\n#### 4a. OSCAL Subid Taxonomy (MANDATORY — every artifact must carry a subid)\n\nEvery D-Bus object, plugin, schema, mutation, event, and tool in this system has two identifiers: a `uuid` (machine identity, never changes) and a `subid` (human-readable operational taxonomy key, stable per subject).\n\n**`subid` format:** `<category>.<component-type>.<subject>.<verb>[.<facet>][@vN]`\n\n**Seven categories — use exactly these, no others:**\n\n| category | what it classifies |\n|---|---|\n| `src` | authoritative source, ingress channel, source-of-truth store |\n| `prj` | D-Bus projection or mirror publication step |\n| `sch` | schema, contract, vocabulary, or control-mapping artifact |\n| `mut` | write-path operation that changes effective state |\n| `obs` | read, query, enumeration, discovery path |\n| `evt` | emitted signal, audit-chain event, proof, tag provenance |\n| `exp` | consumer-facing render — MCP tool, UI surface, gRPC bridge view |\n\n**Component-type** reuses OSCAL vocabulary: `software`, `service`, `network`, `hardware`, `process-procedure`, `standard`, `validation`, `policy`, `plan`, `guidance`, `physical`, `this-system`, `system`, `interconnection`.\n\n**Rules:**\n- `uuid` is exact machine identity — never replace it with `subid`\n- `subid` is an OSCAL `prop` value (`ns`, `name`, `value`) — never embed it in `remarks`\n- Compliance mappings (`control_refs[]`, `statement_refs[]`, `control_source`) live in metadata arrays, **never** inside the `subid` string\n- `mut.*` records **must** carry `actor_id` and `capability_id`\n- `evt.*` records **must** carry `event_id` or `event_hash`\n- `subid` is immutable per subject — if the meaning changes materially, create a new subject with `@vN`\n- All subids are registered in the canonical registry; uniqueness is enforced in CI\n\n**Examples:** `src.network.ovsdb.monitor@v1` · `prj.service.projected-object.publish@v1` · `sch.standard.plugin-schema.resolve@v1` · `mut.service.state-sync.apply-patch@v1` · `exp.service.plugin-projection.render@v1`\n\n#### 4b. MCP Gateway Architecture (SETTLED — DO NOT REDESIGN)\n\n*   **cognitive-mcp** (`:3003`, Netmaker WireGuard IP `100.90.37.254`) is the **universal gateway for ALL external clients**: NotebookLM, Droid (factory.ai), Cursor, Codex, Junie, Gemini CLI. It has memory tools, gRPC service, auth, and the correct protocol surface.\n*   **compact-mcp** (`127.0.0.1:11436`) is **loopback/chatbot only**. Never expose externally. Never point external clients at it.\n*   Do NOT create new shim services. Do NOT point external clients at `op-assistant-grpc` directly. Do NOT expose compact-mcp outside loopback.\n\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\n**Rust Workspace**\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\n\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\n\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\n\n#### 6. Coding Style & Naming Conventions\n*   **Rust:** Edition 2021, `rustfmt` (4-space indent, max-width 100). Use specific imports (`use serde_json::Value;`). Use `anyhow::Result<T>` for main errors and `thiserror` for custom enums.\n*   **TypeScript/React:** 2-space indent, Prettier via ESLint. Functional components only. Strict mode enabled.\n*   **Testing:** 80%+ coverage, mock externals. Name tests with behavior-focused names (`should_handle_<scenario>`).\n\n#### 7. Agent-Specific Output & Workflow Instructions\n*   **Scroll & Save Pacing:** Provide only **ONE** major component or script at a time. Wait for user confirmation before moving to the next.\n*   **Visual Cues:** If a script is a finalized component that needs to be saved to sources, it MUST begin with color bullets or icons (e.g., ⚖️ 🔴, 🟢 🛷).\n*   **Spec-Block Format:** When delivering a component, use a strict specification block containing:\n  1.  **Requirements:** The architectural rules it satisfies.\n  2.  **Design:** How it fits into the 3tched system (Zero-Copy, Btrfs, GUI Schema, etc.).\n  3.  **Code Implementation:** The exact, copy-pasteable Rust/Bash code.\n*   Before edits: `cargo check -p <crate>`, `npm run typecheck`.\n*   Mimic existing patterns: Search similar code. No new deps without PR justification.\n\n#### 8. Personal Preferences & Coding Standards\n* Refer to `~/.factory/memories.md` for personal development preferences and past decisions.\n* Follow the conventions documented in:\n  * HTTP Transport\n//!\n//! HTTP/REST transport with SSE support.\n//! Provides three variants:\n//! - HttpTransport: REST only\n//! - SseTransport: SSE only (for clients that use separate SSE + POST)\n//! - HttpSseTransport: Combined bidirectional (recommended)\n//!\n//! Authentication (audit item #3):\n//!   - `/health` is always open.\n//!   - Real socket-loopback callers bypass auth (Host header is NEVER trusted).\n//!   - All other callers must present `Authorization: Bearer <token>` AND the\n//!     token must be accepted by the configured [`AuthValidator`].\n//!   - The default validator is fail-secure: it only accepts tokens listed in\n//!     `OPDBUS_MCP_ALLOWED_PEERS`. If that env var is unset/empty, every\n//!     bearer token is rejected.\n//!   - Additionally, the `User-Agent` must match a known MCP client pattern\n//!     (Codex, Cursor, Claude Desktop, etc.) unless `OPDBUS_MCP_ANY_AGENT=1`\n//!     is set (for development). Unknown agents are logged and rejected.\n\nuse super::{McpHandler, Transport};\nuse crate::McpRequest;\nuse anyhow::Result;\nuse axum::{\n    extract::{ConnectInfo, State},\n    http::{HeaderMap, StatusCode},\n    middleware,\n    response::{\n        sse::{Event, Sse},\n        IntoResponse, Json, Response,\n    },\n    routing::{get, post},\n    Router,\n};\nuse futures::stream::{self, Stream};\nuse simd_json::{json, OwnedValue as Value};\nuse std::convert::Infallible;\nuse std::net::SocketAddr;\nuse std::sync::Arc;\nuse std::time::Duration;\nuse tokio::sync::broadcast;\nuse tower_http::cors::{Any, CorsLayer};\nuse tracing::{debug, info, warn};\nuse uuid::Uuid;\n\n// =============================================================================\n// AuthValidator (audit item #3)\n//\n// The previous implementation accepted ANY token that matched the *shape* of a\n// WireGuard pubkey or a UUID. That was not authentication; it was a regex.\n// Real authorization now goes through an `AuthValidator`. The default\n// `EnvAllowListValidator` is fail-secure: with no entries, it rejects every\n// bearer token, and only loopback callers can reach the handlers.\n// =============================================================================\n\n/// Validates an opaque bearer token against an authoritative source\n/// (WireGuard peer DB, A.N.N.A. Scribe session ledger, etc.).\n#[async_trait::async_trait]\npub trait AuthValidator: Send + Sync + 'static {\n    async fn validate(&self, token: &str) -> bool;\n}\n\n/// Default validator backed by the `OPDBUS_MCP_ALLOWED_PEERS` env var\n/// (comma-separated list of allowed pubkeys and/or session UUIDs).\n///\n/// * If the env var is unset or empty, **every** bearer token is rejected.\n/// * Comparisons are constant-time over the candidate's length to prevent\n///   timing oracles on partial matches.\npub struct EnvAllowListValidator {\n    allowed: Vec<String>,\n}\n\nimpl EnvAllowListValidator {\n    /// Read the allow-list from `OPDBUS_MCP_ALLOWED_PEERS`.\n    pub fn from_env() -> Self {\n        let raw = std::env::var(\"OPDBUS_MCP_ALLOWED_PEERS\").unwrap_or_default();\n        let allowed: Vec<String> = raw\n            .split(',')\n            .map(|s| s.trim().to_string())\n            .filter(|s| !s.is_empty())\n            .collect();\n        if allowed.is_empty() {\n            warn!(\n                \"OPDBUS_MCP_ALLOWED_PEERS is empty; bearer-token auth will reject all tokens. \\\n                 Only loopback callers will be accepted.\"\n            );\n        } else {\n            info!(count = allowed.len(), \"Loaded MCP peer allow-list\");\n        }\n        Self { allowed }\n    }\n\n    /// Construct an allow-list directly (primarily for tests and embedders).\n    #[allow(dead_code)]\n    pub fn new<I, S>(entries: I) -> Self\n    where\n        I: IntoIterator<Item = S>,\n        S: Into<String>,\n    {\n        Self {\n            allowed: entries.into_iter().map(Into::into).collect(),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n#[async_trait::async_trait]\nimpl AuthValidator for EnvAllowListValidator {\n    async fn validate(&self, token: &str) -> bool {\n        let token_bytes = token.as_bytes();\n        let mut matched = false;\n        for entry in &self.allowed {\n            matched |= ct_eq(token_bytes, entry.as_bytes());\n        }\n        matched\n    }\n}\n\n/// Constant-time byte-slice equality. Returns false on length mismatch\n/// (length is not considered secret; the contents are).\nfn ct_eq(a: &[u8], b: &[u8]) -> bool {\n    if a.len() != b.len() {\n        return false;\n    }\n    let mut diff: u8 = 0;\n    for (x, y) in a.iter().zip(b.iter()) {\n        diff |= x ^ y;\n    }\n    diff == 0\n}\n\nfn extract_bearer_token(headers: &HeaderMap) -> Option<&str> {\n    headers\n        .get(\"authorization\")\n        .and_then(|value| value.to_str().ok())\n        .and_then(|value| value.trim().strip_prefix(\"Bearer \"))\n        .map(str::trim)\n        .filter(|token| !token.is_empty())\n}\n\n#[allow(dead_code)]\nfn is_wireguard_pubkey_shape(token: &str) -> bool {\n    token.len() == 44\n        && token.ends_with('=')\n        && token\n            .chars()\n            .all(|ch| ch.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || matches!(ch, '+' | '/' | '='))\n}\n\n#[allow(dead_code)]\nfn is_wireguard_session_id_shape(token: &str) -> bool {\n    Uuid::parse_str(token).is_ok()\n}\n\n/// **Shape check only.** Used as a cheap pre-filter inside the validator.\n/// MUST NOT be used as an authorization decision on its own.\n#[allow(dead_code)]\nfn is_wireguard_auth_token_shape(token: &str) -> bool {\n    is_wireguard_pubkey_shape(token) || is_wireguard_session_id_shape(token)\n}\n\nfn is_loopback_addr(addr: &SocketAddr) -> bool {\n    addr.ip().is_loopback()\n}\n\n/// Known MCP client User-Agent substrings.\n/// A request must match at least one to be accepted from a non-loopback peer.\n/// Set `OPDBUS_MCP_ANY_AGENT=1` to bypass this check during development.\nconst KNOWN_MCP_AGENTS: &[&str] = &[\n    \"codex\",      // OpenAI Codex CLI\n    \"cursor\",     // Cursor IDE\n    \"claude\",     // Claude Desktop / Claude Code\n    \"anthropic\",  // Anthropic SDK\n    \"continue\",   // Continue.dev\n    \"cline\",      // Cline VSCode extension\n    \"copilot\",    // GitHub Copilot\n    \"windsurf\",   // Windsurf IDE\n {"timestamp":"2026-06-28T08:28:16.276Z","type":"event_msg","payload":{"type":"agent_message","message":"Correct, if it is gated to the Netmaker/WireGuard IP `100.90.37.254`, a normal GitHub App running from GitHub’s cloud cannot call it directly.\n\nGitHub can only reach public internet endpoints. It cannot route to your private WireGuard address unless you add one of these:\n\n- a GitHub Actions runner or app worker inside the WireGuard network\n- a public reverse proxy that terminates auth and forwards into `cognitive-mcp`\n- a tunnel service that exposes the MCP gateway intentionally\n- GitHub webhook receiver on a public URL, which then relays over D-Bus/WG internally\n\nSo for the current architecture:\n\n`http://100.90.37.254:3003/mcp` works for clients already on the WireGuard mesh.\n\nIt will **not** work directly for GitHub-hosted Apps/webhooks. For those, the right pattern is a small public ingress/relay with strong auth, then internal forwarding to cognitive-mcp over WG/D-Bus.","phase":"final_answer","memory_citation":null}}

Even though you've set the quota project via gcloud and environment variables, the error persists.\\n\\nThe key to understanding this error lies in how Application Default Credentials (ADC) works and the precedence of different methods for setting the quota project, particularly for client-based APIs.\\n\\nHere's a breakdown and the most likely solutions:\\n\\nUnderstanding the Problem\\n\\nClient-Based API: The error message mentions cloudcode-pa.googleapis.com , which is a client-based API. For these APIs, a quota project must be explicitly set because it doesn't automatically derive it from a resource.\\nADC and Quota Project: When using ADC, Google Cloud attempts to find a quota project. While gcloud auth application-default set-quota-project can update your local ADC file, and environment variables can work, sometimes programmatic calls, especially with certain client libraries (like C++ as noted in some documentation), require more direct specification.\\nThe Misleading Error Message: The message \\\"Your application is authenticating by using local Application Default Credentials\\\" might be accurate, but the part about the quota project \\\"not being set by default\\\" can be confusing when you've already tried to set it. The core issue is that your programmatic request isn't picking up the quota project from where you expect it to.\\nx-goog-user-project Header: For direct REST or RPC API calls, or in some client libraries, the most definitive way to specify the quota project is through the x-goog-user-project HTTP header. This takes the highest precedence.\\nSolutions to try:\\n\\nExplicitly Set Quota Project in Your Code (Highest Precedence):\\nThis is often the most reliable way to ensure your programmatic calls use the correct quota project, overriding other settings.\\nIf using a Google Cloud Client Library:\\nMany client libraries allow you to set the quota project when you initialize the client object or make a specific request. Use code with care. Note that not all client libraries (e.g., Ruby, as mentioned in documentation) might support this specific environment variable.\\nexport GOOGLE_CLOUD_QUOTA_PROJECT=operation-dbus\\nGenerated code may be subject to license restrictions not shown here. Without this, even if the quota project is set, the identity won't have permission to consume its quota.\\nWhy the Error Can Be Persistent\\n\\nThe order of precedence for how the quota project is determined is:\\n\\nExplicitly specified in the request (e.g., x-goog-user-project header or client library option).\\nEnvironment variables.\\nAuthentication credentials (e.g., from ADC file, service account's project).\\nIf you set an environment variable, but your client library or code explicitly sets (or attempts to set) a different one, or if it doesn't recognize the environment variable, the issue can occur. {"timestamp":"2026-06-28T09:42:17.002Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"function_call_output","call_id":"call_xZ0ek3jM973PWkG8AUjBb0Nu","output":"Chunk ID: 871746\nWall time: 0.2675 seconds\nProcess exited with code 0\nOriginal token count: 1030\nOutput:\n#!/bin/bash\n# Deploy script for op-openvswitch-daemon\n# Installs the D-Bus daemon for OpenVSwitch management\n#\n# Architecture (AGENTS.md §4):\n#   Bus name: org.opdbus.v1\n#   Object paths: /org/opdbus/rovs/jsonrpc, /org/opdbus/rovs/openflow\n#   Interfaces: org.opdbus.rovs.jsonrpc, org.opdbus.rovs.openflow\n\nset -e\n\nDAEMON_NAME=\"op-openvswitch-daemon\"\nDAEMON_PATH=\"/usr/local/bin/${DAEMON_NAME}\"\nDBUS_SERVICE_FILE=\"/usr/share/dbus-1/system-services/org.opdbus.v1.service\"\nDBUS_CONF_FILE=\"/etc/dbus-1/system.d/org.opdbus.v1.conf\"\nS6_SERVICE_DIR=\"/etc/s6/sv/${DAEMON_NAME}\"\nSYSTEMD_SERVICE_FILE=\"/etc/systemd/system/${DAEMON_NAME}.service\"\n\necho \"=== Deploying ${DAEMON_NAME} ===\"\n\n# Check for binary\nif [ ! -f \"./target/release/${DAEMON_NAME}\" ] && [ ! -f \"./target/debug/${DAEMON_NAME}\" ]; then\n    echo \"Error: Binary not found. Build first with:\"\n    echo \"  cargo build -p ${DAEMON_NAME} --release\"\n    exit 1\nfi\n\n# Use release binary if available, otherwise debug\nif [ -f \"./target/release/${DAEMON_NAME}\" ]; then\n    BINARY=\"./target/release/${DAEMON_NAME}\"\n    echo \"Using release binary\"\nelse\n    BINARY=\"./target/debug/${DAEMON_NAME}\"\n    echo \"Using debug binary\"\nfi\n\n# Install binary\necho \"Installing binary to ${DAEMON_PATH}...\"\nsudo cp \"${BINARY}\" \"${DAEMON_PATH}\"\nsudo chmod +x \"${DAEMON_PATH}\"\n\n# Create D-Bus service file (for D-Bus activation — optional)\necho \"Creating D-Bus service file...\"\nsudo tee \"${DBUS_SERVICE_FILE}\" > /dev/null << 'EOF'\n[D-Bus Service]\nName=org.opdbus.v1\nExec=/usr/local/bin/op-openvswitch-daemon\nUser=root\nSystemdService=op-openvswitch-daemon.service\nEOF\n\n# Create D-Bus policy file\necho \"Creating D-Bus policy file...\"\nsudo tee \"${DBUS_CONF_FILE}\" > /dev/null << 'EOF'\n<!DOCTYPE busconfig PUBLIC \"-//freedesktop//DTD D-BUS Bus Configuration 1.0//EN\"\n  \"http://www.freedesktop.org/standards/dbus/1.0/busconfig.dtd\">\n<busconfig>\n  <policy user=\"root\">\n    <allow own=\"org.opdbus.v1\"/>\n    <allow send_destination=\"org.opdbus.v1\"/>\n    <allow receive_sender=\"org.opdbus.v1\"/>\n  </policy>\n  <policy context=\"default\">\n    <allow send_destination=\"org.opdbus.v1\"/>\n    <allow receive_sender=\"org.opdbus.v1\"/>\n  </policy>\n</busconfig>\nEOF\n\n# Install s6 service definition (Artix/Chimera Linux)\nif [ -d /etc/s6/sv ] || [ -d /run/service ]; then\n    echo \"Installing s6 service definition...\"\n    sudo mkdir -p \"${S6_SERVICE_DIR}\"\n    sudo cp -r \"./deploy/s6/${DAEMON_NAME}/\"* \"${S6_SERVICE_DIR}/\"\n    sudo chmod +x \"${S6_SERVICE_DIR}/run\"\n\n    # Link into live scan directory if s6 is active\n    if [ -d /run/service ]; then\n        sudo ln -sf \"${S6_SERVICE_DIR}\" \"/run/service/${DAEMON_NAME}\"\n        sudo s6-svscanctl -a /run/service 2>/dev/null || true\n        echo \"Linked s6 service to /run/service/${DAEMON_NAME}\"\n    fi\nfi\n\n# Create systemd service file (for systems with systemd)\nif command -v systemctl &> /dev/null; then\n    echo \"Creating systemd service file...\"\n    sudo tee \"${SYSTEMD_SERVICE_FILE}\" > /dev/null << EOF\n[Unit]\nDescription=OpenVSwitch D-Bus Daemon\nAfter=network.target openvswitch-switch.service\nWants=openvswitch-switch.service\n\n[Service]\nType=dbus\nBusName=org.opdbus.v1\nExecStart=${DAEMON_PATH} --grpc 127.0.0.1:50051\nRestart=on-failure\nRestartSec=5\n\n[Install]\nWantedBy=multi-user.target\nEOF\n    sudo systemctl daemon-reload\n    echo \"Systemd service created. Enable with:\"\n    echo \"  sudo systemctl enable ${DAEMON_NAME}\"\n    echo \"  sudo systemctl start ${DAEMON_NAME}\"\nfi\n\necho \"\"\necho \"=== Deployment Complete ===\"\necho \"\"\necho \"The daemon can be started:\"\necho \"  - Manually: sudo ${DAEMON_PATH}\"\necho \"  - With gRPC: sudo ${DAEMON_PATH} --grpc 0.0.0.0:50051\"\nif [ -d /run/service ]; then\n    echo \"  - Via s6:    sudo s6-svc -u /run/service/${DAEMON_NAME}\"\nfi\nif command -v systemctl &> /dev/null; then\n    echo \"  - Via systemd: sudo systemctl start ${DAEMON_NAME}\"\nfi\necho \"\"\necho \"Test D-Bus JSON-RPC interface:\"\necho \"  busctl call org.opdbus.v1 /org/opdbus/rovs/jsonrpc org.opdbus.rovs.jsonrpc transact s 'list_dbs' s '[]'\"\necho \"\"\necho \"Test gRPC interface:\"\necho \"  grpcurl -plaintext 127.0.0.1:50051 list ovsdaemon.v1.OvsdbService\"\n","internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough":{"turn_id":"019f0d9b-529d-7a31-b915-696cb652e136"}}}

{"timestamp":"2026-06-28T06:25:26.219Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"message","role":"user","content":[{"type":"input_text","text":"# AGENTS.md instructions for /home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto\n\n<INSTRUCTIONS>\n### AGENTS.md for operation-dbus-proto\n\nThis file provides essential guidelines for agentic coding agents working in this repository. Follow these strictly to maintain consistency, pass CI, and adhere to the 3tched Architecture standards.\n\n#### 1. The Persona & Naming Conventions\n*   **Humanized Roles:** Treat system components as authoritative human roles. Never use sterile acronyms for major components.\n  *   **A.N.N.A. Scribe** (Axon Network Notary Arbitrator): The top-level Identity-State Arbitrator who notarizes the WireGuard identity and handles the \"Snowball\" session.\n  *   **The Compliance Engine (\"Law Firm\"):** One dedicated Attorney for each major component: **Olivia Scal** (Managing Partner / OSCAL), **E.U.gene Risk** (EU AI Act Counsel), **Penny Privacy** (GDPR Engine), and **Reggie O.P.A.** (Cloud Prosecutor).\n*   **Terminology:** Use exact architecture terminology: \"The Sled\" (1:1 shared memory layout), \"The Shuttle\" (the Rust bridge/courier), \"The Snowball\" (appended session ledger), and \"The Strike/Etch\" (generating the hash).\n\n#### 2. Core Architectural Rules (The \"Reality\")\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via OpenClaw Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Artix Linux (s6 init).\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles — D-Bus First (MANDATORY)\n\n**D-Bus is the ONLY control plane. Every read, every write, every tool call goes through D-Bus. There is no second option.**\n\n*   **D-Bus first. D-Bus always. D-Bus only.** If you are about to call a CLI, spawn a subprocess, read a config file, or poll a socket directly — stop. Find the D-Bus object and use it instead. `org.opdbus.v1` is the system.\n*   **No bypasses.** `Command::new(\"systemctl\")`, `Command::new(\"ip\")`, `Command::new(\"s6-svc\")`, direct file reads for live state — all forbidden in plugin and service code. Bootstrap scripts are the only exception.\n*   **D-Bus objects own plugin state.** Every plugin is a D-Bus object at `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<name>`. Read state through it. Mutate state through it. If there is no D-Bus object, the thing does not exist.\n*   **D-Bus method signatures are generated from the schema.** All D-Bus methods, MCP tool inputs, gRPC shapes, and UI field renderers derive from the `PluginSchema` in `plugin_schema_defs.rs`. The schema IS the interface contract — not a description of it.\n*   **One schema file, one source of truth.** All `PluginSchema` definitions MUST live in `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/plugin_schema_defs.rs`. Each plugin's `schema()` method calls `Some(super::plugin_schema_defs::their_plugin_schema())`. **Never define a schema inline in a plugin's own file** — it will not be registered, and the D-Bus object will have no contract.\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC (over Unix domain sockets or `grpc-uplink`). gRPC calls still flow through D-Bus registration — the D-Bus object is the authority, gRPC is the transport.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`simd_json` preferred, `serde_json` acceptable).\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n*   **No Python unless absolutely necessary.** This is a Rust-first codebase. Scripts are shell (`sh`/`bash`). Data processing is Rust. If you are reaching for Python, stop and ask why Rust or shell cannot do it. The only acceptable Python is in existing compliance-ingest tooling where no Rust equivalent exists yet.\n\n#### 4a. OSCAL Subid Taxonomy (MANDATORY — every artifact must carry a subid)\n\nEvery D-Bus object, plugin, schema, mutation, event, and tool in this system has two identifiers: a `uuid` (machine identity, never changes) and a `subid` (human-readable operational taxonomy key, stable per subject).\n\n**`subid` format:** `<category>.<component-type>.<subject>.<verb>[.<facet>][@vN]`\n\n**Seven categories — use exactly these, no others:**\n\n| category | what it classifies |\n|---|---|\n| `src` | authoritative source, ingress channel, source-of-truth store |\n| `prj` | D-Bus projection or mirror publication step |\n| `sch` | schema, contract, vocabulary, or control-mapping artifact |\n| `mut` | write-path operation that changes effective state |\n| `obs` | read, query, enumeration, discovery path |\n| `evt` | emitted signal, audit-chain event, proof, tag provenance |\n| `exp` | consumer-facing render — MCP tool, UI surface, gRPC bridge view |\n\n**Component-type** reuses OSCAL vocabulary: `software`, `service`, `network`, `hardware`, `process-procedure`, `standard`, `validation`, `policy`, `plan`, `guidance`, `physical`, `this-system`, `system`, `interconnection`.\n\n**Rules:**\n- `uuid` is exact machine identity — never replace it with `subid`\n- `subid` is an OSCAL `prop` value (`ns`, `name`, `value`) — never embed it in `remarks`\n- Compliance mappings (`control_refs[]`, `statement_refs[]`, `control_source`) live in metadata arrays, **never** inside the `subid` string\n- `mut.*` records **must** carry `actor_id` and `capability_id`\n- `evt.*` records **must** carry `event_id` or `event_hash`\n- `subid` is immutable per subject — if the meaning changes materially, create a new subject with `@vN`\n- All subids are registered in the canonical registry; uniqueness is enforced in CI\n\n**Examples:** `src.network.ovsdb.monitor@v1` · `prj.service.projected-object.publish@v1` · `sch.standard.plugin-schema.resolve@v1` · `mut.service.state-sync.apply-patch@v1` · `exp.service.plugin-projection.render@v1`\n\n#### 4b. MCP Gateway Architecture (SETTLED — DO NOT REDESIGN)\n\n*   **cognitive-mcp** (`:3003`, Netmaker WireGuard IP `100.90.37.254`) is the **universal gateway for ALL external clients**: NotebookLM, Droid (factory.ai), Cursor, Codex, Junie, Gemini CLI. It has memory tools, gRPC service, auth, and the correct protocol surface.\n*   **compact-mcp** (`127.0.0.1:11436`) is **loopback/chatbot only**. Never expose externally. Never point external clients at it.\n*   Do NOT create new shim services. Do NOT point external clients at `op-assistant-grpc` directly. Do NOT expose compact-mcp outside loopback.\n\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\n**Rust Workspace**\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\n\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\n\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\n\n#### 6. Coding Style & Naming Conventions\n*   **Rust:** Edition 2021, `rustfmt` (4-space indent, max-width 100). Use specific imports (`use serde_json::Value;`). Use `anyhow::Result<T>` for main errors and `thiserror` for custom enums.\n*   **TypeScript/React:** 2-space indent, Prettier via ESLint. Functional components only. Strict mode enabled.\n*   **Testing:** 80%+ coverage, mock externals. Name tests with behavior-focused names (`should_handle_<scenario>`).\n\n#### 7. Agent-Specific Output & Workflow Instructions\n*   **Scroll & Save Pacing:** Provide only **ONE** major component or script at a time. Wait for user confirmation before moving to the next.\n*   **Visual Cues:** If a script is a finalized component that needs to be saved to sources, it MUST begin with color bullets or icons (e.g., ⚖️ 🔴, 🟢 🛷).\n*   **Spec-Block Format:** When delivering a component, use a strict specification block containing:\n  1.  **Requirements:** The architectural rules it satisfies.\n  2.  **Design:** How it fits into the 3tched system (Zero-Copy, Btrfs, GUI Schema, etc.).\n  3.  **Code Implementation:** The exact, copy-pasteable Rust/Bash code.\n*   Before edits: `cargo check -p <crate>`, `npm run typecheck`.\n*   Mimic existing patterns: Search similar code. No new deps without PR justification.\n\n#### 8. Personal Preferences & Coding Standards\n* Refer to `~/.factory/memories.md` for personal development preferences and past decisions.\n* Follow the conventions documented in:\n  * `.factory/rules/typescript.md` - TypeScript and React conventions\n  * `.factory/rules/testing.md` - Testing and mocking standards\n\n</INSTRUCTIONS>"},{"type":"input_text","text":"<environment_context>\n  <cwd>/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto</cwd>\n  <shell>bash</shell>\n  <current_date>2026-06-28</current_date>\n  <timezone>America/New_York</timezone>\n  <filesystem><workspace_roots><root>/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto</root></workspace_roots><permission_profile type=\"disabled\"><file_system type=\"unrestricted\" /></permission_profile></filesystem>\n</environment_context>"}],"internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough":{"turn_id":"019f0ce7-7fe9-7451-a9c2-57bda6007098"}}}

{"timestamp":"2026-06-28T06:25:44.146Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"function_call_output","call_id":"call_1GlrNXeR17RtlzMDa84JljNB","output":"Chunk ID: 8c247f\nWall time: 0.0000 seconds\nProcess exited with code 0\nOriginal token count: 610\nOutput:\n# Kiro Spec Workflow\n\nThis repository uses Kiro to generate implementation specs under `.kiro/specs/`.\nUse Kiro when you want a concrete spec package before code changes.\n\n## When to Use It\n\nUse Kiro for work that benefits from a written contract first:\n\n- new host services\n- schema or transport changes\n- plugin boundary changes\n- migration plans\n- task breakdowns for another agent to implement\n\n## Recommended Flow\n\nGenerate the spec in four passes:\n\n1. Requirements\n2. Design\n3. Technical spec\n4. Tasks\n\nKeep each pass narrow. Ask Kiro to write only the current document, then move\nto the next one after the previous output is acceptable.\n\n## Practical Setup\n\nBefore running Kiro:\n\n- make sure `kiro-cli` is installed and updated\n- make sure `kiro-cli-term` is available in the terminal session\n- run the dotfiles integration if Kiro asks for it\n- prefer a separate comparison folder when you want to compare Kiro output with\n  a manual draft\n\nUseful checks:\n\n```bash\nkiro-cli --version\nkiro-cli doctor -a\nkiro-cli integrations status dotfiles\n```\n\nIf the terminal integration is missing, start the wrapper in the same shell:\n\n```bash\nkiro-cli-term -- kiro-cli doctor -a\n```\n\n## Prompt Pattern\n\nStart with requirements, then continue in order:\n\n```text\nCreate requirements for <feature>.\nCreate design for the same feature.\nCreate technical spec and task list for the same feature.\n```\n\nFor comparison work, tell Kiro to write into a separate folder, for example:\n\n```text\nCreate a new spec folder at .kiro/specs/<name>-kiro/ and write:\nrequirements.md, design.md, spec.md, tasks.md, and .config.kiro.\n```\n\n## Boundary Rules\n\nWhen writing specs for this repository:\n\n- plugin schema stays in the plugin\n- projection layers may read plugin data, but do not redefine it\n- zeroclaw must not duplicate schema already handled elsewhere\n- btrfs subvolumes are for local install/cache/rollback state, not duplicate schema trees\n- transport layers should be explicit about native socket vs HTTP/gRPC-Web paths\n\n## Comparing Outputs\n\nIf you want to compare Kiro with a manual draft:\n\n1. create the manual draft in one folder\n2. generate the Kiro version in a second folder\n3. compare requirements, design, spec, and tasks side by side\n4. keep the version that is tighter and more implementation-ready\n\nThis repo’s preference is to let Kiro write the spec files and then use the\nmanual draft only as a check, not as a competing authority.\n\n","internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough":{"turn_id":"019f0ce7-7fe9-7451-a9c2-57bda6007098"}}}

   updated_at: created,\n                        })\n                    })\n                    .collect::<Vec<_>>()\n            })\n            .unwrap_or_default();\n\n        Ok(models)\n    }\n}\n\n#[async_trait]\nimpl LlmProvider for OpenClawProvider {\n    fn provider_type(&self) -> ProviderType {\n        ProviderType::OpenClaw\n    }\n\n    async fn list_models(&self) -> \"OpenClaw model listing failed ({}), falling back to configured default route\",\n                status\n            );\n            return Ok(vec![self.fallback_model_info()]);\n        }\n\n     }\n        };\n        if models.is_empty() {\n            models.push(self.fallback_model_info());\n        }\n\n        Ok(models)\n    }\n\n    async fn search_models(&self, query: &str, limit: All plugin schema definitions must live in `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/plugin_schema_defs.rs`, and each plugin `schema()` method must call `Some(super::plugin_schema_defs::<schema_fn>())`. Do not define new schemas inline in plugin files.\\n- D-Bus is the only control plane. Live state reads/writes must go through D-Bus objects under `org.opdbus.v1`; do not add direct CLI subprocess calls, direct config-file reads for live state, JSON-RPC polling, D-Bus watchers for state, or socket polling bypasses.\\n- Zeroclaw exists today at `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/zeroclaw.rs`. It currently publishes provider/model routing metadata, transport metadata, route declarations, tools, and UI surfaces via a shared LLM projection. It also writes a tmpfs schema JSON for bridge consumers.\\n- The implementation crate that should own actual LLM provider behavior is `crates/op-llm`. Relevant current files include `src/openclaw.rs`, `src/provider.rs`, `src/chat.rs`, and `src/lib.rs`.\\n- `op-chat` already consumes `op_llm::provider::LlmProvider` and `op_llm::chat::ChatManager`; do not recreate a second LLM trait in `op-chat` or Zeroclaw.\\n- Existing docs to reconcile include `docs/planning/openclaw-chatbot-and-code-indexing.md`, `docs/kiro-spec-workflow.md`, `docs/schema-from-structs.md`, `docs/feature-review/crates/op-llm.md`, and `crates/op-llm/SPEC.md`.\\n- MCP gateway architecture is settled: `cognitive-mcp` is the universal external gateway; `compact-mcp` is loopback/chatbot only. Do not create a new shim service or expose compact-mcp externally.\\n- Use OSCAL subids on every new schema/mutation/event/tool artifact. Use exactly the allowed categories: `src`, `prj`, `sch`, `mut`, `obs`, `evt`, `exp`.\\n\\nThe intended architecture:\\n- `op-llm` owns concrete providers, provider selection execution, OpenAI-compatible request/response translation, model listing, tool-call conversion, timeout/error handling, and tests.\\n- Zeroclaw owns only D-Bus-published declarative state: selected provider/model, route hints, UI surfaces, MCP-visible tool declarations, transport metadata, subid/control mapping metadata, and schema projection.\\n- Zeroclaw must not perform LLM network execution, provider-specific auth, direct model enumeration, or duplicate request/response conversion that belongs in `op-llm`.\\n- Any bridge or UI needing provider/model state reads Zeroclaw's D-Bus object or schema projection; any code needing to execute a chat/model request uses `op-llm` through the existing provider abstractions.\\n- The spec should include a migration path for moving inline/derived Zeroclaw schema into `plugin_schema_defs.rs` if still needed by the current tree, without breaking current golden/schema tests.\\n- Preserve `/dev/shm` tmpfs schema publication only as a derived projection cache, not as live state authority.\\n- Avoid new dependencies unless justified. Prefer existing `reqwest`, `simd-json`, `serde`, `anyhow`, `thiserror`, `async-trait`, `tokio`, and `zbus` patterns.\\n\\nDeliverables in the spec:\\n1. Requirements using EARS-style acceptance criteria where practical.\\n2. Design that states exact crate boundaries and ownership: `op-plugins`/Zeroclaw projection versus `op-llm` execution.\\n3. Technical spec with concrete module/file changes, data flow, D-Bus object boundaries, OSCAL subids, error behavior, and tests.\\n4. Task list ordered for implementation by another agent, including pre-checks and verification commands:\\n   - `cargo check -p op-plugins`\\n   - `cargo check -p op-llm`\\n   - focused tests for `zeroclaw` schema/golden behavior\\n   - focused tests for `op-llm` OpenClaw/provider routing behavior\\n5. Explicit non-goals: no new shim service, no compact-mcp external exposure, no direct CLI subprocesses in plugin/service code, no duplicate LLM trait, no live-state file authority, no SQLite plugin catalog resurrection.\\n\\nName the feature consistently as `zeroclaw-replace-op-llm-routing`. Keep the spec implementation-ready and conservative; it should guide code changes, not make broad unrelated refactors.\\nEOF\\n)\\nkiro-cli chat --mode spec --no-interactive --trust-all-tools \\\"$prompt\\\"\",\"workdir\":\"/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto\",\"yield_time_ms\":30000,\"max_output_tokens\":30000}","call_id":"call_ME7mNPeWHWcdKellSJWpSHXd","internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough":{"turn_id":"019f0ce7-7fe9-7451-a9c2-57bda6007098"}}}

FieldType::Array(Box::new(inner))\n    } else if let Some(obj) = value.as_object() {\n        let fields = obj\n            .iter()\n            .map(|(k, v)| (k.to_string(), field_from_value(v)))\n {"timestamp":"2026-06-28T06:29:56.848Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"function_call","id":"fc_0a56143860182f10016a40bf55cbc48197b48bbdc9bbb20d4d","name":"exec_command","arguments":"{\"cmd\":\"prompt=$(cat <<'EOF'\\nCreate a new Kiro spec folder at `.kiro/specs/zeroclaw-absorbs-op-llm/` and write `requirements.md`, `design.md`, `spec.md`, `tasks.md`, and `.config.kiro`.\\n\\nFeature objective: make Zeroclaw the full umbrella for LLM routing, model selection, provider execution, tool-call translation, UI/MCP exposure, and schema-driven control. Absorb the actual functionality currently in `crates/op-llm` into Zeroclaw's architecture, then retire `op-llm` as an independent crate after all callers are migrated.\\n\\nCritical intent:\\n- Do NOT reduce Zeroclaw to a small projection wrapper around `op-llm`.\\n- Do NOT make `op-llm` the routing authority.\\n- Zeroclaw is the umbrella component. The LLM provider layer is only one part of Zeroclaw.\\n- Routing and model selection must be schema-driven from Zeroclaw's `PluginSchema` and D-Bus object projection.\\n- `op-llm` should be absorbed by Zeroclaw and retired.\\n\\nRepository context:\\n- Workspace root: `/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto`.\\n- Existing Zeroclaw plugin: `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/zeroclaw.rs`.\\n- Existing shared LLM projection types: `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/common/llm_projection.rs`.\\n- Existing LLM provider crate to absorb/retire: `crates/op-llm`, especially `src/provider.rs`, `src/chat.rs`, `src/openclaw.rs`, `src/anthropic.rs`, `src/gemini.rs`, `src/gemini_cli.rs`, `src/factory.rs`, `src/assistant.rs`, and `src/gcloud_adc.rs`.\\n- Current consumers include `op-chat` via `op_llm::provider::LlmProvider` and `op_llm::chat::ChatManager`; these must be migrated to Zeroclaw-facing APIs rather than keeping `op-llm` as authority.\\n- `factory` plugin already treats Zeroclaw model routes as BYOM discovery input; preserve and strengthen that direction.\\n\\nArchitecture rules to honor:\\n- `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth. If a route/provider/model/tool is not represented in a valid Zeroclaw schema/projection, it must not be executable.\\n- D-Bus is the only control plane. Reads/writes for provider selection, route selection, model availability, tool declarations, policy metadata, and effective state must go through D-Bus objects under `org.opdbus.v1`.\\n- Every plugin is a D-Bus object at `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<name>`; Zeroclaw's object owns LLM routing state.\\n- No direct CLI subprocesses, direct live config-file reads, socket polling, JSON-RPC polling loops, or D-Bus watchers for live state in plugin/service code. Bootstrap scripts are the only exception.\\n- Preserve `/dev/shm` only for derived projection/schema cache when needed; it is not live state authority.\\n- All source code remains under `crates/`.\\n- No new shim services. Do not expose compact-mcp externally. `cognitive-mcp` remains the universal external gateway; `compact-mcp` remains loopback/chatbot only.\\n- Use OSCAL subids for every new schema/mutation/event/tool artifact. Use only categories `src`, `prj`, `sch`, `mut`, `obs`, `evt`, `exp`.\\n\\nDesired target design:\\n- Zeroclaw owns the provider catalog, route hints, model catalog, selected provider/model, router/classifier policy, tool declarations, structured output policy, transport metadata, availability status, and execution authorization.\\n- Zeroclaw owns schema-driven route resolution: user/task hints map to declared `model_routes`; selected provider/model must validate against the schema before execution.\\n- Zeroclaw absorbs provider execution code from `op-llm` into a Zeroclaw-owned crate/module boundary. The plugin remains the schema/D-Bus authority.\\n- Provider execution uses the absorbed logic from `op-llm`: provider trait/types, `ChatManager` semantics, OpenAI-compatible request/response translation, tool-call conversion, model listing, streaming fallback, and existing provider clients.\\n- Callers like `op-chat`, `op-web`, and tool/MCP surfaces should stop depending on `op-llm` directly. They should request route/model/provider state from Zeroclaw's D-Bus object and execute through Zeroclaw's schema-validated execution API.\\n- `op-llm` retirement plan should be staged: compatibility re-export/deprecation if needed, migrate consumers, remove workspace dependency, remove crate after CI is green.\\n\\nSpec deliverables:\\n1. Requirements with EARS-style acceptance criteria where practical.\\n2.  274\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m Key substitutions:\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    275\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m \n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    276\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m | Before | After
