3.3 ZeroclawState snapshot acquisition in op-chat\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    284\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m \n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    285\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m `op-chat`'s chat actor reads the current `ZeroclawState` snapshot via zbus at\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    286\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m startup and after any `ZeroclawPlugin` state-change signal. It passes the\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    287\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m snapshot to `ZeroclawExecutor::new()` / `update_state()`. The D-Bus read is\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    288\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m scoped to `op-chat`'s actor initialization — not inside the hot path.\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    289\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m \n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    290\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m Pattern:\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    291\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m ```rust\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    292\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m // In op-chat actor init:\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    293\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m let proxy = ZeroclawProxy::new(&conn).await?;\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    294\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m let state_json = proxy.state_snapshot().await?;\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    295\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m let zeroclaw_state: ZeroclawState = serde_json::from_str(&state_json)?;\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    296\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m let executor = ZeroclawExecutor::new(zeroclaw_state);\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    297\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m \n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    298\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m // In chat request handler:\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    299\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m let hint = derive_hint_from_context(&ctx);  // \"code\", \"fast\", \"local\", \"auto\"\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    300\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m let response = executor.execute(&hint, request).await?;\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    301\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m ```\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    302\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m \n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    303\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m ---\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    304\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m \n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    305\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m ## 4. op-llm Shim (Stage 1)\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    306\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m \n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    307\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m Replace `crates/op-llm/src/lib.rs` contents with:\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    308\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m \n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    309\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m ```rust\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    310\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m //! op-llm — DEPRECATED shim. All types have moved to op-zeroclaw.\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    311\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m //! This crate exists only for backward-compat during migration.\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    312\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m //! Remove this crate after all callers are migrated (Stage 4).\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    313\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m #![deprecated(note = \"Use op-zeroclaw directly. op-llm will be removed.\")]\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    314\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m \n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    315\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m pub use op_zeroclaw::*;\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    316\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m ```\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    317\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m \n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    318\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m `op-llm/Cargo.toml` adds:\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    319\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m ```toml\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    320\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m op-zeroclaw = { path = \"../op-zeroclaw\" }\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    321\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m ```\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    322\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m \n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    323\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m All other `op-llm` module files can be removed or #[cfg(any())] gated after the\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    324\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m shim is proven.\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    325\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m \n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    326\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m ---\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    327\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m \n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    328\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m ## 5. Schema Validation Points\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    329\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m \n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    330\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m Route validation is enforced at the following points. Each check is a hard gate\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    331\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m that returns `ZeroclawError` before any network call:\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    332\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m \n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    333\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m | Point | Check | Error |\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    334\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m |---|---|---|\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    335\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m | `RouteResolver::resolve` entry | hint present in model_routes | `RouteNotFound` |\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    336\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m | `RouteResolver::resolve` post-match | `route.available || !policy.require_available` | `RouteUnavailable` |\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    337\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m | `ZeroclawExecutor::execute` pre-dispatch | provider_id in provider catalog | `ProviderNotInCatalog` |\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    338\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m | D-Bus `SetProvider` handler | provider_id in provider catalog | D-Bus error reply |\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    339\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m | D-Bus `ProjectRoute` handler | hint matches at least one declared route | D-Bus error reply |\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    340\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m \n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    341\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m ---\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    342\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m \n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    343\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m ## 6. Error Behavior\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    344\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m \n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    345\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m - `RouteNotFound` — returned to caller as-is; logged at WARN level with hint name.\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    346\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m - `RouteUnavailable` — returned to caller; logged at INFO with `status_reason`.\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    347\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m - `ProviderNotInCatalog` — returned to caller; logged at ERROR (indicates schema/state inconsistency).\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    348\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m - `ProviderError` — wraps the underlying `anyhow::Error`; logged at ERROR with provider name and model.\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    349\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m - All errors carry enough context for the caller to produce a user-facing message without inspecting internals.\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    350\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m \n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    351\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m ---\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    352\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m \n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    353\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m ## 7. OSCAL Subid Registration\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    354\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m \n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    355\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m All new subids listed in Design §5 must be added to\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    356\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m `op-plugins/src/state_plugins/oscal_subid_registry.rs` under their respective\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    357\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m categories. The CI subid uniqueness check will enforce this.\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    358\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m \n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    359\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m ---\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    360\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m \n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    361\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m ## 8. `/dev/shm` Contract (unchanged)\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    362\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m \n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    363\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m `/dev/shm/opdbus/schemas/zeroclaw.json` is written only by\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    364\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m `ZeroclawPlugin::write_schema_file_to()` and read by `op-grpc-bridge`. Ownership Boundaries\n\n```\n┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│  ZEROCLAW UMBRELLA                                                          │\n│                                                                             │\n│  ┌──────────────────────────────┐   ┌─────────────────────────────────┐    │\n│  │  op-plugins / zeroclaw.rs    │   │  crates/op-zeroclaw             │    │\n│  │  ─────────────────────────── │   │  ──────────────────────────────  │    │\n│  │  ZeroclawState (schema)      │◄──│  ZeroclawExecutor               │    │\n│  │  PluginSchema (D-Bus contract)│  │  ChatManager                    │    │\n│  │  StatePlugin impl            │   │  LlmProvider trait + types      │    │\n│  │  D-Bus object authority      │   │  Provider clients (all absorbed  │    │\n│  │  write_schema_file_to /shm   │   │    from op-llm)                 │    │\n│  │  OSCAL subid registry        │   │  RouteResolver                  │    │\n│  └──────────────────────────────┘   └─────────────────────────────────┘    │\n│            ▲  D-Bus R/W                          ▲                         │\n│            │                                     │ dep                     │\n│  ┌─────────┴──────────────────────────────────── ┤                         │\n│  │  D-Bus Control Plane  (/org/opdbus/v1/...)    │                         │\n│  │  Methods: SetProvider, SetModel,              │                         │\n│  │           ProjectRoute, GetModelRoutes,       │                         │\n│  │           Execute, GetTools                   │                         │\n│  └───────────────────────────────────────────────┘                         │\n└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n\nCALLERS (read schema / call Execute via D-Bus or in-process via op-zeroclaw API)\n\n  op-chat  ──────► ZeroclawExecutor::execute(route_hint, request)\n  op-web   ──────► (via op-chat or op-grpc-bridge)\n  cognitive-mcp ─► ZeroclawState.tools (via D-Bus GetTools)\n  compact-mcp ──► ZeroclawExecutor (loopback only)\n  factory plugin ► D-Bus GetModelRoutes() for BYOM discovery\n\nRETIRED (after Stage 4)\n\n  op-llm   ──────► REMOVED from workspace\n```\n\n---\n\n## 2. Component Responsibilities\n\n### 2a. `op-plugins/src/state_plugins/zeroclaw.rs` — Schema + D-Bus Authority\n\nOwns:\n- `ZeroclawState` struct: the authoritative shape of all Zeroclaw state.\n- `LlmTransport`, `ZeroclawPlugin` (StatePlugin impl).\n- `zeroclaw_schema()` — canonical `PluginSchema` derived via schemars.\n- `write_schema_file_to()` — the only writer to `/dev/shm/opdbus/schemas/zeroclaw.json`.\n- D-Bus object registration under `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/zeroclaw`.\n- OSCAL subid metadata for every schema field.\n\nDoes NOT own:\n- Provider client implementations.\n- HTTP request dispatch.\n- Model listing against live endpoints.\n\nNew additions to this file (schema only, no execution logic):\n- `provider_catalog_schema` field already exists via `LlmProjection.providers`.\n- New `execution_policy` sub-struct: `require_schema_validation: bool`,\n  `allow_undeclared_routes: bool` (defaults: `true`, `false`).\n- New D-Bus methods defined in schema as LlmTool entries:\n  - `zeroclaw.route.set_provider` — mut subid\n  - `zeroclaw.route.set_model` — mut subid\n  - `zeroclaw.route.project_availability` — mut subid\n\n### 2b. `crates/op-zeroclaw/` — Execution Crate (new)\n\nStructure:\n```\ncrates/op-zeroclaw/\n  Cargo.toml\n  src/\n    lib.rs           — public API: ZeroclawExecutor, re-exports\n    executor.rs      — ZeroclawExecutor: route resolution + dispatch\n    route_resolver.rs — RouteResolver: schema-validated hint → ModelRoute\n    provider.rs      — LlmProvider trait, types (moved from op-llm)\n    chat.rs          — ChatManager (moved from op-llm, adapted)\n    providers/\n      mod.rs\n      openclaw.rs\n      anthropic.rs\n      gemini.rs\n      gemini_cli.rs\n      factory.rs\n      assistant.rs\n      gcloud_adc.rs\n      antigravity.rs\n      antigravity_replay.rs\n      huggingface.rs\n      perplexity.rs\n      headless_oauth.rs\n      pty_bridge.rs\n  tests/\n    route_resolution.rs\n    provider_tool_calls.rs\n    schema_validation.rs\n```\n\n`ZeroclawExecutor` is the single public entry point for execution callers. It:\n1. Holds a reference to the current `ZeroclawState` snapshot (read from D-Bus\n   or passed in for tests).\n2. Calls `RouteResolver::resolve(hint, state)` to get a validated `ModelRoute`.\n3. Instantiates (or caches) the provider client for that route.\n4. Dispatches `LlmProvider::chat_with_request()`.\n5. Returns `ChatResponse` or a typed `ZeroclawError`.\n\n### 2c. D-Bus Projection Layer\n\nThe D-Bus object at `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/zeroclaw` is the control-plane\nauthority. It exposes:\n\n```\ninterface org.opdbus.v1.Plugin.Zeroclaw {\n    // Properties (read)\n    readonly property string   SelectedProvider\n    readonly property string   SelectedModel\n    readonly property string   Status\n    readonly property string[] AvailableHints\n\n    // Mutations (write, require actor_id + capability_id)\n    method SetProvider(provider_id: string, actor_id: string, capability_id: string) -> bool\n    method SetModel(model_id: string, actor_id: string, capability_id: string) -> bool\n    method ProjectRoute(hint: string, available: bool, reason: string, actor_id: string, capability_id: string) -> bool\n\n    // Query\n    method GetModelRoutes() -> array<struct ModelRoute>\n    method GetTools() -> array<struct LlmTool>\n    method GetProviderCatalog() -> array<struct Provider>\n\n    // Execution authorization gate (returns token callers must pass to Execute)\n    method AuthorizeExecution(hint: string, actor_id: string) -> string  // exec_token\n\n    // Signals\n    signal ProviderSelected(provider_id: string, actor_id: string)\n    signal ModelSelected(model_id: string, actor_id: string)\n    signal RouteProjected(hint: string, available: bool, reason: string)\n}\n```\n\n### 2d. `op-chat` Migration\n\n`op-chat` currently holds `op-llm` as a direct dependency and uses:\n- `op_llm::provider::{LlmProvider, ChatMessage, ChatRequest, ChatResponse, ...}`\n- `op_llm::chat::ChatManager`\n\nAfter migration:\n- Replace `op-llm = { path = \"../op-llm\" }` in `op-chat/Cargo.toml` with\n  `op-zeroclaw = { path = \"../op-zeroclaw\" }`.\n- Replace `use op_llm::...` imports with `use op_zeroclaw::...`.\n- Replace `ChatManager::new()` instantiation with `ZeroclawExecutor::new(state)`.\n- The chat actor passes a hint (derived from its routing context) to\n  `ZeroclawExecutor::execute(hint, request)` instead of picking a provider\n  itself.\n\n### 2e. factory BYOM Discovery\n\nThe `factory` plugin in `op-plugins` calls `GetModelRoutes()` on the Zeroclaw\nD-Bus object instead of importing `op-llm` types. The returned `ModelRoute`\nslice is the BYOM catalog. No code change is needed in `factory.rs` beyond\nreplacing any `op-llm` import with an `op-zeroclaw` import or a D-Bus call.\n\n### 2f. cognitive-mcp and compact-mcp\n\n- `cognitive-mcp` reads `GetTools()` from Zeroclaw's D-Bus object to populate\n  its MCP tool catalog. No `op-llm` dependency needed.\n- `compact-mcp` uses `ZeroclawExecutor` for in-process execution; no external\n  binding change.\n\n---\n\n## 3. Route Resolution Algorithm\n\n```\nresolve(hint: &str, state: &ZeroclawState) -> Result<&ModelRoute, ZeroclawError>\n\n1. Normalize hint (lowercase, trim).\n2. Search state.projection.model_routes for entries where route.hint == hint.\n   If no match, return Err(RouteNotFound { hint }).\n3. From matching routes, prefer available == true. If none available,\n   check execution_policy.allow_undeclared_routes; if false return\n   Err(RouteUnavailable { hint, reason: route.status_reason }).\n4. If multiple available routes match the same hint, prefer the route whose\n   provider matches state.selected_provider; otherwise take the first.\n5. Return the resolved &ModelRoute.\n```\n\nThis resolution is pure and deterministic — no env-vars, no file reads.\n\n---\n\n## 4. Data Flow\n\n```\nop-chat / op-web / MCP surface\n    │\n    │ chat_request + hint (\"code\" | \"fast\" | \"local\" | ...)\n    ▼\nZeroclawExecutor::execute(hint, ChatRequest)\n    │\n    ├── RouteResolver::resolve(hint, zeroclaw_state_snapshot)\n    │       └── validates against ZeroclawState.projection.model_routes\n    │           returns ModelRoute { provider, model, transport, available }\n    │\n    ├── if !route.available && !force → Err(RouteUnavailable)\n    │\n    ├── provider_client = ProviderRegistry::get_or_create(route.provider, config)\n    │       (config sourced from ZeroclawState / env bootstrap only)\n    │\n    └── provider_client.chat_with_request(route.model, request)\n            └── returns ChatResponse\n```\n\n---\n\n## 5. OSCAL Subid Inventory (new artifacts)\n\n| subid | what |\n|---|---|\n| `sch.software.zeroclaw-execution-policy.schema@v1` | execution_policy sub-struct in ZeroclawState |\n| `mut.service.zeroclaw.set-provider@v1` | SetProvider D-Bus method |\n| `mut.service.zeroclaw.set-model@v1` | SetModel D-Bus method |\n| `mut.service.zeroclaw.project-route@v1` | ProjectRoute D-Bus method |\n| `obs.service.zeroclaw.get-model-routes@v1` | GetModelRoutes D-Bus query |\n| `obs.service.zeroclaw.get-tools@v1` | GetTools D-Bus query |\n| `exp.service.zeroclaw.authorize-execution@v1` | AuthorizeExecution gate |\n| `evt.service.zeroclaw.provider-selected@v1` | ProviderSelected signal |\n| `evt.service.zeroclaw.model-selected@v1` | ModelSelected signal |\n| `evt.service.zeroclaw.route-projected@v1` | RouteProjected signal |\n| `src.software.op-zeroclaw.provider-catalog@v1` | op-zeroclaw ProviderRegistry source |\n| `exp.service.zeroclaw-executor.execute@v1` | ZeroclawExecutor::execute() |\n\n---\n\n## 6. op-llm Retirement Stages\n\n| Stage | Actions | CI Gate |\n|---|---|---|\n| 1 — shim | `op-llm/src/lib.rs` becomes `pub use op_zeroclaw::*;`. All types re-exported. | `cargo build --workspace` green |\n| 2 — migrate | Update all callers: replace `op-llm` dep with `op-zeroclaw` in Cargo.toml, replace `op_llm::` use paths | `cargo check -p op-chat`, `cargo check -p op-web` green |\n| 3 — remove dep | Remove `op-llm` from all callers' Cargo.toml | `cargo build --workspace` green, no `op-llm` in dep trees |\n| 4 — retire | Remove `crates/op-llm/` from workspace, remove from `Cargo.toml` members | All workspace tests pass |\n\n---\n\n## 7. Constraints Preserved\n\n- `/dev/shm/opdbus/schemas/zeroclaw.json` written only by `ZeroclawPlugin::write_schema_file_to()`, read by `op-grpc-bridge`. Never used as live-state authority.\n- No Python introduced.\n- `cognitive-mcp` remains the universal external gateway; `compact-mcp` remains loopback only.\n- No new MCP shim service.\n- All source under `crates/`.\n- `PluginSchema` in `plugin_schema_defs.rs` pattern preserved — `zeroclaw_schema()` calls the schemars adapter; no inline schema definition.\n","internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough":{"turn_id":"019f0ceb-0ab9-7d90-bcff-8bfe5c9a7c04"}}}

{"timestamp":"2026-06-28T06:38:12.735Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"custom_tool_call","id":"ctc_01796fb848b24a06016a40c142954c81978301f2a56b36d03a","status":"completed","call_id":"call_aB0ZKAKk9YM4gIOoEYHUN4Gp","name":"apply_patch","input":"*** Begin Patch\n*** Add File: .kiro/specs/zeroclaw-absorbs-op-llm/architecture-correction.md\n+# Architecture Correction — Dynamic Zeroclaw Router\n+\n+This correction supersedes any earlier wording in this spec that proposes a\n+separate static `op-zeroclaw` crate or a fixed executor boundary.\n+\n+## Correct Target\n+\n+Zeroclaw is a dynamic schema-driven runtime. It absorbs `op-llm` functionality\n+into the existing Zeroclaw umbrella and retires `op-llm`, but it does not create\n+a new static Zeroclaw crate as the authority.\n+\n+The authority remains:\n+\n+- Zeroclaw `PluginSchema`\n+- Zeroclaw D-Bus object at `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/zeroclaw`\n+- Zeroclaw dynamic route/model/provider projection\n+\n+Provider execution code may be moved into a Zeroclaw-owned module boundary, but\n+route choice, model choice, availability, cost policy, and effort policy are\n+runtime data declared through Zeroclaw schema and read through D-Bus.\n+\n+## Automatic Model Selection\n+\n+Zeroclaw must automatically select a model for each request using schema-declared\n+policy inputs:\n+\n+- task class: `chat`, `code`, `reasoning`, `tool`, `vision`, `compliance`\n+- effort: `low`, `medium`, `high`, `max`\n+- cost ceiling: maximum cost per request or token budget\n+- latency target: interactive, background, batch\n+- context requirement: short, long, repository-aware, tool-heavy\n+- privacy/compliance tier: local-only, trusted gateway, external allowed\n+- route availability and health\n+- selected provider/model overrides, when explicitly set by D-Bus mutation\n+\n+The model selector must reject undeclared routes. If a model is not declared in\n+Zeroclaw schema, it does not exist for execution.\n+\n+## Schema Additions\n+\n+Add or extend Zeroclaw schema fields for:\n+\n+- `selection_policy`\n+- `model_routes[].cost`\n+- `model_routes[].effort`\n+- `model_routes[].latency_class`\n+- `model_routes[].context_window`\n+- `model_routes[].privacy_tier`\n+- `model_routes[].health`\n+- `model_routes[].priority`\n+- `model_routes[].fallbacks`\n+\n+Every new artifact must carry OSCAL subids.\n+\n+Suggested subids:\n+\n+- `sch.software.zeroclaw-selection-policy.schema@v1`\n+- `mut.service.zeroclaw-selection-policy.effort@v1`\n+- `mut.service.zeroclaw-selection-policy.cost-ceiling@v1`\n+- `obs.software.zeroclaw-model-route.cost@v1`\n+- `obs.software.zeroclaw-model-route.effort@v1`\n+- `obs.software.zeroclaw-model-route.latency-class@v1`\n+- `obs.software.zeroclaw-model-route.health@v1`\n+- `exp.service.zeroclaw-model-selector.select@v1`\n+\n+## Selection Algorithm\n+\n+For each request:\n+\n+1. Read current Zeroclaw state through D-Bus.\n+2. Normalize request metadata into a `SelectionRequest`:\n+   `task_class`, `effort`, `cost_ceiling`, `latency_target`,\n+   `privacy_tier`, `requires_tools`, and optional explicit provider/model.\n+3. Filter `model_routes` to declared, available routes matching task class.\n+4. Apply hard constraints:\n+   privacy tier, explicit overrides, tool support, context window, cost ceiling.\n+5. Score remaining routes:\n+   lower cost for same capability wins; higher effort allows higher quality and\n+   higher cost; lower latency wins for interactive requests; healthier routes\n+   win over degraded routes.\n+6. Select the highest scoring route.\n+7. Emit a selection event containing selected provider/model, score inputs,\n+   cost estimate, effort level, and fallback chain.\n+8. Execute through the absorbed provider adapter only after selection succeeds.\n+\n+## Non-Negotiable Constraints\n+\n+- No separate static `op-zeroclaw` crate as the new authority.\n+- No static hardcoded model picker.\n+- No caller selects provider/model directly except through a Zeroclaw D-Bus\n+  mutation or request metadata.\n+- No execution of undeclared models.\n+- `op-llm` is retired only after its provider adapters are absorbed behind the\n+  dynamic Zeroclaw router.\n*** Update File: .kiro/specs/zeroclaw-absorbs-op-llm/requirements.md\n@@\n # Requirements — zeroclaw-absorbs-op-llm\n \n+> Correction: see `architecture-correction.md`. Zeroclaw is a dynamic\n+> schema-driven router, not a separate static `op-zeroclaw` crate. Automatic\n+> model selection by effort, cost, latency, task class, health, and privacy tier\n+> is now a first-class requirement and supersedes any static-executor wording\n+> below.\n+\n ## Feature Objective\n*** Update File: .kiro/specs/zeroclaw-absorbs-op-llm/design.md\n@@\n # Design — zeroclaw-absorbs-op-llm\n \n+> Correction: see `architecture-correction.md`. The final design must not create\n+> a separate static `op-zeroclaw` authority. Zeroclaw remains dynamic:\n+> `PluginSchema` + D-Bus state drive provider/model selection at runtime,\n+> including automatic model choice for effort and cost.\n+\n ## 1. Ownership Boundaries\n*** Update File: .kiro/specs/zeroclaw-absorbs-op-llm/spec.md\n@@\n # Technical Spec — zeroclaw-absorbs-op-llm\n \n+> Correction: see `architecture-correction.md`. Sections that propose a new\n+> static `crates/op-zeroclaw` crate are superseded. The implementation must\n+> absorb provider adapters behind Zeroclaw's existing dynamic schema/D-Bus\n+> routing surface and add automatic effort/cost-aware model selection.\n+\n ## 1. New Crate: `crates/op-zeroclaw`\n*** Update File: .kiro/specs/zeroclaw-absorbs-op-llm/tasks.md\n@@\n # Tasks — zeroclaw-absorbs-op-llm\n \n+> Correction: see `architecture-correction.md`. Do not execute tasks that create\n+> a separate static `op-zeroclaw` crate. Replace Phase 1 with dynamic Zeroclaw\n+> router work: extend the Zeroclaw schema, add effort/cost selection policy,\n+> absorb provider adapters behind the existing Zeroclaw D-Bus authority, then\n+> migrate callers away from `op-llm`.\n+\n Ordered for a single implementing agent. Each task includes a pre-check,\n*** End Patch\n","internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough":{"turn_id":"019f0cf1-911e-7e51-b048-ee28be640bcc"}}}

It keeps the branch green between phases.\n+- **Schema Agent**: extends Zeroclaw `PluginSchema`, `LlmProjection`,\n+  selection policy, OSCAL subids, and golden/schema tests.\n+- **D-Bus Agent**: implements Zeroclaw methods, properties, signals, mutation\n+  audit metadata, and route/query surfaces.\n+- **Provider Absorption Agent**: moves `op-llm` provider adapters behind\n+  Zeroclaw without changing behavior, then deletes duplicate authority.\n+- **Router Agent**: implements dynamic effort/cost/latency/privacy model\n+  selection using only schema/D-Bus state.\n+- **Caller Migration Agent**: migrates `op-chat`, `op-web`, MCP surfaces, and\n+  factory BYOM discovery away from direct `op-llm` usage.\n+- **Test Agent**: adds focused route-selection, provider-translation, D-Bus,\n+  schema, subid, and regression tests.\n+- **Review Agent**: performs code review for bypasses, stale `op-llm`\n+  authority, static model selection, direct live-state reads, and missing tests.\n+\n+Agents must coordinate through explicit handoff artifacts in the spec folder:\n+\n+- `handoff-schema.md`\n+- `handoff-dbus.md`\n+- `handoff-provider-absorption.md`\n+- `handoff-router.md`\n+- `handoff-callers.md`\n+- `handoff-tests.md`\n+- `handoff-review.md`\n+\n+Each handoff must include:\n+\n+1. Scope completed.\n+2. Files changed.\n+3. Contract changes.\n+4. Verification commands run.\n+5. Known risks or blocked items.\n+6. Next agent dependencies.\n+\n+The coordinator only advances to the next phase after the previous phase has\n+passed its local verification commands. Full workspace checks happen at phase\n+boundaries, not after every tiny edit.\n*** Update File: .kiro/specs/zeroclaw-absorbs-op-llm/tasks.md\n@@\n > Correction: see `architecture-correction.md`. {"timestamp":"2026-06-28T06:45:20.711Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"function_call","id":"fc_05f82baa0369715d016a40c2da09748190b304ce8ab413b814","name":"exec_command","arguments":"{\"cmd\":\"prompt=$(cat <<'EOF'\\nCreate a new Kiro spec folder at `.kiro/specs/zeroclaw-absorbs-op-llm/` and write exactly these files: `requirements.md`, `design.md`, `spec.md`, `tasks.md`, and `.config.kiro`.\\n\\nThis must be a pure Kiro-generated spec. Do not assume any prior files in that folder. The old folder was deleted because earlier output incorrectly proposed a separate static Zeroclaw crate.\\n\\nFeature name: `zeroclaw-absorbs-op-llm`.\\n\\nFinal objective:\\nZeroclaw is the dynamic umbrella for LLM routing, automatic model selection, provider execution, tool-call translation, UI/MCP exposure, and schema-driven control. Absorb the functionality currently in `crates/op-llm` into Zeroclaw's dynamic plugin/schema architecture, then retire `op-llm` as an independent crate after callers are migrated.\\n\\nCritical corrections and non-negotiables:\\n- Do NOT create a separate static `op-zeroclaw` crate.\\n- Do NOT make `op-llm` the authority.\\n- Do NOT reduce Zeroclaw to a wrapper around `op-llm`.\\n- Zeroclaw is dynamic. Provider/model routing, model selection, cost/effort policy, availability, tool declarations, and execution authorization are schema/D-Bus driven at runtime.\\n- `op-llm` should be absorbed by Zeroclaw and retired.\\n- This is a large refactor and must be executed as orchestrated multi-agent execution, not a single-agent linear refactor.\\n\\nMost important architecture rule to emphasize:\\n- The Zeroclaw plugin is the schema.\\n- The schema is the plugin.\\n- The plugin schema is the single source of truth for all calls.\\n- If provider/model/tool/route/capability is not in a valid Zeroclaw plugin schema projection, it does not exist and must not execute.\\n- All calls derive from plugin schema and D-Bus projection, not from hardcoded static Rust route tables.\\n- The monolithic all-plugin schema projection lives under `/dev/shm/opdbus/` as the all-plugins JSON artifact, and individual plugin schema projections live under `/dev/shm/opdbus/schemas/*` such as `/dev/shm/opdbus/schemas/zeroclaw.json`.\\n- `/dev/shm/opdbus/<monolithic-all-plugins>.json` is the derived all-plugin schema catalog used by consumers that need the full system contract.\\n- `/dev/shm/opdbus/schemas/*` contains derived individual plugin schema projections.\\n- These `/dev/shm` files are derived schema/projection artifacts, not alternate live-state authorities. The D-Bus object and PluginSchema remain authoritative.\\n- Zeroclaw owns its schema projection and is the writer for its individual schema projection. Consumers may read the projections but must not mutate them.\\n\\nRepository context:\\n- Workspace root: `/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto`.\\n- Existing Zeroclaw plugin: `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/zeroclaw.rs`.\\n- Existing shared LLM projection types: `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/common/llm_projection.rs`.\\n- Existing schema aggregator/re-export file: `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/plugin_schema_defs.rs`.\\n- Existing LLM provider crate to absorb/retire: `crates/op-llm`, especially `src/provider.rs`, `src/chat.rs`, `src/openclaw.rs`, `src/anthropic.rs`, `src/gemini.rs`, `src/gemini_cli.rs`, `src/factory.rs`, `src/assistant.rs`, and `src/gcloud_adc.rs`.\\n- Current consumers include `op-chat` via `op_llm::provider::LlmProvider` and `op_llm::chat::ChatManager`; these must be migrated to Zeroclaw schema/D-Bus driven APIs.\\n- `factory` plugin already treats Zeroclaw model routes as BYOM discovery input; preserve and strengthen that direction.\\n\\nArchitecture rules to honor:\\n- D-Bus is the only control plane. Reads/writes for provider selection, route selection, model availability, tool declarations, policy metadata, execution authorization, and effective state go through D-Bus objects under `org.opdbus.v1`.\\n- Every plugin is a D-Bus object at `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<name>`; Zeroclaw's object owns LLM routing state.\\n- No direct CLI subprocesses, direct live config-file reads, socket polling, JSON-RPC polling loops, or D-Bus watchers for live state in plugin/service code. Bootstrap scripts are the only exception.\\n- Preserve `/dev/shm` only for derived schema/projection cache and shared-memory schema transport; it is not a second live state authority.\\n- Source code remains under `crates/`.\\n- No new shim service. Do not expose compact-mcp externally. `cognitive-mcp` remains the universal external gateway; `compact-mcp` remains loopback/chatbot only.\\n- Use OSCAL subids for every new schema/mutation/event/tool artifact. Use only categories `src`, `prj`, `sch`, `mut`, `obs`, `evt`, `exp`.\\n- No Python for this refactor.\\n\\nDesired target design:\\n- Zeroclaw owns provider catalog, route hints, model catalog, selected provider/model, automatic model selector policy, router/classifier policy, tool declarations, structured output policy, transport metadata, availability/health status, cost metadata, effort metadata, fallback metadata, and execution authorization.\\n- Zeroclaw owns schema-driven route resolution: user/task hints map to declared `model_routes`; selected provider/model must validate against Zeroclaw schema before execution.\\n- Zeroclaw owns automatic model selection for effort and cost:\\n  - input metadata: task class, requested effort, cost ceiling, latency target, context requirement, privacy/compliance tier, tool needs, explicit overrides if authorized\\n  - hard filters: declared route only, availability, privacy tier, tool support, context window, cost ceiling\\n  - scoring: lower cost for equivalent capability, higher quality for higher effort, lower latency for interactive requests, route health, fallback chain\\n  - output: selected provider/model, reason, estimated cost, effort level, confidence/score, fallback route list, event metadata\\n- Automatic model selection must be dynamic and data-driven from Zeroclaw schema/D-Bus state, not hardcoded in static Rust match tables.\\n- Provider execution logic currently in `op-llm` should be absorbed into Zeroclaw-owned modules under the existing plugin/control-plane architecture. Do not introduce a new authority crate. If implementation needs module separation, keep it within existing crates and boundaries that preserve Zeroclaw plugin/D-Bus/schema authority.\\n- Callers like `op-chat`, `op-web`, MCP surfaces, and factory BYOM discovery must stop depending on `op-llm` as an independent authority. They should request route/model/provider state and execution authorization from Zeroclaw's schema/D-Bus surface.\\n- `op-llm` retirement plan should be staged: inventory consumers, absorb provider adapters, compatibility shim only if needed, migrate callers, remove workspace dependency, remove crate after CI is green.\\n\\nRefactor execution model:\\nThis refactor must be orchestrated as multi-agent execution. The spec must define a coordinator and focused implementation agents:\\n- Coordinator Agent: owns migration graph, sequencing, integration checkpoints, final acceptance, and keeps branch green.\\n- Schema Agent: extends Zeroclaw PluginSchema, LlmProjection, automatic selection policy, OSCAL subids, monolithic and individual `/dev/shm/opdbus` schema projection requirements, and golden/schema tests.\\n- D-Bus Agent: implements Zeroclaw methods/properties/signals, mutation audit metadata, schema query surfaces, route/query surfaces, and execution authorization.\\n- Provider Absorption Agent: moves or absorbs `op-llm` provider adapters behind Zeroclaw without behavior changes, then deletes duplicate authority.\\n- Router Agent: implements dynamic effort/cost/latency/privacy model selection using only Zeroclaw schema/D-Bus state.\\n- Caller Migration Agent: migrates `op-chat`, `op-web`, MCP surfaces, and factory BYOM discovery away from direct `op-llm` usage.\\n- Projection Agent: verifies monolithic all-plugin schema projection under `/dev/shm/opdbus/` and individual plugin projections under `/dev/shm/opdbus/schemas/*`, including Zeroclaw schema projection.\\n- Test Agent: adds route-selection, model-selection, provider-translation, D-Bus, schema, projection, subid, and regression tests.\\n- Review Agent: reviews for bypasses, stale `op-llm` authority, static model selection, direct live-state reads, missing tests, and `/dev/shm` misuse.\\n\\nThe spec must require handoff artifacts in the spec folder:\\n- `handoff-schema.md`\\n- `handoff-dbus.md`\\n- `handoff-provider-absorption.md`\\n- `handoff-router.md`\\n- `handoff-callers.md`\\n- `handoff-projection.md`\\n- `handoff-tests.md`\\n- `handoff-review.md`\\nEach handoff must include: scope completed, files changed, contract changes, verification commands run, known risks or blocked items, and next-agent dependencies.\\n\\nSpec deliverables:\\n1. `requirements.md` with EARS-style acceptance criteria where practical.\\n2. `design.md` with exact ownership boundaries, emphasizing that Zeroclaw plugin schema is the single source of truth for all calls and that `/dev/shm/opdbus/<monolithic-all-plugins>.json` plus `/dev/shm/opdbus/schemas/*` are derived schema projections.\\n3. `spec.md` with concrete file/module changes, dynamic automatic model selection algorithm, schema fields, D-Bus method/property/signal shape, `/dev/shm` projection contract, OSCAL subids, data flow, error behavior, op-llm absorption plan, compatibility/deprecation plan, and Automatic Model Selection Algorithm\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    114\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m \n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    115\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m Input (`SelectionInput`):\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    116\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m \n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    117\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m ```\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    118\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m task_class:          String         // \"code\", \"chat\", \"reasoning\", \"vision\", ...\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    119\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m requested_effort:    String         // \"low\", \"medium\", \"high\", \"max\"\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    120\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m cost_ceiling:        Option<f64>    // USD per 1M tokens; None = no limit\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    121\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m latency_target:      Option<String> // \"interactive\", \"batch\", None\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    122\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m context_tokens:      u32            // estimated token count\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    123\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m privacy_tier:        String         // \"public\", \"internal\", \"confidential\"\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    124\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m tool_needs:          Vec<String>    // tool names required\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    125\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m explicit_provider:   Option<String> // authorized override\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    126\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m explicit_model:      Option<String> // authorized override\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    127\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m ```\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    128\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m \n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    129\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m Phase 1 — Hard Filters (applied in order, all must pass):\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    130\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m \n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    131\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m 1. Route declared in `model_routes[]` — else reject.\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    132\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m 2. `available == true` — else skip.\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    133\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m 3. `privacy_tier` ≤ request tier — else skip.\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    134\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m 4. Tool needs satisfied (`tools[]` declared) — else skip.\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    135\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m 5. `context_window ≥ context_tokens` — else skip.\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    136\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m 6. `cost_per_token * context_tokens ≤ cost_ceiling` (if ceiling set) — else skip.\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    137\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m \n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    138\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m Phase 2 — Scoring (higher = better, all values from schema state):\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    139\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m \n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    140\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m ```\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    141\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m score = capability_match_bonus\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    142\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m       + effort_quality_score(route.effort_level, requested_effort)\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    143\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m       - cost_weight * route.cost_per_token\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    144\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m       - latency_penalty(route.latency_class, latency_target)\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    145\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m       + route_health_bonus(route.available, route.health_score)\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    146\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m ```\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    147\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m \n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    148\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m Phase 3 — Output (`SelectionOutput`):\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    149\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m \n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    150\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m ```\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    151\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m selected_provider:  String\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    152\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m selected_model:     String\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    153\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m reason:             String\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    154\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m estimated_cost:     f64\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    155\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m effort_level:       String\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    156\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m confidence:         f64        // 0.0–1.0\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    157\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m fallback_routes:    Vec<String>  // ordered hints of next-best routes\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    158\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m event_metadata:     { trace_id, timestamp, selector_version }\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    159\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m ```\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    160\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m \n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    161\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m The algorithm reads exclusively from `ZeroclawState` fields projected via\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    162\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m D-Bus. No `match` arm on `ProviderType` enum in the selection path.\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    163\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m \n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    164\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m ---\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    165\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m \n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    166\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m ## 5. Provider Adapter Absorption\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    167\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m \n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    168\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m The six adapters in `op-llm` (Anthropic, Gemini, GeminiCli, Factory,\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    169\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m OpenClaw, GCloudADC) plus `AssistantProvider` are moved into a module\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    170\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m owned by the architecture boundary that holds Zeroclaw execution logic.\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    171\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m They become private implementation details behind the Zeroclaw D-Bus surface.\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    172\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m \n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    173\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m Absorption steps:\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    174\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m 1. Move adapter source files; update `mod` declarations; fix imports.\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    175\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m 2. Remove `op-llm` from workspace `Cargo.toml` after all callers are migrated.\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    176\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m 3. No behavior changes to adapters during absorption — behavioral parity is\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    177\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m    validated by existing adapter tests, now run from the new location.\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    178\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m \n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    179\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m A compatibility re-export shim (`pub use`) inside `op-llm` MAY exist\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    180\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m temporarily to avoid breaking callers mid-migration. The shim is removed\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    181\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m in the final Caller Migration phase.\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    182\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m \n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    183\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m ---\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    184\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m \n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    185\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m ## 6. `/dev/shm/opdbus` Projection Contract\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    186\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m \n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    187\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m ```\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    188\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m /dev/shm/opdbus/\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    189\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m   schemas/\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    190\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m     zeroclaw.json          ← written by ZeroclawPlugin on state change\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    191\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m     antigravity.json       ← written by AntrigravityPlugin\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    192\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m     ...\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    193\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m   <monolithic-all-plugins>.json  ← written by schema aggregation layer\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    194\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m ```\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    195\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m \n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    196\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m - **Zeroclaw is the sole writer** of `schemas/zeroclaw.json`.\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    197\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m - The file is a JSON snapshot of `ZeroclawState` serialized through the\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    198\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m   `PluginSchema` projection. It is written atomically (write to `.tmp`, then\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    199\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m   `rename`).\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    200\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m - The monolithic file is written by the schema aggregation layer (not by\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    201\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m   individual plugins) and combines all plugin schemas.\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    202\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m - Consumers (e.g., `op-grpc-bridge`, factory BYOM) MAY read these files for\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    203\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m   display or discovery. They MUST NOT treat them as live state.\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    204\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m - `op-chat` and MCP surfaces MUST use D-Bus, not `/dev/shm` reads, for\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    205\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m   execution-path decisions.\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    206\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m \n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    207\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m ---\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    208\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m \n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    209\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m ## 7. Caller Migration Map\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    210\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m \n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    211\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m | Caller | Current import | Target after migration |\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    212\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m |---|---|---|\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    213\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m | `op-chat` | `op_llm::provider::LlmProvider`, `op_llm::chat::ChatManager` | Zeroclaw D-Bus `ResolveRoute` + `AuthorizeExecution` + absorbed adapter |\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    214\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m | `op-web` | `op_llm::*` (if any) | Zeroclaw D-Bus query |\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    215\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m | `cognitive-mcp` | `op_llm::*` (if any) | Zeroclaw D-Bus query; gateway role unchanged |\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    216\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m | `factory` BYOM | reads model routes | Reads `model_routes[]` from Zeroclaw schema projection |\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    217\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m \n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    218\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m ---\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    219\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m \n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    220\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m ## 8. Non-goals\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    221\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m \n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    222\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m - No separate `op-zeroclaw` crate.\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    223\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m - No independent `op-llm` authority after migration.\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    224\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m - No duplicate LLM provider trait in `op-chat`.\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    225\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m - No direct live-state file authority from `/dev/shm`.\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    226\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m - No SQLite plugin catalog.\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    227\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m - No new MCP shim service.\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    228\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m - No `compact-mcp` external exposure.\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    229\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m - No static hardcoded model picker (`match effort { ... }`).\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    230\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m - No execution of undeclared models/routes/tools.\n\u001b[0m\u001b[K\nCreating: \u001b[m/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/.kiro/specs/zeroclaw-absorbs-op-llm/design.md\u001b[0m\n\u001b[m - Completed in 0.0s\u001b[0m\n\n\u001b[?25l\u001b[0m\u001b[?25l\u001b[0m\u001b[0mI'll create the following file: \u001b[m/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/.kiro/specs/zeroclaw-absorbs-op-llm/spec.md\u001b[0m\u001b[m (using tool: write)\u001b[0m\nPurpose: Write spec.md\n\n\u001b[m\u001b[m+      1\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m # Spec — zeroclaw-absorbs-op-llm\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+      2\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m \n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+      3\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m ---\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+      4\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m \n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+      5\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m ## 1. Overview\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+      6\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m \n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+      7\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m Zeroclaw is the dynamic umbrella for all LLM execution: provider catalog,\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+      8\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m route resolution, model selection, tool-call translation, execution\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+      9\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m authorization, and MCP/UI/gRPC exposure. This spec governs absorbing\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+     10\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m `crates/op-llm` into Zeroclaw's plugin/schema/D-Bus architecture and retiring\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+     11\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m `op-llm` as an independent crate.\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+     12\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m \n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+     13\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m **Primary authority file:**\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+     14\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/zeroclaw.rs`\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+     15\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m \n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+     16\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m **D-Bus object:**\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+     17\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/zeroclaw` on bus `org.opdbus.v1`\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+     18\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m \n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+     19\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m **Schema re-export:**\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+     20\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/plugin_schema_defs.rs`\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+     21\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m \n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+     22\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m **Individual projection:**\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+     23\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m `/dev/shm/opdbus/schemas/zeroclaw.json`\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+     24\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m \n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+     25\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m **Monolithic catalog:**\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+     26\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m `/dev/shm/opdbus/<monolithic-all-plugins>.json`\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+     27\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m \n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+     28\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m ---\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+     29\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m \n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+     30\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m ## 2. The correct location is within the existing crates that\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    169\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m already carry Zeroclaw's plugin/control-plane authority — specifically, the\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    170\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m provider execution module belongs in a new private sub-module of the crate\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    171\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m that houses Zeroclaw plugin execution (to be confirmed by Schema Agent and\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    172\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m D-Bus Agent at their handoff, since the exact execution host crate depends on\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    173\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m the D-Bus dispatch layer).\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    174\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m \n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    175\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m The Schema Agent will confirm the exact target crate. The Provider Absorption\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    176\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m Agent MUST NOT create a new crate.\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    177\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m \n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    178\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m ### 5c. `ChatManager` retirement\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    179\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m \n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    180\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m `ChatManager`'s env-driven provider selection is replaced by the Zeroclaw\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    181\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m D-Bus `SelectModel` + `AuthorizeExecution` flow. `ChatManager` as a type is\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    182\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m removed from the public API after callers are migrated.\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    183\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m \n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    184\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m ### 5d. Compatibility shim\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    185\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m \n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    186\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m During Caller Migration, a thin `pub use` re-export in `op-llm` preserves\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    187\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m the `LlmProvider` trait and `ChatMessage` type at their old paths for callers\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    188\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m not yet migrated. The shim is removed in the final Caller Migration task.\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    189\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m \n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    190\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m ---\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    191\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m \n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    192\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m ## 6. `/dev/shm/opdbus` Projection Contract\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    193\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m \n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    194\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m ### Write path\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    195\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m \n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    196\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m 1. On successful `apply()` in `ZeroclawPlugin`, serialize `ZeroclawState`\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    197\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m    to JSON.\n\u001b[0m\u001b[m\u001b[m+    198\u001b[0m:\u001b[m\u001b[m 2. {"timestamp":"2026-06-28T06:51:09.213Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"function_call_output","call_id":"call_VsHOlYIFnWoe8u9X99fSOqVd","output":"Chunk ID: 5fd33f\nWall time: 0.0002 seconds\nProcess exited with code 0\nOriginal token count: 1528\nOutput:\n# Requirements — zeroclaw-absorbs-op-llm\n\nFeature: Zeroclaw absorbs `op-llm` and becomes the sole dynamic authority for LLM\nrouting, provider execution, model selection, tool-call translation, and\nschema-driven execution authorization.\n\n---\n\n## REQ-01 — Zeroclaw is the single source of truth for all LLM execution\n\n**WHEN** any component needs a provider, model, route, tool declaration, or\nexecution authorization,\n**THEN** it MUST query the Zeroclaw D-Bus object at\n`/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/zeroclaw` (bus `org.opdbus.v1`).\n\nAcceptance criteria:\n- No caller resolves a provider or model outside of a Zeroclaw D-Bus read.\n- No fallback to environment-variable provider selection in plugin/service code\n  after migration is complete (bootstrap scripts remain the sole exception).\n- `cargo grep` for `op_llm::provider::` or `op_llm::chat::` produces zero hits\n  outside `op-llm` itself after Caller Migration is complete.\n\n---\n\n## REQ-02 — Provider/model/tool/route must be declared in Zeroclaw PluginSchema\n\n**WHEN** any component attempts to execute an LLM call,\n**THEN** the selected provider, model, route, and any tool being invoked MUST be\npresent in the Zeroclaw `PluginSchema` as projected via D-Bus.\n\nAcceptance criteria:\n- A call with a provider/model combination absent from `model_routes` MUST be\n  rejected with `Err` before any network I/O.\n- A tool call whose `name` does not appear in `tools[]` in the schema MUST be\n  rejected.\n- Tests demonstrate that attempts to execute undeclared routes return\n  `RouteNotDeclared` errors.\n\n---\n\n## REQ-03 — Dynamic automatic model selection\n\n**WHEN** a caller supplies task metadata (task class, effort, cost ceiling,\nlatency target, context requirement, privacy tier, tool needs),\n**THEN** Zeroclaw MUST select provider and model entirely from live\nschema/D-Bus state with no static match tables in Rust.\n\nAcceptance criteria:\n- The selector reads only from Zeroclaw `PluginSchema` fields projected at\n  runtime; no `match provider_type` arms in the selection path.\n- Hard filter: routes where `available == false` or `privacy_tier` violates the\n  request MUST be excluded before scoring.\n- Scoring order: capability match → quality/effort → cost → latency → route\n  health.\n- Output includes: `selected_provider`, `selected_model`, `reason`,\n  `estimated_cost`, `effort_level`, `confidence`, `fallback_routes[]`,\n  `event_metadata`.\n- Tests cover: lowest-cost-wins, effort-ceiling-respected,\n  unavailable-route-excluded, privacy-tier-enforced.\n\n---\n\n## REQ-04 — `op-llm` provider adapters absorbed into Zeroclaw architecture\n\n**WHEN** migration is complete,\n**THEN** the provider execution adapters currently in\n`crates/op-llm/src/{anthropic,gemini,gemini_cli,factory,openclaw,assistant,gcloud_adc}.rs`\nMUST live inside the existing crate boundary that preserves Zeroclaw\nplugin/D-Bus/schema authority, with no duplicate authority crate.\n\nAcceptance criteria:\n- `op-llm` is removed from workspace `Cargo.toml` after callers are migrated.\n- `cargo build --workspace` passes with `op-llm` removed.\n- All adapter behavior (OpenAI-compatible chat, tool-call translation,\n  Anthropic content-block format, streaming, GCloud ADC) is preserved.\n\n---\n\n## REQ-05 — D-Bus is the only control plane\n\n**WHEN** any plugin or service code reads or writes provider selection,\nroute selection, model availability, tool declarations, policy metadata, or\nexecution authorization,\n**THEN** it MUST do so through D-Bus methods/properties on\n`/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/zeroclaw`.\n\nAcceptance criteria:\n- No `Command::new(\"...\")` invocations for live state in plugin or service code.\n- No direct live-state file reads outside bootstrap scripts.\n- No JSON-RPC polling loops or D-Bus watchers for live state.\n\n---\n\n## REQ-06 — `/dev/shm/opdbus` files are derived projection artifacts, not authorities\n\n**WHEN** Zeroclaw writes `/dev/shm/opdbus/schemas/zeroclaw.json`,\n**THEN** that file MUST be a snapshot of the D-Bus-authoritative schema, not\nthe source of truth. Consumer reads of that file MUST NOT mutate it.\n\nAcceptance criteria:\n- Zeroclaw is the sole writer of `/dev/shm/opdbus/schemas/zeroclaw.json`.\n- The monolithic all-plugin catalog at\n  `/dev/shm/live-schema.json` is written by the schema\n  aggregation layer, not by individual plugins.\n- No consumer reads `/dev/shm` paths for live state decisions.\n\n---\n\n## REQ-07 — OSCAL subids on every new artifact\n\n**WHEN** any new schema field, D-Bus method, mutation record, event, or MCP\ntool is added,\n**THEN** it MUST carry an `x-oscal-subid` annotation using one of the seven\ncategories (`src`, `prj`, `sch`, `mut`, `obs`, `evt`, `exp`) per AGENTS.md\n§4a.\n\nAcceptance criteria:\n- CI subid uniqueness check passes.\n- No new field or method exists without a registered subid.\n\n---\n\n## REQ-08 — `op-chat`, `op-web`, MCP surfaces, factory BYOM migrate off `op-llm`\n\n**WHEN** migration is complete,\n**THEN** `op-chat`, `op-web`, cognitive-mcp, and factory BYOM discovery MUST\nNOT import `op-llm` traits or types for provider selection or execution.\n\nAcceptance criteria:\n- `op-chat` calls Zeroclaw D-Bus for provider/model resolution before sending.\n- Factory BYOM discovery reads `model_routes` from Zeroclaw schema projection.\n- `cognitive-mcp` remains the external gateway; `compact-mcp` remains loopback\n  only — neither is changed by this refactor.\n\n---\n\n## REQ-09 — No new crate, no new shim service\n\n**WHEN** implementing this refactor,\n**THEN** no new `op-zeroclaw` crate and no new shim/proxy service MUST be\nintroduced.\n\nAcceptance criteria:\n- Workspace `Cargo.toml` member count does not increase.\n- No new binary service is registered with s6.\n\n---\n\n## REQ-10 — Handoff artifacts produced per agent\n\n**WHEN** each agent completes its phase,\n**THEN** it MUST deposit a handoff file in\n`.kiro/specs/zeroclaw-absorbs-op-llm/` per the contract in spec.md §8.\n\nAcceptance criteria:\n- All eight handoff files exist and are non-empty at final acceptance.\n- Each handoff records: scope, files changed, contract changes, verification\n  commands run, known risks, next-agent dependencies.\n","internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough":{"turn_id":"019f0cfe-e2ef-7c91-9192-629d651ed5e0"}}}
{"timestamp":"2026-06-28T06:51:09.232Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"function_call_output","call_id":"call_XY4jvrThg83jshMfCt1TO2vX","output":"Chunk ID: 81a645\nWall time: 0.0000 seconds\nProcess exited with code 0\nOriginal token count: 2324\nOutput:\n# Design — zeroclaw-absorbs-op-llm\n\n---\n\n## 1. Ownership Boundary\n\n### Zeroclaw plugin — sole authority\n\n```\ncrates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/zeroclaw.rs          ← ZeroclawPlugin, ZeroclawState\ncrates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/common/llm_projection.rs  ← shared schema types\ncrates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/plugin_schema_defs.rs     ← schema aggregator/re-export\n```\n\nZeroclaw owns every runtime LLM concern:\n\n| Concern | Owner |\n|---|---|\n| Provider catalog | `ZeroclawState::projection.providers[]` |\n| Model route table | `ZeroclawState::projection.model_routes[]` |\n| Selected provider | `ZeroclawState::selected_provider` |\n| Selected model | `ZeroclawState::selected_model` |\n| Automatic selector policy | `ZeroclawState::selector_policy` (new) |\n| Router / classifier config | `ZeroclawState::projection.router` |\n| Tool declarations | `ZeroclawState::projection.tools[]` |\n| Structured output policy | `ZeroclawState::projection.structured_output` |\n| Transport metadata | `ZeroclawState::transport` |\n| Availability / health | per-`ModelRoute.available` + new `health_status` field |\n| Cost metadata | new `ModelRoute.cost_per_token` / `cost_ceiling` |\n| Effort metadata | new `ModelRoute.effort_level` |\n| Privacy / compliance tier | new `ModelRoute.privacy_tier` |\n| Fallback chain | new `ModelRoute.fallback_routes[]` |\n| Execution authorization | Zeroclaw D-Bus method `AuthorizeExecution` |\n\n### What is NOT owned by Zeroclaw\n\n- Message persistence and session history — `op-chat` / `op-cozo-store`\n- Semantic memory — `op-cognitive-mcp`\n- gRPC bridge topology — `op-grpc-bridge`\n- Web surface — `op-web`\n- Identity — `op-identity`\n\n---\n\n## 2. The Schema = The Plugin = The Contract\n\n```\nPluginSchema (in plugin_schema_defs.rs)\n    └─ ZeroclawState (serde + schemars)\n          ├─ LlmProjection (flattened)\n          │     ├─ providers: Vec<Provider>\n          │     ├─ model_routes: Vec<ModelRoute>    ← extended with cost/effort/privacy\n          │     ├─ router: Router\n          │     ├─ tools: Vec<LlmTool>\n          │     ├─ structured_output: StructuredOutput\n          │     ├─ config_schema: ConfigSchema\n          │     └─ ui_surface: UiSurface\n          ├─ selected_provider: String\n          ├─ selected_model: String\n          ├─ transport: LlmTransport\n          └─ selector_policy: SelectorPolicy  ← new\n```\n\nThe schema is generated by `schemars` from these types. It is re-exported\nthrough `plugin_schema_defs.rs`. It is the input to D-Bus method generation,\nMCP tool declarations, gRPC shape derivation, and UI field rendering.\n\nIf a provider/model/tool/route is not in this schema projection, it does not\nexist and cannot execute.\n\n---\n\n## 3. D-Bus Object\n\n**Object path:** `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/zeroclaw`\n**Bus name:** `org.opdbus.v1`\n**Interface:** `org.opdbus.v1.Plugin`\n\n### Properties (read from ZeroclawState)\n\n| Property | Type | subid |\n|---|---|---|\n| `Status` | String | `obs.software.zeroclaw.status@v1` |\n| `SelectedProvider` | String | `mut.service.zeroclaw.selected-provider@v1` |\n| `SelectedModel` | String | `exp.service.zeroclaw.selected-model@v1` |\n| `SchemaJson` | String (JSON) | `prj.service.zeroclaw.schema-json@v1` |\n\n### Methods\n\n| Method | Inputs | Output | subid |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| `ResolveRoute(hint, context_tokens, task_class)` | Strings | `RouteResolution` JSON | `obs.service.zeroclaw.resolve-route@v1` |\n| `SelectModel(SelectionInput)` | JSON | `SelectionOutput` JSON | `mut.service.zeroclaw.select-model@v1` |\n| `AuthorizeExecution(provider, model, tool?)` | Strings | Bool + reason | `mut.service.zeroclaw.authorize-execution@v1` |\n| `SetProvider(provider_id)` | String | ApplyResult | `mut.service.zeroclaw.set-provider@v1` |\n| `SetModel(model_id)` | String | ApplyResult | `mut.service.zeroclaw.set-model@v1` |\n| `GetProviderCatalog()` | — | JSON array | `obs.service.zeroclaw.provider-catalog@v1` |\n| `GetModelRoutes()` | — | JSON array | `obs.service.zeroclaw.model-routes@v1` |\n| `GetTools()` | — | JSON array | `obs.service.zeroclaw.tools@v1` |\n\n### Signals\n\n| Signal | Payload | subid |\n|---|---|---|\n| `ProviderChanged` | `{old, new, reason, actor_id}` | `evt.service.zeroclaw.provider-changed@v1` |\n| `ModelChanged` | `{old, new, reason, actor_id}` | `evt.service.zeroclaw.model-changed@v1` |\n| `RouteHealthChanged` | `{route_hint, available, reason}` | `evt.service.zeroclaw.route-health-changed@v1` |\n| `ExecutionAuthorized` | `{provider, model, tool?, trace_id}` | `evt.service.zeroclaw.execution-authorized@v1` |\n| `ExecutionDenied` | `{provider, model, tool?, reason, trace_id}` | `evt.service.zeroclaw.execution-denied@v1` |\n\n---\n\n## 4. Automatic Model Selection Algorithm\n\nInput (`SelectionInput`):\n\n```\ntask_class:          String         // \"code\", \"chat\", \"reasoning\", \"vision\", ...\nrequested_effort:    String         // \"low\", \"medium\", \"high\", \"max\"\ncost_ceiling:        Option<f64>    // USD per 1M tokens; None = no limit\nlatency_target:      Option<String> // \"interactive\", \"batch\", None\ncontext_tokens:      u32            // estimated token count\nprivacy_tier:        String         // \"public\", \"internal\", \"confidential\"\ntool_needs:          Vec<String>    // tool names required\nexplicit_provider:   Option<String> // authorized override\nexplicit_model:      Option<String> // authorized override\n```\n\nPhase 1 — Hard Filters (applied in order, all must pass):\n\n1. Route declared in `model_routes[]` — else reject.\n2. `available == true` — else skip.\n3. `privacy_tier` ≤ request tier — else skip.\n4. Tool needs satisfied (`tools[]` declared) — else skip.\n5. `context_window ≥ context_tokens` — else skip.\n6. `cost_per_token * context_tokens ≤ cost_ceiling` (if ceiling set) — else skip.\n\nPhase 2 — Scoring (higher = better, all values from schema state):\n\n```\nscore = capability_match_bonus\n      + effort_quality_score(route.effort_level, requested_effort)\n      - cost_weight * route.cost_per_token\n      - latency_penalty(route.latency_class, latency_target)\n      + route_health_bonus(route.available, route.health_score)\n```\n\nPhase 3 — Output (`SelectionOutput`):\n\n```\nselected_provider:  String\nselected_model:     String\nreason:             String\nestimated_cost:     f64\neffort_level:       String\nconfidence:         f64        // 0.0–1.0\nfallback_routes:    Vec<String>  // ordered hints of next-best routes\nevent_metadata:     { trace_id, timestamp, selector_version }\n```\n\nThe algorithm reads exclusively from `ZeroclawState` fields projected via\nD-Bus. No `match` arm on `ProviderType` enum in the selection path.\n\n---\n\n## 5. Provider Adapter Absorption\n\nThe six adapters in `op-llm` (Anthropic, Gemini, GeminiCli, Factory,\nOpenClaw, GCloudADC) plus `AssistantProvider` are moved into a module\nowned by the architecture boundary that holds Zeroclaw execution logic.\nThey become private implementation details behind the Zeroclaw D-Bus surface.\n\nAbsorption steps:\n1. Move adapter source files; update `mod` declarations; fix imports.\n2. Remove `op-llm` from workspace `Cargo.toml` after all callers are migrated.\n3. No behavior changes to adapters during absorption — behavioral parity is\n   validated by existing adapter tests, now run from the new location.\n\nA compatibility re-export shim (`pub use`) inside `op-llm` MAY exist\ntemporarily to avoid breaking callers mid-migration. The shim is removed\nin the final Caller Migration phase.\n\n---\n\n## 6. `/dev/shm/opdbus` Projection Contract\n\n```\n/dev/shm/opdbus/\n  schemas/\n    zeroclaw.json          ← written by ZeroclawPlugin on state change\n    antigravity.json       ← written by AntrigravityPlugin\n    ...\n  /dev/shm/live-schema.json  ← written by schema aggregation layer\n```\n\n- **Zeroclaw is the sole writer** of `schemas/zeroclaw.json`.\n- The file is a JSON snapshot of `ZeroclawState` serialized through the\n  `PluginSchema` projection. It is written atomically (write to `.tmp`, then\n  `rename`).\n- The monolithic file is written by the schema aggregation layer (not by\n  individual plugins) and combines all plugin schemas.\n- Consumers (e.g., `op-grpc-bridge`, factory BYOM) MAY read these files for\n  display or discovery. They MUST NOT treat them as live state.\n- `op-chat` and MCP surfaces MUST use D-Bus, not `/dev/shm` reads, for\n  execution-path decisions.\n\n---\n\n## 7. Caller Migration Map\n\n| Caller | Current import | Target after migration |\n|---|---|---|\n| `op-chat` | `op_llm::provider::LlmProvider`, `op_llm::chat::ChatManager` | Zeroclaw D-Bus `ResolveRoute` + `AuthorizeExecution` + absorbed adapter |\n| `op-web` | `op_llm::*` (if any) | Zeroclaw D-Bus query |\n| `cognitive-mcp` | `op_llm::*` (if any) | Zeroclaw D-Bus query; gateway role unchanged |\n| `factory` BYOM | reads model routes | Reads `model_routes[]` from Zeroclaw schema projection |\n\n---\n\n## 8. Non-goals\n\n- No separate `op-zeroclaw` crate.\n- No independent `op-llm` authority after migration.\n- No duplicate LLM provider trait in `op-chat`.\n- No direct live-state file authority from `/dev/shm`.\n- No SQLite plugin catalog.\n- No new MCP shim service.\n- No `compact-mcp` external exposure.\n- No static hardcoded model picker (`match effort { ... }`).\n- No execution of undeclared models/routes/tools.\n","internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough":{"turn_id":"019f0cfe-e2ef-7c91-9192-629d651ed5e0"}}}

The Schema = The Plugin = The Contract\n    46\t\n    47\t```\n    48\tPluginSchema (in plugin_schema_defs.rs)\n    49\t    └─ ZeroclawState (serde + schemars)\n    50\t          ├─ LlmProjection (flattened)\n    51\t          │     ├─ providers: Vec<Provider>\n    52\t          │     ├─ model_routes: Vec<ModelRoute>    ← extended with cost/effort/privacy\n    53\t          │     ├─ router: Router\n    54\t          │     ├─ tools: Vec<LlmTool>\n    55\t          │     ├─ structured_output: StructuredOutput\n    56\t          │     ├─ config_schema: ConfigSchema\n    57\t          │     └─ ui_surface: UiSurface\n    58\t          ├─ selected_provider: String\n    59\t          ├─ selected_model: String\n    60\t          ├─ transport: LlmTransport\n    61\t          └─ selector_policy: SelectorPolicy  ← new\n    62\t```\n    63\t\n    64\tThe schema is generated by `schemars` from these types. It is re-exported\n    65\tthrough `plugin_schema_defs.rs`. It is the input to D-Bus method generation,\n    66\tMCP tool declarations, gRPC shape derivation, and UI field rendering.\n    67\t\n    68\tIf a provider/model/tool/route is not in this schema projection, it does not\n    69\texist and cannot execute.\n    70\t\n    71\t---\n    72\t\n    73\t## 3. 112\t\n   113\t## 4. Automatic Model Selection Algorithm\n   114\t\n   115\tInput (`SelectionInput`):\n   116\t\n   117\t```\n   118\ttask_class:          String         // \"code\", \"chat\", \"reasoning\", \"vision\", ...\n   119\trequested_effort:    String         // \"low\", \"medium\", \"high\", \"max\"\n   120\tcost_ceiling:        Option<f64>    // USD per 1M tokens; None = no limit\n   121\tlatency_target:      Option<String> // \"interactive\", \"batch\", None\n   122\tcontext_tokens:      u32            // estimated token count\n   123\tprivacy_tier:        String         // \"public\", \"internal\", \"confidential\"\n   124\ttool_needs:          Vec<String>    // tool names required\n   125\texplicit_provider:   Option<String> // authorized override\n   126\texplicit_model:      Option<String> // authorized override\n   127\t```\n   128\t\n   129\tPhase 1 — Hard Filters (applied in order, all must pass):\n   130\t\n   131\t1. Route declared in `model_routes[]` — else reject.\n   132\t2. `available == true` — else skip.\n   133\t3. `privacy_tier` ≤ request tier — else skip.\n   134\t4. Tool needs satisfied (`tools[]` declared) — else skip.\n   135\t5. `context_window ≥ context_tokens` — else skip.\n   136\t6. `cost_per_token * context_tokens ≤ cost_ceiling` (if ceiling set) — else skip.\n   137\t\n   138\tPhase 2 — Scoring (higher = better, all values from schema state):\n   139\t\n   140\t```\n   141\tscore = capability_match_bonus\n   142\t      + effort_quality_score(route.effort_level, requested_effort)\n   143\t      - cost_weight * route.cost_per_token\n   144\t      - latency_penalty(route.latency_class, latency_target)\n   145\t      + route_health_bonus(route.available, route.health_score)\n   146\t```\n   147\t\n   148\tPhase 3 — Output (`SelectionOutput`):\n   149\t\n   150\t```\n   151\tselected_provider:  String\n   152\tselected_model:     String\n   153\treason:             String\n   154\testimated_cost:     f64\n   155\teffort_level:       String\n   156\tconfidence:         f64        // 0.0–1.0\n   157\tfallback_routes:    Vec<String>  // ordered hints of next-best routes\n   158\tevent_metadata:     { trace_id, timestamp, selector_version }\n   159\t```\n   160\t\n   161\tThe algorithm reads exclusively from `ZeroclawState` fields projected via\n   162\tD-Bus. No `match` arm on `ProviderType` enum in the selection path.\n   163\t\n   164\t---\n   165\t\n   166\t## 5. Provider Adapter Absorption\n   167\t\n   168\tThe six adapters in `op-llm` (Anthropic, Gemini, GeminiCli, Factory,\n   169\tOpenClaw, GCloudADC) plus `AssistantProvider` are moved into a module\n   170\towned by the architecture boundary that holds Zeroclaw execution logic.\n   171\tThey become private implementation details behind the Zeroclaw D-Bus surface.\n   172\t\n   173\tAbsorption steps:\n   174\t1. Move adapter source files; update `mod` declarations; fix imports.\n   175\t2. Remove `op-llm` from workspace `Cargo.toml` after all callers are migrated.\n   176\t3. No behavior changes to adapters during absorption — behavioral parity is\n   177\t   validated by existing adapter tests, now run from the new location.\n   178\t\n   179\tA compatibility re-export shim (`pub use`) inside `op-llm` MAY exist\n   180\ttemporarily to avoid breaking callers mid-migration. The shim is removed\n   181\tin the final Caller Migration phase.\n   182\t\n   183\t---\n   184\t\n   185\t## 6. `/dev/shm/opdbus` Projection Contract\n   186\t\n   187\t```\n   188\t/dev/shm/opdbus/\n   189\t  schemas/\n   190\t    zeroclaw.json          ← written by ZeroclawPlugin on state change\n   191\t    antigravity.json       ← written by AntrigravityPlugin\n   192\t    ...\n   193\t  /dev/shm/live-schema.json  ← written by schema aggregation layer\n   194\t```\n   195\t\n   196\t- **Zeroclaw is the sole writer** of `schemas/zeroclaw.json`.\n   197\t- The file is a JSON snapshot of `ZeroclawState` serialized through the\n   198\t  `PluginSchema` projection. It is written atomically (write to `.tmp`, then\n   199\t  `rename`).\n   200\t- The monolithic file is written by the schema aggregation layer (not by\n   201\t  individual plugins) and combines all plugin schemas.\n   202\t- Consumers (e.g., `op-grpc-bridge`, factory BYOM) MAY read these files for\n   203\t  display or discovery. Non-goals\n   221\t\n   222\t- No separate `op-zeroclaw` crate.\n   223\t- No independent `op-llm` authority after migration.\n   224\t- No duplicate LLM provider trait in `op-chat`.\n   225\t- No direct live-state file authority from `/dev/shm`.\n   226\t- No SQLite plugin catalog.\n   227\t- No new MCP shim service.\n   228\t- No `compact-mcp` external exposure.\n   229\t- No static hardcoded model picker (`match effort { ... }`).\n   230\t- No execution of undeclared models/routes/tools.\n","internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough":{"turn_id":"019f0cfe-e2ef-7c91-9192-629d651ed5e0"}}}

{"timestamp":"2026-06-28T06:52:07.812Z","type":"event_msg","payload":{"type":"agent_message","message":"**Findings**\n\n1. [`.config.kiro`](/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/.kiro/specs/zeroclaw-absorbs-op-llm/.config.kiro:15) still has the old placeholder path: `/dev/shm/opdbus/<monolithic-all-plugins>.json`.\nYou replaced the docs, but the machine-readable Kiro metadata still points agents at the wrong path. This should be `/dev/shm/live-schema.json`.\n\n2. [`spec.md`](/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/.kiro/specs/zeroclaw-absorbs-op-llm/spec.md:196) and [design.md](/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/.kiro/specs/zeroclaw-absorbs-op-llm/design.md:197) say `/dev/shm/opdbus/schemas/zeroclaw.json` is a serialized `ZeroclawState`. Current code writes a serialized `PluginSchema` via `ZeroclawPlugin::write_schema_file_to`, and the test round-trips it as `PluginSchema`. That is a contract-level mismatch. The spec should say the file is the derived Zeroclaw `PluginSchema`, not state.\n\n3. [`tasks.md`](/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/.kiro/specs/zeroclaw-absorbs-op-llm/tasks.md:22), [`spec.md`](/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/.kiro/specs/zeroclaw-absorbs-op-llm/spec.md:196), and [`tasks.md`](/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/.kiro/specs/zeroclaw-absorbs-op-llm/tasks.md:328) refer to `ZeroclawPlugin::apply`, but the actual plugin implements `apply_state`. Also, current `apply_state` does not appear to call `write_schema_file`. The spec needs to name the real lifecycle hook: either `apply_state`, plugin startup/registration, or `SchemaEngine` projection publication.\n\n4. [`tasks.md`](/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/.kiro/specs/zeroclaw-absorbs-op-llm/tasks.md:293) allows factory BYOM discovery to read `/dev/shm/opdbus/schemas/zeroclaw.json`, while REQ-05/REQ-06 say live routing state must use D-Bus and `/dev/shm` is not an authority. That should be tightened: factory should use D-Bus `GetModelRoutes`; `/dev/shm` can be a projection validation/display fallback only.\n\n5. [`spec.md`](/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/.kiro/specs/zeroclaw-absorbs-op-llm/spec.md:167) leaves the provider absorption target unresolved, and [`tasks.md`](/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/.kiro/specs/zeroclaw-absorbs-op-llm/tasks.md:208) punts it to a later agent. For a refactor this large, that is too vague.
