Correct lifecycle ownership.\\n   - Remove references to `ZeroclawPlugin::apply` as the projection write/lifecycle point.\\n   - Do not assume direct `apply_state` is the schema projection lifecycle either.\\n   - Describe the lifecycle in terms of `SchemaEngine` and `MutationEngine`: SchemaEngine owns schema registration/projection and writes derived schema catalogs; MutationEngine owns validated state mutations against `PluginSchema`.\\n   - The gRPC bridge is being refactored: it creates all D-Bus objects automatically from schema. The spec must not require hand-written per-plugin D-Bus object plumbing when the schema/gRPC bridge generation path should own it.\\n   - D-Bus objects are generated from `PluginSchema`; D-Bus first remains the control plane.\\n\\n4. Factory correction.\\n   - Do NOT make factory a separate D-Bus object or BYOM control object in this spec.\\n   - Factory should be modeled as a multi-model provider in Zeroclaw’s provider catalog, like OpenRouter, Kilocode, Opencode, etc.\\n   - Factory model routes are declared in Zeroclaw schema as provider/model routes. Zeroclaw’s selector may choose factory routes using the same schema-driven route selection as other providers.\\n   - Remove wording that treats factory BYOM discovery as a separate object/control plane. If factory is mentioned, treat it as a provider category/route source under Zeroclaw.\\n\\n5. Cost semantics correction.\\n   - Do not invent `cost_per_token` or incompatible units.\\n   - Cost fields and scoring must refer to Zeroclaw’s own cost/budget schema and terminology. If the exact Zeroclaw names are not known in this repository, specify that the Schema Agent must inspect Zeroclaw’s existing cost model/config schema before naming fields.\\n   - Use neutral schema placeholders such as `cost_profile`, `budget_class`, `estimated_cost`, and `cost_policy` only if the exact Zeroclaw field names are unknown, and explicitly require replacing them with Zeroclaw-native names during Schema Agent work.\\n   - Remove inconsistent math like `cost_per_token * context_tokens <= cost_ceiling` unless the unit model is defined.\\n\\n6. Provider absorption boundary correction.\\n   - The spec currently punts the adapter target location too vaguely. Fix it without creating a new crate.\\n   - State that provider adapters are absorbed behind Zeroclaw’s schema/D-Bus authority and must not become a second authority.\\n   - The exact module target should be the existing Zeroclaw/plugin execution boundary identified by SchemaEngine/MutationEngine/gRPC-bridge refactor. If not identifiable from current repo files, require a short pre-implementation spike/handoff to name the existing module before moving code.\\n   - Do not tell agents to move provider execution blindly into `op-plugins` if that would make the schema crate own too much runtime behavior. Keep `PluginSchema` authority separate from adapter implementation details while preserving Zeroclaw authority.\\n\\n7. D-Bus / gRPC bridge correction.\\n   - gRPC bridge creates D-Bus objects from schema automatically.\\n   - D-Bus method/property/signal surfaces are generated from `PluginSchema`; the spec should define schema contract additions and generated surfaces, not manual D-Bus handler boilerplate unless the repo requires it.\\n   - All calls flow through D-Bus; gRPC bridge is transport/projection, not authority.\\n\\n8. Command corrections.\\n   - Replace `cargo grep` with real commands such as `rg 'op_llm::' crates -g '*.rs'` and `rg 'op-llm' crates -g Cargo.toml`.\\n\\n9. Preserve and strengthen these requirements:\\n   - No separate static `op-zeroclaw` crate.\\n   - No static hardcoded model picker.\\n   - No execution of undeclared models/routes/tools.\\n   - `op-llm` retired only after provider adapters are absorbed and callers migrate.\\n   - Multi-agent orchestration remains in `tasks.md` and `spec.md` with handoff files.\\n   - `cognitive-mcp` remains universal external gateway; `compact-mcp` remains loopback only.\\n\\n10. Review output quality requirements:\\n   - Keep changes implementation-ready and internally consistent.\\n   - Make the spec decisive where the repo already has facts: `/dev/shm/live-schema.json`, `/dev/shm/opdbus/schemas/zeroclaw.json`, SchemaEngine, MutationEngine, PluginSchema, D-Bus generation from schema.\\n   - Mark only truly unknown implementation details as a spike/handoff task.\\n   - After editing, run a textual check for forbidden stale phrases and report results: `<monolithic-all-plugins>`, `ZeroclawPlugin::apply`, `cost_per_token`, `cargo grep`, `op-zeroclaw`, and `factory BYOM`.\\n\\nImportant: Do not use Python. Do not add source code. {"timestamp":"2026-06-28T07:00:27.435Z","type":"event_msg","payload":{"type":"agent_message","message":"Yes, directionally. Absorbing `op-llm` into Zeroclaw is the right move **if Zeroclaw is meant to be the policy and routing brain**, not just another provider adapter.\n\nThe key distinction:\n\n- **Right move:** Zeroclaw owns schema, route policy, automatic model selection, cost/effort decisions, execution authorization, and provider catalog.\n- **Wrong move:** Zeroclaw becomes a giant pile of HTTP clients and runtime details inside `op-plugins`.\n\nSo I’d frame the refactor like this:\n\nZeroclaw should own the **control plane and contract**:\n`PluginSchema -> SchemaEngine -> generated D-Bus objects -> MutationEngine -> selected route/model/tool`.\n\nThe absorbed `op-llm` code should become **provider adapter implementation behind Zeroclaw**, not a second authority. Ideally adapters live behind a clean internal boundary, while the Zeroclaw plugin/schema remains the source of truth.\n\nThe strongest reason to do it: model selection by effort/cost/privacy/tooling cannot be correct if it lives in `op-llm`, because `op-llm` does not know the whole system contract. Zeroclaw does.\n\nThe main risk: putting too much runtime behavior directly in `op-plugins`. If that happens, the plugin crate becomes both schema authority and provider runtime, which could get messy fast. The spec should force a boundary: Zeroclaw owns decisions; provider adapters only execute schema-authorized decisions.\n\nSo yes: retire `op-llm` as an authority. But keep Zeroclaw’s schema/D-Bus authority clean, and treat provider clients as replaceable adapters under that authority.","phase":"final_answer","memory_citation":null}}

Ideally adapters live behind a clean internal boundary, while the Zeroclaw plugin/schema remains the source of truth.\n\nThe strongest reason to do it: model selection by effort/cost/privacy/tooling cannot be correct if it lives in `op-llm`, because `op-llm` does not know the whole system contract. {"timestamp":"2026-06-28T07:00:27.475Z","type":"event_msg","payload":{"type":"task_complete","turn_id":"019f0d07-6bfa-7c83-81b4-6616d086f335","last_agent_message":"Yes, directionally. Absorbing `op-llm` into Zeroclaw is the right move **if Zeroclaw is meant to be the policy and routing brain**, not just another provider adapter.\n\nThe key distinction:\n\n- **Right move:** Zeroclaw owns schema, route policy, automatic model selection, cost/effort decisions, execution authorization, and provider catalog.\n- **Wrong move:** Zeroclaw becomes a giant pile of HTTP clients and runtime details inside `op-plugins`.\n\nSo I’d frame the refactor like this:\n\nZeroclaw should own the **control plane and contract**:\n`PluginSchema -> SchemaEngine -> generated D-Bus objects -> MutationEngine -> selected route/model/tool`.\n\nThe absorbed `op-llm` code should become **provider adapter implementation behind Zeroclaw**, not a second authority. Ideally adapters live behind a clean internal boundary, while the Zeroclaw plugin/schema remains the source of truth.\n\nThe strongest reason to do it: model selection by effort/cost/privacy/tooling cannot be correct if it lives in `op-llm`, because `op-llm` does not know the whole system contract. Zeroclaw does.\n\nThe main risk: putting too much runtime behavior directly in `op-plugins`. If that happens, the plugin crate becomes both schema authority and provider runtime, which could get messy fast. The spec should force a boundary: Zeroclaw owns decisions; provider adapters only execute schema-authorized decisions.\n\nSo yes: retire `op-llm` as an authority. But keep Zeroclaw’s schema/D-Bus authority clean, and treat provider clients as replaceable adapters under that authority.","completed_at":1782630027,"duration_ms":9429,"time_to_first_token_ms":3208}}

Add an explicit architecture boundary section based on the following clarification.\\n\\nContext: Zeroclaw absorbing `op-llm` is the right direction only if the spec prevents two bad outcomes:\\n1. `op-llm` survives as the hidden authority under a new name.\\n2. `op-plugins` becomes a runtime blob full of provider HTTP clients and policy/runtime mixed together.\\n\\nRequired addition: define three explicit layers and dependency direction.\\n\\nLayer 1 — Zeroclaw Contract Layer:\\n- Owns `PluginSchema`, `ZeroclawState`, route declarations, provider catalog declarations, selector policy schema, OSCAL subids, generated D-Bus surface, and `/dev/shm` schema projections.\\n- The Zeroclaw plugin is the schema; the schema is the plugin; `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for all calls.\\n- This layer must not contain provider HTTP client/network adapter implementation.\\n\\nLayer 2 — Zeroclaw Orchestration Layer:\\n- Owns dynamic model selection, effort/cost scoring, route resolution, execution authorization, fallback planning, MutationEngine integration, trace/event emission, and handoff to provider adapters.\\n- Reads effective contract/state only through SchemaEngine/MutationEngine/D-Bus generated from PluginSchema.\\n- Does not implement provider wire formats directly.\\n\\nLayer 3 — Provider Adapter Layer:\\n- Owns OpenAI/Anthropic/Gemini/OpenClaw/Factory/Kilocode/Opencode/OpenRouter/etc. wire formats, request/response conversion, streaming parsing, auth headers, and network calls.\\n- Cannot select models, mutate routes, read live state, bypass D-Bus, or execute undeclared schema routes.\\n- Takes only a schema-authorized execution plan/selected route from the orchestration layer.\\n- Provider adapters are replaceable implementation details under Zeroclaw authority.\\n\\nDependency direction:\\n- Contract Layer defines schema and generated surface.\\n- Orchestration Layer consumes contract/state and produces an execution plan.\\n- Provider Adapter Layer consumes execution plan and performs the provider call.\\n- Provider Adapter Layer must not call back into route selection or policy.\\n\\nUpdate requirements/design/spec/tasks accordingly:\\n- Add a dedicated “Layer Boundaries” section to `design.md` and `spec.md`.\\n- Update provider absorption tasks so the Provider Absorption Agent must first identify/create an internal adapter module boundary without creating a new crate or a new authority.\\n- State that provider adapters must not be moved directly into `op-plugins` if doing so mixes schema authority with runtime HTTP clients; if the repo lacks a clean host, the agent must do a short boundary spike and document the existing module target before moving code.\\n- Update the review checklist to include: no provider adapter owns selection, no orchestration layer owns provider wire formats, no contract layer owns HTTP clients, no adapter reads `/dev/shm` or D-Bus live state.\\n- Keep no separate `op-zeroclaw` crate. Keep `op-llm` retirement. Keep D-Bus first and gRPC bridge generated from PluginSchema.\\n\\nAlso preserve prior corrections:\\n- `.config.kiro` monolithic path is `/dev/shm/live-schema.json`.\\n- `/dev/shm/opdbus/schemas/zeroclaw.json` is PluginSchema projection, not ZeroclawState.\\n- SchemaEngine/MutationEngine lifecycle, not `ZeroclawPlugin::apply`.\\n- Factory is a multi-model provider route like OpenRouter/Kilocode/Opencode, not a separate object/control plane.\\n- Cost semantics follow Zeroclaw-native cost policy; do not invent cost_per_token.\\n\\nAfter editing, run a textual check and report remaining hits for: `op-zeroclaw`, `cost_per_token`, `ZeroclawPlugin::apply`, `<monolithic-all-plugins>`, `factory BYOM`, and `Provider Adapter Layer`.\\nEOF\\n)\\nkiro-cli chat --mode spec --no-interactive --trust-all-tools \\\"$prompt\\\"\",\"workdir\":\"/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto\",\"yield_time_ms\":30000,\"max_output_tokens\":30000}","call_id":"call_mmUeVYpRlotW2TngTdw6zzmc","internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough":{"turn_id":"019f0d26-3d2d-7ed0-91d5-0b94fb767fa3"}}}

Follow these strictly to maintain consistency, pass CI, and adhere to the 3tched Architecture standards.\n\n#### 1. The Persona & Naming Conventions\n*   **Humanized Roles:** Treat system components as authoritative human roles. Never use sterile acronyms for major components.\n  *   **A.N.N.A. Scribe** (Axon Network Notary Arbitrator): The top-level Identity-State Arbitrator who notarizes the WireGuard identity and handles the \"Snowball\" session.\n  *   **The Compliance Engine (\"Law Firm\"):** One dedicated Attorney for each major component: **Olivia Scal** (Managing Partner / OSCAL), **E.U.gene Risk** (EU AI Act Counsel), **Penny Privacy** (GDPR Engine), and **Reggie O.P.A.** (Cloud Prosecutor).\n*   **Terminology:** Use exact architecture terminology: \"The Sled\" (1:1 shared memory layout), \"The Shuttle\" (the Rust bridge/courier), \"The Snowball\" (appended session ledger), and \"The Strike/Etch\" (generating the hash).\n\n#### 2. Core Architectural Rules (The \"Reality\")\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via OpenClaw Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Artix Linux (s6 init).\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles — D-Bus First (MANDATORY)\n\n**D-Bus is the ONLY control plane. Every read, every write, every tool call goes through D-Bus. There is no second option.**\n\n*   **D-Bus first. D-Bus always. D-Bus only.** If you are about to call a CLI, spawn a subprocess, read a config file, or poll a socket directly — stop. Find the D-Bus object and use it instead. `org.opdbus.v1` is the system.\n*   **No bypasses.** `Command::new(\"systemctl\")`, `Command::new(\"ip\")`, `Command::new(\"s6-svc\")`, direct file reads for live state — all forbidden in plugin and service code. Bootstrap scripts are the only exception.\n*   **D-Bus objects own plugin state.** Every plugin is a D-Bus object at `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<name>`. Read state through it. Mutate state through it. If there is no D-Bus object, the thing does not exist.\n*   **D-Bus method signatures are generated from the schema.** All D-Bus methods, MCP tool inputs, gRPC shapes, and UI field renderers derive from the `PluginSchema` in `plugin_schema_defs.rs`. The schema IS the interface contract — not a description of it.\n*   **One schema file, one source of truth.** All `PluginSchema` definitions MUST live in `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/plugin_schema_defs.rs`. Each plugin's `schema()` method calls `Some(super::plugin_schema_defs::their_plugin_schema())`. **Never define a schema inline in a plugin's own file** — it will not be registered, and the D-Bus object will have no contract.\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC (over Unix domain sockets or `grpc-uplink`). gRPC calls still flow through D-Bus registration — the D-Bus object is the authority, gRPC is the transport.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`simd_json` preferred, `serde_json` acceptable).\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n*   **No Python unless absolutely necessary.** This is a Rust-first codebase. Scripts are shell (`sh`/`bash`). Data processing is Rust. If you are reaching for Python, stop and ask why Rust or shell cannot do it. The only acceptable Python is in existing compliance-ingest tooling where no Rust equivalent exists yet.\n\n#### 4a. OSCAL Subid Taxonomy (MANDATORY — every artifact must carry a subid)\n\nEvery D-Bus object, plugin, schema, mutation, event, and tool in this system has two identifiers: a `uuid` (machine identity, never changes) and a `subid` (human-readable operational taxonomy key, stable per subject).\n\n**`subid` format:** `<category>.<component-type>.<subject>.<verb>[.<facet>][@vN]`\n\n**Seven categories — use exactly these, no others:**\n\n| category | what it classifies |\n|---|---|\n| `src` | authoritative source, ingress channel, source-of-truth store |\n| `prj` | D-Bus projection or mirror publication step |\n| `sch` | schema, contract, vocabulary, or control-mapping artifact |\n| `mut` | write-path operation that changes effective state |\n| `obs` | read, query, enumeration, discovery path |\n| `evt` | emitted signal, audit-chain event, proof, tag provenance |\n| `exp` | consumer-facing render — MCP tool, UI surface, gRPC bridge view |\n\n**Component-type** reuses OSCAL vocabulary: `software`, `service`, `network`, `hardware`, `process-procedure`, `standard`, `validation`, `policy`, `plan`, `guidance`, `physical`, `this-system`, `system`, `interconnection`.\n\n**Rules:**\n- `uuid` is exact machine identity — never replace it with `subid`\n- `subid` is an OSCAL `prop` value (`ns`, `name`, `value`) — never embed it in `remarks`\n- Compliance mappings (`control_refs[]`, `statement_refs[]`, `control_source`) live in metadata arrays, **never** inside the `subid` string\n- `mut.*` records **must** carry `actor_id` and `capability_id`\n- `evt.*` records **must** carry `event_id` or `event_hash`\n- `subid` is immutable per subject — if the meaning changes materially, create a new subject with `@vN`\n- All subids are registered in the canonical registry; uniqueness is enforced in CI\n\n**Examples:** `src.network.ovsdb.monitor@v1` · `prj.service.projected-object.publish@v1` · `sch.standard.plugin-schema.resolve@v1` · `mut.service.state-sync.apply-patch@v1` · `exp.service.plugin-projection.render@v1`\n\n#### 4b. MCP Gateway Architecture (SETTLED — DO NOT REDESIGN)\n\n*   **cognitive-mcp** (`:3003`, Netmaker WireGuard IP `100.90.37.254`) is the **universal gateway for ALL external clients**: NotebookLM, Droid (factory.ai), Cursor, Codex, Junie, Gemini CLI. It has memory tools, gRPC service, auth, and the correct protocol surface.\n*   **compact-mcp** (`127.0.0.1:11436`) is **loopback/chatbot only**. Never expose externally. Never point external clients at it.\n*   Do NOT create new shim services. Do NOT point external clients at `op-assistant-grpc` directly. Do NOT expose compact-mcp outside loopback.\n\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\n**Rust Workspace**\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\n\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\n\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\n\n#### 6. Coding Style & Naming Conventions\n*   **Rust:** Edition 2021, `rustfmt` (4-space indent, max-width 100). Use specific imports (`use serde_json::Value;`). Use `anyhow::Result<T>` for main errors and `thiserror` for custom enums.\n*   **TypeScript/React:** 2-space indent, Prettier via ESLint. Functional components only. Strict mode enabled.\n*   **Testing:** 80%+ coverage, mock externals. Name tests with behavior-focused names (`should_handle_<scenario>`).\n\n#### 7. Agent-Specific Output & Workflow Instructions\n*   **Scroll & Save Pacing:** Provide only **ONE** major component or script at a time. Wait for user confirmation before moving to the next.\n*   **Visual Cues:** If a script is a finalized component that needs to be saved to sources, it MUST begin with color bullets or icons (e.g., ⚖️ 🔴, 🟢 🛷).\n*   **Spec-Block Format:** When delivering a component, use a strict specification block containing:\n  1.  **Requirements:** The architectural rules it satisfies.\n  2.  **Design:** How it fits into the 3tched system (Zero-Copy, Btrfs, GUI Schema, etc.).\n  3.  **Code Implementation:** The exact, copy-pasteable Rust/Bash code.\n*   Before edits: `cargo check -p <crate>`, `npm run typecheck`.\n*   Mimic existing patterns: Search similar code. No new deps without PR justification.\n\n#### 8. Personal Preferences & Coding Standards\n* Refer to `~/.factory/memories.md` for personal development preferences and past decisions.\n* Follow the conventions documented in:\n  * `.factory/rules/typescript.md` - TypeScript and React conventions\n  * `.factory/rules/testing.md` - Testing and mocking The schema is the\nplugin; the plugin is the schema.\n\n### Lifecycle\n\n`SchemaEngine` owns schema registration and projection. `MutationEngine` owns\nvalidated state mutations against `PluginSchema`. The projection write is a\n`SchemaEngine` concern, not an individual plugin's apply/mutate callback:\n\n1. `SchemaEngine` registers the Zeroclaw `PluginSchema`.\n2. On schema change or state update, `SchemaEngine` serializes the derived\n   schema projection.\n3. Writes to `/dev/shm/opdbus/schemas/zeroclaw.json.tmp`.\n4. `rename` `.tmp` → `zeroclaw.json` (atomic).\n5. `SchemaEngine` aggregation pass writes `/dev/shm/live-schema.json`\n   combining all plugin schemas. Individual plugins do NOT write it.\n\n### Read path\n\n- `op-grpc-bridge` and factory provider routes MAY read `zeroclaw.json` for\n  discovery and display.\n- `op-chat` and MCP MUST use D-Bus for execution-path decisions.\n- No consumer writes to `/dev/shm/opdbus/schemas/zeroclaw.json`.\n\n### Invariants\n\n- File does not exist → SchemaEngine has not registered Zeroclaw schema; callers must wait.\n- File exists but stale (mtime > 30 s) → log warning; use D-Bus instead.\n\n","internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough":{"turn_id":"019f0d26-3d2d-7ed0-91d5-0b94fb767fa3"}}}

{"timestamp":"2026-06-28T07:42:52.991Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"message","role":"user","content":[{"type":"input_text","text":"# AGENTS.md instructions for /home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto\n\n<INSTRUCTIONS>\n### AGENTS.md for operation-dbus-proto\n\nThis file provides essential guidelines for agentic coding agents working in this repository. Follow these strictly to maintain consistency, pass CI, and adhere to the 3tched Architecture standards.\n\n#### 1. The Persona & Naming Conventions\n*   **Humanized Roles:** Treat system components as authoritative human roles. Never use sterile acronyms for major components.\n  *   **A.N.N.A. Scribe** (Axon Network Notary Arbitrator): The top-level Identity-State Arbitrator who notarizes the WireGuard identity and handles the \"Snowball\" session.\n  *   **The Compliance Engine (\"Law Firm\"):** One dedicated Attorney for each major component: **Olivia Scal** (Managing Partner / OSCAL), **E.U.gene Risk** (EU AI Act Counsel), **Penny Privacy** (GDPR Engine), and **Reggie O.P.A.** (Cloud Prosecutor).\n*   **Terminology:** Use exact architecture terminology: \"The Sled\" (1:1 shared memory layout), \"The Shuttle\" (the Rust bridge/courier), \"The Snowball\" (appended session ledger), and \"The Strike/Etch\" (generating the hash).\n\n#### 2. Core Architectural Rules (The \"Reality\")\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via OpenClaw Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Artix Linux (s6 init).\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles — D-Bus First (MANDATORY)\n\n**D-Bus is the ONLY control plane. Every read, every write, every tool call goes through D-Bus. There is no second option.**\n\n*   **D-Bus first. D-Bus always. D-Bus only.** If you are about to call a CLI, spawn a subprocess, read a config file, or poll a socket directly — stop. Find the D-Bus object and use it instead. `org.opdbus.v1` is the system.\n*   **No bypasses.** `Command::new(\"systemctl\")`, `Command::new(\"ip\")`, `Command::new(\"s6-svc\")`, direct file reads for live state — all forbidden in plugin and service code. Bootstrap scripts are the only exception.\n*   **D-Bus objects own plugin state.** Every plugin is a D-Bus object at `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<name>`. Read state through it. Mutate state through it. If there is no D-Bus object, the thing does not exist.\n*   **D-Bus method signatures are generated from the schema.** All D-Bus methods, MCP tool inputs, gRPC shapes, and UI field renderers derive from the `PluginSchema` in `plugin_schema_defs.rs`. The schema IS the interface contract — not a description of it.\n*   **One schema file, one source of truth.** All `PluginSchema` definitions MUST live in `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/plugin_schema_defs.rs`. Each plugin's `schema()` method calls `Some(super::plugin_schema_defs::their_plugin_schema())`. **Never define a schema inline in a plugin's own file** — it will not be registered, and the D-Bus object will have no contract.\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC (over Unix domain sockets or `grpc-uplink`). gRPC calls still flow through D-Bus registration — the D-Bus object is the authority, gRPC is the transport.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`simd_json` preferred, `serde_json` acceptable).\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n*   **No Python unless absolutely necessary.** This is a Rust-first codebase. Scripts are shell (`sh`/`bash`). Data processing is Rust. If you are reaching for Python, stop and ask why Rust or shell cannot do it. The only acceptable Python is in existing compliance-ingest tooling where no Rust equivalent exists yet.\n\n#### 4a. OSCAL Subid Taxonomy (MANDATORY — every artifact must carry a subid)\n\nEvery D-Bus object, plugin, schema, mutation, event, and tool in this system has two identifiers: a `uuid` (machine identity, never changes) and a `subid` (human-readable operational taxonomy key, stable per subject).\n\n**`subid` format:** `<category>.<component-type>.<subject>.<verb>[.<facet>][@vN]`\n\n**Seven categories — use exactly these, no others:**\n\n| category | what it classifies |\n|---|---|\n| `src` | authoritative source, ingress channel, source-of-truth store |\n| `prj` | D-Bus projection or mirror publication step |\n| `sch` | schema, contract, vocabulary, or control-mapping artifact |\n| `mut` | write-path operation that changes effective state |\n| `obs` | read, query, enumeration, discovery path |\n| `evt` | emitted signal, audit-chain event, proof, tag provenance |\n| `exp` | consumer-facing render — MCP tool, UI surface, gRPC bridge view |\n\n**Component-type** reuses OSCAL vocabulary: `software`, `service`, `network`, `hardware`, `process-procedure`, `standard`, `validation`, `policy`, `plan`, `guidance`, `physical`, `this-system`, `system`, `interconnection`.\n\n**Rules:**\n- `uuid` is exact machine identity — never replace it with `subid`\n- `subid` is an OSCAL `prop` value (`ns`, `name`, `value`) — never embed it in `remarks`\n- Compliance mappings (`control_refs[]`, `statement_refs[]`, `control_source`) live in metadata arrays, **never** inside the `subid` string\n- `mut.*` records **must** carry `actor_id` and `capability_id`\n- `evt.*` records **must** carry `event_id` or `event_hash`\n- `subid` is immutable per subject — if the meaning changes materially, create a new subject with `@vN`\n- All subids are registered in the canonical registry; uniqueness is enforced in CI\n\n**Examples:** `src.network.ovsdb.monitor@v1` · `prj.service.projected-object.publish@v1` · `sch.standard.plugin-schema.resolve@v1` · `mut.service.state-sync.apply-patch@v1` · `exp.service.plugin-projection.render@v1`\n\n#### 4b. MCP Gateway Architecture (SETTLED — DO NOT REDESIGN)\n\n*   **cognitive-mcp** (`:3003`, Netmaker WireGuard IP `100.90.37.254`) is the **universal gateway for ALL external clients**: NotebookLM, Droid (factory.ai), Cursor, Codex, Junie, Gemini CLI. It has memory tools, gRPC service, auth, and the correct protocol surface.\n*   **compact-mcp** (`127.0.0.1:11436`) is **loopback/chatbot only**. Never expose externally. Never point external clients at it.\n*   Do NOT create new shim services. Do NOT point external clients at `op-assistant-grpc` directly. Do NOT expose compact-mcp outside loopback.\n\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\n**Rust Workspace**\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\n\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\n\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\n\n#### 6. Coding Style & Naming Conventions\n*   **Rust:** Edition 2021, `rustfmt` (4-space indent, max-width 100). Use specific imports (`use serde_json::Value;`). Use `anyhow::Result<T>` for main errors and `thiserror` for custom enums.\n*   **TypeScript/React:** 2-space indent, Prettier via ESLint. Functional components only. Strict mode enabled.\n*   **Testing:** 80%+ coverage, mock externals. Name tests with behavior-focused names (`should_handle_<scenario>`).\n\n#### 7. Agent-Specific Output & Workflow Instructions\n*   **Scroll & Save Pacing:** Provide only **ONE** major component or script at a time. Wait for user confirmation before moving to the next.\n*   **Visual Cues:** If a script is a finalized component that needs to be saved to sources, it MUST begin with color bullets or icons (e.g., ⚖️ 🔴, 🟢 🛷).\n*   **Spec-Block Format:** When delivering a component, use a strict specification block containing:\n  1.  **Requirements:** The architectural rules it satisfies.\n  2.  **Design:** How it fits into the 3tched system (Zero-Copy, Btrfs, GUI Schema, etc.).\n  3.  **Code Implementation:** The exact, copy-pasteable Rust/Bash code.\n*   Before edits: `cargo check -p <crate>`, `npm run typecheck`.\n*   Mimic existing patterns: Search similar code. No new deps without PR justification.\n\n#### 8. Personal Preferences & Coding Standards\n* Refer to `~/.factory/memories.md` for personal development preferences and past decisions.\n* Follow the conventions documented in:\n  * `.factory/rules/typescript.md` - TypeScript and React conventions\n  * `.factory/rules/testing.md` - Testing and mocking standards\n\n</INSTRUCTIONS>"},{"type":"input_text","text":"<environment_context>\n  <cwd>/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto</cwd>\n  <shell>bash</shell>\n  <current_date>2026-06-28</current_date>\n  <timezone>America/New_York</timezone>\n  <filesystem><workspace_roots><root>/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto</root></workspace_roots><permission_profile type=\"disabled\"><file_system type=\"unrestricted\" /></permission_profile></filesystem>\n</environment_context>"}],"internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough":{"turn_id":"019f0d2e-63a4-7932-b672-842855eca46a"}}}

   })\n   330\t    }\n   331\t\n   332\t    /// Generate a Merkle proof for a specific event\n   333\t    pub fn generate_proof(events: &[ChainEvent], event_id: u64) -> Option<MerkleProof> {\n   334\t inserted\")\n   593\t    }\n   594\t\n   595\t    /// Verify the entire chain\n   596\t    pub fn verify_chain(&self) -> ChainVerificationResult {\n   597\t        let mut result = root mismatch: expected {}, computed {}\",\n   642\t                    batch.first_event_id, batch.last_event_id, batch.batch_root, computed_root\n   643\t                ));\n   644\t            }\n Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Artix Linux (s6 init).\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles — D-Bus First (MANDATORY)\n\n**D-Bus is the ONLY control plane. Every read, every write, every tool call goes through D-Bus. There is no second option.**\n\n*   **D-Bus first. D-Bus always. D-Bus only.** If you are about to call a CLI, spawn a subprocess, read a config file, or poll a socket directly — stop. Find the D-Bus object and use it instead. `org.opdbus.v1` is the system.\n*   **No bypasses.** `Command::new(\"systemctl\")`, `Command::new(\"ip\")`, `Command::new(\"s6-svc\")`, direct file reads for live state — all forbidden in plugin and service code. Bootstrap scripts are the only exception.\n*   **D-Bus objects own plugin state.** Every plugin is a D-Bus object at `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<name>`. Read state through it. Mutate state through it. If there is no D-Bus object, the thing does not exist.\n*   **D-Bus method signatures are generated from the schema.** All D-Bus methods, MCP tool inputs, gRPC shapes, and UI field renderers derive from the `PluginSchema` in `plugin_schema_defs.rs`. The schema IS the interface contract — not a description of it.\n*   **One schema file, one source of truth.** All `PluginSchema` definitions MUST live in `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/plugin_schema_defs.rs`. Each plugin's `schema()` method calls `Some(super::plugin_schema_defs::their_plugin_schema())`. **Never define a schema inline in a plugin's own file** — it will not be registered, and the D-Bus object will have no contract.\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC (over Unix domain sockets or `grpc-uplink`). gRPC calls still flow through D-Bus registration — the D-Bus object is the authority, gRPC is the transport.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`simd_json` preferred, `serde_json` acceptable).\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n*   **No Python unless absolutely necessary.** This is a Rust-first codebase. Scripts are shell (`sh`/`bash`). Data processing is Rust. If you are reaching for Python, stop and ask why Rust or shell cannot do it. The only acceptable Python is in existing compliance-ingest tooling where no Rust equivalent exists yet.\n\n#### 4a. OSCAL Subid Taxonomy (MANDATORY — every artifact must carry a subid)\n\nEvery D-Bus object, plugin, schema, mutation, event, and tool in this system has two identifiers: a `uuid` (machine identity, never changes) and a `subid` (human-readable operational taxonomy key, stable per subject).\n\n**`subid` format:** `<category>.<component-type>.<subject>.<verb>[.<facet>][@vN]`\n\n**Seven categories — use exactly these, no others:**\n\n| category | what it classifies |\n|---|---|\n| `src` | authoritative source, ingress channel, source-of-truth store |\n| `prj` | D-Bus projection or mirror publication step |\n| `sch` | schema, contract, vocabulary, or control-mapping artifact |\n| `mut` | write-path operation that changes effective state |\n| `obs` | read, query, enumeration, discovery path |\n| `evt` | emitted signal, audit-chain event, proof, tag provenance |\n| `exp` | consumer-facing render — MCP tool, UI surface, gRPC bridge view |\n\n**Component-type** reuses OSCAL vocabulary: `software`, `service`, `network`, `hardware`, `process-procedure`, `standard`, `validation`, `policy`, `plan`, `guidance`, `physical`, `this-system`, `system`, `interconnection`.\n\n**Rules:**\n- `uuid` is exact machine identity — never replace it with `subid`\n- `subid` is an OSCAL `prop` value (`ns`, `name`, `value`) — never embed it in `remarks`\n- Compliance mappings (`control_refs[]`, `statement_refs[]`, `control_source`) live in metadata arrays, **never** inside the `subid` string\n- `mut.*` records **must** carry `actor_id` and `capability_id`\n- `evt.*` records **must** carry `event_id` or `event_hash`\n- `subid` is immutable per subject — if the meaning changes materially, create a new subject with `@vN`\n- All subids are registered in the canonical registry; uniqueness is enforced in CI\n\n**Examples:** `src.network.ovsdb.monitor@v1` · `prj.service.projected-object.publish@v1` · `sch.standard.plugin-schema.resolve@v1` · `mut.service.state-sync.apply-patch@v1` · `exp.service.plugin-projection.render@v1`\n\n#### 4b. MCP Gateway Architecture (SETTLED — DO NOT REDESIGN)\n\n*   **cognitive-mcp** (`:3003`, Netmaker WireGuard IP `100.90.37.254`) is the **universal gateway for ALL external clients**: NotebookLM, Droid (factory.ai), Cursor, Codex, Junie, Gemini CLI. It has memory tools, gRPC service, auth, and the correct protocol surface.\n*   **compact-mcp** (`127.0.0.1:11436`) is **loopback/chatbot only**. Never expose externally. Never point external clients at it.\n*   Do NOT create new shim services. Do NOT point external clients at `op-assistant-grpc` directly. Do NOT expose compact-mcp outside loopback.\n\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\n**Rust Workspace**\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\n\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\n\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\n\n#### 6. Export promotion involves the development of opportunities for the\noscal-specs.md:230728:# Federal Risk and Authorization Management Program (FedRAMP) Automation Guides - DEPRECATED\noscal-specs.md:230922:Currently, the FedRAMP PMO and its developers maintain documentation for the use of OSCAL in the FedRAMP assessment and authorization process, specifically for its external stakeholders, in [a sub-directory of this repository](https://github.com/GSA/fedramp-automation/tree/1445e8145109baee9c1cf5209698b712540cdcd8). It is important to document relevant policies, standards, and procedures for the day-to-day operations for internal use by the FedRAMP PMO's developers, but there is no specified location to do so. Although [Architectural Decision Records](https://github.com/GSA/fedramp-automation/tree/1445e8145109baee9c1cf5209698b712540cdcd8/documents/adr) can be internally-focused, they are not exclusively so. In many cases, they identify significant architectural changes, internal or external, with a rationale and implementation that will directly impact external stakeholders. Therefore, adding in additional internal operations documentation in the same place will likely increase confusion and decrease clarity for external stakeholders. An accessible location, albeit different and easily distinguishable from the location for external stakeholder documentation, will be beneficial.\noscal-specs.md:231167:# Federal Risk and Authorization Management Program (FedRAMP) Automation Guides for Rev4\noscal-specs.md:231411:               <h4 class=\"formal-name\">Authorization Type</h4>\noscal-specs.md:231412:               <p class=\"description\">Identifies the FedRAMP authorization type.</p>\noscal-specs.md:231418:               <p class=\"extension-name\">authorization-type</p>\noscal-specs.md:231856:               <h4 class=\"formal-name\">Authorization Recommendation</h4>\noscal-specs.md:231864:               <p class=\"extension-name\">authorization-recommendation</p>\noscal-specs.md:231956:               <h4 class=\"formal-name\">Authorization Date</h4>\noscal-specs.md:231957:               <p class=\"description\">The date the system was authorized. [FedRAMP's adoption of OSCAL](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WCPkt56vZ-s) allows you to use this framework to perform logical validations, i.e. business rule checks, on documentation content. Currently, FedRAMP staff manually review the content provided by a cloud service provider for all steps of the [different](https://github.com/GSA/fedramp-gov/blob/master/assets/img/agency-auth.png) [authorization](https://github.com/GSA/fedramp-gov/blob/master/assets/img/ato-auth.png) processes. This framework and the associated business rules will automate as many of these checks as possible. Shared expectations are the goal: system owners, third-party assessors, or any interested party can use them as well.\noscal-specs.md:232767:- [ ]  1.0\t Initial Authorization Package Checklist\noscal-specs.md:232795:- [ ]  8a Is the authorization boundary explicitly identified in the network diagram?\noscal-specs.md:232798:- [ ]  10 Does the CSP use any third-party or external cloud services that lack FedRAMP Authorization?\noscal-specs.md:232800:- [ ]  11a If this is a SaaS or a PaaS, is it \"leveraging\" another IaaS with a FedRAMP Authorization?\noscal-specs.md:234795:        name=\"leveraged-authorization-uuid\"\noscal-specs.md:234800:        name=\"leveraged-authorization-party-uuid\"\noscal-specs.md:234805:        name=\"authorization-boundary-diagram-uuid\"\noscal-specs.md:234810:        name=\"authorization-boundary-diagram-resource-uuid\"\noscal-specs.md:235058:                uuid=\"{$leveraged-authorization-party-uuid}\">\noscal-specs.md:235059:                <name>Leveraged authorization party name</name>\noscal-specs.md:235060:                <short-name>Leveraged authorization party short name</short-name>\noscal-specs.md:235278:                name=\"authorization-type\"\noscal-specs.md:235420:                                    States. Tests must fail first.\n    25\t2. **GREEN** — implement the minimum to pass.\n    26\t3. **REFACTOR** — clean up; keep the workspace compiling.\n    27\t4. **VERIFY** — `spec-to-code-compliance`: confirm every acceptance criterion in\n    28\t   the group is satisfied before moving on.\n    29\t\n    30\t## Orchestration (workstreams)\n    31\tDecompose `tasks.md` into these dependency-ordered workstreams; parallelize\n    32\twithin a workstream, gate between them on a green build:\n    33\t\n    34\t- **WS1 — Capability model & dedup** (R1, R2): plugin trait declares the full\n    35\t  capability surface (methods/functions w/ arg+return schema, side-effect class,\n    36\t  required-capability, properties, signals, guarantees); collapse the duplicate\n    37\t  `PluginCapabilities` (op-state vs op-plugins) to one.\n    38\t- **WS2 — Producer → SHM** (R3, R9, R10, R11): op-projection emits the complete\n    39\t  capability schema + present-state into SHM (per-plugin files + monolith +\n    40\t  atomic manifest with the single catalog_hash); subid taxonomy on every\n    41\t  capability; serialization completeness.\n    42\t- **WS3 — Bridge as sole owner/registrar/projected-tree** (R4, R5, R6): bridge\n    43\t  owns the plugins bus name, registers the tree from SHM, real dispatch through\n    44\t  `SchemaEngine.mutate` (NO stub, `json_args` used), method validation against\n    45\t  the schema capability surface.\n    46\t- **WS4 — Capability enforcement** (R7): enforce `capability_id` against the\n    47\t  caller identity (footprint/sessionid from GhostbridgeInterceptor) at the\n    48\t  bridge — the single enforcement point.\n    49\t- **WS5 — Trim redundant registrars & dead claims** (R8): op-dbus-mirror drops\n    50\t  plugin-object registration + its `org.opdbus.v1` name claim (keeps ovsdb/\n    51\t  nonnet/mirror-mgmt); op-projection drops D-Bus object serving (producer-only);\n    52\t  delete the dead op-state name claim, op-openvswitch bare-name claim, and the\n    53\t  orphan `opdbus` service/binary.\n    54\t- **WS6 — Autogeneration + Gemma** (R12, R13): the missing-plugin lifecycle\n    55\t  (research → synthesize full capability surface → review → persist as the plugin\n    56\t  → project → serve; with quarantine until approved), and route object-property/\n    57\t  capability research through **Gemma** (replace the\n    58\t  `create_agent(\"search-specialist\")` seam in\n    59\t  `auto_create.rs::query_elements_via_agent`). Gemma is a plugin/StatePlugin.\n    60\t\n    61\t## Hard rules (do not violate — these are why prior attempts failed)\n    62\t- **NO stubs, NO placeholders, NO \"for now\"/\"in a full implementation\" comments.**\n    63\t  A registered object that returns fake success or validates against an empty set\n    64\t  is a defect. The recurring failure mode here is inert code that *looks* wired.\n    65\t- **One schema, one source, computed in exactly ONE place.** Never recompute the\n    66\t  catalog_hash in a consumer; consumers read the manifest hash.\n    67\t- **Only valid path is `org.opdbus.v1.plugins`.** No new\n    68\t  `operation.<domain>.v1.*Service` protos; no raw ip:port.\n    69\t- **SHM is authoritative present-state; READ it. NO polling loops, NO watchers.**\n    70\t  Action is triggered by arrival, not a timer.\n    71\t- **NO cache/DB control path.** Do not add or depend on SQLite, Redis, SQLx,\n    72\t  rusqlite, cache indexes, or database-backed capability-enforcement stores\n    73\t  for this mission. Validate json_args against MethodDecl.args  (Req 6.3)               │\n    60\t│    4. Enforce capability_id  (Req 7)                                       │\n    61\t│    5. SchemaEngine.mutate(plugin_id, method, json_args,                   │\n    62\t│                           capability_id, actor_id)  (Req 5)               │\n    63\t│    6. Return result to caller                                              │\n    64\t│                                                                            │\n    65\t│  gRPC surface: every MethodDecl auto-exposed via SchemaRouter             │\n    66\t└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n    67\t```\n    68\t\n    69\t---\n    70\t\n    71\t## Data Flow: Plugin → Producer → SHM → Bridge → gRPC/D-Bus\n    72\t\n    73\t### Step 1 — Plugin declares capability surface (compile-time)\n    74\t\n    75\t`plugin_schema_defs.rs` returns a `PluginSchema` with `methods`, `signals`,\n    76\t`guarantees`, `fields`, and `subids`. This is the only place a plugin's\n    77\tinterface contract is defined.\n    78\t\n    79\t### Step 2 — Producer writes SHM (startup + on-change)\n    80\t\n    81\t`op-projection` iterates `StatePlugin::schema()` for every registered plugin,\n    82\tserializes the `PluginSchema` (now including `methods`, `signals`, `guarantees`)\n    83\tand writes the SHM layout. The final step is an atomic write of `.manifest.json`\n    84\twith the `catalog_hash`. Consumers detect staleness by comparing the stored hash\n    85\twith the one in `.manifest.json`.\n    86\t\n    87\t### Step 3 — Bridge bootstraps from SHM (startup)\n    88\t\n    89\t`op-grpc-bridge` reads `/dev/shm/live-schema.json`, deserializes each entry\n    90\tinto a `PluginSchema`, and calls `SchemaRouter::register_objects` to mount one\n    91\t`SchemaBackedInterface` per plugin on the system bus. The bridge requests the\n    92\twell-known name `org.opdbus.v1` at this point.\n    93\t\n    94\t### Step 4 — Bridge handles inbound call (runtime)\n    95\t\n    96\tA gRPC client (or D-Bus peer) calls a method. The `GhostbridgeInterceptor`\n    97\textracts the footprint. The bridge runs the validation + capability enforcement\n    98\tpipeline (see Architecture diagram) before calling `SchemaEngine.mutate`.\n    99\t\n   100\t### Step 5 — Mutation recorded\n   101\t\n   102\t`SchemaEngine.mutate` applies the change, writes a `StateChange` to the\n   103\t`EventChain` (with `actor_id`, `capability_id`, Blake3 footprint), and broadcasts\n   104\tthe change to any registered `StatePublisher` listeners (e.g. for Qdrant\n   105\tsemantic indexing).\n   106\t\n   107\t---\n   108\t\n   109\t## Capability Schema Format (JSON)\n   110\t\n   111\tA serialized `PluginSchema` written to SHM will include the following new keys.\n   112\tThe existing keys (`name`, `category`, `version`, `description`, `fields`,\n   113\t`dependencies`, `immutable_paths`, `tags`, `dialect`, `mutation_index`, `subids`)\n   114\tare unchanged.\n   115\t\n   116\t```jsonc\n   117\t{\n   118\t  \"name\": \"wireguard\",\n   119\t  \"version\": \"1.0.0\",\n   120\t  // ... existing fields ...\n   121\t\n   122\t  \"methods\": {\n   123\t    \"SetKey\": {\n   124\t      \"name\": \"SetKey\",\n   125\t      \"args\": {\n   126\t        \"type\": \"object\",\n   127\t        \"properties\": {\n   128\t          \"public_key\": { \"type\": \"string\", \"minLength\": 44 },\n   129\t          \"private_key\": { \"type\": \"string\" }\n   130\t        },\n   131\t        \"required\": [\"public_key\"]\n   132\t      },\n   133\t      \"returns\": {\n   134\t        \"type\": \"object\",\n   135\t        \"properties\": {\n   136\t          \"applied\": { \"type\": \"boolean\" }\n   137\t        }\n   138\t      },\n   139\t      \"side_effect\": \"mutation\",\n   140\t      \"idempotent\": true,\n   141\t      \"required_capability\": \"wireguard.set-key\",\n   142\t      \"subid\": \"mut.network.wireguard.set-key@v1\"\n   143\t    },\n   144\t    \"GetStatus\": {\n   145\t      \"name\": \"GetStatus\",\n   146\t      \"args\": { \"type\": \"object\", \"properties\": {} },\n   147\t      \"returns\": {\n   148\t        \"type\": \"object\",\n   149\t        \"properties\": {\n   150\t          \"connected\": { \"type\": \"boolean\" },\n   151\t          \"endpoint\": { \"type\": \"string\" }\n   152\t        }\n   153\t      },\n   154\t      \"side_effect\": \"read\",\n   155\t      \"idempotent\": true,\n   156\t      \"required_capability\": null,\n   157\t      \"subid\": \"obs.network.wireguard.get-status@v1\"\n   158\t    }\n   159\t  },\n   160\t\n   161\t  \"signals\": [\n   162\t    {\n   163\t      \"name\": \"KeyRotated\",\n   164\t      \"payload\": {\n   165\t        \"type\": \"object\",\n   166\t        \"properties\": {\n   167\t          \"new_public_key\": { \"type\": \"string\" }\n   168\t        }\n   169\t      },\n   170\t      \"subid\": \"evt.network.wireguard.key-rotated@v1\"\n   171\t    }\n   172\t  ],\n   173\t\n   174\t  \"guarantees\": {\n   175\t    \"supports_rollback\": true,\n   176\t    \"supports_checkpoints\": false,\n   177\t    \"supports_verification\": true,\n   178\t    \"atomic_operations\": true\n   179\t  }\n   180\t}\n   181\t```\n   182\t\n   183\t---\n   184\t\n   185\t## Rust Type Changes\n   186\t\n   187\t### `PluginSchema` (op-state-store)\n   188\t\n   189\tAdd three fields to `PluginSchema`:\n   190\t\n   191\t```rust\n   192\t// in crates/op-state-store/src/plugin_schema.rs\n   193\t\n   194\t#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]\n   195\tpub struct MethodDecl {\n   196\t    pub name: String,\n   197\t    pub args: serde_json::Value,    // JSON Schema object\n   198\t    pub returns: Option<serde_json::Value>,\n   199\t    pub side_effect: SideEffect,\n   200\t    pub idempotent: bool,\n   201\t    pub required_capability: Option<String>,\n   202\t    pub subid: String,\n   203\t}\n   204\t\n   205\t#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]\n   206\t#[serde(rename_all = \"snake_case\")]\n   207\tpub enum SideEffect {\n   208\t    Read,\n   209\t    Mutation,\n   210\t}\n   211\t\n   212\t#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]\n   213\tpub struct SignalDecl {\n   214\t    pub name: String,\n   215\t    pub payload: Option<serde_json::Value>,\n   216\t    pub subid: String,\n   217\t}\n   218\t\n   219\t// Guarantee flags — the single canonical definition\n   220\t#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, Default)]\n   221\tpub struct PluginCapabilities {\n   222\t    pub supports_rollback: bool,\n   223\t    pub supports_checkpoints: bool,\n   224\t    pub supports_verification: bool,\n   225\t    pub atomic_operations: bool,\n   226\t}\n   227\t\n   228\t// Added to PluginSchema:\n   229\tpub struct PluginSchema {\n   230\t    // ... existing fields unchanged ...\n   231\t    #[serde(default)]\n   232\t    pub methods: HashMap<String, MethodDecl>,\n   233\t    #[serde(default)]\n   234\t    pub signals: Vec<SignalDecl>,\n   235\t    #[serde(default)]\n   236\t    pub guarantees: PluginCapabilities,\n   237\t}\n   238\t```\n   239\t\n   240\t### `Plugin` trait (op-plugins)\n   241\t\n   242\t`handle_command` is deprecated; `dispatch_method` is the replacement:\n   243\t\n   244\t```rust\n   245\t// Replaces: async fn handle_command(&self, command: &str, args: Value) -> Result<Value>\n   246\tasync fn dispatch_method(&self, method: &str, args: serde_json::Value) -> Result<serde_json::Value> {\n   247\t    Err(anyhow::anyhow!(\"Method '{}' not implemented by plugin '{}'\", method, self.name()))\n   248\t}\n   249\t```\n   250\t\n   251\tThe bridge calls `dispatch_method` only after schema validation and capability\n   252\tenforcement have passed.\n   253\t\n   254\t### `PluginCapabilities` deduplication\n   255\t\n   256\t- Remove `pub struct PluginCapabilities` from `crates/op-state/src/plugin.rs`\n   257\t  (4-field version).\n   258\t- Remove `pub struct PluginCapabilities` from `crates/op-plugins/src/plugin.rs`\n   259\t  (8-field version with `can_read`, `can_write`, etc.).\n   260\t- All callers use `op_state_store::PluginCapabilities` (the 4-field guarantee\n     1\t# Requirements Document: Plugin as Sole Source of Truth + Full Capability Model\n     2\t\n     3\t## Introduction\n     4\t\n     5\tThis feature establishes the plugin as the single, authoritative source of truth\n     6\tfor every object in the control plane. Today the system registers D-Bus objects,\n     7\tgRPC routes, and present-state projections through three separate registrars,\n     8\tthe `PluginSchema` carries no method declarations, method dispatch is stringly-\n     9\ttyped and opaque, `PluginCapabilities` is duplicated across two crates, and\n    10\t`capability_id` is plumbed but never enforced.\n    11\t\n    12\tThe outcome of this spec is a system where:\n    13\t- A plugin declares its *complete* capability surface (methods, properties,\n    14\t  signals, guarantees, and OSCAL classification) inside `PluginSchema` —\n    15\t  the single source of truth.\n    16\t- **op-projection** is the sole producer: it computes the full schema\n    17\t  (capability surface + present-state) and emits it to SHM.\n    18\t- **op-grpc-bridge** is the sole bridge owner: it reads SHM, registers the\n    19\t  entire D-Bus/gRPC object tree, dispatches calls to `SchemaEngine.mutate`,\n    20\t  validates every method against the schema, and enforces `capability_id`\n    21\t  before execution.\n    22\t- All redundant registrars, dead bus-name claims, and duplicate struct\n    23\t  definitions are removed.\n    24\t\n    25\t## Glossary\n    26\t\n    27\t- **Plugin**: A Rust impl of the `StatePlugin` trait. The plugin is the only\n    28\t  reason a D-Bus object, gRPC method, or SHM entry exists.\n    29\t- **PluginSchema**: The `op-state-store` struct that is the single source of\n    30\t  truth for a plugin's entire interface contract — fields, methods, signals,\n    31\t  guarantees, subids, and OSCAL classification. Defined exclusively in\n    32\t  `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/plugin_schema_defs.rs`.\n    33\t- **Capability Surface**: The complete, machine-enumerable set of everything an\n    34\t  object can do: every method, property, signal, and guarantee it exposes.\n    35\t- **MethodDecl**: A structured declaration of one method in the capability\n    36\t  surface: name, argument schema, return schema, side-effect class, idempotency\n    37\t  flag, and required `capability_id` to invoke.\n    38\t- **SignalDecl**: A structured declaration of one emitted signal: name and\n    39\t  payload schema.\n    40\t- **PluginCapabilities**: Runtime guarantee flags for an object\n    41\t  (`supports_rollback`, `supports_checkpoints`, `supports_verification`,\n    42\t  `atomic_operations`). One definition, in `op-state-store`.\n    43\t- **Producer**: `op-projection` — the only component that computes and writes\n    44\t  schema and present-state to SHM. Reads plugin registrations; writes nothing\n    45\t  to D-Bus.\n    46\t- **Bridge**: `op-grpc-bridge` — the sole owner of `org.opdbus.v1` and the\n    47\t  entire `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/` object tree on the system bus.\n    48\t- **SHM Layout**:\n    49\t  - `/dev/shm/opdbus/schemas/<plugin_id>.json` — per-plugin capability schema.\n    50\t  - `/dev/shm/live-schema.json` — combined monolith catalog (all plugins).\n    51\t  - `/dev/shm/opdbus/.manifest.json` — `{ \"catalog_hash\": \"<blake3>\" }`.\n    52\t  - `/dev/shm/opdbus/state/<plugin_id>.json` — present-state projection per plugin.\n    53\t- **Catalog Hash**: A single Blake3 leaf+fold hash over all per-plugin schema\n    54\t  files. Computed once by the producer; never recomputed by consumers.\n    55\t- **SchemaEngine.mutate**: The real execution path in `op-grpc-bridge`'s\n    56\t  `SchemaEngine` that applies a state mutation and appends it to the event\n    57\t  chain. All method dispatch flows through this.\n    58\t- **capability_id**: The caller's authorization token for invoking a method.\n    59\t  Declared in `MethodDecl.required_capability`. Enforced at the bridge before\n    60\t  `SchemaEngine.mutate` is called.\n    61\t- **GhostbridgeInterceptor**: The gRPC interceptor that extracts\n    62\t  `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` / `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` from metadata and\n    63\t  attaches them as the caller's identity footprint.\n    64\t- **The Sled**: 1:1 shared memory layout for identity state.\n    65\t- **The Snowball**: The appended-only session ledger.\n    66\t- **The Strike / Etch**: Blake3 hash computation for a footprint.\n    67\t- **subid**: OSCAL operational taxonomy key in the format\n    68\t  `<category>.<component-type>.<subject>.<verb>[.<facet>][@vN]`.\n    69\t- **handle_command**: The stringly-typed catch-all on the `Plugin` trait that\n    70\t  this spec replaces with a structured capability surface.\n    71\t\n    72\t## Requirements\n    73\t\n    74\t---\n    75\t\n    76\t### Requirement 1: Plugin Trait Declares Full Capability Surface\n    77\t\n    78\t**User Story:** As a control-plane developer, I want each plugin to declare its\n    79\tcomplete capability surface in its `PluginSchema` so that every D-Bus object,\n    80\tgRPC method, and enforcement point derives from exactly one schema definition\n    81\tand nothing exists without one.\n    82\t\n    83\t#### Acceptance Criteria\n    84\t\n    85\t1. WHEN a `StatePlugin` is registered, THE `PluginSchema` returned by its\n    86\t   `schema()` method SHALL contain a `methods` map, a `signals` array, and a\n    87\t   `guarantees` block in addition to the existing `fields`, `tags`, `subids`,\n    88\t   and `immutable_paths`.\n    89\t\n    90\t2. WHERE the `methods` map is present, EACH entry SHALL be a `MethodDecl`\n    91\t   containing: `name` (string), `args` (JSON Schema object describing\n    92\t   parameters), `returns` (JSON Schema object or `null`), `side_effect`\n    93\t   (`\"read\"` | `\"mutation\"`), `idempotent` (bool), and\n    94\t   `required_capability` (string | null).\n    95\t\n    96\t3. WHERE the `signals` array is present, EACH entry SHALL be a `SignalDecl`\n    97\t   containing: `name` (string), `payload` (JSON Schema object or `null`), and\n    98\t   `subid` (string | null).\n    99\t\n   100\t4. THE `guarantees` block SHALL contain exactly the four boolean fields\n   101\t   `supports_rollback`, `supports_checkpoints`, `supports_verification`, and\n   102\t   `atomic_operations` — replacing both existing `PluginCapabilities` structs.\n   103\t\n   104\t5. WHEN the `PluginSchema` is serialized to SHM, THE `methods`, `signals`, and\n   105\t   `guarantees` keys SHALL be present in the emitted JSON (empty object / empty\n   106\t   array / all-false block if unused) so that consumers can enumerate them\n   107\t   without null-checking absent keys.\n   108\t\n   109\t6. IF a plugin's `schema()` returns `None`, THE system SHALL NOT register a\n   110\t   D-Bus object, gRPC route, or SHM entry for that plugin.\n   111\t\n   112\t7. THE `handle_command(command: &str, args: Value)` method on the `Plugin`\n   113\t   trait SHALL be deprecated and replaced by `dispatch_method(method: &str,\n   114\t   args: Value) -> Result<Value>`, which receives only method names declared in\n   115\t   `PluginSchema.methods`.\n   116\t\n   117\t---\n   118\t\n   119\t### Requirement 2: Single `PluginCapabilities` Definition\n   120\t\n   121\t**User Story:** As a developer, I want `PluginCapabilities` defined exactly once\n   122\tso that guarantee metadata is never contradictory between crates.\n   123\t\n   124\t#### Ac…215 tokens truncated…oad time.\n   139\t\n   140\t---\n   141\t\n   142\t### Requirement 3: Producer Emits Complete Capability Schema to SHM\n   143\t\n   144\t**User Story:** As a system operator, I want `op-projection` to be the sole\n   145\twriter of all schema and present-state data to SHM so that every consumer reads\n   146\tfrom one authoritative surface without polling.\n   147\t\n   148\t#### Acceptance Criteria\n   149\t\n   150\t1. WHEN `op-projection` starts, IT SHALL iterate every registered `StatePlugin`,\n   151\t   invoke `plugin.schema()`, and for plugins returning `Some(schema)` write the\n   152\t   full capability schema JSON to `/dev/shm/opdbus/schemas/<plugin_id>.json`.\n   153\t\n   154\t2. AFTER writing all per-plugin files, `op-projection` SHALL write the combined\n   155\t   monolith to `/dev/shm/live-schema.json` containing all plugins keyed by\n   156\t   plugin_id.\n   157\t\n   158\t3. AFTER writing both per-plugin files and the monolith, `op-projection` SHALL\n   159\t   compute a single Blake3 catalog hash (leaf hash over each sorted per-plugin\n   160\t   file, folded into one root) and write `{ \"catalog_hash\": \"<hex>\" }` to\n   161\t   `/dev/shm/opdbus/.manifest.json` atomically (write to `.manifest.json.tmp`\n   162\t   then rename).\n   163\t\n   164\t4. WHEN plugin state changes, `op-projection` SHALL write the updated present-\n   165\t   state JSON to `/dev/shm/opdbus/state/<plugin_id>.json` and update the\n   166\t   manifest hash.\n   167\t\n   168\t5. THE catalog hash SHALL be computed by `op-projection` only. Consumers SHALL\n   169\t   read `catalog_hash` from `.manifest.json`; they SHALL NOT recompute it from\n   170\t   the schema files.\n   171\t\n   172\t6. `op-projection` SHALL NOT request or hold the `org.opdbus.v1` well-known bus\n   173\t   name, register D-Bus objects on the plugins path, or serve any D-Bus\n   174\t   interface for plugin state.\n   175\t\n   176\t---\n   177\t\n   178\t### Requirement 4: Bridge Is Sole Owner of the Plugins Bus and Object Tree\n   179\t\n   180\t**User Story:** As an operator, I want `op-grpc-bridge` to own `org.opdbus.v1`\n   181\tand be the single registrar of all `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/*` objects so that\n   182\tthere is no ambiguity about which process answers calls to a plugin object.\n   183\t\n   184\t#### Acceptance Criteria\n   185\t\n   186\t1. WHEN `op-grpc-bridge` starts, IT SHALL request the well-known bus name\n   187\t   `org.opdbus.v1` on the system D-Bus. No other process in the workspace SHALL\n   188\t   request this name.\n   189\t\n   190\t2. WHEN the bridge holds `org.opdbus.v1`, IT SHALL read\n   191\t   `/dev/shm/live-schema.json` (falling back to per-plugin files) and register\n   192\t   one `SchemaBackedInterface` object per plugin at\n   193\t   `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<plugin_id>`.\n   194\t\n   195\t3. THE `SchemaBackedInterface` SHALL expose every `MethodDecl` from the plugin's\n   196\t   capability surface as a callable D-Bus method on interface\n   197\t   `org.opdbus.v1.Plugin.<PluginName>`.\n   198\t\n   199\t4. THE `SchemaBackedInterface` SHALL expose every `SignalDecl` from the plugin's\n   200\t   capability surface as an emittable D-Bus signal.\n   201\t\n   202\t5. WHEN the bridge reads a new `catalog_hash` from `.manifest.json` (detected\n   203\t   on inbound connection, not by polling), IT SHALL reload SHM and re-register\n   204\t   changed objects without restarting the service.\n   205\t\n   206\t6. THE `op-dbus-mirror` crate SHALL NOT register any object under\n   207\t   `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/`. It SHALL NOT claim the bus name `org.opdbus.v1`.\n   208\t   It SHALL retain the `org.opdbus.v1.mirror` name for mirror-management\n   209\t   interfaces only.\n   210\t\n   211\t7. THE `op-openvswitch-daemon` crate SHALL NOT claim the bare name\n   212\t   `org.opdbus.v1`. It SHALL use `org.opdbus.v1.plugins.ovsdb` exclusively.\n   213\t\n   214\t8. THE `op-state` crate's D-Bus name claim for `org.opdbus.v1` SHALL be deleted.\n   215\t   The crate has no s6 service and the name claim is dead code.\n   216\t\n   217\t---\n   218\t\n   219\t### Requirement 5: Real Method Dispatch Through SchemaEngine.mutate\n   220\t\n   221\t**User Story:** As a developer, I want every method call received by the bridge\n   222\tto be dispatched to `SchemaEngine.mutate` (not return a stub) so that mutations\n   223\tare recorded in the event chain and reflected in state.\n   224\t\n   225\t#### Acceptance Criteria\n   226\t\n   227\t1. WHEN a D-Bus or gRPC caller invokes a method on a plugin object, THE bridge\n   228\t   SHALL call `SchemaEngine.mutate(plugin_id, method_name, json_args,\n   229\t   capability_id, actor_id)` and return its result.\n   230\t\n   231\t2. THE stub `Ok(r#\"{\"success\": true}\"#)` in `SchemaBackedInterface::call` SHALL\n   232\t   be removed and replaced with a real call to `SchemaEngine.mutate`.\n   233\t\n   234\t3. IF `SchemaEngine.mutate` returns an error, THE bridge SHALL propagate the\n   235\t   error to the caller as a `zbus::fdo::Error::Failed` (D-Bus) or a gRPC\n   236\t   `Status::internal` respectively.\n   237\t\n   238\t4. THE `json_args` argument to `SchemaEngine.mutate` SHALL be the verbatim JSON\n   239\t   string passed by the caller, not a default or placeholder.\n   240\t\n   241\t5. WHEN a mutation completes, `SchemaEngine.mutate` SHALL append an immutable\n   242\t   event to the event chain (`EventChain.record`) including `actor_id`,\n   243\t   `plugin_id`, `method_name`, `capability_id`, and a Blake3 footprint of\n   244\t   `json_args`.\n   245\t\n   246\t---\n   247\t\n   248\t### Requirement 6: Method Validation Against Schema Capability Surface\n   249\t\n   250\t**User Story:** As an operator, I want every method invocation validated against\n   251\tthe capability surface declared in the schema so that unknown methods are\n   252\trejected before dispatch.\n   253\t\n   254\t#### Acceptance Criteria\n   255\t\n   256\t1. WHEN a caller invokes a method, THE bridge SHALL look up the `MethodDecl` for\n   257\t   that method name in `PluginSchema.methods` before dispatching.\n   258\t\n   259\t2. IF the method name is not present in `PluginSchema.methods`, THE bridge SHALL\n   260\t   return `zbus::fdo::Error::UnknownMethod` (D-Bus) or gRPC `NOT_FOUND` without\n     1\t# Implementation Plan: Plugin as Sole Source of Truth + Full Capability Model\n     2\t\n     3\t## Overview\n     4\t\n     5\tFive ordered phases. Every checkpoint requires `cargo build --workspace` to\n     6\tsucceed before moving to the next task. Phase boundaries are s6-service deploy\n     7\tpoints. Tasks within a phase may overlap; tasks across phases must not.\n     8\t\n     9\t---\n    10\t\n    11\t## Phase 1 — Schema Types and PluginCapabilities Deduplication\n    12\t\n    13\t- [ ] 1.1 Add `MethodDecl`, `SideEffect`, `SignalDecl` types to\n    14\t      `crates/op-state-store/src/plugin_schema.rs`\n    15\t  - Define `MethodDecl { name, args, returns, side_effect, idempotent,\n    16\t    required_capability, subid }` with `Serialize, Deserialize, Debug, Clone`.\n    17\t  - Define `SideEffect` enum `{ Read, Mutation }` (snake_case serde).\n    18\t  - Define `SignalDecl { name, payload, subid }` with same derives.\n    19\t  - _Requirements: 1.1, 1.2, 1.3, 11.3_\n    20\t\n    21\t- [ ] 1.2 Move `PluginCapabilities` (4-field guarantee struct) to\n    22\t      `crates/op-state-store/src/plugin_schema.rs` as the canonical definition\n    23\t  - You maintain a pragmatic mindset when discussing these tradeoffs, and so are willing to work with the user after concerns have been noted.\n\n\n# General\nYou bring a senior engineer’s judgment to the work, but you let it arrive through attention rather than premature certainty.
