{"timestamp":"2026-06-28T15:00:04.357Z","type":"event_msg","payload":{"type":"agent_message","message":"To get `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins` owned on the opdbus session bus, set the projection server back to session bus:\n\n```bash\nOP_DBUS_PROJECTION_BUS=session\nDBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS=unix:path=/run/opdbus/session-bus.sock\n```\n\nThe code already supports it in [dbus_server.rs](/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/crates/op-projection/src/dbus_server.rs:504):\n\n```rust\nmatch OP_DBUS_PROJECTION_BUS {\n  \"session\" => Builder::session()?.serve_at(\"/org/opdbus/v1/plugins\", root)?\n  _ => Builder::system()?.serve_at(\"/org/opdbus/v1/plugins\", root)?\n}\n```\n\nRight now `/etc/op-dbus/environment` has:\n\n```bash\nOP_DBUS_PROJECTION_BUS=system\n```\n\nChange it to:\n\n```bash\nOP_DBUS_PROJECTION_BUS=session\n```\n\nThen restart only the projection service. After restart, verify with:\n\n```bash\nsudo -n env DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS=unix:path=/run/opdbus/session-bus.sock \\\n  busctl --user tree org.opdbus.v1.plugins\n```\n\nor:\n\n```bash\nsudo -n busctl --address=unix:path=/run/opdbus/session-bus.sock \\\n  introspect org.opdbus.v1.plugins /org/opdbus/v1/plugins\n```\n\nImportant distinction: this moves the projection root `org.opdbus.v1.plugins` to session. `org.opdbus.v1.plugins.ovsdb` is a separate daemon and is currently hardcoded to `Connection::system()` in `op-openvswitch-daemon`; that would need its own env-driven bus selector if you want that specific OVSDB service on session too.","phase":"final_answer","memory_citation":null}}

This is the\n/// dynamic-mount mechanism: no gRPC, no polling, no inotify — the tree is\n/// derived on demand.\npub struct ProjectionRoot {\n    objects: Arc<Mutex<HashSet<String>>>,\n    schemas: Arc<HashMap<String, PluginSchema>>,\n}\n\n#[interface(name = \"org.opdbus.v1.plugins.ProjectionRoot\")]\nimpl ProjectionRoot {\n    /// List of plugin IDs currently projected in shm (live read).\n    #[zbus(property)]\n    async fn plugins(&self) -> Vec<String> {\n        op_core::projection_shm::list_projected_plugins()\n    }\n\n    /// Number of D-Bus objects currently mounted.\n    #[zbus(property)]\n    async fn object_count(&self) -> u64 {\n        self.objects.lock().await.len() as u64\n    }\n\n    /// Re-read shm and sync the D-Bus tree. Mounts new objects, unmounts stale\n    /// ones. Returns the total object count after refresh.\n    ///\n    /// Call this after a mutation has written new state to shm. The\n    /// MutationEngine can call this via D-Bus after writing to shm, or any\n    /// client can call it to force a tree refresh.\n    async fn refresh(&self, #[zbus(connection)] conn: &Connection) -> u64 {\n        let mut objects = self.objects.lock().await;\n        match sync_all_from_shm(conn, &mut objects, &self.schemas).await {\n            Ok(()) => objects.len() as u64,\n            Err(e) => {\n                tracing::warn!(error = %e, \"refresh() failed\");\n                objects.len() as u64\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Read all plugins from shm, derive paths, and sync the D-Bus tree.\n///\n/// For each plugin in shm, derives all nested object paths from the JSON\n/// structure and mounts/unmounts `ProjectedObject` instances to match.\n/// Plugins that are in shm but not yet mounted are added; objects that are\n/// mounted but no longer in shm are removed.\nasync fn sync_all_from_shm(\n    conn: &Connection,\n    objects: &mut HashSet<String>,\n    schemas: &HashMap<String, PluginSchema>,\n) -> Result<()> {\n    let plugins = op_core::projection_shm::list_projected_plugins();\n\n    // Unmount plugins that are no longer in shm.\n    let plugin_root_base = op_plugins::canonical::plugin_path(\"\");\n    let _ = plugin_root_base; // path prefix helper\n\n    let to_remove: Vec<String> = objects\n        .iter()\n        .filter(|p| {\n            // Keep only paths whose plugin is still in shm\n            let parts: Vec<&str> = p.trim_start_matches('/').split('/').collect();\n            if parts.len() >= 5\n                && parts[0] == \"org\"\n                && parts[1] == \"opdbus\"\n                && parts[2] == \"v1\"\n                && parts[3] == \"plugins\"\n            {\n                let plugin_id = parts[4];\n                !plugins.iter().any(|p| p.as_str() == plugin_id)\n            } else {\n                false\n            }\n        })\n        .cloned()\n        .collect();\n\n    for path in to_remove {\n        if objects.remove(&path) {\n            conn.object_server()\n                .remove::<ProjectedObject, _>(path.as_str())\n plugins currently in shm.\n    for plugin_id in &plugins {\n        if let Some(paths) = read_and_derive_paths(plugin_id) {\n            sync_plugin_paths(conn, objects, plugin_id, &paths, schemas).await?;\n        }\n    }\n\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n/// Sync a single plugin's D-Bus objects to match the derived paths.\nasync fn sync_plugin_paths(\n    conn: &Connection,\n    objects: &mut HashSet<String>,\n    plugin_id: &str,\n    paths: &[Vec<String>],\n    schemas: &HashMap<String, PluginSchema>,\n) -> Result<()> {\n    let new_paths: HashSet<String> = paths\n        .iter()\n        .map(|segs| build_projected_path(plugin_id, segs))\n        .collect();\n\n    let plugin_root = op_plugins::canonical::plugin_path(plugin_id);\n    let plugin_prefix = format!(\"{}/\", plugin_root);\n\n    // Unmount paths that no longer exist in the derived set.\n    let to_remove: Vec<String> = objects\n        .iter()\n        .filter(|p| {\n            (**p == plugin_root || p.starts_with(&plugin_prefix)) && !new_paths.contains(*p)\n        })\n        .cloned()\n        .collect();\n\n    for path in to_remove {\n        if objects.remove(&path) {\n            conn.object_server()\n                .remove::<ProjectedObject, _>(path.as_str())\n                .await?;\n            debug!(path, \"Unmounted stale D-Bus projection object\");\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Mount all current paths.\n    for segs in paths {\n        let path = build_projected_path(plugin_id, segs);\n        if !objects.contains(&path) {\n            let obj =\n The MutationEngine writes one file per plugin on every mutation (atomic\n//! temp+rename). The projection D-Bus server reads 1:1 from these files on\n//! every property access — zero-copy, memory-speed, no held cache.\n//!\n//! Both depend on op-core, so the path constants and I/O\n//! helpers live here.\n\nuse simd_json::prelude::*;\nuse std::fs;\nuse std::io::Write;\n\n/// Directory for per-plugin projection files (one JSON file per plugin).\npub const SHM_PROJECTION_DIR: &str = \"/dev/shm/opdbus/projections\";\n\n/// Manifest carrying the monotonic `generation` counter. Written LAST as the\n/// atomic commit point after each projection write. Consumers read it to\n/// detect staleness (compare generation before/after a read).\npub const SHM_PROJECTION_MANIFEST: &str = \"/dev/shm/opdbus/projections/.manifest.json\";\n\n/// Atomically publish `bytes` to a `/dev/shm` path via a sibling temp file +\n/// rename, so readers see either the old or new content, never a torn write.\npub fn atomic_write_shm(path: &str, bytes: &[u8]) -> anyhow::Result<()> {\n    let tmp = format!(\"{}.tmp\", path);\n    {\n        let mut file =\n            fs::File::create(&tmp).map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!(\"Cannot create {}: {}\", tmp, e))?;\n        file.write_all(bytes)\n            .map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!(\"Failed to write {}: {}\", tmp, e))?;\n        file.sync_all()\n            .map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!(\"Failed to sync {}: {}\", tmp, e))?;\n    }\n    fs::rename(&tmp, path)\n        .map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!(\"Failed to rename {} -> {}: {}\", tmp, path, e))?;\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n/// Sanitize a plugin id into a safe flat filename (no path separators or NUL).\nfn safe_filename(plugin_id: &str) -> String {\n    plugin_id\n        .chars()\n        .map(|c| {\n            if c == '/' || c == '\\\\' || c == '\\0' {\n                '_'\n            } else {\n                c\n            }\n        })\n        .collect()\n}\n\n/// File path for a specific plugin's projection.\npub fn projection_file_path(plugin_id: &str) -> String {\n    format!(\"{}/{}.json\", SHM_PROJECTION_DIR, safe_filename(plugin_id))\n}\n\n/// Write a plugin's full projected state to shm and bump the manifest\n/// generation.\n///\n/// Called by the MutationEngine on every mutation that changes a plugin's\n/// state. `json_bytes` is the JSON serialization of the plugin's current state\n/// (the mutation fold from `state_cache`).\npub fn write_projection(plugin_id: &str, json_bytes: &[u8]) -> anyhow::Result<()> {\n    fs::create_dir_all(SHM_PROJECTION_DIR).map_err(|e| {\n        anyhow::anyhow!(\"Cannot create projection dir {}: {}\", SHM_PROJECTION_DIR, e)\n    })?;\n\n    let path = projection_file_path(plugin_id);\n    atomic_write_shm(&path, json_bytes)?;\n\n    // Bump manifest generation (atomic commit point, written last).\n    let generation = read_manifest_generation().wrapping_add(1);\n    let manifest = format!(\"{{\\\"generation\\\":{}}}\", generation);\n    atomic_write_shm(SHM_PROJECTION_MANIFEST, manifest.as_bytes())?;\n\n    tracing::debug!(plugin_id, generation, \"Projection written to shm\");\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n/// Read the raw bytes of a plugin's projection from shm.\npub fn read_projection_bytes(plugin_id: &str) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {\n    fs::read(projection_file_path(plugin_id)).ok()\n}\n\n/// Read the current manifest `generation`, or 0 if no manifest exists yet.\npub fn read_manifest_generation() -> u64 {\n    let mut bytes = match fs::read(SHM_PROJECTION_MANIFEST) {\n        Ok(b) => b,\n        Err(_) => return 0,\n    };\n    let value = match simd_json::from_slice::<simd_json::OwnedValue>(&mut bytes) {\n        Ok(v) => v,\n        Err(_) => return 0,\n    };\n    match value.get(\"generation\") {\n        Some(g) => {"timestamp":"2026-06-28T15:20:13.167Z","type":"event_msg","payload":{"type":"agent_message","message":"Yes. Zeroclaw should not be treated as “the LLM plugin.” It is closer to a tag-based routing and capability surface that can route many kinds of work, including non-LLM objects.\n\nThe right mental model:\n\n```text\nPluginSchema object\n  -> tags / subids / capabilities / methods / state shape\n  -> Zeroclaw resolves route or tool surface\n  -> target can be LLM, D-Bus object, gRPC method, MCP tool, UI renderer, or policy check\n```\n\nSo `zeroclaw` can cover:\n\n- model/provider routing\n- tool selection\n- structured output schema selection\n- UI surface routing\n- D-Bus method exposure\n- capability-gated method calls\n- plugin object discovery\n- non-LLM object routes like `procfs`, `freedesktop`, `ovsdb_daemon`, `net`, `wireguard`, `unix_socket`\n\nThe earlier `large_language_model` name is too narrow. If consumers read `large_language_model`, they will miss the broader contract. `zeroclaw` should own the routing vocabulary, and LLM routing is only one facet inside it.\n\nTag-based routing should mean something like:\n\n```text\ntag: llm.provider.openai       -> model route\ntag: dbus.plugin.procfs        -> projected object route\ntag: network.ovsdb.bridge      -> D-Bus method route\ntag: ui.schema.form            -> renderer route\ntag: capability.state.write    -> authorization route\ntag: mcp.tool.memory.search    -> MCP gateway route\n```\n\nSo yes: Zeroclaw can and should translate tags into non-LLM object routes.","phase":"final_answer","memory_citation":null}}
{"timestamp":"2026-06-28T15:20:13.173Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"message","id":"msg_067d24187f70e9cd016a413baf9aac819090622543e718b46b","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"output_text","text":"Yes. Zeroclaw should not be treated as “the LLM plugin.” It is closer to a tag-based routing and capability surface that can route many kinds of work, including non-LLM objects.\n\nThe right mental model:\n\n```text\nPluginSchema object\n  -> tags / subids / capabilities / methods / state shape\n  -> Zeroclaw resolves route or tool surface\n  -> target can be LLM, D-Bus object, gRPC method, MCP tool, UI renderer, or policy check\n```\n\nSo `zeroclaw` can cover:\n\n- model/provider routing\n- tool selection\n- structured output schema selection\n- UI surface routing\n- D-Bus method exposure\n- capability-gated method calls\n- plugin object discovery\n- non-LLM object routes like `procfs`, `freedesktop`, `ovsdb_daemon`, `net`, `wireguard`, `unix_socket`\n\nThe earlier `large_language_model` name is too narrow. If consumers read `large_language_model`, they will miss the broader contract. `zeroclaw` should own the routing vocabulary, and LLM routing is only one facet inside it.\n\nTag-based routing should mean something like:\n\n```text\ntag: llm.provider.openai       -> model route\ntag: dbus.plugin.procfs        -> projected object route\ntag: network.ovsdb.bridge      -> D-Bus method route\ntag: ui.schema.form            -> renderer route\ntag: capability.state.write    -> authorization route\ntag: mcp.tool.memory.search    -> MCP gateway route\n```\n\nSo yes: Zeroclaw can and should translate tags into non-LLM object routes."}],"phase":"final_answer","internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough":{"turn_id":"019f0ed0-f211-7153-b9a4-a4fe4f41d9df"}}}

Zeroclaw should not be treated as “the LLM plugin.” It is closer to a tag-based routing and capability surface that can route many kinds of work, including non-LLM objects.\n\nThe right mental model:\n\n```text\nPluginSchema object\n  -> tags / subids / capabilities / methods / state shape\n  -> Zeroclaw resolves route or tool surface\n  -> target can be LLM, D-Bus object, gRPC method, MCP tool, UI renderer, or policy check\n```\n\nSo `zeroclaw` can cover:\n\n- model/provider routing\n- tool selection\n- structured output schema selection\n- UI surface routing\n- D-Bus method exposure\n- capability-gated method calls\n- plugin object discovery\n- non-LLM object routes like `procfs`, `freedesktop`, `ovsdb_daemon`, `net`, `wireguard`, `unix_socket`\n\nThe earlier `large_language_model` name is too narrow. If consumers read `large_language_model`, they will miss the broader contract. `zeroclaw` should own the routing vocabulary, and LLM routing is only one facet inside it.\n\nTag-based routing should mean something like:\n\n```text\ntag: llm.provider.openai       -> model route\ntag: dbus.plugin.procfs        -> projected object route\ntag: network.ovsdb.bridge      -> D-Bus method route\ntag: ui.schema.form            -> renderer route\ntag: capability.state.write    -> authorization route\ntag: mcp.tool.memory.search    -> MCP gateway route\n```\n\nSo yes: Zeroclaw can and should translate tags into non-LLM object routes.","completed_at":1782660013,"duration_ms":10904,"time_to_first_token_ms":4244}}

{"timestamp":"2026-06-28T15:21:22.559Z","type":"event_msg","payload":{"type":"agent_message","message":"Correct.\n\nZeroclaw should be the routing/control vocabulary for more than model routes. It can manage or expose:\n\n```text\nchannels   -> where work/messages/events flow\nskills     -> executable capabilities or agent procedures\nplugins    -> D-Bus projected objects and schema-backed methods\ntools      -> MCP/gRPC/D-Bus callable surfaces\nproviders  -> LLM or non-LLM service providers\npolicies   -> capability gates, tag rules, selector policy\nsurfaces   -> UI render targets and interaction modes\n```\n\nSo the concept is broader than “route prompt to model.” It is more like:\n\n```text\ntag + schema + capability + context\n  -> select channel / skill / plugin / tool / provider / UI surface\n  -> enforce policy\n  -> execute through D-Bus/gRPC/MCP\n  -> record trace/footprint\n```\n\nThat also means `large_language_model` should not be the organizing object. LLMs are one provider class inside Zeroclaw, not the top-level abstraction.","phase":"final_answer","memory_citation":null}}

Initialize Schema Engine + discover plugin schemas (writes to shm).\n    let mut schema_engine = SchemaEngine::new();\n\n    let plugin_reader = match SystemPluginReader::new().await {\n        Ok(reader) => reader,\n        Err(error) => {\n            warn!(\n                error = %error,\n                \"Failed to initialize plugin reader; continuing with empty schema catalog\"\n            );\n            SystemPluginReader::empty()\n        }\n    };\n\n    let projection_schemas = plugin_reader.projection_schemas();\n    let schema_map: HashMap<String, PluginSchema> = projection_schemas\n        .iter()\n        .map(|schema| (schema.name.clone(), schema.clone()))\n        .collect();\n\n    for schema in projection_schemas {\n        register_schema_if_missing(&mut schema_engine, schema)?;\n    }\n\n    info!(\n        schemas = schema_engine.list_schemas().len(),\n        \"Schema catalog published to shm\"\n    );\n\n    // 2. Initialize D-Bus server (owns org.opdbus.v1.plugins, root interface\n    //    at /org/opdbus/v1/plugins is always present for introspection).\n    let dbus_server = ProjectionDbusServer::new_with_schemas(schema_map.clone())\n        .await\n        .context(\"failed to start projection D-Bus server\")?;\n\n    // 3. Initial tree sync: mount from shm (mutations) then seed all known\n    //    plugin roots from the schema catalog so the tree is never empty.\n    dbus_server.sync_from_shm().await?;\n\n    let known_plugins: Vec<String> = schema_map.keys().cloned().collect();\n    dbus_server.seed_plugin_roots(&known_plugins).await?;\n\n    let count = dbus_server.object_count().await;\n    info!(\n        objects = count,\n        plugins = known_plugins.len(),\n        \"Initial tree sync complete\"\n    );\n\n    // 4. Initialize JSON-stream server (for WebSocket clients).\n    let mut stream_server = ProjectionStreamServer::new();\n    stream_server.start(8082)?;\n\n    // 5. Run forever. The tree is derived on-demand via the `refresh()` D-Bus\n    //    method on the ProjectionRoot interface. No gRPC, no polling.\n    info!(\"Projection server ready — tree syncs on refresh() D-Bus call or restart\");\n    tokio::signal::ctrl_c().await?;\n\n    Ok(())\n}\n\nfn register_schema_if_missing(\n    schema_engine: &mut SchemaEngine,\n    schema: PluginSchema,\n) -> Result<()> {\n    if schema_engine.has_valid_schema(&schema.name) {\n        return Ok(());\n    }\n\n    let schema_name = schema.name.clone();\n    schema_engine\n        .register_schema(schema)\n        .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to register projection schema '{}'\", schema_name))?;\n    Ok(())\n}\n","internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough":{"turn_id":"019f0ed6-74e2-70a2-a07d-0f3faa088607"}}}

Follow these strictly to maintain consistency, pass CI, and adhere to the 3tched Architecture standards.\n\n#### 1. The Persona & Naming Conventions\n*   **Humanized Roles:** Treat system components as authoritative human roles. Never use sterile acronyms for major components.\n  *   **A.N.N.A. Scribe** (Axon Network Notary Arbitrator): The top-level Identity-State Arbitrator who notarizes the WireGuard identity and handles the \"Snowball\" session.\n  *   **The Compliance Engine (\"Law Firm\"):** One dedicated Attorney for each major component: **Olivia Scal** (Managing Partner / OSCAL), **E.U.gene Risk** (EU AI Act Counsel), **Penny Privacy** (GDPR Engine), and **Reggie O.P.A.** (Cloud Prosecutor).\n*   **Terminology:** Use exact architecture terminology: \"The Sled\" (1:1 shared memory layout), \"The Shuttle\" (the Rust bridge/courier), \"The Snowball\" (appended session ledger), and \"The Strike/Etch\" (generating the hash).\n\n#### 2. Core Architectural Rules (The \"Reality\")\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via OpenClaw Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Artix Linux (s6 init).\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles — D-Bus First (MANDATORY)\n\n**D-Bus is the ONLY control plane. Every read, every write, every tool call goes through D-Bus. There is no second option.**\n\n*   **D-Bus first. D-Bus always. D-Bus only.** If you are about to call a CLI, spawn a subprocess, read a config file, or poll a socket directly — stop. Find the D-Bus object and use it instead. `org.opdbus.v1` is the system.\n*   **No bypasses.** `Command::new(\"systemctl\")`, `Command::new(\"ip\")`, `Command::new(\"s6-svc\")`, direct file reads for live state — all forbidden in plugin and service code. Bootstrap scripts are the only exception.\n*   **D-Bus objects own plugin state.** Every plugin is a D-Bus object at `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<name>`. Read state through it. Mutate state through it. If there is no D-Bus object, the thing does not exist.\n*   **D-Bus method signatures are generated from the schema.** All D-Bus methods, MCP tool inputs, gRPC shapes, and UI field renderers derive from the `PluginSchema` in `plugin_schema_defs.rs`. The schema IS the interface contract — not a description of it.\n*   **One schema file, one source of truth.** All `PluginSchema` definitions MUST live in `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/plugin_schema_defs.rs`. Each plugin's `schema()` method calls `Some(super::plugin_schema_defs::their_plugin_schema())`. **Never define a schema inline in a plugin's own file** — it will not be registered, and the D-Bus object will have no contract.\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC (over Unix domain sockets or `grpc-uplink`). gRPC calls still flow through D-Bus registration — the D-Bus object is the authority, gRPC is the transport.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`simd_json` preferred, `serde_json` acceptable).\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n*   **No Python unless absolutely necessary.** This is a Rust-first codebase. Scripts are shell (`sh`/`bash`). Data processing is Rust. If you are reaching for Python, stop and ask why Rust or shell cannot do it. The only acceptable Python is in existing compliance-ingest tooling where no Rust equivalent exists yet.\n\n#### 4a. OSCAL Subid Taxonomy (MANDATORY — every artifact must carry a subid)\n\nEvery D-Bus object, plugin, schema, mutation, event, and tool in this system has two identifiers: a `uuid` (machine identity, never changes) and a `subid` (human-readable operational taxonomy key, stable per subject).\n\n**`subid` format:** `<category>.<component-type>.<subject>.<verb>[.<facet>][@vN]`\n\n**Seven categories — use exactly these, no others:**\n\n| category | what it classifies |\n|---|---|\n| `src` | authoritative source, ingress channel, source-of-truth store |\n| `prj` | D-Bus projection or mirror publication step |\n| `sch` | schema, contract, vocabulary, or control-mapping artifact |\n| `mut` | write-path operation that changes effective state |\n| `obs` | read, query, enumeration, discovery path |\n| `evt` | emitted signal, audit-chain event, proof, tag provenance |\n| `exp` | consumer-facing render — MCP tool, UI surface, gRPC bridge view |\n\n**Component-type** reuses OSCAL vocabulary: `software`, `service`, `network`, `hardware`, `process-procedure`, `standard`, `validation`, `policy`, `plan`, `guidance`, `physical`, `this-system`, `system`, `interconnection`.\n\n**Rules:**\n- `uuid` is exact machine identity — never replace it with `subid`\n- `subid` is an OSCAL `prop` value (`ns`, `name`, `value`) — never embed it in `remarks`\n- Compliance mappings (`control_refs[]`, `statement_refs[]`, `control_source`) live in metadata arrays, **never** inside the `subid` string\n- `mut.*` records **must** carry `actor_id` and `capability_id`\n- `evt.*` records **must** carry `event_id` or `event_hash`\n- `subid` is immutable per subject — if the meaning changes materially, create a new subject with `@vN`\n- All subids are registered in the canonical registry; uniqueness is enforced in CI\n\n**Examples:** `src.network.ovsdb.monitor@v1` · `prj.service.projected-object.publish@v1` · `sch.standard.plugin-schema.resolve@v1` · `mut.service.state-sync.apply-patch@v1` · `exp.service.plugin-projection.render@v1`\n\n#### 4b. MCP Gateway Architecture (SETTLED — DO NOT REDESIGN)\n\n*   **cognitive-mcp** (`:3003`, Netmaker WireGuard IP `100.90.37.254`) is the **universal gateway for ALL external clients**: NotebookLM, Droid (factory.ai), Cursor, Codex, Junie, Gemini CLI. It has memory tools, gRPC service, auth, and the correct protocol surface.\n*   **compact-mcp** (`127.0.0.1:11436`) is **loopback/chatbot only**. Never expose externally. Never point external clients at it.\n*   Do NOT create new shim services. Do NOT point external clients at `op-assistant-grpc` directly. Do NOT expose compact-mcp outside loopback.\n\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\n**Rust Workspace**\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\n\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\n\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\n\n#### 6. Coding Style & Naming Conventions\n*   **Rust:** Edition 2021, `rustfmt` (4-space indent, max-width 100). Use specific imports (`use serde_json::Value;`). Use `anyhow::Result<T>` for main errors and `thiserror` for custom enums.\n*   **TypeScript/React:** 2-space indent, Prettier via ESLint. Functional components only. {"timestamp":"2026-06-28T15:29:33.866Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"function_call_output","call_id":"call_FoeTTb2RPZasPLr7HF82cweO","output":"Chunk ID: c18848\nWall time: 0.0000 seconds\nProcess exited with code 0\nOriginal token count: 926\nOutput:\n//! Projection Server: pure read-through D-Bus projection of the plugin tree.\n//!\n//! Mounts the projected plugin tree at `org.opdbus.v1.plugins` and serves\n//! each plugin's state as a `ProjectedObject` that reads 1:1 from the shm\n//! projection layer (`/dev/shm/opdbus/projections/<plugin>.json`).\n//!\n//! The MutationEngine (the single write door) writes each plugin's full state\n//! to shm on every mutation. This server mounts the tree from shm on startup\n//! and exposes a `refresh()` D-Bus method on the root interface that re-reads\n//! shm and syncs the tree (mount/unmount). No gRPC subscription, no polling,\n//! no inotify — the tree is derived on demand.\n\nuse anyhow::{Context, Result};\nuse op_projection::*;\nuse std::collections::HashMap;\nuse tracing::{info, warn};\nuse tracing_subscriber::{EnvFilter, FmtSubscriber};\n\n#[tokio::main]\nasync fn main() -> Result<()> {\n    let subscriber = FmtSubscriber::builder()\n        .with_env_filter(EnvFilter::from_default_env())\n        .finish();\n    tracing::subscriber::set_global_default(subscriber)?;\n\n    info!(\"Starting Operation-DBus Projection Server (read-through)\");\n\n    // 1. Initialize Schema Engine + discover plugin schemas (writes to shm).\n    let mut schema_engine = SchemaEngine::new();\n\n    let plugin_reader = match SystemPluginReader::new().await {\n        Ok(reader) => reader,\n        Err(error) => {\n            warn!(\n                error = %error,\n                \"Failed to initialize plugin reader; continuing with empty schema catalog\"\n            );\n            SystemPluginReader::empty()\n        }\n    };\n\n    let projection_schemas = plugin_reader.projection_schemas();\n    let schema_map: HashMap<String, PluginSchema> = projection_schemas\n        .iter()\n        .map(|schema| (schema.name.clone(), schema.clone()))\n        .collect();\n\n    for schema in projection_schemas {\n        register_schema_if_missing(&mut schema_engine, schema)?;\n    }\n\n    info!(\n        schemas = schema_engine.list_schemas().len(),\n        \"Schema catalog published to shm\"\n    );\n\n    // 2. Initialize D-Bus server (owns org.opdbus.v1.plugins, root interface\n    //    at /org/opdbus/v1/plugins is always present for introspection).\n    let dbus_server = ProjectionDbusServer::new_with_schemas(schema_map.clone())\n        .await\n        .context(\"failed to start projection D-Bus server\")?;\n\n    // 3. Initial tree sync: mount from shm (mutations) then seed all known\n    //    plugin roots from the schema catalog so the tree is never empty.\n    dbus_server.sync_from_shm().await?;\n\n    let known_plugins: Vec<String> = schema_map.keys().cloned().collect();\n    dbus_server.seed_plugin_roots(&known_plugins).await?;\n\n    let count = dbus_server.object_count().await;\n    info!(\n        objects = count,\n        plugins = known_plugins.len(),\n        \"Initial tree sync complete\"\n    );\n\n    // 4. Initialize JSON-stream server (for WebSocket clients).\n    let mut stream_server = ProjectionStreamServer::new();\n    stream_server.start(8082)?;\n\n    // 5. Run forever. The tree is derived on-demand via the `refresh()` D-Bus\n    //    method on the ProjectionRoot interface. No gRPC, no polling.\n    info!(\"Projection server ready — tree syncs on refresh() D-Bus call or restart\");\n    tokio::signal::ctrl_c().await?;\n\n    Ok(())\n}\n\nfn register_schema_if_missing(\n    schema_engine: &mut SchemaEngine,\n    schema: PluginSchema,\n) -> Result<()> {\n    if schema_engine.has_valid_schema(&schema.name) {\n        return Ok(());\n    }\n\n    let schema_name = schema.name.clone();\n    schema_engine\n        .register_schema(schema)\n        .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to register projection schema '{}'\", schema_name))?;\n    Ok(())\n}\n","internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough":{"turn_id":"019f0ed8-5d61-7cb2-ad7d-b861ffa74233"}}}

To add a field, add it to the\n/// plugin state — never hand-write a field definition.\npub(crate) fn schema_from_state(\n    name: &str,\n    category: &str,\n    version: &str,\n    description: &str,\n    state: &Value,\n) -> PluginSchema {\n    use simd_json::prelude::*;\n\n    let mut builder = PluginSchema::builder(name)\n        .version(version)\n        .category(category)\n        .description(description);\n\n    if let Some(obj) = state.as_object() {\n        for (key, value) in obj.iter() {\n            builder = builder.field(&key.to_string(), field_from_value(value));\n        }\n    }\n\n    builder.example(state.clone()).build()\n}\n\n/// Infer a `FieldSchema` (type + example) from a live state value.\npub(crate) fn field_from_value(value: &Value) -> FieldSchema {\n    FieldSchema {\n        field_type: infer_field_type(value),\n        required: false,\n        description: String::new(),\n        default: None,\n        example: Some(value.clone()),\n        constraints: Vec::new(),\n        read_only: false,\n        read_only_when: None,\n    }\n}\n\n/// Infer a `FieldType` from a live state value, recursing into arrays/objects.\npub(crate) fn infer_field_type(value: &Value) -> FieldType {\n    use simd_json::prelude::*;\n\n    if value.is_null() {\n        FieldType::Any\n    } else if value.as_bool().is_some() {\n        FieldType::Boolean\n    } else if value.as_i64().is_some() || value.as_u64().is_some() {\n        FieldType::Integer\n    } else if value.as_f64().is_some() {\n        FieldType::Float\n    } else if value.as_str().is_some() {\n        FieldType::String\n    } else if let Some(arr) = value.as_array() {\n        let inner = arr.first().map(infer_field_type).unwrap_or(FieldType::Any);\n        FieldType::Array(Box::new(inner))\n    } else if let Some(obj) = value.as_object() {\n        let fields = obj\n            .iter()\n            .map(|(k, v)| (k.to_string(), field_from_value(v)))\n            .collect();\n        FieldType::Object(fields)\n    } else {\n        FieldType::Any\n    }\n}\n\npub(crate) fn any_field(required: bool, description: &str, default: Option<Value>) -> FieldSchema {\n    FieldSchema {\n        field_type: FieldType::Any,\n        required,\n        description: description.to_string(),\n        default,\n        example: None,\n        constraints: Vec::new(),\n        read_only: false,\n        read_only_when: None,\n    }\n}\n\npub(crate) fn cap_method(\n    name: &str,\n    side_effect: SideEffect,\n    idempotent: bool,\n    required_capability: &str,\n    subid: &str,\n) -> MethodDecl {\n    MethodDecl {\n        name: name.to_string(),\n        args: json!({\"type\": \"object\", \"additionalProperties\": true}),\n        returns: json!({\"type\": \"object\", \"additionalProperties\": true}),\n        side_effect,\n        idempotent,\n        required_capability: Some(required_capability.to_string()),\n        subid: subid.to_string(),\n    }\n}\n\npub(crate) fn simple_schema(\n    name: &str,\n    description: &str,\n    dependencies: &[&str],\n    fields: Vec<(&str, FieldSchema)>,\n) -> PluginSchema {\n    let mut builder = PluginSchema::builder(name)\n        .version(\"1.0.0\")\n        .description(description);\n    for dep in dependencies {\n        builder = builder.dependency(dep);\n    }\n    for (field_name, schema) in fields {\n        builder = builder.field(field_name, schema);\n    }\n    builder.build()\n}\n","internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough":{"turn_id":"019f0eda-f202-7f72-a784-2feed6b2db9e"}}}

{"timestamp":"2026-06-28T15:32:19.818Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"function_call_output","call_id":"call_pWIXDInUah25XZRBM5mwHxrx","output":"Chunk ID: 32e877\nWall time: 0.0000 seconds\nProcess exited with code 0\nOriginal token count: 1271\nOutput:\n//! Shared-memory projection layer for the projected plugin tree.\n//!\n//! The projected plugin tree lives in tmpfs (`/dev/shm/opdbus/projections/`).\n//! The MutationEngine writes one file per plugin on every mutation (atomic\n//! temp+rename). The projection D-Bus server reads 1:1 from these files on\n//! every property access — zero-copy, memory-speed, no held cache.\n//!\n//! This module is the shared contract between the **writer** (op-grpc-bridge\n//! MutationEngine, the single write door) and the **reader** (op-projection\n//! D-Bus server). Both depend on op-core, so the path constants and I/O\n//! helpers live here.\n\nuse simd_json::prelude::*;\nuse std::fs;\nuse std::io::Write;\n\n/// Directory for per-plugin projection files (one JSON file per plugin).\npub const SHM_PROJECTION_DIR: &str = \"/dev/shm/opdbus/projections\";\n/// Legacy/current present-state directory produced by the projection server.\n///\n/// Readers prefer `SHM_PROJECTION_DIR` because that is the mutation projection\n/// contract. Until every producer writes there, this fallback keeps the D-Bus\n/// tree derived from the live tmpfs state instead of exposing schema roots only.\npub const SHM_STATE_DIR: &str = \"/dev/shm/opdbus/state\";\n\n/// Manifest carrying the monotonic `generation` counter. Written LAST as the\n/// atomic commit point after each projection write. Consumers read it to\n/// detect staleness (compare generation before/after a read).\npub const SHM_PROJECTION_MANIFEST: &str = \"/dev/shm/opdbus/projections/.manifest.json\";\n\n/// Atomically publish `bytes` to a `/dev/shm` path via a sibling temp file +\n/// rename, so readers see either the old or new content, never a torn write.\npub fn atomic_write_shm(path: &str, bytes: &[u8]) -> anyhow::Result<()> {\n    let tmp = format!(\"{}.tmp\", path);\n    {\n        let mut file =\n            fs::File::create(&tmp).map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!(\"Cannot create {}: {}\", tmp, e))?;\n        file.write_all(bytes)\n            .map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!(\"Failed to write {}: {}\", tmp, e))?;\n        file.sync_all()\n            .map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!(\"Failed to sync {}: {}\", tmp, e))?;\n    }\n    fs::rename(&tmp, path)\n        .map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!(\"Failed to rename {} -> {}: {}\", tmp, path, e))?;\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n/// Sanitize a plugin id into a safe flat filename (no path separators or NUL).\nfn safe_filename(plugin_id: &str) -> String {\n    plugin_id\n        .chars()\n        .map(|c| {\n            if c == '/' || c == '\\\\' || c == '\\0' {\n                '_'\n            } else {\n                c\n            }\n        })\n        .collect()\n}\n\n/// File path for a specific plugin's projection.\npub fn projection_file_path(plugin_id: &str) -> String {\n    format!(\"{}/{}.json\", SHM_PROJECTION_DIR, safe_filename(plugin_id))\n}\n\nfn state_file_path(plugin_id: &str) -> String {\n    format!(\"{}/{}.json\", SHM_STATE_DIR, safe_filename(plugin_id))\n}\n\n/// Write a plugin's full projected state to shm and bump the manifest\n/// generation.\n///\n/// Called by the MutationEngine on every mutation that changes a plugin's\n/// state. `json_bytes` is the JSON serialization of the plugin's current state\n/// (the mutation fold from `state_cache`).\npub fn write_projection(plugin_id: &str, json_bytes: &[u8]) -> anyhow::Result<()> {\n    fs::create_dir_all(SHM_PROJECTION_DIR).map_err(|e| {\n        anyhow::anyhow!(\"Cannot create projection dir {}: {}\", SHM_PROJECTION_DIR, e)\n    })?;\n\n    let path = projection_file_path(plugin_id);\n    atomic_write_shm(&path, json_bytes)?;\n\n    // Bump manifest generation (atomic commit point, written last).\n    let generation = read_manifest_generation().wrapping_add(1);\n    let manifest = format!(\"{{\\\"generation\\\":{}}}\", generation);\n    atomic_write_shm(SHM_PROJECTION_MANIFEST, manifest.as_bytes())?;\n\n    tracing::debug!(plugin_id, generation, \"Projection written to shm\");\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n/// Read the raw bytes of a plugin's projection from shm.\npub fn read_projection_bytes(plugin_id: &str) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {\n    fs::read(projection_file_path(plugin_id))\n        .or_else(|_| fs::read(state_file_path(plugin_id)))\n        .ok()\n}\n\n/// Read the current manifest `generation`, or 0 if no manifest exists yet.\npub fn read_manifest_generation() -> u64 {\n    let mut bytes = match fs::read(SHM_PROJECTION_MANIFEST) {\n        Ok(b) => b,\n        Err(_) => return 0,\n    };\n    let value = match simd_json::from_slice::<simd_json::OwnedValue>(&mut bytes) {\n        Ok(v) => v,\n        Err(_) => return 0,\n    };\n    match value.get(\"generation\") {\n        Some(g) => g.as_u64().unwrap_or(0),\n        None => 0,\n    }\n}\n\n/// List all plugin ids that currently have projection files in shm.\n///\n/// The manifest file (`.manifest.json`) is excluded. Plugin filenames are\n/// unsanitized back to their original form (the safe-filename transform is\n/// lossless for valid plugin ids).\npub fn list_projected_plugins() -> Vec<String> {\n    let mut plugins = list_plugin_files(SHM_PROJECTION_DIR);\n    if plugins.is_empty() {\n        plugins = list_plugin_files(SHM_STATE_DIR);\n    }\n    plugins.sort();\n    plugins\n}\n\n","internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough":{"turn_id":"019f0eda-f202-7f72-a784-2feed6b2db9e"}}}

It never\n+/// queries a plugin backend and never invents data outside the contract:\n+/// field defaults win, then examples, then an empty value matching the field\n+/// type. The MutationEngine writes this once when no projection exists yet;\n+/// later mutations replace it through the normal `/dev/shm/opdbus/projections`\n+/// write door.\n+pub(crate) fn materialize_state_from_schema(schema: &PluginSchema) -> Value {\n+    let mut state = simd_json::value::owned::Object::new();\n+    let mut fields = schema.fields.iter().collect::<Vec<_>>();\n+    fields.sort_by(|(a, _), (b, _)| a.cmp(b));\n+\n+    for (name, field) in fields {\n+        state.insert(name.clone(), materialize_field(field));\n+    }\n+\n+    Value::Object(Box::new(state))\n+}\n+\n+fn materialize_field(field: &FieldSchema) -> Value {\n+    if let Some(value) = &field.default {\n+        return value.clone();\n+    }\n+    if let Some(value) = &field.example {\n+        return value.clone();\n+    }\n+\n+    match &field.field_type {\n+        FieldType::String => json!(\"\"),\n+        FieldType::Integer => json!(0),\n+        FieldType::Float => json!(0.0),\n+        FieldType::Boolean => json!(false),\n+        FieldType::Array(_) => json!([]),\n+        FieldType::Object(fields) => {\n+            let mut object = simd_json::value::owned::Object::new();\n+            let mut fields = fields.iter().collect::<Vec<_>>();\n+            fields.sort_by(|(a, _), (b, _)| a.cmp(b));\n+            for (name, field) in fields {\n+                object.insert(name.clone(), materialize_field(field));\n+            }\n+            Value::Object(Box::new(object))\n+        }\n+        FieldType::Any => json!(null),\n+    }\n+}\n+\n /// Format a plugin's live state into a `PluginSchema`.\n ///\n /// This is a *formatter*, not a schema authority — nothing here is indexed. Adding a domain service is done in [`build_operation_routes`], not here.\npub async fn run_grpc_server(\n    addr: std::net::SocketAddr,\n    mutation_engine: Arc<MutationEngine>,\n    plugin_provider: Option<Arc<dyn PluginSchemaProvider>>,\n    tls_identity: Option<Identity>,\n) -> Result<(), tonic::transport::Error> {\n    // Imports here back only the `health_reporter.set_serving::<T>()` type args;\n    // the service *instances* are mounted in `build_operation_routes`.\n    use crate::proto::event_chain_service_server::EventChainServiceServer;\n    use crate::proto::mail::mail_service_server::MailServiceServer;\n    use crate::proto::ovsdb_mirror_server::OvsdbMirrorServer;\n    use crate::proto::plugin_service_server::PluginServiceServer;\n    use crate::proto::privacy::privacy_network_service_server::PrivacyNetworkServiceServer;\n    use crate::proto::registration::registration_service_server::RegistrationServiceServer;\n    use crate::proto::registry::component_registry_server::ComponentRegistryServer;\n    use crate::proto::runtime_mirror_server::RuntimeMirrorServer;\n    use crate::proto::state_sync_server::StateSyncServer;\n\n    let server = if let Some(provider) = plugin_provider {\n        OperationGrpcServer::with_plugin_provider(mutation_engine, provider)\n    } else {\n        OperationGrpcServer::new(mutation_engine)\n    };\n    let server = match QdrantSemanticShuttle::new().await {\n        Ok(shuttle) => server.with_semantic_shuttle(Arc::new(shuttle)),\n        Err(error) => {\n            warn!(%error, \"semantic shuttle unavailable; SearchSemanticTrace will return failed_precondition\");\n            server\n        }\n    };\n\n    // Health — standard gRPC health protocol for deploy verification and LB probes.\n    let (mut health_reporter, health_service) = tonic_health::server::health_reporter();\n    health_reporter\n        .set_serving::<StateSyncServer<OperationGrpcServer>>()\n        .await;\n    health_reporter\n        .set_serving::<PluginServiceServer<OperationGrpcServer>>()\n        .await;\n    health_reporter\n        .set_serving::<EventChainServiceServer<OperationGrpcServer>>()\n","internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough":{"turn_id":"019f0edc-dd40-7300-866f-3494cb514638"}}}

chat(&self, messages: Vec<ChatMessage>) -> Result<ChatResponse> {\n        let provider_type = self.resolve_provider().await?;\n        let model = self.current_model.read().unwrap().clone();\n\n        let provider = self\n            .providers\n            .get(&provider_type)\n            .ok_or_else(|| anyhow!(\"Provider not available\"))?;\n\n        provider.chat(&model, messages).await\n    }\n\n    /// Send chat with specific provider and model\n    pub async fn chat_with(\n        &self,\n        provider_type: &ProviderType,\n        model: &str,\n        messages: Vec<ChatMessage>,\n    ) -> Result<ChatResponse> {\n        let provider = self\n            .providers\n            .get(provider_type)\n            .ok_or_else(|| anyhow!(\"Provider {:?} not available\", provider_type))?;\n\n        provider.chat(model, messages).await\n    }\n\n    /// Send chat stream with specific provider and model\n    pub async fn chat_stream_with(\n        &self,\n        provider_type: &ProviderType,\n        model: &str,\n        messages: Vec<ChatMessage>,\n    ) -> Result<tokio::sync::mpsc::Receiver<Result<String>>> {\n        let provider = self\n            .providers\n            .get(provider_type)\n            .ok_or_else(|| anyhow!(\"Provider {:?} not available\", provider_type))?;\n\n        provider.chat_stream(model, messages).await\n    }\n\n    /// Find which provider supports the given model\n    pub async fn find_provider_for_model(&self, model: &str) -> Option<ProviderType> {\n        let providers = self.available_providers();\n        // 1. Direct match in list_models_for_provider\n        for ptype in &providers {\n            if let Ok(models) = self.list_models_for_provider(ptype).await {\n                if models.iter().any(|m| m.id == model) {\n                    return Some(ptype.clone());\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        // 2. Prefix / substring match\n        let model_lower = model.to_lowercase();\n        if (model_lower.contains(\"factory\")\n            || model_lower.contains(\"droid\")\n            || model_lower.contains(\"kimi\"))\n            && providers.contains(&ProviderType::Factory)\n        {\n            return Some(ProviderType::Factory);\n        }\n        if model_lower.contains(\"claude\") && providers.contains(&ProviderType::Anthropic) {\n            return Some(ProviderType::Anthropic);\n        }\n        if model_lower.contains(\"gemini\") {\n            // Check in order of preference\n            if providers.contains(&ProviderType::Antigravity) {\n                return Some(ProviderType::Antigravity);\n            }\n            if providers.contains(&ProviderType::Gemini) {\n                return Some(ProviderType::Gemini);\n            }\n            if providers.contains(&ProviderType::GeminiCli) {\n                return Some(ProviderType::GeminiCli);\n            }\n        }\n        if model_lower.contains(\"gpt\") {\n            if providers.contains(&ProviderType::OpenClaw) {\n                return Some(ProviderType::OpenClaw);\n            }\n            if providers.contains(&ProviderType::Assistant) {\n                return Some(ProviderType::Assistant);\n            }\n            if providers.contains(&ProviderType::OpenAI) {\n                return Some(ProviderType::OpenAI);\n            }\n        }\n\n        // 3. Fallback to first available provider\n        providers.first().cloned()\n    }\n\n    /// Get status\n    pub async fn get_status(&self) -> simd_json::OwnedValue {\n        let provider = self.current_provider.read().unwrap().clone();\n        let model = self.current_model.read().unwrap().clone();\n        let providers: Vec<String> = self\n            .available_providers()\n            .iter()\n            .map(|p| p.to_string())\n            .collect();\n\n        simd_json::json!({\n            \"provider\": provider.to_string(),\n            \"model\": model,\n            \"available_providers\": providers,\n        })\n    }\n","internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough":{"turn_id":"019f0faa-8004-7e21-b800-a5f5b1ea03ee"}}}

{"timestamp":"2026-06-28T19:18:19.395Z","type":"event_msg","payload":{"type":"agent_message","message":"Yes: Zeroclaw should be the D-Bus routing authority.\n\nCurrent state from the code:\n- `zeroclaw` declares routes in `ZeroclawState.model_routes`.\n- `reasoning` currently points to `factory -> antigravity -> gemini-3-pro-preview`.\n- That is a static declared route, not “cheapest available high reasoning.”\n- `op-llm` still does provider selection internally with env vars and heuristics.\n- `factory` tries to read Zeroclaw routes from stale shm path `/dev/shm/plugin-zeroclaw.json`, which is the wrong shape now. It should read D-Bus/projection.\n\nWhat you want conceptually:\n\n1. Zeroclaw owns the policy:\n   “I need high reasoning, minimize cost, only use available models.”\n\n2. Provider plugins publish facts through D-Bus:\n   - available models\n   - model capabilities/tags: `reasoning`, `code`, `vision`, `tool_use`\n   - cost metadata\n   - latency/status/auth availability\n   - context window\n   - max reasoning/thinking support\n\n3. Zeroclaw `ResolveRoute` reads those D-Bus objects and returns the selected provider/model.\n\nSo the request should look like:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"hint\": \"reasoning\",\n  \"constraints\": {\n    \"optimize\": \"cost\",\n    \"min_reasoning\": \"high\",\n    \"available_only\": true\n  }\n}\n```\n\nAnd Zeroclaw should resolve that to something like:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"provider\": \"...\",\n  \"model\": \"...\",\n  \"transport\": \"dbus|direct|grpc\",\n  \"reason\": \"cheapest available model tagged high_reasoning\"\n}\n```\n\nThe missing piece is the schema: `ModelRoute` does not currently carry enough routing data to choose “cheapest high reasoning.” It needs fields like `capabilities/tags`, `input_cost`, `output_cost`, `reasoning_level`, `context_window`, maybe `latency_class`.\n\nSo: yes, use D-Bus routing. Zeroclaw should not hardcode “Gemini 3 Pro for reasoning.” It should ask the D-Bus model catalog, filter by tags, then rank by cost.","phase":"final_answer","memory_citation":null}}

They are carried by the schema artifact that seeds the live projection.","phase":"final_answer","memory_citation":null}}

{"timestamp":"2026-06-28T19:30:01.848Z","type":"event_msg","payload":{"type":"agent_message","message":"Correct expected behavior, but not fully implemented yet.\n\nWhat should happen:\n\n1. You add OpenRouter as a provider through D-Bus, with an API key reference, not raw key in the projection.\n2. The OpenRouter provider object validates auth.\n3. It calls OpenRouter’s model catalog endpoint.\n4. It publishes discovered models into its D-Bus projection.\n5. Zeroclaw reads that D-Bus model catalog and can route against it.\n\nCurrent repo state:\n\n- `zeroclaw` declares `openrouter` as a provider.\n- It has OpenRouter routes like `openrouter -> anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.6`.\n- But I do not see a real OpenRouter plugin/catalog writer yet.\n- The `api_key` field in routes is only a placeholder/null.\n- There is no live “enter OpenRouter key, fetch models, populate projection” path wired.\n\nSo the answer is: yes, that is the intended architecture, but we need an OpenRouter provider projection to make it real.\n\nThe right shape is probably:\n\n`/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/openrouter`\n- `ProviderStatus`\n- `AuthStatus`\n- `Models`\n- `RefreshModels`\n- `SetApiKeyRef`\n\nThen Zeroclaw should consume that via D-Bus, not store OpenRouter’s whole catalog inside hardcoded `zeroclaw` state.","phase":"final_answer","memory_citation":null}}

Zeroclaw or the provider plugin validates the key.\n4. It fetches the live model catalog.\n5. It writes the populated provider/model catalog into the D-Bus projection.\n6. Routes become available from that live catalog.\n\nSo before onboarding, OpenRouter should only be a supported provider type/schema capability, not necessarily a live populated provider object.\n\nAfter onboarding, yes, it should populate automatically.\n\nThe important distinction:\n\n- Schema says: “OpenRouter is a supported provider kind.”\n- Onboarding creates: “This system has an OpenRouter provider configured.”\n- Live projection says: “Here are the actual OpenRouter models available for this key.”\n\nThat is the right model.","phase":"final_answer","memory_citation":null}}

#[serde(skip_serializing_if = \"Option::is_none\")]\n    pub enabled: Option<bool>,\n}\n\n/// Top-level desired state for the s6 plugin.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, PartialEq)]\npub struct S6Config {\n    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = \"Option::is_none\")]\n    pub units: Option<Vec<S6UnitConfig>>,\n}\n\n/// S6 state plugin — routes mutations through D-Bus, read-only via s6-rc CLI.\n///\n/// Automatically resolves systemd-style unit names to s6 primitives at runtime:\n/// - \"nginx.service\" → \"nginx\"\n/// - \"backup.timer\"  → s6-cron job\n/// - \"api.socket\"    → s6-socketmux\n///\n/// Detects actual unit type by inspecting the s6 service directory structure.\npub struct S6StatePlugin {\n    dbus: S6DbusClient,\n}\n\n/// Strip known systemd unit-type suffixes from a name.\nfn normalize_unit_name(name: &str) -> &str {\n    for suffix in [\n        \".service\", \".timer\", \".socket\", \".target\", \".mount\", \".device\", \".path\",\n    ] {\n        if let Some(base) = name.strip_suffix(suffix) {\n            return base;\n        }\n    }\n    name\n}\n\n/// Detect the systemd-compatible suffix for a bare s6 service by inspecting\n/// its service-directory structure under `/run/service/<name>/`.\nasync fn detect_systemd_suffix(name: &str) -> &'static str {\n    let base = normalize_unit_name(name);\n    let svc_dir = format!(\"/run/service/{base}\");\n    let meta = tokio::fs::metadata(&svc_dir).await;\n    if !meta.as_ref().is_ok_and(|m| m.is_dir()) {\n        return \".service\"; // default assumption\n    }\n\n    // Check for cron subdirectory → timer\n    if tokio::fs::metadata(format!(\"{svc_dir}/cron\")).await.is_ok() {\n        return \".timer\";\n    }\n    // Check for socket subdirectory or s6-socketmux\n    if tokio::fs::metadata(format!(\"{svc_dir}/socket\"))\n        .await\n        .is_ok()\n        || tokio::fs::metadata(format!(\"{svc_dir}/env/SOCKET\"))\n            .await\n            .is_ok()\n    {\n        return \".socket\";\n    }\n    // Check for ftrig / path trigger\n    if tokio::fs::metadata(format!(\"{svc_dir}/ftrig\"))\n        .await\n        .is_ok()\n        || tokio::fs::metadata(format!(\"{svc_dir}/env/PATH\"))\n            .await\n            .is_ok()\n    {\n        return \".path\";\n    }\n    // Check for mount-related env\n    if tokio::fs::metadata(format!(\"{svc_dir}/env/MOUNTPOINT\"))\n        .await\n        .is_ok()\n    {\n        return \".mount\";\n    }\n    \".service\"\n}\n\nimpl S6StatePlugin {\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        Self {\n            dbus: S6DbusClient::new(),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Return the names of all currently-up services.\n    ///\n    /// Tries D-Bus first; falls back to `s6-rc -a list` when the daemon isn't running.\n    /// subid: `obs.service.s6.list-units@v1`\n    async fn list_running(&self) -> Result<Vec<String>> {\n        if let Ok(units) = self.dbus.list_units().await {\n            let mut running = Vec::new();\n            for unit in units {\n                if let Some(name) = unit.get(\"name\").and_then(|v| v.as_str()) {\n                    if let Some(active) = unit.get(\"active\").and_then(|v| v.as_str()) {\n                        if active == \"true\" || active == \"up\" {\n                            running.push(name.to_string());\n                        }\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n            return Ok(running);\n        }\n\n        // Fallback: direct s6-rc query\n        let output = tokio::process::Command::new(\"s6-rc\")\n            .args([\"-a\", \"list\"])\n            .output()\n            .await\n            .context(\"s6-rc -a list\")?;\n        let stdout = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout);\n        Ok(stdout\n            .lines()\n            .map(|l| l.trim().to_string())\n            .filter(|l| !l.is_empty())\n            .collect())\n    }\n\n    /// Return *all* available service names.\n    ///\n    /// Tries D-Bus first; falls back to scanning `/etc/s6/sv/`.\n    async fn list_all(&self) -> Result<Vec<String>> {\n        if let Ok(files) = self.dbus.list_unit_files().await {\n            let mut all = Vec::new();\n            for file in files {\n                if let Some(name) = file.get(\"name\").and_then(|v| v.as_str()) {\n                    all.push(name.to_string());\n                }\n            }\n            if !all.is_empty() {\n                return Ok(all);\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Fallback: scan the s6 service directory\n        let mut all = Vec::new();\n        if let Ok(mut dir) = tokio::fs::read_dir(\"/etc/s6/sv\").await {\n            while let Ok(Some(entry)) = dir.next_entry().await {\n                if let Ok(name) = entry.file_name().into_string() {\n                    all.push(name);\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        Ok(all)\n    }\n\n    /// Check if a service is enabled by looking at the bundle.\n    async fn is_enabled(&self, name: &str) -> bool {\n        let bundle_path = format!(\"/etc/s6-rc/bundle/default/contents.d/{name}\");\n        tokio::fs::metadata(&bundle_path).await.is_ok()\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Default for S6StatePlugin {\n    fn default() -> Self {\n        Self::new()\n    }\n}\n\n#[async_trait]\nimpl StatePlugin for S6StatePlugin {\n    fn name(&self) -> &str {\n        \"s6\"\n    }\n\n    fn version(&self) -> &str {\n        \"1.0.0\"\n    }\n\n    fn schema(&self) -> Option<op_state_store::PluginSchema> {\n        Some(s6_schema())\n    }\n\n    fn is_available(&self) -> bool {\n        std::path::Path::new(S6_RC_LIVE).exists()\n    }\n\n    fn unavailable_reason(&self) -> String {\n        format!(\"s6-rc live directory not found at {S6_RC_LIVE}\")\n    }\n\n    async fn calculate_diff(&self, current: &Value, desired: &Value) -> Result<StateDiff> {\n        let current_config: S6Config = simd_json::serde::from_owned_value(current.clone())?;\n        let desired_config: S6Config = simd_json::serde::from_owned_value(desired.clone())?;\n        let mut actions = Vec::new();\n\n        // Normalize names (strip .service/.timer etc.) so \"nginx\" and \"nginx.service\" match\n        let current_map: std::collections::HashMap<String, S6UnitConfig> = current_config\n            .units\n            .unwrap_or_default()\n            .into_iter()\n            .map(|u| (normalize_unit_name(&u.name).to_string(), u))\n            .collect();\n\n        if let Some(desired_units) = desired_config.units {\n            for mut desired in desired_units {\n                let normalized = normalize_unit_name(&desired.name).to_string();\n                desired.name = normalized.clone();\n                let current = current_map.get(&normalized);\n                if current != Some(&desired) {\n                    actions.push(StateAction::Modify {\n                        resource: normalized,\n                        changes: simd_json::serde::to_owned_value(&desired)?,\n                    });\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        Ok(StateDiff {\n            plugin: self.name().to_string(),\n            actions,\n            metadata: DiffMetadata {\n                timestamp: chrono::Utc::now().timestamp(),\n                current_hash: format!(\"{:x}\", md5::compute(simd_json::to_string(current)?)),\n                desired_hash: format!(\"{:x}\", md5::compute(simd_json::to_string(desired)?)),\n            },\n        })\n    }\n\n    async fn apply_state(&self, diff: &StateDiff) -> Result<ApplyResult> {\n//! Service plugin - auto-generating, validating, init-agnostic service management.\n\nuse super::plugin_schema_defs::{any_field, simple_schema};\nuse crate::service_def::{\n    ExecCommand, LogType, std::path::{Path, PathBuf};\nuse std::time::{SystemTime, UNIX_EPOCH};\nuse zbus::{Connection, Proxy};\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]\npub struct ServiceLifecycle {\n    pub last_active: Option<u64>,\n    pub days_since_active: Option<u64>,\n    pub is_orphaned: bool,\n    pub orphan_reason: Option<String>,\n}\n\n/// Path to the s6-rc live database.\nconst S6_RC_LIVE: &str = \"/run/s6-rc\";\n\npub struct ServicePlugin {\n    backend: ServiceBackend,\n}\n\nenum ServiceBackend {\n    S6,\n    Systemd,\n}\n\nimpl Default for ServicePlugin {\n    fn default() -> Self {\n        Self::new()\n    }\n}\n\nimpl ServicePlugin {\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        // Prefer s6 when the live directory exists; fall back to systemd.\n        let backend = if Path::new(S6_RC_LIVE).exists() || Path::new(\"/etc/s6/sv\").exists() {\n            ServiceBackend::S6\n        } else {\n            ServiceBackend::Systemd\n        };\n        Self { backend }\n    }\n\n    /// Connect to systemd via D-Bus.\n    async fn connect_systemd(&self) -> Result<Proxy<'static>> {\n        let conn = Connection::system()\n            .await\n            .context(\"Failed to connect to system D-Bus\")?;\n        Proxy::new(\n            &conn,\n            \"org.freedesktop.systemd1\",\n            \"/org/freedesktop/systemd1\",\n            \"org.freedesktop.systemd1.Manager\",\n        )\n        .await\n        .context(\"Failed to create systemd D-Bus proxy\")\n    }\n\n    /// List systemd services via D-Bus.\n    async fn list_systemd_services(&self) -> Result<Vec<String>> {\n        let proxy = self.connect_systemd().await?;\n        #[allow(clippy::type_complexity)]\n        let units: Vec<(\n            String,\n            String,\n            String,\n            String,\n            String,\n            String,\n            zbus::zvariant::OwnedObjectPath,\n            u32,\n            String,\n            zbus::zvariant::OwnedObjectPath,\n        )> = proxy\n            .call(\"ListUnits\", &())\n            .await\n            .context(\"Failed to list systemd units\")?;\n        Ok(units\n            .into_iter()\n            .filter(|(name, _, _, _, _, _, _, _, _, _)| name.ends_with(\".service\"))\n            .map(|(name, _, _, _, _, _, _, _, _, _)| name)\n            .collect())\n    }\n\n    /// Query ActiveEnterTimestamp for a systemd unit via D-Bus.\n    async fn systemd_last_active(&self, name: &str) -> Result<Option<u64>> {\n        let proxy = self.connect_systemd().await?;\n        let path: zbus::zvariant::OwnedObjectPath = proxy\n            .call(\"GetUnit\", &(name,))\n            .await\n            .context(\"Failed to get unit path\")?;\n        let conn = Connection::system().await?;\n        let unit_proxy = Proxy::new(\n            &conn,\n            \"org.freedesktop.systemd1\",\n            path,\n            \"org.freedesktop.systemd1.Unit\",\n        )\n        .await?;\n        let ts_usec: u64 = unit_proxy\n            .get_property::<u64>(\"ActiveEnterTimestamp\")\n            .await\n            .unwrap_or(0);\n        if ts_usec > 0 {\n            Ok(Some(ts_usec / 1_000_000))\n        } else {\n            Ok(None)\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Auto-generate service from installed binary\n    pub async fn auto_generate_service(&self, binary_path: &Path) -> Result<ServiceDef> {\n        let name = binary_path\n            .file_name()\n            .and_then(|n| n.to_str())\n            .ok_or_else(|| anyhow::anyhow!(\"invalid binary name\"))?;\n\n        Ok(ServiceDef {\n            name: ServiceName::new(name)?,\n            service_type: ServiceType::Simple,\n            exec_start: ExecCommand::new(binary_path.to_path_buf(), vec![])?,\n            exec_stop: None,\n            working_dir: None,\n            user: None,\n            group: None,\n            depends_on: vec![],\n            waits_for: vec![],\n            restart: RestartPolicy::default(),\n            environment: HashMap::new(),\n            env_file: None,\n            resources: None,\n            log_type: LogType::None,\n            ready_notification: ReadyNotification::None,\n            chain_to: None,\n            smooth_recovery: false,\n            enabled: false,\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Convert from systemd unit file (Helper moved to ServicePlugin to avoid polluting schema)\n    fn from_systemd_unit(path: &Path) -> Result<ServiceDef> {\n        let content = std::fs::read_to_string(path)?;\n        let mut exec_start = None;\n        let mut exec_stop = None;\n        let mut working_dir = None;\n        let mut user = None;\n        let mut depends = vec![];\n        let mut env = HashMap::new();\n\n        for line in content.lines() {\n            let line = line.trim();\n            if let Some((k, v)) = line.split_once('=') {\n                match k.trim() {\n                    \"ExecStart\" => {\n                        let parts: Vec<&str> = v.split_whitespace().collect();\n                        if !parts.is_empty() {\n                            if let Ok(cmd) = ExecCommand::new(\n                                PathBuf::from(parts[0]),\n                                parts[1..].iter().map(|s| s.to_string()).collect(),\n                            ) {\n                                exec_start = Some(cmd);\n                            }\n                        }\n                    }\n                    \"ExecStop\" => {\n                        let parts: Vec<&str> = v.split_whitespace().collect();\n                        if !parts.is_empty() {\n                            if let Ok(cmd) = ExecCommand::new(\n                                PathBuf::from(parts[0]),\n                                parts[1..].iter().map(|s| s.to_string()).collect(),\n                            ) {\n                                exec_stop = Some(cmd);\n                            }\n                        }\n                    }\n                    \"WorkingDirectory\" => working_dir = Some(PathBuf::from(v.trim())),\n                    \"User\" => user = Some(v.trim().to_string()),\n                    \"Requires\" | \"Wants\" | \"After\" => {\n                        for dep in v.split_whitespace() {\n     \"Environment\" => {\n                        if let Some((ek, ev)) = v.split_once('=') {\n                            env.insert(ek.trim().to_string(), ev.trim().to_string());\n                        }\n                    }\n                    _ => {}\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        let file_name = path\n            .file_name()\n            .and_then(|n| n.to_str())\n            .unwrap_or(\"unknown\");\n        let name = ServiceName::new(file_name)?;\n\n        Ok(ServiceDef {\n            name,\n            service_type: ServiceType::Simple, // Default, logic should improve\n            exec_start: exec_start.ok_or_else(|| anyhow::anyhow!(\"no ExecStart\"))?,\n            exec_stop,\n            working_dir,\n            user,\n            group: None,\n            depends_on: depends,\n            waits_for: vec![],\n            restart: RestartPolicy::default(),\n            environment: env,\n            env_file: None,\n            resources: None,\n            log_type: LogType::None,\n            ready_notification: ReadyNotification::None,\n            chain_to: None,\n            smooth_recovery: false,\n            enabled: false,\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Convert all systemd units to s6 service definitions\n    pub async fn convert_systemd_to_s6(&self) -> Result<Vec<ServiceDef>> {\n        let mut services = vec![];\n        let systemd_dir = Path::new(\"/etc/systemd/system\");\n\n        if !systemd_dir.exists() {\n            return Ok(services);\n        }\n\n        for entry in std::fs::read_dir(systemd_dir)? {\n            let entry = entry?;\n            let path = entry.path();\n\n            if path.extension().and_then(|e| e.to_str()) == Some(\"service\") {\n                match Self::from_systemd_unit(&path) {\n                    Ok(svc) => {\n                        services.push(svc);\n                    }\n                    Err(e) => {\n                        log::warn!(\"Failed to convert {}: {}\", path.display(), e);\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        Ok(services)\n    }\n//! s6_systemctl plugin — projects the op-s6-systemctl D-Bus daemon state.\n//!\n//! Exposes the daemon's liveness, interface metadata, and a snapshot of all\n//! s6 service units so the UI can render a service manager panel from the schema.\n//!\n//! Schema-driven: every field here maps 1:1 to a UI widget in the schema renderer.\n//!\n//! OSCAL subids:\n//!   obs.service.s6_systemctl.status@v1   — daemon liveness + unit list\n//!   mut.service.s6_systemctl.start@v1    — start a unit via D-Bus\n//!   mut.service.s6_systemctl.stop@v1     — stop a unit via D-Bus\n//!   mut.service.s6_systemctl.restart@v1  — restart a unit via D-Bus\n//!   mut.service.s6_systemctl.enable@v1   — enable a unit via D-Bus\n//!   mut.service.s6_systemctl.disable@v1  — disable a unit via D-Bus\n\nuse anyhow::Result;\nuse async_trait::async_trait;\nuse op_state::{\n    ApplyResult, Checkpoint, DiffMetadata, PluginCapabilities, StateAction, StateDiff, StatePlugin,\n};\nuse op_state_store::{FieldSchema, FieldType, PluginSchema};\nuse serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};\nuse simd_json::{json, OwnedValue as Value};\n\n// ── State structs ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, PartialEq)]\npub struct S6SystemctlState {\n    /// Whether the op-s6-systemctl D-Bus daemon is reachable.\n    pub daemon_running: bool,\n    /// D-Bus bus name the daemon registers.\n    pub bus_name: String,\n    /// D-Bus object path.\n    pub object_path: String,\n    /// D-Bus interface name.\n    pub interface: String,\n    /// All s6 service units with their current status.\n    pub units: Vec<S6UnitStatus>,\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, PartialEq)]\npub struct S6UnitStatus {\n    /// Service name (bare, no suffix).\n    pub id: String,\n    /// \"active\" | \"inactive\" | \"failed\" | \"unknown\"\n    pub active_state: String,\n    /// \"running\" | \"dead\" | \"unknown\"\n    pub sub_state: String,\n    /// Whether the unit starts at boot.\n    pub enabled: bool,\n    /// Main PID if running.\n    pub main_pid: Option<u32>,\n    /// Seconds the process has been up.\n    pub up_time: Option<String>,\n}\n\n// ── Plugin ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\npub struct S6SystemctlPlugin;\n\nimpl S6SystemctlPlugin {\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        Self\n    }\n\n    /// Probe the daemon and enumerate units. Falls back to direct s6 CLI when\n    /// the daemon isn't on the bus yet.\n    async fn collect_state(&self) -> S6SystemctlState {\n        let daemon_running = self.probe_daemon().await;\n        let units = self.enumerate_units(daemon_running).await;\n\n        S6SystemctlState {\n            daemon_running,\n            bus_name: \"org.opdbus.v1.S6.Systemctl\".to_string(),\n            object_path: \"/org/opdbus/v1/s6/systemctl\".to_string(),\n            interface: \"org.opdbus.v1.S6.Systemctl\".to_string(),\n            units,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Check if the daemon is registered on the system bus.\n    async fn probe_daemon(&self) -> bool {\n        use zbus::Connection;\n        let Ok(conn) = Connection::system().await else {\n            return false;\n        };\n        conn.call_method(\n            Some(\"org.freedesktop.DBus\"),\n            \"/org/freedesktop/DBus\",\n            Some(\"org.freedesktop.DBus\"),\n            \"GetNameOwner\",\n            &\"org.opdbus.v1.S6.Systemctl\",\n        )\n        .await\n        .is_ok()\n    }\n\n    /// Enumerate all units. Uses direct s6 CLI — no dependency on the daemon.\n    async fn enumerate_units(&self, daemon_running: bool) -> Vec<S6UnitStatus> {\n        // Get running services\n        let running: std::collections::HashSet<String> = tokio::process::Command::new(\"s6-rc\")\n            .args([\"-a\", \"list\"])\n            .output()\n            .await\n            .map(|o| {\n                String::from_utf8_lossy(&o.stdout)\n                    .lines()\n                    .map(|l| l.trim().to_string())\n                    .filter(|l| !l.is_empty())\n                    .collect()\n            })\n            .unwrap_or_default();\n\n        // Get all available services from /etc/s6/sv\n        let mut all_names: Vec<String> = Vec::new();\n        if let Ok(mut dir) = tokio::fs::read_dir(\"/etc/s6/sv\").await {\n            while let Ok(Some(entry)) = dir.next_entry().await {\n                if let Ok(name) = entry.file_name().into_string() {\n                    all_names.push(name);\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        all_names.sort();\n\n        let mut units = Vec::new();\n        for name in all_names {\n            let is_active = running.contains(&name);\n            let enabled =\n                tokio::fs::metadata(format!(\"/etc/s6-rc/bundle/default/contents.d/{}\", name))\n                    .await\n                    .is_ok();\n\n            // Get pid/uptime from s6-svstat if active\n            let (main_pid, up_time) = if is_active {\n                self.svstat_info(&name).await\n            } else {\n                (None, None)\n            };\n\n            let _ = daemon_running; // available for future D-Bus enrichment\n\n            units.push(S6UnitStatus {\n                id: name,\n                active_state: if is_active {\n                    \"active\".to_string()\n                } else {\n                    \"inactive\".to_string()\n                },\n                sub_state: if is_active {\n                    \"running\".to_string()\n                } else {\n                    \"dead\".to_string()\n                },\n                enabled,\n                main_pid,\n format!(\"/etc/s6/sv/{}\", name);\n        let Ok(output) = tokio::process::Command::new(\"s6-svstat\")\n            .arg(&path)\n            .output()\n            .await\n        else {\n            return (None, None);\n        };\n        let text = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout);\n        // \"up (pid 1234) 3600 seconds\"\n        let pid = text\n            .split(\"pid \")\n            .nth(1)\n            .and_then(|s| s.split(')').next())\n            .and_then(|p| p.trim().parse::<u32>().ok());\n        let uptime = text.split_whitespace().rev().nth(1).map(|s| s.to_string());\n        (pid, uptime)\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Default for S6SystemctlPlugin {\n    fn default() -> Self {\n        Self::new()\n    }\n}\n\n#[async_trait]\nimpl StatePlugin for S6SystemctlPlugin {\n    fn name(&self) -> &str {\n        \"s6_systemctl\"\n    }\n\n    fn version(&self) -> &str {\n        \"1.0.0\"\n    }\n\n    fn is_available(&self) -> bool {\n        // Available as long as s6 is installed; daemon liveness is a field in state\n        std::path::Path::new(\"/etc/s6/sv\").exists()\n    }\n\n    fn schema(&self) -> Option<PluginSchema> {\n  )\n                .field(\n                    \"object_path\",\n                    FieldSchema {\n                        field_type: FieldType::String,\n                        required: true,\n                        description: \"D-Bus object path\".to_string(),\n                        default: Some(json!(\"/org/opdbus/v1/s6/systemctl\")),\n                        example: None,\n                        constraints: Vec::new(),\n                        read_only: true,\n                        read_only_when: None,\n                    },\n                )\n                .field(\n                    \"interface\",\n                    FieldSchema {\n                        field_type: FieldType::String,\n                        required: true,\n                        description: \"D-Bus interface name\".to_string(),\n                        default: Some(json!(\"org.opdbus.v1.S6.Systemctl\")),\n                        example: None,\n                        constraints: Vec::new(),\n                        read_only: true,\n                        read_only_when: None,\n                    },\n                )\n                .field(\n                    \"units\",\n                    FieldSchema {\n                        field_type: FieldType::Any,\n                        required: true,\n                        description: \"All s6 service units
