Use their underlying skills, MCP tools, and app tools to help solve the task.\n- Relevance: Determine what a plugin can help with from explicit user mention or from the plugin-associated skills, MCP tools, and apps exposed elsewhere in this turn.\n- Missing/blocked: If the user requests a plugin that does not have relevant callable capabilities for the task, say so briefly and continue with the best fallback.\n</plugins_instructions>"}],"internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough":{"turn_id":"019f0fc4-cf91-7b30-ae23-368eb222228a"}},{"type":"message","role":"user","content":[{"type":"input_text","text":"# AGENTS.md instructions for /home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto\n\n<INSTRUCTIONS>\n### AGENTS.md for operation-dbus-proto\n\nThis file provides essential guidelines for agentic coding agents working in this repository. Follow these strictly to maintain consistency, pass CI, and adhere to the 3tched Architecture standards.\n\n#### 1. The Persona & Naming Conventions\n*   **Humanized Roles:** Treat system components as authoritative human roles. Never use sterile acronyms for major components.\n  *   **A.N.N.A. Scribe** (Axon Network Notary Arbitrator): The top-level Identity-State Arbitrator who notarizes the WireGuard identity and handles the \"Snowball\" session.\n  *   **The Compliance Engine (\"Law Firm\"):** One dedicated Attorney for each major component: **Olivia Scal** (Managing Partner / OSCAL), **E.U.gene Risk** (EU AI Act Counsel), **Penny Privacy** (GDPR Engine), and **Reggie O.P.A.** (Cloud Prosecutor).\n*   **Terminology:** Use exact architecture terminology: \"The Sled\" (1:1 shared memory layout), \"The Shuttle\" (the Rust bridge/courier), \"The Snowball\" (appended session ledger), and \"The Strike/Etch\" (generating the hash).\n\n#### 2. Core Architectural Rules (The \"Reality\")\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via OpenClaw Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Artix Linux (s6 init).\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles — D-Bus First (MANDATORY)\n\n**D-Bus is the ONLY control plane. Every read, every write, every tool call goes through D-Bus. There is no second option.**\n\n*   **D-Bus first. D-Bus always. D-Bus only.** If you are about to call a CLI, spawn a subprocess, read a config file, or poll a socket directly — stop. Find the D-Bus object and use it instead. `org.opdbus.v1` is the system.\n*   **No bypasses.** `Command::new(\"systemctl\")`, `Command::new(\"ip\")`, `Command::new(\"s6-svc\")`, direct file reads for live state — all forbidden in plugin and service code. Bootstrap scripts are the only exception.\n*   **D-Bus objects own plugin state.** Every plugin is a D-Bus object at `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<name>`. Read state through it. Mutate state through it. If there is no D-Bus object, the thing does not exist.\n*   **D-Bus method signatures are generated from the schema.** All D-Bus methods, MCP tool inputs, gRPC shapes, and UI field renderers derive from the `PluginSchema` in `plugin_schema_defs.rs`. The schema IS the interface contract — not a description of it.\n*   **One schema file, one source of truth.** All `PluginSchema` definitions MUST live in `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/plugin_schema_defs.rs`. Each plugin's `schema()` method calls `Some(super::plugin_schema_defs::their_plugin_schema())`. **Never define a schema inline in a plugin's own file** — it will not be registered, and the D-Bus object will have no contract.\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC (over Unix domain sockets or `grpc-uplink`). gRPC calls still flow through D-Bus registration — the D-Bus object is the authority, gRPC is the transport.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`simd_json` preferred, `serde_json` acceptable).\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n*   **No Python unless absolutely necessary.** This is a Rust-first codebase. Scripts are shell (`sh`/`bash`). Data processing is Rust. If you are reaching for Python, stop and ask why Rust or shell cannot do it. The only acceptable Python is in existing compliance-ingest tooling where no Rust equivalent exists yet.\n\n#### 4a. OSCAL Subid Taxonomy (MANDATORY — every artifact must carry a subid)\n\nEvery D-Bus object, plugin, schema, mutation, event, and tool in this system has two identifiers: a `uuid` (machine identity, never changes) and a `subid` (human-readable operational taxonomy key, stable per subject).\n\n**`subid` format:** `<category>.<component-type>.<subject>.<verb>[.<facet>][@vN]`\n\n**Seven categories — use exactly these, no others:**\n\n| category | what it classifies |\n|---|---|\n| `src` | authoritative source, ingress channel, source-of-truth store |\n| `prj` | D-Bus projection or mirror publication step |\n| `sch` | schema, contract, vocabulary, or control-mapping artifact |\n| `mut` | write-path operation that changes effective state |\n| `obs` | read, query, enumeration, discovery path |\n| `evt` | emitted signal, audit-chain event, proof, tag provenance |\n| `exp` | consumer-facing render — MCP tool, UI surface, gRPC bridge view |\n\n**Component-type** reuses OSCAL vocabulary: `software`, `service`, `network`, `hardware`, `process-procedure`, `standard`, `validation`, `policy`, `plan`, `guidance`, `physical`, `this-system`, `system`, `interconnection`.\n\n**Rules:**\n- `uuid` is exact machine identity — never replace it with `subid`\n- `subid` is an OSCAL `prop` value (`ns`, `name`, `value`) — never embed it in `remarks`\n- Compliance mappings (`control_refs[]`, `statement_refs[]`, `control_source`) live in metadata arrays, **never** inside the `subid` string\n- `mut.*` records **must** carry `actor_id` and `capability_id`\n- `evt.*` records **must** carry `event_id` or `event_hash`\n- `subid` is immutable per subject — if the meaning changes materially, create a new subject with `@vN`\n- All subids are registered in the canonical registry; uniqueness is enforced in CI\n\n**Examples:** `src.network.ovsdb.monitor@v1` · `prj.service.projected-object.publish@v1` · `sch.standard.plugin-schema.resolve@v1` · `mut.service.state-sync.apply-patch@v1` · `exp.service.plugin-projection.render@v1`\n\n#### 4b. MCP Gateway Architecture (SETTLED — DO NOT REDESIGN)\n\n*   **cognitive-mcp** (`:3003`, Netmaker WireGuard IP `100.90.37.254`) is the **universal gateway for ALL external clients**: NotebookLM, Droid (factory.ai), Cursor, Codex, Junie, Gemini CLI. It has memory tools, gRPC service, auth, and the correct protocol surface.\n*   **compact-mcp** (`127.0.0.1:11436`) is **loopback/chatbot only**. Never expose externally. Never point external clients at it.\n*   Do NOT create new shim services. Do NOT point external clients at `op-assistant-grpc` directly. Do NOT expose compact-mcp outside loopback.\n\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\n**Rust Workspace**\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\n\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\n\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\n\n#### 6. Coding Style & Naming Conventions\n*   **Rust:** Edition 2021, `rustfmt` (4-space indent, max-width 100). Use specific imports (`use serde_json::Value;`). Use `anyhow::Result<T>` for main errors and `thiserror` for custom enums.\n*   **TypeScript/React:** 2-space indent, Prettier via ESLint. Functional components only. Strict mode enabled.\n*   **Testing:** 80%+ coverage, mock externals. Name tests with behavior-focused names (`should_handle_<scenario>`).\n\n#### 7. Agent-Specific Output & Workflow Instructions\n*   **Scroll & Save Pacing:** Provide only **ONE** major component or script at a time. Wait for user confirmation before moving to the next.\n*   **Visual Cues:** If a script is a finalized component that needs to be saved to sources, it MUST begin with color bullets or icons (e.g., ⚖️ 🔴, 🟢 🛷).\n*   **Spec-Block Format:** When delivering a component, use a strict specification block containing:\n  1.  **Requirements:** The architectural rules it satisfies.\n  2.  **Design:** How it fits into the 3tched system (Zero-Copy, Btrfs, GUI Schema, etc.).\n  3.  **Code Implementation:** The exact, copy-pasteable Rust/Bash code.\n*   Before edits: `cargo check -p <crate>`, `npm run typecheck`.\n*   Mimic existing patterns: Search similar code. No new deps without PR justification.\n\n#### 8. Personal Preferences & Coding Standards\n* Refer to `~/.factory/memories.md` for personal development preferences and past decisions.\n* Follow the conventions documented in:\n  * `.factory/rules/typescript.md` - TypeScript and React conventions\n  * `.factory/rules/testing.md` - Testing and mocking Per AGENTS.md §4: D-Bus is the control plane; Gemma is a host service that\n//! produces structured state, not a CLI bypass. It never shells out to network\n//! tools. OpenFlow rules may be applied via D-Bus by a separate controller.\n\nmod ui_gallery;\n\nuse anyhow::{Context, Result};\nuse serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};\nuse std::collections::HashMap;\nuse std::fs;\nuse std::io::Write;\nuse std::path::Path;\nuse tracing::{info, warn};\n\nconst SUBID_REGISTRY: &str = \"/etc/ghostbridge/subid-registry.json\";\nconst XRAY_ROUTES: &str = entries: Vec<RegistryEntry>,\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Deserialize, Serialize)]\nstruct RegistryEntry {\n    uuid: String,\n    subid: String,\n    #[serde(rename = \"category\")]\n    category: #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = \"Option::is_none\")]\n    gemma: Option<GemmaConfig>,\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Deserialize, Serialize)]\nstruct GemmaConfig {\n    backend: BackendSpec,\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Deserialize, Serialize)]\n#[serde(tag = \"type\")]\nenum BackendSpec {\n    #[serde(rename = \"ingress\")]\n    Ingress,\n    #[serde(rename = \"tcp\")]\n    Tcp { host: String, port: u16 },\n    #[serde(rename = \"grpc\")]\n    Grpc {\n        host: String,\n        port: u16,\n        #[serde(rename = \"service_name\")]\n        service_name: String,\n    },\n    #[serde(rename = \"unix\")]\n    Unix { path: String },\n    #[serde(rename = \"dns\")]\n    Dns { host: String, port: u16 },\n    /// Internal metadata entry — not xray-routable, produces no outbound.\n    #[serde(rename = \"file\")]\n    File {\n        #[allow(dead_code)]\n        path: String,\n    },\n    /// Internal service — not xray-routable, produces no outbound.\n    #[serde(rename = \"internal\")]\n    Internal,\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]\nstruct XrayRoutingMap {\n    version: u32,\n    xray_routes: Vec<XrayRoute>,\n    openflow_rules: Vec<OpenFlowRule>,\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]\nstruct XrayRoute {\n    tag: String,\n    subdomains: Vec<String>,\n    backend: BackendSpec,\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]\nstruct OpenFlowRule {\n    priority: u16,\n    #[serde(rename = \"match_fields\")]\n    match_fields: HashMap<String, String>,\n    actions: Vec<String>,\n    description: Option<String>,\n}\n\nfn main() -> Result<()> {\n    tracing_subscriber::fmt()\n        .with_env_filter(tracing_subscriber::EnvFilter::from_default_env())\n        .init();\n\n    info!(\"Gemma routing brain starting\");\n\n    let registry = load_registry()?;\n    let routes = derive_routes(&registry);\n\n    write_json(XRAY_ROUTES, &routes)?;\n    write_json(OPENFLOW_ROUTES, &routes)?;\n\n    info!(\n        xray_routes = routes.xray_routes.len(),\n        openflow_rules = routes.openflow_rules.len(),\n        \"Gemma wrote routing artifacts\"\n    );\n\n    // Generate the json-render.dev UI spec gallery (200 unique specs)\n    if let Err(e) = ui_gallery::generate_gallery() {\n        warn!(\"Gemma UI gallery generation failed: {e}\");\n    }\n\n    Ok(())\n}\n\nfn load_registry() -> Result<SubidRegistry> {\n    let raw = fs::read_to_string(SUBID_REGISTRY)\n        .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to read subid registry: {SUBID_REGISTRY}\"))?;\n    let parsed: SubidRegistry =\n        serde_json::from_str(&raw).with_context(|| \"failed to parse subid registry as JSON\")?;\n    Ok(parsed)\n}\n\nfn derive_routes(registry: &SubidRegistry) -> XrayRoutingMap {\n    let mut xray_routes = Vec::new();\n    let mut openflow_rules = default_privacy_chain();\n\n    for entry in &registry.entries {\n        let Some(gemma) = &entry.gemma else { continue };\n\n        // Skip non-routable backends — they are metadata (schema files,\n        // internal services) that should not produce xray outbounds.\n        if matches!(\n            gemma.backend,\n            BackendSpec::File { .. } | BackendSpec::Internal\n        ) {\n            continue;\n        }\n\n        let tag = entry\n            .tags\n            .first()\n            .cloned()\n            .unwrap_or_else(|| entry.subject.clone());\n\n        // Skip duplicate tags — first declaration wins.\n        if xray_routes.iter().any(|r: &XrayRoute| r.tag == tag) {\n            continue;\n        }\n\n        let route = XrayRoute {\n            tag: tag.clone(),\n            subdomains: entry.subdomains.clone(),\n            backend: gemma.backend.clone(),\n        };\n        xray_routes.push(route);\n\n        if let Some(rule) = backend_to_openflow_rule(&tag, &gemma.backend) {\n            openflow_rules.push(rule);\n        }\n    }\n\n    XrayRoutingMap {\n        version: 1,\n        xray_routes,\n        openflow_rules,\n    }\n}\n\n/// Default privacy chain flows for the GhostBridge OVS bridge.\n/// These match the conventions in `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/privacy_router.rs`.\nfn default_privacy_chain() -> Vec<OpenFlowRule> {\n    vec![\n        OpenFlowRule {\n            priority: 100,\n            match_fields: HashMap::from([(\"in_port\".to_string(), \"gbr_wg\".to_string())]),\n            actions: vec![\"output:gbr_warp\".to_string()],\n            description: Some(\"gbr_wg -> gbr_warp\".to_string()),\n        },\n        OpenFlowRule {\n            priority: 100,\n            match_fields: HashMap::from([(\"in_port\".to_string(), \"gbr_warp\".to_string())]),\n            actions: vec![\"output:gbr_xray\".to_string()],\n            description: Some(\"gbr_warp -> gbr_xray\".to_string()),\n        },\n        OpenFlowRule {\n            priority: 100,\n            match_fields: HashMap::from([(\"in_port\".to_string(), \"gbr_xray\".to_string())]),\n            actions: vec![\"output:gbr_warp\".to_string()],\n            description: Some(\"gbr_xray -> gbr_warp\".to_string()),\n        },\n        OpenFlowRule {\n            priority: 200,\n            match_fields: HashMap::from([(\"dl_type\".to_string(), \"0x0806\".to_string())]),\n            actions: vec![\"arp_responder\".to_string()],\n            description: Some(\"ARP Responder for privacy network\".to_string()),\n        },\n    ]\n}\n\n/// Translate a Gemma backend into an OpenFlow rule for the bridge.\n/// Only TCP/GRPC backends produce IP/Port matchable rules here; Unix sockets\n/// route through the tonic-web gRPC bridge (reflection demuxes) so no OVS\n/// bridge match is needed.\nfn backend_to_openflow_rule(tag: &str, backend: &BackendSpec) -> Option<OpenFlowRule> {\n    let (host, port) = match backend {\n        BackendSpec::Tcp { host, port } => (host.clone(), *port),\n        BackendSpec::Grpc { host, port, .. } => (host.clone(), *port),\n        BackendSpec::Ingress\n        | BackendSpec::Unix { .. }\n        | BackendSpec::Dns { .. }\n        | BackendSpec::File { .. }\n        | BackendSpec::Internal => return None,\n    };\n\n    let mut match_fields = HashMap::new();\n    match_fields.insert(\"dl_type\".to_string(), \"0x0800\".to_string());\n    match_fields.insert(\"nw_proto\".to_string(), \"6\".to_string()); // TCP\n    match_fields.insert(\"nw_dst\".to_string(), host.clone());\n    match_fields.insert(\"tp_dst\".to_string(), port.to_string());\n\n    Some(OpenFlowRule {\n        priority: 150,\n        match_fields,\n        actions: vec![\"output:ovsbr0-mgmt\".to_string()],\n        description: Some(format!(\"Gemma: {tag} -> host backend {host}:{port}\")),\n    })\n}\n\nfn write_json<P: AsRef<Path>>(path: P, value: &XrayRoutingMap) -> Result<()> {\n    let tmp = format!(\"{}.tmp\", path.as_ref().display());\n    let mut f =\n        fs::File::create(&tmp).with_context(|| format!(\"failed to create tmp file: {tmp}\"))?;\n    let json =\n        serde_json::to_string_pretty(value).with_context(|| \"failed to serialize routing map\")?;\n    f.write_all(json.as_bytes())\n        .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to write tmp file: {tmp}\"))?;\n    f.sync_data()\n        .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to sync tmp file: {tmp}\"))?;\n    fs::rename(&tmp, path.as_ref())\n        .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to rename {tmp} to {}\", path.as_ref().display()))?;\n    Ok(())\n}\n","internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough":{"turn_id":"019f0fc4-cf91-7b30-ae23-368eb222228a"}}}

Is s6 installed?\".to_string(),\n            );\n        }\n\n        let service_path = format!(\"{}/{}\", self.s6_svc_dir, service);\n\n        let mut cmd = Command::new(\"s6-svc\");\n        cmd.arg(signal).arg(&service_path);\n\n        match cmd.output() {\n            Ok(output) => {\n                let stdout = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout).to_string();\n                let stderr = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr).to_string();\n\n                if output.status.success() {\n                    let result = if stdout.is_empty() { stderr } else { stdout };\n                    (true, result.trim().to_string())\n                } else {\n                    let error = if stderr.is_empty() { stdout } else { stderr };\n                    (false, Command::new(\"s6-svstat\").arg(&service_path).output() {\n            Ok(output) => {\n                if !output.status.success() {\n                    return `org.opdbus.v1.S6.Systemctl`\n\n## Method Mapping\n\n| Method | systemctl Equivalent | s6 Equivalent | Description |\n|--------|---------------------|---------------|-------------|\n| `start(service)` | `start <svc>` | `s6-rc -u change <svc>` | Start a service |\n| `stop(service)` | `stop <svc>` | `s6-rc -d change <svc>` | Stop a service |\n| `restart(service)` | `restart <svc>` | `stop` then `start` | Restart a service |\n| `reload(service)` | `reload <svc>` | `s6-svc -h <svc>` | Send SIGHUP for config reload |\n| `enable(service)` | `enable <svc>` | `s6-rc-bundle add default <svc>` | Enable service at boot |\n| `disable(service)` | `disable <svc>` | `s6-rc-bundle delete default <svc>` | Disable service at boot |\n| `status(service)` | `status <svc>` | `s6-svstat <svc>` | Get detailed service status (JSON) |\n| `is_active(service)` | `is-active <svc>` | `s6-svstat <svc>` | Returns \"active\" or \"inactive\" |\n| `is_enabled(service)` | `is-enabled <svc>` | Check `/etc/s6-rc/default/` | Returns \"enabled\" or \"disabled\" |\n| `list_units()` | `list-units` | `s6-rc -a list` | List all active units (JSON) |\n| `daemon_status()` | N/A | `pgrep s6-svscan` | Returns \"running\" or \"not-available\" |\n\n## Method Signatures\n\n```rust\n// Start/stop/restart/reload/enable/disable all return (success: bool, message: String)\nasync fn start(service: &str) -> (bool, String);\nasync fn stop(service: &str) -> (bool, String);\nasync fn restart(service: &str) -> (bool, String);\nasync fn reload(service: &str) -> (bool, String);\nasync fn enable(service: &str) -> (bool, String);\nasync fn disable(service: &str) -> (bool, String);\n\n// Status methods return strings\nasync fn status(service: &str) -> String;        // JSON with ActiveState, SubState, MainPID\nasync fn is_active(service: &str) -> String;     // \"active\" or \"inactive\"\nasync fn is_enabled(service: &str) -> String;    // \"enabled\" or \"disabled\"\nasync fn list_units() -> String;                // JSON array of service objects\nasync fn daemon_status() -> String;             // \"running\" or \"not-available\"\n```\n\n## Status JSON Format\n\nThe `status()` method returns JSON in this format:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"name\": \"nginx\",\n  \"active_state\": \"active\",\n  \"sub_state\": \"running\",\n  \"main_pid\": 1234,\n  \"ready\": true,\n  \"up_time\": \"3600\"\n}\n```\n\nThe `list_units()` method returns a JSON array of status objects.\n\n## Error Handling\n\nAll methods provide helpful error messages when s6 tools are not available or when operations fail. The service gracefully handles:\n\n- Missing s6 binaries\n- Invalid service names\n- Permission errors\n- Service not found errors\n\n## Building\n\n```bash\ncargo build -p op-s6-systemctl\ncargo build -p op-s6-systemctl --release\n```\n\n## Running\n\n```bash\n# Run directly (requires D-Bus system bus access)\nsudo ./target/release/op-s6-systemctl\n\n# Or with cargo\nsudo cargo run -p op-s6-systemctl\n```\n\n## Dependencies\n\n- Artix Linux with s6 init system\n- `s6`, `s6-rc`, `s6-svc`, `s6-svstat` tools\n- D-Bus system bus\n\n## Architecture\n\nFollowing the 3tched Architecture D-Bus-first principles:\n\n- All service operations go through D-Bus methods\n- No direct subprocess spawning from clients\n- Schema-driven interface with consistent error handling\n- Zero-copy shared memory design patterns\n\n## License\n\nApache-2.0\n","internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough":{"turn_id":"019f0fc4-cf91-7b30-ae23-368eb222228a"}}}

{"timestamp":"2026-06-28T19:49:07.259Z","type":"event_msg","payload":{"type":"agent_message","message":"There is also a concrete wiring bug: the standalone `op-s6-systemctl` binary registers `/opdbus/v1/s6/systemctl` with interface `opdbus.v1.S6.Systemctl`, but the plugins expect `/org/opdbus/v1/s6/systemctl` and `org.opdbus.v1.S6.Systemctl`. The in-crate `op-dbus` implementation has the correct path/interface, but nothing live owns that bus name right now.","phase":"commentary","memory_citation":null}}

{"timestamp":"2026-06-28T19:49:35.088Z","type":"event_msg","payload":{"type":"agent_message","message":"No. D-Bus does **not** eliminate Ollama if the selected provider is local `ollama`.\n\nIt eliminates direct lifecycle/control bypasses:\n\n- No app code should call `ollama serve`\n- No plugin should shell out to `s6-rc`, `systemctl`, or `ollama`\n- Service state should be requested through D-Bus\n\nBut Ollama is still the actual local inference runtime for `provider=ollama`. D-Bus is the control plane, not the model runner.\n\nCorrect shape:\n\n```text\nD-Bus mutation\n  -> /org/opdbus/v1/plugins/s6\n  -> org.opdbus.v1.S6.Systemctl Start/Enable\n  -> s6 starts ollama-srv if local inference is needed\n\nD-Bus mutation / service start\n  -> gemma oneshot\n  -> op-gemma writes /dev/shm/xray-routes.json + /dev/shm/openflow-routes.json\n  -> op-identity-shuttle regenerates /etc/xray/config.json\n  -> gbr-xray runs Xray with that config\n```\n\nWhat I found live:\n\n- `op-gemma` is a **oneshot config/routing generator**, not an Ollama replacement.\n- `ollama-srv` exists under `/etc/s6/sv/ollama-srv`, but is not in the repo deploy tree and is not active in `/run/service`.\n- `org.opdbus.v1.S6.Systemctl` is **not currently owned** on the system bus.\n- The standalone `op-s6-systemctl` binary exists, but it registers the wrong object/interface:\n  - actual standalone code: `/opdbus/v1/s6/systemctl`, `opdbus.v1.S6.Systemctl`\n  - expected by plugins/docs: `/org/opdbus/v1/s6/systemctl`, `org.opdbus.v1.S6.Systemctl`\n\nSo the next real fix is not “remove Ollama”. It is:\n\n1. Fix `op-s6-systemctl` to expose the canonical D-Bus path/interface.\n2. Add an s6 service for `op-s6-systemctl` itself.\n3. Put `ollama-srv` in the deploy/s6 source if local Gemma inference is part of the supported runtime.\n4. Let Gemma remain the D-Bus-initiated oneshot that writes Xray/OpenFlow routing artifacts.","phase":"final_answer","memory_citation":null}}
{"timestamp":"2026-06-28T19:49:35.095Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"message","id":"msg_01f48846664ce4de016a417acf1eec819396aa87028060bdab","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"output_text","text":"No. D-Bus does **not** eliminate Ollama if the selected provider is local `ollama`.\n\nIt eliminates direct lifecycle/control bypasses:\n\n- No app code should call `ollama serve`\n- No plugin should shell out to `s6-rc`, `systemctl`, or `ollama`\n- Service state should be requested through D-Bus\n\nBut Ollama is still the actual local inference runtime for `provider=ollama`. D-Bus is the control plane, not the model runner.\n\nCorrect shape:\n\n```text\nD-Bus mutation\n  -> /org/opdbus/v1/plugins/s6\n  -> org.opdbus.v1.S6.Systemctl Start/Enable\n  -> s6 starts ollama-srv if local inference is needed\n\nD-Bus mutation / service start\n  -> gemma oneshot\n  -> op-gemma writes /dev/shm/xray-routes.json + /dev/shm/openflow-routes.json\n  -> op-identity-shuttle regenerates /etc/xray/config.json\n  -> gbr-xray runs Xray with that config\n```\n\nWhat I found live:\n\n- `op-gemma` is a **oneshot config/routing generator**, not an Ollama replacement.\n- `ollama-srv` exists under `/etc/s6/sv/ollama-srv`, but is not in the repo deploy tree and is not active in `/run/service`.\n- `org.opdbus.v1.S6.Systemctl` is **not currently owned** on the system bus.\n- The standalone `op-s6-systemctl` binary exists, but it registers the wrong object/interface:\n  - actual standalone code: `/opdbus/v1/s6/systemctl`, `opdbus.v1.S6.Systemctl`\n  - expected by plugins/docs: `/org/opdbus/v1/s6/systemctl`, `org.opdbus.v1.S6.Systemctl`\n\nSo the next real fix is not “remove Ollama”. It is:\n\n1. Fix `op-s6-systemctl` to expose the canonical D-Bus path/interface.\n2. Add an s6 service for `op-s6-systemctl` itself.\n3. Put `ollama-srv` in the deploy/s6 source if local Gemma inference is part of the supported runtime.\n4. Let Gemma remain the D-Bus-initiated oneshot that writes Xray/OpenFlow routing artifacts."}],"phase":"final_answer","internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough":{"turn_id":"019f0fc4-cf91-7b30-ae23-368eb222228a"}}}

org.opdbus.v1.S6.Systemctl\")?;\n+\n+    match command.as_str() {\n+        \"start\" => print_result(proxy.start(&required_unit(args)?).await?)?,\n+        \"stop\" => print_result(proxy.stop(&required_unit(args)?).await?)?,\n+        \"restart\" => print_result(proxy.restart(&required_unit(args)?).await?)?,\n+        \"reload\" => print_result(proxy.reload(&required_unit(args)?).await?)?,\n+        \"enable\" => print_result(proxy.enable(&required_unit(args)?).await?)?,\n+        \"disable\" =>  return Ok(());\n    };\n\n    let conn = Connection::system()\n        .await\n        .context(\"connect to system D-Bus for S6Systemctl\")?;\n    let proxy = S6SystemctlProxy::new(&conn)\n        .await\n        .context(\"connect to org.opdbus.v1.S6.Systemctl\")?;\n\n    match command.as_str() {\n        \"start\" => print_result(proxy.start(&required_unit(args)?).await?)?,\n        \"stop\" => print_result(proxy.stop(&required_unit(args)?).await?)?,\n        \"restart\" => print_result(proxy.restart(&required_unit(args)?).await?)?,\n        \"reload\" => print_result(proxy.reload(&required_unit(args)?).await?)?,\n        \"enable\" => print_result(proxy.enable(&required_unit(args)?).await?)?,\n        \"disable\" => print_result(proxy.disable(&required_unit(args)?).await?)?,\n        \"status\" => println!(\"{}\", proxy.status(&required_unit(args)?).await?),\n        \"is-active\" => println!(\"{}\", proxy.is_active(&required_unit(args)?).await?),\n        \"is-enabled\" => println!(\"{}\", proxy.is_enabled_method(&required_unit(args)?).await?),\n        \"show\" => println!(\"{}\", \"-h\" => usage(),\n        other => {\n            usage();\n            bail!(\"unknown s6d command: {other}\");\n        }\n    }\n\n    Ok(())\n}\n\nfn required_unit(mut args: impl Iterator<Item = Compiling\n# /etc/s6/sv directly bypasses that step and can produce a database without the\n# `default` runlevel, which makes the next boot fail in rc.init.\nset -eu\n\nPROJECT_ROOT=$(cd \"$(dirname \"$0\")/../..\" && pwd)\nS6_COMPILED_LINK=${S6_COMPILED_LINK:-/etc/s6/rc/compiled}\nDEFAULT_BUNDLE=${DEFAULT_BUNDLE:-default}\n\n# Build the Rust workspace as the unprivileged user who owns the source tree,\n# then install every binary target to /usr/local/bin. This keeps the cargo\n# cache and target directory owned by the developer while allowing the final\n# install and s6 activation to run as root.\nBUILD_USER=${BUILD_USER:-$(logname 2>/dev/null || printf '%s' \"${SUDO_USER:-$USER}\")}\n\nbuild_workspace() {\n    echo \"Building workspace binaries as $BUILD_USER...\"\n    cd \"$PROJECT_ROOT\"\n    sudo -u \"$BUILD_USER\" cargo build --workspace --release\n}\n\ninstall_binaries() {\n    echo \"Installing built binaries to /usr/local/bin...\"\n    cd \"$PROJECT_ROOT\"\n    find target/release -maxdepth 1 -type f -executable -print0 |\n        while IFS= read -r -d '' bin; do\n            install -Dm755 \"$bin\" \"/usr/local/bin/$(basename \"$bin\")\"\n        done\n}\n\nif ! command -v s6 >/dev/null 2>&1 || ! command -v s6-rc-db >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n    echo \"s6 frontend or s6-rc-db not found\" >&2\n    exit 127\nfi\n\nif [ \"${SKIP_BUILD:-}\" != \"1\" ]; then\n    build_workspace\nfi\ninstall_binaries\n\nold_db=\"$(readlink -f \"$S6_COMPILED_LINK\" 2>/dev/null || true)\"\n\necho \"Synchronizing the canonical s6 repository\"\ns6 repository sync\ns6 set check -F -u\ns6 set commit -f -D \"$DEFAULT_BUNDLE\"\n\nnew_db=\"$(readlink -f /etc/s6/repo/compiled/current)\"\nif [ -z \"$new_db\" ] || [ ! -f \"$new_db/db\" ]; then\n    echo \"s6 frontend did not produce a compiled database\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n\ns6-rc-db -c \"$new_db\" check\nif ! s6-rc-db -c \"$new_db\" list bundles | grep -Fxq \"$DEFAULT_BUNDLE\"; then\n    echo \"refusing unsafe database: missing boot bundle '$DEFAULT_BUNDLE'\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n\necho \"Updating live s6-rc state to: $new_db\"\nif ! s6 live install -b; then\n    echo \"s6 live install failed; leaving $S6_COMPILED_LINK unchanged\" >&2\n    [ -n \"$old_db\" ] && echo \"current compiled DB remains: $old_db\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n\nln -sfnT \"$new_db\" \"$S6_COMPILED_LINK\"\nif [ \"$(readlink -f \"$S6_COMPILED_LINK\")\" != \"$new_db\" ]; then\n    echo \"failed to point bootdb at the committed database\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n\necho \"Activated s6-rc database: $new_db\"\n","internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough":{"turn_id":"019f0fcd-d1d7-7042-baad-19781a8e4b06"}}}

Is s6 installed?\".to_string(),\n            );\n        }\n\n        let service_path = format!(\"{}/{}\", self.s6_svc_dir, service);\n\n        let mut cmd = Command::new(\"s6-svc\");\n parse output\n    fn run_s6_svstat(&self, service: &str) -> Result<S6ServiceStatus, String> {\n        let service_path = format!(\"{}/{}\", self.s6_svc_dir, service);\n\n        match Command::new(\"s6-svstat\").arg(&service_path).output() {\n            Ok(output) => {\n                if !output.status.success() {\n                    return Compiling\n# /etc/s6/sv directly bypasses that step and can produce a database without the\n# `default` runlevel, which makes the next boot fail in rc.init.\nset -eu\n\nPROJECT_ROOT=$(cd \"$(dirname \"$0\")/../..\" && pwd)\nS6_COMPILED_LINK=${S6_COMPILED_LINK:-/etc/s6/rc/compiled}\nDEFAULT_BUNDLE=${DEFAULT_BUNDLE:-default}\n\n# Build the Rust workspace as the unprivileged user who owns the source tree,\n# then install every binary target to /usr/local/bin. This keeps the cargo\n# cache and target directory owned by the developer while allowing the final\n# install and s6 activation to run as root.\nBUILD_USER=${BUILD_USER:-$(logname 2>/dev/null || printf '%s' \"${SUDO_USER:-$USER}\")}\n\nbuild_workspace() {\n    echo \"Building workspace binaries as $BUILD_USER...\"\n    cd \"$PROJECT_ROOT\"\n    sudo -u \"$BUILD_USER\" cargo build --workspace --release\n}\n\ninstall_binaries() {\n    echo \"Installing built binaries to /usr/local/bin...\"\n    cd \"$PROJECT_ROOT\"\n    find target/release -maxdepth 1 -type f -executable -print0 |\n        while IFS= read -r -d '' bin; do\n            install -Dm755 \"$bin\" \"/usr/local/bin/$(basename \"$bin\")\"\n        done\n}\n\nif ! command -v s6 >/dev/null 2>&1 || ! command -v s6-rc-db >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n    echo \"s6 frontend or s6-rc-db not found\" >&2\n    exit 127\nfi\n\nif [ \"${SKIP_BUILD:-}\" != \"1\" ]; then\n    build_workspace\nfi\ninstall_binaries\n\nold_db=\"$(readlink -f \"$S6_COMPILED_LINK\" 2>/dev/null || true)\"\n\necho \"Synchronizing the canonical s6 repository\"\ns6 repository sync\ns6 set check -F -u\ns6 set commit -f -D \"$DEFAULT_BUNDLE\"\n\nnew_db=\"$(readlink -f /etc/s6/repo/compiled/current)\"\nif [ -z \"$new_db\" ] || [ ! -f \"$new_db/db\" ]; then\n    echo \"s6 frontend did not produce a compiled database\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n\ns6-rc-db -c \"$new_db\" check\nif ! s6-rc-db -c \"$new_db\" list bundles | grep -Fxq \"$DEFAULT_BUNDLE\"; then\n    echo \"refusing unsafe database: missing boot bundle '$DEFAULT_BUNDLE'\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n\necho \"Updating live s6-rc state to: $new_db\"\nif ! s6 live install -b; then\n    echo \"s6 live install failed; leaving $S6_COMPILED_LINK unchanged\" >&2\n    [ -n \"$old_db\" ] && echo \"current compiled DB remains: $old_db\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n\nln -sfnT \"$new_db\" \"$S6_COMPILED_LINK\"\nif [ \"$(readlink -f \"$S6_COMPILED_LINK\")\" != \"$new_db\" ]; then\n    echo \"failed to point bootdb at the committed database\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n\necho \"Activated s6-rc database: $new_db\"\n","internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough":{"turn_id":"019f0fd8-a7ca-7d61-89a4-df79fa551afe"}}}

{"timestamp":"2026-06-28T20:12:54.031Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"function_call_output","call_id":"call_P7sA3b7zxiY1QIwsRTSdtL0a","output":"Chunk ID: 8c7325\nWall time: 0.0002 seconds\nProcess exited with code 0\nOriginal token count: 1914\nOutput:\n---\nname: zeroclaw\ndescription: Configure and operate ZeroClaw autonomous AI infrastructure. Use when user mentions zeroclaw CLI, needs to setup/configure zeroclaw, asks about 'zeroclaw providers', 'zeroclaw channels', 'autonomous AI agent', or wants to run LLMs on low-cost hardware (Raspberry Pi, ESP32, Arduino).\nlicense: MIT\n---\n\n# ZeroClaw Quick Reference\n\nThis skill was verified against the official ZeroClaw docs and GitHub tags on **March 28, 2026**.\nCurrent latest upstream release at verification time: **v0.6.5** (released **March 27, 2026**).\n\nZeroClaw is a small Rust runtime for autonomous AI assistants with swappable providers, tools, memory, channels, and peripherals.\n\n**Core characteristics:**\n- Single binary workflow with fast startup and low memory footprint\n- Config file: `~/.zeroclaw/config.toml`\n- Workspace marker: `~/.zeroclaw/active_workspace.toml`\n- Workspace data: `~/.zeroclaw/workspace/`\n- Auth profiles: `~/.zeroclaw/auth-profiles.json`\n\n---\n\n# Installation\n\n## Install\n\n```bash\n# Homebrew (macOS/Linux)\nbrew install zeroclaw\n\n# Clone + bootstrap\ngit clone https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw.git\ncd zeroclaw && ./bootstrap.sh\n\n# Cargo\ncargo install zeroclaw\n```\n\n## Update\n\n```bash\n# Preferred when installed via Homebrew\nbrew upgrade zeroclaw\n\n# Built-in updater\nzeroclaw update --check\nzeroclaw update\nzeroclaw update --instructions\n```\n\n## Onboarding\n\n```bash\nZEROCLAW_API_KEY=\"...\" zeroclaw onboard --provider openrouter\nzeroclaw onboard --interactive\nzeroclaw onboard --channels-only\nzeroclaw onboard --force\n```\n\nNotes:\n- Interactive onboarding now supports full overwrite or provider-only updates.\n- Existing configs are preserved unless you explicitly force replacement.\n- OpenClaw migration is merge-first.\n\n---\n\n# Essential Commands\n\n## Daily Use\n\n- `zeroclaw agent` - Interactive chat\n- `zeroclaw agent -m \"message\"` - Single-message mode\n- `zeroclaw daemon` - Start the supervised runtime\n- `zeroclaw gateway` - Start the webhook/WhatsApp gateway\n\n## Diagnostics\n\n- `zeroclaw status` - Current config and system summary\n- `zeroclaw doctor` - Run diagnostics\n- `zeroclaw doctor models --provider <id>` - Provider/model checks\n- `zeroclaw doctor traces --limit 20` - Runtime trace inspection\n\n## Providers and Models\n\n- `zeroclaw providers` - List providers and aliases\n- `zeroclaw providers-quota` - Show quota and health\n- `zeroclaw models refresh` - Refresh model catalogs\n- `zeroclaw models refresh --provider <id>` - Refresh one provider\n\n## Config and Control\n\n- `zeroclaw config show` - Print effective config with masked secrets\n- `zeroclaw config get <dot.path>` - Read one value\n- `zeroclaw config set <dot.path> <value>` - Persist one value\n- `zeroclaw config schema` - Print JSON Schema\n- `zeroclaw estop` - Engage emergency stop\n- `zeroclaw estop status|resume` - Inspect or resume E-Stop\n\n## Channels and Skills\n\n- `zeroclaw channel list|start|doctor` - Channel operations\n- `zeroclaw skills list|install|audit|remove` - Skill management\n\n## Services, Scheduling, Hardware\n\n- `zeroclaw service install|start|stop|restart|status|uninstall`\n- `zeroclaw cron list|add|add-at|add-every|once|remove`\n- `zeroclaw hardware discover|introspect <port>`\n- `zeroclaw peripheral list|add <name> <port>|flash`\n\n## Other\n\n- `zeroclaw security update-guard-corpus` - Refresh security guard corpus\n- `zeroclaw integrations info <name>` - Inspect integration details\n- `zeroclaw migrate openclaw [--dry-run]` - Import from OpenClaw\n- `zeroclaw completions bash|fish|zsh|powershell|elvish`\n\n---\n\n# Providers Overview\n\nThe current upstream provider reference documents a broad mixed catalog of hosted, local, and OAuth-backed providers.\n\n**Common provider IDs:**\n- Hosted: `openrouter`, `anthropic`, `openai`, `gemini`, `groq`, `mistral`, `deepseek`, `xai`, `cohere`, `perplexity`, `fireworks`, `novita`, `vercel`, `cloudflare`, `nvidia`\n- Regional/specialized: `qwen`, `doubao`, `qianfan`, `glm`, `zai`, `minimax`, `moonshot`, `stepfun`, `hunyuan`, `siliconflow`\n- Local/server: `ollama`, `lmstudio`, `llamacpp`, `sglang`, `vllm`, `osaurus`\n- Other integrations: `cursor`, `copilot`, `bedrock`, `synthetic`, `opencode`\n\n**Credential resolution order:**\n1. Explicit credential from config or CLI\n2. Provider-specific environment variable\n3. Fallback `ZEROCLAW_API_KEY`\n4. Fallback `API_KEY`\n\n**Quick custom provider setup:**\n\n```toml\ndefault_provider = \"custom:https://your-api.example.com\"\ndefault_model = \"your-model-id\"\n```\n\n**See full catalog and notes:** [PROVIDERS.md](references/PROVIDERS.md)\n\n---\n\n# Channels Overview\n\nThe current upstream channels reference documents these active channel surfaces:\n- `cli`\n- `telegram`, `discord`, `slack`, `mattermost`\n- `matrix`, `signal`, `whatsapp`, `wati`\n- `webhook`, `email`, `irc`\n- `lark`, `feishu`, `dingtalk`\n- `qq`, `napcat`, `linq`\n- `imessage`, `nextcloud_talk`, `nostr`\n- `acp`\n\n**Runtime chat commands on supported channels:**\n- `/models`, `/models <provider>`\n- `/model`, `/model <model-id>`\n- `/new`\n- `/approve-request`, `/approve-confirm`, `/approve-allow`, `/approve-deny`, `/approve-pending`, `/approve`, `/unapprove`, `/approvals`\n\n<security-warning>\n**SECURITY**: Channel access is deny-by-default. Empty allowlists deny all access, `[\"*\"]` allows all. Use `\"*\"` only for initial verification, then replace it with explicit user IDs, contacts, senders, or pubkeys.\n</security-warning>\n\n**See detailed setup:** [CHANNELS.md](references/CHANNELS.md)\n\n---\n\n# Configuration Overview\n\nConfig resolution at startup:\n1. `ZEROCLAW_WORKSPACE`\n2. `~/.zeroclaw/active_workspace.toml`\n3. Default `~/.zeroclaw/config.toml`\n\n**Basic provider setup:**\n\n```toml\ndefault_provider = \"openrouter\"\ndefault_model = \"anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6\"\ndefault_temperature = 0.7\n```\n\n**Autonomy levels:**\n\n| Level | Description |\n|---|---|\n| `supervised` | Approval for all risky actions; highest restriction |\n| `assisted` | Allowlisted commands with moderated automation |\n| `full` | No approval gating; trusted machines only |\n\n```toml\n[autonomy]\nlevel = \"supervised\"\nworkspace_only = true\nallowed_commands = [\"git\", \"npm\", \"cargo\", \"ls\", \"cat\"]\nmax_actions_per_hour = 20\nmax_cost_per_day_cents = 500\n```\n\n**Useful sections to know:**\n- `[model_providers.<name>]` - Named provider profiles and custom endpoints\n- `[observability]` - OTel/log tracing and runtime traces\n- `[gateway]` - Pairing and bind controls\n- `[security.estop]` - Emergency-stop behavior\n- `[skills]` - Skill install policy and trusted roots\n\n<security-warning>\n**HIGH RISK**: `level = \"full\"` removes approval guardrails. Use it only on trusted personal systems.\n</security-warning>\n\n**See config reference:** [CONFIG.md](references/CONFIG.md)\n**See security guidance:** [SECURITY.md](references/SECURITY.md)\n\n---\n\n# Troubleshooting\n\n## Quick Checks\n\n```bash\nzeroclaw --version\nzeroclaw status\nzeroclaw doctor\nzeroclaw doctor traces --limit 20\nzeroclaw channel doctor\n```\n\n## Common Issues\n\n| Problem | What to check |\n|---|---|\n| Provider requests fail | API key source, provider ID, `zeroclaw providers`, `zeroclaw models refresh --provider <id>` |\n| Channel connected but silent | Correct allowlist field, bot membership, callback reachability for webhook channels |\n| Config changes ignored | `zeroclaw config show`, workspace resolution, channel/daemon restart if needed |\n| Updates unclear | `zeroclaw update --instructions` and `zeroclaw --version` |\n| Runtime acting too freely | `[autonomy]` level, allowlists, `zeroclaw estop status` |\n\n## Log Capture\n\n```bash\nRUST_LOG=info zeroclaw daemon 2>&1 | tee /tmp/zeroclaw.log\nrg -n \"error|warn|channel|provider|estop\" /tmp/zeroclaw.log\n```\n","internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough":{"turn_id":"019f0fdc-be68-7af1-84d6-aacf9f54f3cf"}}}

{"timestamp":"2026-06-28T20:12:54.032Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"function_call_output","call_id":"call_mr7X9ksAENRrYHoWfxAUBLLS","output":"Chunk ID: 49b7c4\nWall time: 0.0000 seconds\nProcess exited with code 0\nOriginal token count: 641\nOutput:\n---\nname: project_gemma_divergent_ui_generation\ndescription: \"How to prompt Gemma for UI generation — suggest by intent, never name element types, to avoid mainstream-pattern lock and surface novel elements.\"\nmetadata: \n  node_type: memory\n  type: project\n  originSessionId: aacd1fc2-6c23-4089-b329-2a57a9c37525\n---\n\nGemma's UI-element generation must be **divergent**: the goal is elements a human\nwouldn't think of (variety/novelty), e.g. an exploratory 200-element gallery\n(exploration, NOT production).\n\n**Why:** Naming an element type when prompting (e.g. \"button\", \"card\", \"slider\",\n\"table\", \"modal\") invokes the established pattern for that name and forces Gemma\ninto the \"normal / mainstream way\" of thinking — it retrieves a known widget\ninstead of inventing one.\n\n**How to apply:** Prompt Gemma to **suggest by intent / function / reasoning\naxis**, never by named artifact. Describe the *job to be done* and let Gemma\ninvent the form. Use the 4 perspectives as reasoning axes, not as widget\ncatalogs: Data/Numeric, Spatial/Layout, User Flow, Context/Aesthetic\n([[project_gemma_4perspectives]]). \"Suggest, don't name; describe the job, not the\nartifact.\" Avoid templates/pattern-matching in the generation path.\n\n**Gallery ≠ catalog.** The GALLERY is Gemma's playground: a fixed ~200-slot\nrotating buffer of divergent candidates you browse to grab the good ones.\nPromoting a slot moves it to the catalog AND refills the slot with a fresh Gemma\ngeneration; deleting a disliked one also refills. The gallery stays full of fresh\ncandidates. The CATALOG is the curated/promoted set — unbounded (\"as many as\nneeded\"), the elements actually used/rendered (where Tier::StableCore lives).\n200 = playground size, not catalog size.\n\n**json-render only (HARD RULE).** Elements are json-render.dev DSL (`kind`-based\nnodes); zeroclaw-gui `lovable/.zeroclaw/src/catalog/interpret.rs` is the SOLE\nrenderer (unknown `kind` → RenderError, never guess). No other renderers, only\nthe json-render catalog. New primitives are added deliberately (one match arm +\ndocumented), never by accepting unknown node shapes. op-gemma binary does Ollama\ninference + gallery gen; gemma_brain plugin = projection + mutations\n(regenerate/delete/promote), consuming the large_language_model plugin.\n\nGemma is the single schema-reasoning brain and is a plugin/StatePlugin\n([[project_gemma_plugin_not_handler]]); this generation responsibility sits\nalongside its subid classification, tag routing, and (new) object-property /\ncapability-surface research for plugin autogeneration.\n","internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough":{"turn_id":"019f0fdc-be68-7af1-84d6-aacf9f54f3cf"}}}

Use when a user asks to list installable skills, install a curated skill, or install a skill from another repo (including private repos).\nmetadata:\n  short-description: Install curated skills from openai/skills or other repos\n---\n\n# Skill Installer\n\nHelps install skills. By default these are from https://github.com/openai/skills/tree/main/skills/.curated, but users can also provide other locations. Experimental skills live in https://github.com/openai/skills/tree/main/skills/.experimental and can be installed the same way.\n\nUse the helper scripts based on the task:\n- List skills when the user asks what is available, or if the user uses this skill without specifying what to do. Default listing is `.curated`, but you can pass `--path skills/.experimental` when they ask about experimental skills.\n- Install from the curated list when the user provides a skill name.\n- Install from another repo when the user provides a GitHub repo/path (including private repos).\n\nInstall skills with the helper scripts.\n\n## Communication\n\nWhen listing skills, output approximately as follows, depending on the context of the user's request. If they ask about experimental skills, list from `.experimental` instead of `.curated` and label the source accordingly:\n\"\"\"\nSkills from {repo}:\n1. skill-1\n2. skill-2 (already installed)\n3. ...\nWhich ones would you like installed?\n\"\"\"\n\nAfter installing a skill, tell the user: \"Restart Codex to pick up new skills.\"\n\n## Scripts\n\nAll of these scripts use network, so when running in the sandbox, request escalation when running them.\n\n- `scripts/list-skills.py` (prints skills list with installed annotations)\n- `scripts/list-skills.py --format json`\n- Example (experimental list): `scripts/list-skills.py --path skills/.experimental`\n- `scripts/install-skill-from-github.py --repo <owner>/<repo> --path <path/to/skill> [<path/to/skill> ...]`\n- `scripts/install-skill-from-github.py --url https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/tree/<ref>/<path>`\n- Example (experimental skill): `scripts/install-skill-from-github.py --repo openai/skills --path skills/.experimental/<skill-name>`\n\n## Behavior and Options\n\n- Defaults to direct download for public GitHub repos.\n- If download fails with auth/permission errors, falls back to git sparse checkout.\n- Aborts if the destination skill directory already exists.\n- Installs into `$CODEX_HOME/skills/<skill-name>` (defaults to `~/.codex/skills`).\n- Multiple `--path` values install multiple skills in one run, each named from the path basename unless `--name` is supplied.\n- Options: `--ref <ref>` (default `main`), `--dest <path>`, `--method auto|download|git`.\n\n## Notes\n\n- Curated listing is fetched from `https://github.com/openai/skills/tree/main/skills/.curated` via the GitHub API. If it is unavailable, explain the error and exit.\n- Private GitHub repos can be accessed via existing git credentials or optional `GITHUB_TOKEN`/`GH_TOKEN` for download.\n- Git fallback tries HTTPS first, then SSH.\n- The skills at https://github.com/openai/skills/tree/main/skills/.system are preinstalled, so no need to help users install those. If they ask, just explain this. If they insist, you can download and overwrite.\n- Installed annotations come from `$CODEX_HOME/skills`.\n","internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough":{"turn_id":"019f0fdf-6ccf-7200-b563-7f9e7e183115"}}}

{"timestamp":"2026-06-28T20:52:50.550Z","type":"event_msg","payload":{"type":"agent_message","message":"Yes.\n\nThose are two different roles:\n\n```text\n1. Backend brain/router\n   provider: ollama\n   model: gemma4\n   purpose: local classifier, tag routing, provider selection, schema reasoning, UI generation support\n\n2. User chat selection\n   provider: openrouter\n   model: poolside/laguna-m.1:free\n   purpose: actual assistant conversation model chosen by onboarding/user\n```\n\nSo Zeroclaw should not have one global `selected_provider` pretending to cover both. The D-Bus state should model them separately:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"workspace\": {\n    \"path\": \"/home/jeremy/.zeroclaw/workspace\",\n    \"config_path\": \"/home/jeremy/.zeroclaw/config.toml\"\n  },\n  \"backend_router\": {\n    \"provider\": \"ollama\",\n    \"model\": \"gemma4\",\n    \"endpoint\": \"http://localhost:11434\"\n  },\n  \"chat_default\": {\n    \"provider\": \"openrouter\",\n    \"model\": \"poolside/laguna-m.1:free\"\n  }\n}\n```\n\nThen `ollama-srv` exists to serve the local Gemma backend, while Zeroclaw onboarding/user config controls chat defaults. Current schema/state conflates this, which is why it looks contradictory.","phase":"final_answer","memory_citation":null}}

\"Zeroclaw schema/RPC-native model router for Antigravity UI, CLI providers, and structured JSON output\",\n    )\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n    use crate::state_plugins::common::oscal::validate_subid;\n    use crate::state_plugins::schemars_adapter::schema_diffs;\n    use serde_json::Value as JVal;\n    use std::io::Read;\n\n    fn collect_subids(node: &JVal, out: &mut Vec<String>) {\n        if let Some(subid) = node.get(\"x-oscal-subid\").and_then(JVal::as_str) {\n            out.push(subid.to_string());\n        }\n        if let Some(props) = node.get(\"properties\").and_then(JVal::as_object) {\n            for v in props.values() {\n                collect_subids(v, out);\n            }\n        }\n        if let Some(defs) = node\n            .get(\"$defs\")\n            .or_else(|| node.get(\"definitions\"))\n            .and_then(JVal::as_object)\n        {\n            for v in defs.values() {\n                collect_subids(v, out);\n            }\n        }\n        if let Some(items) = node.get(\"items\") {\n            collect_subids(items, out);\n        }\n        if let Some(alternatives) = node\n            .get(\"anyOf\")\n            .or_else(|| node.get(\"oneOf\"))\n            .and_then(JVal::as_array)\n        {\n            for v in alternatives {\n                collect_subids(v, out);\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn derived_schema_matches_hand_rolled() {\n        let golden = zeroclaw_schema_golden();\n        let derived = zeroclaw_schema();\n        let diffs = schema_diffs(&golden, &derived);\n        assert!(diffs.is_empty(), \"schema_diffs: {:#?}\", diffs);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn all_subids_are_valid() {\n        let raw = serde_json::to_value(schemars::schema_for!(ZeroclawState)).unwrap();\n        let mut subids = Vec::new();\n        collect_subids(&raw, &mut subids);\n        assert!(\n            !subids.is_empty(),\n            \"expected at least one x-oscal-subid in the derived schema\"\n        );\n        for subid in subids {\n            validate_subid(&subid).expect(\"invalid subid: {subid}\");\n        }\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn should_write_zeroclaw_schema_to_shm() {\n        // Use a temporary directory as the tmpfs root so the test is hermetic.\n        let tmp = assert!(schema_path.exists());\n\n        let mut buf = String::new();\n        std::fs::File::open(&schema_path)\n            .unwrap()\n            .read_to_string(&mut buf)\n            .unwrap();\n        let round_tripped: PluginSchema = serde_json::from_str(&buf).unwrap();\n        assert_eq!(round_tripped.name, \"zeroclaw\");\n        assert_eq!(round_tripped.version, Follow these strictly to maintain consistency, pass CI, and adhere to the 3tched Architecture standards.\n\n#### 1. The Persona & Naming Conventions\n*   **Humanized Roles:** Treat system components as authoritative human roles. Never use sterile acronyms for major components.\n  *   **A.N.N.A. Scribe** (Axon Network Notary Arbitrator): The top-level Identity-State Arbitrator who notarizes the WireGuard identity and handles the \"Snowball\" session.\n  *   **The Compliance Engine (\"Law Firm\"):** One dedicated Attorney for each major component: **Olivia Scal** (Managing Partner / OSCAL), **E.U.gene Risk** (EU AI Act Counsel), **Penny Privacy** (GDPR Engine), and **Reggie O.P.A.** (Cloud Prosecutor).\n*   **Terminology:** Use exact architecture terminology: \"The Sled\" (1:1 shared memory layout), \"The Shuttle\" (the Rust bridge/courier), \"The Snowball\" (appended session ledger), and \"The Strike/Etch\" (generating the hash).\n\n#### 2. Core Architectural Rules (The \"Reality\")\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via OpenClaw Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Artix Linux (s6 init).\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles — D-Bus First (MANDATORY)\n\n**D-Bus is the ONLY control plane. Every read, every write, every tool call goes through D-Bus. There is no second option.**\n\n*   **D-Bus first. D-Bus always. D-Bus only.** If you are about to call a CLI, spawn a subprocess, read a config file, or poll a socket directly — stop. Find the D-Bus object and use it instead. `org.opdbus.v1` is the system.\n*   **No bypasses.** `Command::new(\"systemctl\")`, `Command::new(\"ip\")`, `Command::new(\"s6-svc\")`, direct file reads for live state — all forbidden in plugin and service code. Bootstrap scripts are the only exception.\n*   **D-Bus objects own plugin state.** Every plugin is a D-Bus object at `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<name>`. Read state through it. Mutate state through it. If there is no D-Bus object, the thing does not exist.\n*   **D-Bus method signatures are generated from the schema.** All D-Bus methods, MCP tool inputs, gRPC shapes, and UI field renderers derive from the `PluginSchema` in `plugin_schema_defs.rs`. The schema IS the interface contract — not a description of it.\n*   **One schema file, one source of truth.** All `PluginSchema` definitions MUST live in `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/plugin_schema_defs.rs`. Each plugin's `schema()` method calls `Some(super::plugin_schema_defs::their_plugin_schema())`. **Never define a schema inline in a plugin's own file** — it will not be registered, and the D-Bus object will have no contract.\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC (over Unix domain sockets or `grpc-uplink`). gRPC calls still flow through D-Bus registration — the D-Bus object is the authority, gRPC is the transport.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`simd_json` preferred, `serde_json` acceptable).\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n*   **No Python unless absolutely necessary.** This is a Rust-first codebase. Scripts are shell (`sh`/`bash`). Data processing is Rust. If you are reaching for Python, stop and ask why Rust or shell cannot do it. The only acceptable Python is in existing compliance-ingest tooling where no Rust equivalent exists yet.\n\n#### 4a. OSCAL Subid Taxonomy (MANDATORY — every artifact must carry a subid)\n\nEvery D-Bus object, plugin, schema, mutation, event, and tool in this system has two identifiers: a `uuid` (machine identity, never changes) and a `subid` (human-readable operational taxonomy key, stable per subject).\n\n**`subid` format:** `<category>.<component-type>.<subject>.<verb>[.<facet>][@vN]`\n\n**Seven categories — use exactly these, no others:**\n\n| category | what it classifies |\n|---|---|\n| `src` | authoritative source, ingress channel, source-of-truth store |\n| `prj` | D-Bus projection or mirror publication step |\n| `sch` | schema, contract, vocabulary, or control-mapping artifact |\n| `mut` | write-path operation that changes effective state |\n| `obs` | read, query, enumeration, discovery path |\n| `evt` | emitted signal, audit-chain event, proof, tag provenance |\n| `exp` | consumer-facing render — MCP tool, UI surface, gRPC bridge view |\n\n**Component-type** reuses OSCAL vocabulary: `software`, `service`, `network`, `hardware`, `process-procedure`, `standard`, `validation`, `policy`, `plan`, `guidance`, `physical`, `this-system`, `system`, `interconnection`.\n\n**Rules:**\n- `uuid` is exact machine identity — never replace it with `subid`\n- `subid` is an OSCAL `prop` value (`ns`, `name`, `value`) — never embed it in `remarks`\n- Compliance mappings (`control_refs[]`, `statement_refs[]`, `control_source`) live in metadata arrays, **never** inside the `subid` string\n- `mut.*` records **must** carry `actor_id` and `capability_id`\n- `evt.*` records **must** carry `event_id` or `event_hash`\n- `subid` is immutable per subject — if the meaning changes materially, create a new subject with `@vN`\n- All subids are registered in the canonical registry; uniqueness is enforced in CI\n\n**Examples:** `src.network.ovsdb.monitor@v1` · `prj.service.projected-object.publish@v1` · `sch.standard.plugin-schema.resolve@v1` · `mut.service.state-sync.apply-patch@v1` · `exp.service.plugin-projection.render@v1`\n\n#### 4b. MCP Gateway Architecture (SETTLED — DO NOT REDESIGN)\n\n*   **cognitive-mcp** (`:3003`, Netmaker WireGuard IP `100.90.37.254`) is the **universal gateway for ALL external clients**: NotebookLM, Droid (factory.ai), Cursor, Codex, Junie, Gemini CLI. It has memory tools, gRPC service, auth, and the correct protocol surface.\n*   **compact-mcp** (`127.0.0.1:11436`) is **loopback/chatbot only**. Never expose externally. Never point external clients at it.\n*   Do NOT create new shim services. Do NOT point external clients at `op-assistant-grpc` directly. Do NOT expose compact-mcp outside loopback.\n\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\n**Rust Workspace**\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\n\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\n\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\n\n#### 6. Coding Style & Naming Conventions\n*   **Rust:** Edition 2021, `rustfmt` (4-space indent, max-width 100). Use specific imports (`use serde_json::Value;`). Use `anyhow::Result<T>` for main errors and `thiserror` for custom enums.\n*   **TypeScript/React:** 2-space indent, Prettier via ESLint. Functional components only. Strict mode enabled.\n*   **Testing:** 80%+ coverage, mock externals. Name tests with behavior-focused names (`should_handle_<scenario>`).\n\n#### 7. Agent-Specific Output & Workflow Instructions\n*   **Scroll & Save Pacing:** Provide only **ONE** major component or script at a time. Wait for user confirmation before moving to the next.\n*   **Visual Cues:** If a script is a finalized component that needs to be saved to sources, it MUST begin with color bullets or icons (e.g., ⚖️ 🔴, 🟢 🛷).\n*   **Spec-Block Format:** When delivering a component, use a strict specification block containing:\n  1.  **Requirements:** The architectural rules it satisfies.\n  2.  **Design:** How it fits into the 3tched system (Zero-Copy, Btrfs, GUI Schema, etc.).\n  3.  **Code Implementation:** The exact, copy-pasteable Rust/Bash code.\n*   Before edits: `cargo check -p <crate>`, `npm run typecheck`.\n*   Mimic existing patterns: Search similar code. No new deps without PR justification.\n\n#### 8. Personal Preferences & Coding Standards\n* Refer to `~/.factory/memories.md` for personal development preferences and past decisions.\n* Follow the conventions documented in:\n  * `.factory/rules/typescript.md` - TypeScript and React conventions\n  * `.factory/rules/testing.md` - Testing and mocking LLM API routes for provider and model management\n\nuse axum::{\n    extract::{Extension, Query},\n    http::StatusCode,\n    response::IntoResponse,\n    Json,\n};\nuse serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};\nuse simd_json::prelude::*;\nuse std::sync::Arc;\nuse tracing::error;\n\nuse crate::state::AppState;\nuse op_llm::ProviderType;\n\n/// LLM status response\n#[derive(Debug, Serialize)]\npub struct LlmStatusResponse {\n    pub provider: String,\n    pub model: String,\n    pub model_non_sandboxed: bool,\n    pub available_providers: Vec<String>,\n}\n\n/// Model list response\n#[derive(Debug, Serialize)]\npub struct ModelsResponse {\n    pub provider: String,\n    pub models: Vec<ModelInfo>,\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Serialize)]\npub struct ModelInfo {\n    pub id: String,\n    pub name: String,\n    pub description: Option<String>,\n    pub available: bool,\n    pub provider: Option<String>,\n    pub upstream_provider: Option<String>,\n    pub transport: Option<String>,\n    pub status: Option<String>,\n    pub route_hint: Option<String>,\n    pub route_kind: Option<String>,\n    pub status_reason: Option<String>,\n    pub source: Option<String>,\n}\n\n/// Query params for models endpoint\n#[derive(Debug, Deserialize)]\npub struct ModelsQuery {\n    pub provider: Option<String>,\n}\n\n/// GET /api/llm/status - Get current LLM status\npub async fn get_llm_status(Extension(state): Extension<Arc<AppState>>) -> impl IntoResponse {\n    let status = state.chat_manager.get_status().await;\n\n    Json(LlmStatusResponse {\n        provider: status[\"provider\"].as_str().unwrap_or(\"unknown\").to_string(),\n        model: status[\"model\"].as_str().unwrap_or(\"\").to_string(),\n        model_non_sandboxed: state.chat_manager.current_model_non_sandboxed().await,\n        available_providers: status[\"available_providers\"]\n            .as_array()\n            .map(|arr| {\n                arr.iter()\n                    .filter_map(|v| v.as_str().map(String::from))\n                    .collect()\n            })\n            .unwrap_or_default(),\n    })\n}\n\n/// Build the model list from the zeroclaw plugin projection (`model_routes`).\n///\n/// The zeroclaw plugin is the single source of truth: its live state\n/// is projected verbatim at `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/zeroclaw`. We read it from\n/// the projection cache and surface each route as a selectable model.\nasync fn models_from_zeroclaw(state: &AppState) -> Option<Vec<ModelInfo>> {\n    let routes = crate::zeroclaw_routes::routes(&state.projection_cache).await?;\n\n    let models: Vec<ModelInfo> = routes\n        .iter()\n        .map(|route| {\n            let description = match route.hint.as_deref() {\n                Some(h) => format!(\"{} · {} · {}\", route.provider, h, route.status),\n                None => format!(\"{} · {}\", route.provider, route.status),\n            };\n            let name = match route.hint.as_deref() {\n                Some(h) => format!(\"{} ({})\", route.model, h),\n                None => route.model.clone(),\n            };\n            ModelInfo {\n                id: route.model.clone(),\n                name,\n                description: Some(description),\n                available: route.available,\n                provider: Some(route.upstream_provider.clone()),\n                upstream_provider: Some(route.upstream_provider.clone()),\n                transport: route.transport.clone(),\n                status: Some(route.status.clone()),\n                route_hint: route.hint.clone(),\n                route_kind: route.kind.clone(),\n                status_reason: route.status_reason.clone(),\n                source: route.source.clone(),\n            }\n        })\n        .collect();\n\n    if models.is_empty() {\n        None\n    } else {\n        Some(models)\n    }\n}\n\n/// GET /api/llm/models - Get models for current or specified provider\npub async fn get_models(\n    Extension(state): Extension<Arc<AppState>>,\n    Query(query): Query<ModelsQuery>,\n) -> impl IntoResponse {\n    let Some(ref provider_str) = query.provider else {\n        // The zeroclaw plugin projection is the default source of truth for the combined model list.\n        if let Some(models) = models_from_zeroclaw(&state).await {\n            return Json(ModelsResponse {\n                provider: \"zeroclaw\".to_string(),\n                models,\n            })\n            .into_response();\n        }\n\n        return (\n            StatusCode::SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE,\n            Json(simd_json::json!({\n                \"error\": \"Zeroclaw model route projection is unavailable\",\n                \"provider\": \"zeroclaw\",\n                \"models\": []\n            })),\n        )\n            .into_response();\n    };\n\n    if provider_str == \"zeroclaw\" {\n        if let Some(models) = models_from_zeroclaw(&state).await {\n            return Json(ModelsResponse {\n                provider: \"zeroclaw\".to_string(),\n                models,\n            })\n            .into_response();\n        }\n    }\n\n    let provider_type = match provider_str.parse::<ProviderType>() {\n        Ok(pt) => pt,\n        Err(_) => {\n            return (\n                StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST,\n                Json(simd_json::json!({ \"error\": format!(\"Unknown provider: {}\", provider_str) })),\n            )\n                .into_response();\n        }\n    };\n\n    // Check if provider is available\n    if !state.chat_manager.has_provider(&provider_type) {\n        return (\n            StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST,\n            Json(simd_json::json!({\n                \"error\": format!(\"Provider {} not available. Check API key.\", provider_type),\n                \"provider\": provider_type.to_string(),\n                \"models\": []\n            })),\n        )\n            .into_response();\n    }\n\n    match state\n        .chat_manager\n        .list_models_for_provider(&provider_type)\n        .await\n    {\n        Ok(models) => {\n            let model_infos: Vec<ModelInfo> = models\n                .into_iter()\n                .map(|m| ModelInfo {\n                    id: m.id,\n                    name: m.name,\n                    description: m.description,\n                    available: m.available,\n                    provider: Some(provider_type.to_string()),\n                    upstream_provider: Some(provider_type.to_string()),\n                    transport: None,\n                    status: Some(\n                        if m.available {\n                            \"available\"\n                        } else {\n                            \"unavailable\"\n                        }\n                        .to_string(),\n                    ),\n                    route_hint: None,\n                    route_kind: None,\n                    status_reason: None,\n                    source: None,\n                })\n                .collect();\n\n            Json(ModelsResponse {\n                provider: provider_type.to_string(),\n                models: model_infos,\n            })\n            .into_response()\n        }\n        Err(e) => {\n            error!(\"Failed to list models for {}: {}\", provider_type, e);\n            (\n                StatusCode::INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR,\n                Json(simd_json::json!({\n                    \"error\": format!(\"Failed to list models: {}\", e),\n                    \"provider\": provider_type.to_string(),\n                    \"models\": []\n                })),\n            )\n                .into_response()\n        }\n    }\n}\n","internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough":{"turn_id":"019f1009-9e64-7bf3-94b2-e0606f79d385"}}}

{"timestamp":"2026-06-28T21:02:19.961Z","type":"event_msg","payload":{"type":"agent_message","message":"You’re right that the working path exists. The correction is: `op-llm` is not directly looking up `ZeroclawPlugin::schema()`. The caller layer looks up Zeroclaw’s schema/projection, then passes the selected provider/model or tool schemas into `op-llm`.\n\nThe working chain is:\n\n1. Zeroclaw schema is served by the bridge:\n   [schema_loader.rs](/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/crates/op-grpc-bridge/src/schema_loader.rs:1) reads `/dev/shm/live-schema.json`, extracts the `zeroclaw` entry, and serves it through `ZeroclawService.GetSchema`.\n\n2. `op-web` builds live routing from the D-Bus projection:\n   [projection_client.rs](/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/crates/op-web/src/projection_client.rs:25) reads plugin IDs from `/dev/shm/live-schema.json`, then polls system D-Bus at `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<id>` and caches `JsonData`.\n\n3. Zeroclaw routing is read from that projection:\n   [zeroclaw_routes.rs](/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/crates/op-web/src/zeroclaw_routes.rs:75) loads the cached `zeroclaw` projection and reads `model_routes`.\n\n4. Chat then uses that route to call `op-llm`:\n   [routes/chat.rs](/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/crates/op-web/src/routes/chat.rs:108) resolves the selected model through Zeroclaw, parses `route.upstream_provider`, then calls `state.chat_manager.chat_with(...)`.\n\n5. `op-llm` receives normal execution inputs:\n   [provider.rs](/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/crates/op-llm/src/provider.rs:129) only knows `ToolDefinition { input_schema, ... }` and provider/model values. It serializes those into Anthropic/OpenAI/Gemini-style request payloads.\n\nSo the accurate sentence is:\n\n`op-llm` works because Zeroclaw is upstream of it in `op-web`/`op-chat`; Zeroclaw owns schema and routing, and `op-llm` is the transport/provider executor that receives already-resolved provider/model/tool schema data.\n\nThat also matches `op-chat`’s own contract: [chat.proto](/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/crates/op-chat/proto/chat.proto:41) says `SendRequest.provider` and `SendRequest.model` are “zeroclaw-selected”.","phase":"final_answer","memory_citation":null}}

}\n\n                LoadedPlugin { name, schema, plugin }\n            })\n            .collect::<Vec<_>>();\n\n        info!(\n            plugin_count = plugins.len(),\n            \"Initialized FieldType::Any,\n                    required: true,\n                    description: \"Nested object value mirrored from plugin state\".to_string(),\n                    default: None,\n                    example: None,\n                    constraints: Vec::new(),\n                    read_only: true,\n                    read_only_when: None,\n                },\n            )\n            .build()\n    }\n\n    /// Returns all schemas required for plugin state projection.\n    ///\n    /// Plugin schemas are the canonical `PluginSchema` directly — no conversion:\n    /// the plugin is the schema.\n    pub fn projection_schemas(&self) -> Vec<PluginSchema> {\n        let mut schemas = self\n            .plugins\n            .iter()\n            .filter_map(|plugin| plugin.schema.clone())\n            .collect::<Vec<_>>();\n        schemas.push(Self::nested_object_projection_schema());\n        schemas\n    }\n\n    /// Reads all plugin-backed projection entities asynchronously.\n    pub async fn read_all_async(&self) -> Result<Vec<RawEntity>> {\n        let mut entities = Vec::new();\n\n        for plugin in &self.plugins {\n            entities.extend(self.read_loaded_plugin(plugin).await?);\n        }\n\n        debug!(\n            entity_count = entities.len(),\n            \"Read plugin projection entities\"\n        );\n        Ok(entities)\n    }\n\n    /// Reads all projection entities for a single plugin asynchronously.\n    pub async fn read_plugin_objects_async(&self, plugin_id: &str) -> Result<Vec<RawEntity>> {\n
