   .into_iter()\n            .filter(|entity| {\n                entity.entity_type == \"plugin.object\"\n                    && entity\n                        .data\n                        .get(\"parent_id\")\n                        .and_then(|value| value.as_str())\n                        == Some(parent_id)\n            })\n            .collect())\n//! Projection Server: pure read-through D-Bus projection of the plugin tree.\n//!\n//! Mounts the projected plugin tree at `org.opdbus.v1.plugins` and serves\n//! each plugin's state as a `ProjectedObject` that reads 1:1 from the shm\n//! projection layer (`/dev/shm/opdbus/projections/<plugin>.json`).\n//!\n//! The MutationEngine (the single write door) writes each plugin's full state\n//! to shm on every mutation. This server mounts the tree from shm on startup\n//! and exposes a `refresh()` D-Bus method on the root interface that re-reads\n//! shm and syncs the tree (mount/unmount). No gRPC subscription, no polling,\n//! no inotify — the tree is derived on demand.\n\nuse anyhow::{Context, Result};\nuse op_projection::*;\nuse std::collections::HashMap;\nuse tracing::{info, warn};\nuse tracing_subscriber::{EnvFilter, FmtSubscriber};\n\n#[tokio::main]\nasync fn main() -> Result<()> {\n    let subscriber = FmtSubscriber::builder()\n        .with_env_filter(EnvFilter::from_default_env())\n        .finish();\n    tracing::subscriber::set_global_default(subscriber)?;\n\n    info!(\"Starting Operation-DBus Projection Server (read-through)\");\n\n    // 1. Initialize Schema Engine + discover plugin schemas (writes to shm).\n    let mut schema_engine = SchemaEngine::new();\n\n    let plugin_reader = match SystemPluginReader::new().await {\n        Ok(reader) => reader,\n        Err(error) => {\n            warn!(\n                error = %error,\n                \"Failed to initialize plugin reader; continuing with empty schema catalog\"\n            );\n            SystemPluginReader::empty()\n        }\n    };\n\n    let projection_schemas = plugin_reader.projection_schemas();\n    let schema_map: HashMap<String, PluginSchema> = projection_schemas\n        .iter()\n        .map(|schema| (schema.name.clone(), schema.clone()))\n        .collect();\n\n    for schema in projection_schemas {\n        register_schema_if_missing(&mut schema_engine, schema)?;\n    }\n\n    info!(\n        schemas = schema_engine.list_schemas().len(),\n        \"Schema catalog published to shm\"\n    );\n\n    // 2. Initialize D-Bus server (owns org.opdbus.v1.plugins, root interface\n    //    at /org/opdbus/v1/plugins is always present for introspection).\n    let dbus_server = ProjectionDbusServer::new_with_schemas(schema_map.clone())\n        .await\n        .context(\"failed to start projection D-Bus server\")?;\n\n    // 3. Initial tree sync: mount from shm (mutations) then seed all known\n    //    plugin roots from the schema catalog so the tree is never empty.\n    dbus_server.sync_from_shm().await?;\n\n    let known_plugins: Vec<String> = schema_map.keys().cloned().collect();\n    dbus_server.seed_plugin_roots(&known_plugins).await?;\n\n    let count = dbus_server.object_count().await;\n    info!(\n        objects = count,\n        plugins = known_plugins.len(),\n        \"Initial tree sync complete\"\n    );\n\n    // 4. Initialize JSON-stream server (for WebSocket clients).\n    let mut stream_server = ProjectionStreamServer::new();\n    stream_server.start(8082)?;\n\n    // 5. Run forever. The tree is derived on-demand via the `refresh()` D-Bus\n    //    method on the ProjectionRoot interface. No gRPC, no polling.\n    info!(\"Projection server ready — tree syncs on refresh() D-Bus call or restart\");\n    tokio::signal::ctrl_c().await?;\n\n    Ok(())\n}\n\nfn register_schema_if_missing(\n    schema_engine: &mut SchemaEngine,\n    schema: PluginSchema,\n) -> Result<()> {\n    if schema_engine.has_valid_schema(&schema.name) {\n        return Ok(());\n    }\n\n    let schema_name = schema.name.clone();\n    schema_engine\n        .register_schema(schema)\n        .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to register projection schema '{}'\", schema_name))?;\n    Ok(())\n}\n","internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough":{"turn_id":"019f100b-6c2b-7a20-b74b-248002632bf2"}}}

D-Bus object server for projections.\n//!\n//! Serves every Projection through org.opdbus.v1.plugins at\n//! /org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<plugin>. Nothing mounts outside the plugins root:\n//! no plugin means no schema means no object.\n//!\n//! Data is read 1:1 from the shared-memory projection layer\n//! (`/dev/shm/opdbus/projections/<plugin>.json`) on every property access.\n//! No held cache — the projected tree is a pure read-through of the mutation\n//! fold written by the MutationEngine (the single write door).\n//!\n//! Tree structure is derived on-demand: the `ProjectionRoot` interface at\n//! `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins` exposes a `refresh()` D-Bus method that re-reads\n//! shm and mounts/unmounts objects to match. No gRPC subscription, no polling,\n//! no inotify — the tree syncs when asked.\n\nuse crate::data_models::PluginSchema;\nuse anyhow::Result;\nuse std::collections::{HashMap, HashSet};\nuse std::sync::Arc;\nuse tokio::sync::Mutex;\nuse tracing::{debug, info};\nuse zbus::{connection::Builder, interface, object_server::SignalEmitter, Connection};\n\n/// A single projected object on the D-Bus object server.\n///\n/// Reads its data 1:1 from the shm projection layer on every property access.\n/// No held cache — the mutation fold in `/dev/shm/opdbus/projections/` is the\n/// single source of truth, written by the MutationEngine on every mutation.\npub struct ProjectedObject {\n    /// The plugin that owns this object (e.g. \"wireguard\").\n    pub plugin_id: String,\n    /// Path segments below the plugin root (empty for the plugin root itself).\n    /// e.g. `[\"interfaces\", \"0\", \"peers\"]` for\n    /// `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/wireguard/interfaces/0/peers`\n    pub path_segments: Vec<String>,\n    /// Canonical schema captured when the D-Bus object is mounted.\n    pub schema: Option<PluginSchema>,\n}\n\nimpl ProjectedObject {\n    fn new(plugin_id: &str, path_segments: Vec<String>, schema: Option<PluginSchema>) -> Self {\n        Self {\n            plugin_id: plugin_id.to_string(),\n            path_segments,\n            schema: schema.or_else(|| read_plugin_schema(plugin_id)),\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn schema_json_value(&self, selector: SchemaSurface) -> String {\n        let Some(schema) = &self.schema else {\n            return \"{}\".to_string();\n        };\n\n        let value = match selector {\n            SchemaSurface::Methods => serde_json::to_value(&schema.methods),\n            SchemaSurface::Signals => serde_json::to_value(&schema.signals),\n            SchemaSurface::Guarantees => serde_json::to_value(&schema.guarantees),\n        };\n\n        value\n            .ok()\n            .and_then(|value| serde_json::to_string(&value).ok())\n            .unwrap_or_else(|| \"{}\".to_string())\n    }\n}\n\nenum SchemaSurface {\n    Methods,\n    Signals,\n    Guarantees,\n}\n\n#[interface(name = \"org.opdbus.v1.plugins.ProjectedObject\")]\nimpl ProjectedObject {\n    /// The schema/entity type for this object (plugin id for roots, \"plugin.object\" for nested)\n    #[zbus(property)]\n    async fn entity_type(&self) -> String {\n        if self.path_segments.is_empty() {\n            self.plugin_id.clone()\n        } else {\n            \"plugin.object\".to_string()\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// The unique entity ID within its type\n    #[zbus(property)]\n    async fn entity_id(&self) -> String {\n        if self.path_segments.is_empty() {\n            self.plugin_id.clone()\n        } else {\n            format!(\"{}:/{}\", self.plugin_id, self.path_segments.join(\"/\"))\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Current projection state: always Valid (1:1 read of canonical state).\n    #[zbus(property)]\n    async fn state(&self) -> String {\n        \"Valid\".to_string()\n    }\n\n    /// Full projection data as a JSON string, read 1:1 from shm.\n    #[zbus(property)]\n    async fn data(&self) -> String {\n        read_projected_data(&self.plugin_id, &self.path_segments)\n    }\n\n    /// Declared D-Bus methods and required capabilities as JSON.\n    #[zbus(property)]\n    async fn methods(&self) -> String {\n        self.schema_json_value(SchemaSurface::Methods)\n    }\n\n    /// Declared D-Bus signals as JSON.\n    #[zbus(property)]\n    async fn signals(&self) -> String {\n        self.schema_json_value(SchemaSurface::Signals)\n    }\n\n    /// Declared operational guarantees as JSON.\n    #[zbus(property)]\n    async fn guarantees(&self) -> String {\n        self.schema_json_value(SchemaSurface::Guarantees)\n    }\n\n    /// Signal emitted when this object's data changes\n    #[zbus(signal)]\n    async fn updated(emitter: &SignalEmitter<'_>, data_json: &str) -> zbus::Result<()>;\n}\n\n/// Read projected data for a plugin/path from the shm layer (1:1, zero held For Gemma, s6, procfs, freedesktop, and plugin-derived child objects, the shape should be: plugin state struct -> schemars PluginSchema -> `/dev/shm/live-schema.json` -> `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/...` projection -> executor receives resolved arguments."}],"phase":"commentary","internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough":{"turn_id":"019f100b-6c2b-7a20-b74b-248002632bf2"}}}
{"timestamp":"2026-06-28T21:04:12.583Z","type":"event_msg","payload":{"type":"agent_message","message":"Yes. Same pattern, generalized:\n\n`PluginState`/`PluginSchema` owns the contract → `SchemaEngine` publishes `/dev/shm/live-schema.json` → `op-projection` mounts `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<plugin>` and derived child objects → callers read the projection and pass resolved values to executors.\n\nSo for what we’re working on:\n\n- Gemma/Ollama config should live in `zeroclaw` or `gemma_brain` state, not hardcoded in `op-llm`.\n- s6 service controls should live as plugin schema/projection state, not raw `s6-svc` calls from consumers.\n- procfs/freedesktop/plugin-derived objects should be derived child objects under `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<plugin>/...`.\n- `op-llm` remains the provider executor. It should receive resolved provider/model/tool schemas, exactly like it does now from `op-web`/Zeroclaw routing.\n\nThe good news: most of the infrastructure already exists in [projection_server.rs](/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/crates/op-projection/src/bin/projection_server.rs:28) and [dbus_server.rs](/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/crates/op-projection/src/dbus_server.rs:313). The next practical change is to remove the remaining Zeroclaw-only assumptions and make the bridge/consumer read any plugin schema by plugin id, the same way `op-web` reads Zeroclaw’s projection today.","phase":"final_answer","memory_citation":null}}

Same pattern, generalized:\n\n`PluginState`/`PluginSchema` owns the contract → `SchemaEngine` publishes `/dev/shm/live-schema.json` → `op-projection` mounts `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<plugin>` and derived child objects → callers read the projection and pass resolved values to executors.\n\nSo for what we’re working on:\n\n- Gemma/Ollama config should live in `zeroclaw` or `gemma_brain` state, not hardcoded in `op-llm`.\n- s6 service controls should live as plugin schema/projection state, not raw `s6-svc` calls from consumers.\n- procfs/freedesktop/plugin-derived objects should be derived child objects under `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<plugin>/...`.\n- `op-llm` remains the provider executor. It should receive resolved provider/model/tool schemas, exactly like it does now from `op-web`/Zeroclaw routing.\n\nThe good news: most of the infrastructure already exists in [projection_server.rs](/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/crates/op-projection/src/bin/projection_server.rs:28) and [dbus_server.rs](/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/crates/op-projection/src/dbus_server.rs:313). Exp,\n}\n\nimpl SubidCategory {\n    pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str {\n        match self {\n            Self::Src => \"src\",\n            Self::Prj => \"prj\",\n            Self::Sch => \"sch\",\n            Self::Mut => \"mut\",\n            Self::Obs => \"obs\",\n            Self::Evt => \"evt\",\n            Self::Exp => \"exp\",\n        }\n    }\n\n    pub fn parse(s: &str) ->      }\n\n        Ok(Self {\n            category,\n            component_type,\n            subject,\n            verb,\n            facet,\n            version,\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Zeroclaw route surface plugin.\n//!\n//! Publishes the Antigravity-facing model and CLI routing contract through\n//! `PluginSchema` so the UI can render provider/model controls from D-Bus.\n//!\n//! Also writes the plugin-owned schema JSON to `/dev/shm/opdbus/schemas/zeroclaw.json`\n//! so that the `op-grpc-bridge` Axum host can read it without duplicating the\n//! schema definition.\n\nuse super::common::llm_projection::{\n    ConfigSchema, LlmProjection, LlmTool, ModelRoute, Provider, Router, StructuredOutput, UiSurface,\n};\nuse anyhow::Result;\nuse async_trait::async_trait;\nuse op_state::{ApplyResult, Checkpoint, DiffMetadata, PluginCapabilities, StateDiff, StatePlugin};\nuse op_state_store::PluginSchema;\nuse serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};\nuse serde_json::Value as JsonValue;\nuse simd_json::OwnedValue as Value;\nuse std::path::Path;\n\nconst ZEROCLAW_SCHEMA_SHM_PATH: &str = \"/dev/shm/opdbus/schemas/zeroclaw.json\";\n\n/// Transport layer metadata for the Zeroclaw plugin.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, Serialize, Deserialize, schemars::JsonSchema)]\n#[schemars(extend(\"x-oscal-subid\" = \"sch.software.zeroclaw-transport.schema@v1\"))]\npub struct LlmTransport {\n    /// D-Bus object path served by this plugin.\n    #[serde(default)]\n    #[schemars(extend(\"x-oscal-subid\" = \"mut.service.zeroclaw-transport.dbus-object@v1\"))]\n    pub dbus_object: String,\n    /// gRPC upstream target.\n    #[serde(default)]\n    #[schemars(extend(\"x-oscal-subid\" = \"mut.service.zeroclaw-transport.grpc-target@v1\"))]\n    pub grpc_target: String,\n//! Zeroclaw error taxonomy (spec §14).\n//!\n//! `ZeroclawError` is a schema-contract type: it derives `schemars::JsonSchema`\n//! so the error shape is surfaced in MCP tool responses and D-Bus method error\n//! payloads. subid: `sch.software.zeroclaw-error.schema@v1`.\n\nuse schemars::JsonSchema;\nuse serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};\nuse thiserror::Error;\n\n/// Failure modes for Zeroclaw route resolution, model selection, and execution\n/// authorization. Every variant maps to a deterministic, schema-derived denial\n/// reason — nothing here reflects a runtime network error (those live in the\n/// Provider Adapter Layer).\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Error, Serialize, Deserialize, JsonSchema)]\n#[serde(tag = \"kind\", rename_all = \"snake_case\")]\npub enum ZeroclawError {\n    #[error(\"route not declared: {hint}\")]\n    RouteNotDeclared { hint: String },\n\n    #[error(\"provider not declared: {provider}\")]\n    ProviderNotDeclared { provider: String },\n\n    #[error(\"model not declared: {model}\")]\n    ModelNotDeclared { model: String },\n\n    #[error(\"tool not declared: {tool}\")]\n    ToolNotDeclared { tool: String },\n\n    #[error(\"route unavailable: {hint} ({reason})\")]\n    RouteUnavailable { hint: String, reason: String },\n\n    #[error(\"privacy tier violation: required {required}, provided {provided}\")]\n    PrivacyTierViolation { required: String, provided: String },\n\n    #[error(\"cost policy violation: {policy} ({reason})\")]\n    CostPolicyViolation { policy: String, reason: String },\n\n    #[error(\"context window exceeded: limit {limit}, requested {requested}\")]\n    ContextWindowExceeded { limit: u32, requested: u32 },\n\n    #[error(\"execution denied: {reason}\")]\n    ExecutionDenied { reason: String },\n\n    #[error(\"no candidate route after filtering\")]\n    NoCandidateAfterFiltering,\n}\n","internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough":{"turn_id":"019f1019-8460-7182-9143-20d4cc11d899"}}}

Use their underlying skills, MCP tools, and app tools to help solve the task.\n- Relevance: Determine what a plugin can help with from explicit user mention or from the plugin-associated skills, MCP tools, and apps exposed elsewhere in this turn.\n- Missing/blocked: If the user requests a plugin that does not have relevant callable capabilities for the task, say so briefly and continue with the best fallback.\n</plugins_instructions>"}],"internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough":{"turn_id":"019f1019-8460-7182-9143-20d4cc11d899"}},{"type":"message","role":"user","content":[{"type":"input_text","text":"# AGENTS.md instructions for /home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto\n\n<INSTRUCTIONS>\n### AGENTS.md for operation-dbus-proto\n\nThis file provides essential guidelines for agentic coding agents working in this repository. Follow these strictly to maintain consistency, pass CI, and adhere to the 3tched Architecture standards.\n\n#### 1. The Persona & Naming Conventions\n*   **Humanized Roles:** Treat system components as authoritative human roles. Never use sterile acronyms for major components.\n  *   **A.N.N.A. Scribe** (Axon Network Notary Arbitrator): The top-level Identity-State Arbitrator who notarizes the WireGuard identity and handles the \"Snowball\" session.\n  *   **The Compliance Engine (\"Law Firm\"):** One dedicated Attorney for each major component: **Olivia Scal** (Managing Partner / OSCAL), **E.U.gene Risk** (EU AI Act Counsel), **Penny Privacy** (GDPR Engine), and **Reggie O.P.A.** (Cloud Prosecutor).\n*   **Terminology:** Use exact architecture terminology: \"The Sled\" (1:1 shared memory layout), \"The Shuttle\" (the Rust bridge/courier), \"The Snowball\" (appended session ledger), and \"The Strike/Etch\" (generating the hash).\n\n#### 2. Core Architectural Rules (The \"Reality\")\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via OpenClaw Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Artix Linux (s6 init).\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles — D-Bus First (MANDATORY)\n\n**D-Bus is the ONLY control plane. Every read, every write, every tool call goes through D-Bus. There is no second option.**\n\n*   **D-Bus first. D-Bus always. D-Bus only.** If you are about to call a CLI, spawn a subprocess, read a config file, or poll a socket directly — stop. Find the D-Bus object and use it instead. `org.opdbus.v1` is the system.\n*   **No bypasses.** `Command::new(\"systemctl\")`, `Command::new(\"ip\")`, `Command::new(\"s6-svc\")`, direct file reads for live state — all forbidden in plugin and service code. Bootstrap scripts are the only exception.\n*   **D-Bus objects own plugin state.** Every plugin is a D-Bus object at `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<name>`. Read state through it. Mutate state through it. If there is no D-Bus object, the thing does not exist.\n*   **D-Bus method signatures are generated from the schema.** All D-Bus methods, MCP tool inputs, gRPC shapes, and UI field renderers derive from the `PluginSchema` in `plugin_schema_defs.rs`. The schema IS the interface contract — not a description of it.\n*   **One schema file, one source of truth.** All `PluginSchema` definitions MUST live in `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/plugin_schema_defs.rs`. Each plugin's `schema()` method calls `Some(super::plugin_schema_defs::their_plugin_schema())`. **Never define a schema inline in a plugin's own file** — it will not be registered, and the D-Bus object will have no contract.\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC (over Unix domain sockets or `grpc-uplink`). gRPC calls still flow through D-Bus registration — the D-Bus object is the authority, gRPC is the transport.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`simd_json` preferred, `serde_json` acceptable).\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n*   **No Python unless absolutely necessary.** This is a Rust-first codebase. Scripts are shell (`sh`/`bash`). Data processing is Rust. If you are reaching for Python, stop and ask why Rust or shell cannot do it. The only acceptable Python is in existing compliance-ingest tooling where no Rust equivalent exists yet.\n\n#### 4a. OSCAL Subid Taxonomy (MANDATORY — every artifact must carry a subid)\n\nEvery D-Bus object, plugin, schema, mutation, event, and tool in this system has two identifiers: a `uuid` (machine identity, never changes) and a `subid` (human-readable operational taxonomy key, stable per subject).\n\n**`subid` format:** `<category>.<component-type>.<subject>.<verb>[.<facet>][@vN]`\n\n**Seven categories — use exactly these, no others:**\n\n| category | what it classifies |\n|---|---|\n| `src` | authoritative source, ingress channel, source-of-truth store |\n| `prj` | D-Bus projection or mirror publication step |\n| `sch` | schema, contract, vocabulary, or control-mapping artifact |\n| `mut` | write-path operation that changes effective state |\n| `obs` | read, query, enumeration, discovery path |\n| `evt` | emitted signal, audit-chain event, proof, tag provenance |\n| `exp` | consumer-facing render — MCP tool, UI surface, gRPC bridge view |\n\n**Component-type** reuses OSCAL vocabulary: `software`, `service`, `network`, `hardware`, `process-procedure`, `standard`, `validation`, `policy`, `plan`, `guidance`, `physical`, `this-system`, `system`, `interconnection`.\n\n**Rules:**\n- `uuid` is exact machine identity — never replace it with `subid`\n- `subid` is an OSCAL `prop` value (`ns`, `name`, `value`) — never embed it in `remarks`\n- Compliance mappings (`control_refs[]`, `statement_refs[]`, `control_source`) live in metadata arrays, **never** inside the `subid` string\n- `mut.*` records **must** carry `actor_id` and `capability_id`\n- `evt.*` records **must** carry `event_id` or `event_hash`\n- `subid` is immutable per subject — if the meaning changes materially, create a new subject with `@vN`\n- All subids are registered in the canonical registry; uniqueness is enforced in CI\n\n**Examples:** `src.network.ovsdb.monitor@v1` · `prj.service.projected-object.publish@v1` · `sch.standard.plugin-schema.resolve@v1` · `mut.service.state-sync.apply-patch@v1` · `exp.service.plugin-projection.render@v1`\n\n#### 4b. MCP Gateway Architecture (SETTLED — DO NOT REDESIGN)\n\n*   **cognitive-mcp** (`:3003`, Netmaker WireGuard IP `100.90.37.254`) is the **universal gateway for ALL external clients**: NotebookLM, Droid (factory.ai), Cursor, Codex, Junie, Gemini CLI. It has memory tools, gRPC service, auth, and the correct protocol surface.\n*   **compact-mcp** (`127.0.0.1:11436`) is **loopback/chatbot only**. Never expose externally. Never point external clients at it.\n*   Do NOT create new shim services. Do NOT point external clients at `op-assistant-grpc` directly. Do NOT expose compact-mcp outside loopback.\n\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\n**Rust Workspace**\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\n\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\n\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\n\n#### 6. Coding Style & Naming Conventions\n*   **Rust:** Edition 2021, `rustfmt` (4-space indent, max-width 100). Use specific imports (`use serde_json::Value;`). Use `anyhow::Result<T>` for main errors and `thiserror` for custom enums.\n*   **TypeScript/React:** 2-space indent, Prettier via ESLint. Functional components only. Strict mode enabled.\n*   **Testing:** 80%+ coverage, mock externals. Name tests with behavior-focused names (`should_handle_<scenario>`).\n\n#### 7. Agent-Specific Output & Workflow Instructions\n*   **Scroll & Save Pacing:** Provide only **ONE** major component or script at a time. Wait for user confirmation before moving to the next.\n*   **Visual Cues:** If a script is a finalized component that needs to be saved to sources, it MUST begin with color bullets or icons (e.g., ⚖️ 🔴, 🟢 🛷).\n*   **Spec-Block Format:** When delivering a component, use a strict specification block containing:\n  1.  **Requirements:** The architectural rules it satisfies.\n  2.  **Design:** How it fits into the 3tched system (Zero-Copy, Btrfs, GUI Schema, etc.).\n  3.  **Code Implementation:** The exact, copy-pasteable Rust/Bash code.\n*   Before edits: `cargo check -p <crate>`, `npm run typecheck`.\n*   Mimic existing patterns: Search similar code. No new deps without PR justification.\n\n#### 8. Personal Preferences & Coding Standards\n* Refer to `~/.factory/memories.md` for personal development preferences and past decisions.\n* Follow the conventions documented in:\n  * `.factory/rules/typescript.md` - TypeScript and React conventions\n  * `.factory/rules/testing.md` - Testing and mocking std::env::var(key).unwrap_or_else(|_| fallback.to_string())\n    }\n\n    /// Serialize the canonical zeroclaw schema to the plugin-owned tmpfs file.\n    ///\n    /// This is the only write path to {"timestamp":"2026-06-28T21:36:45.235Z","type":"event_msg","payload":{"type":"agent_message","message":"Yes, the generic solution is still there.\n\nWhat changed:\n\n- `op-grpc-bridge` now looks up schemas generically by `plugin_id`.\n- Primary source: `/dev/shm/live-schema.json`\n- Fallback/cache: `/dev/shm/opdbus/schemas/<plugin>.json`\n- `PluginSchemaProvider::list_plugins()` and `get_schema(plugin_id)` work for all plugins, not just Zeroclaw.\n- `SchemaLoader::new_for_plugin(path, plugin_id)` can extract any plugin from the live-schema monolith.\n\nThe Zeroclaw-specific change is separate:\n\n- [op-llm/src/schema.rs](/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/crates/op-llm/src/schema.rs) now imports Zeroclaw’s schema from the Zeroclaw plugin module.\n- That does not replace the generic bridge lookup.\n- It just keeps `op-llm` from defining or importing a second divergent LLM schema.\n\nSo the model is:\n\n```text\nall plugins:\n  SchemaEngine -> /dev/shm/live-schema.json -> op-grpc-bridge lookup by plugin_id\n\nzeroclaw/op-llm only:\n  op-llm includes ZeroclawPlugin::schema contract directly for typed LLM adapter code\n```\n\nThe remaining smell is that some code still has per-plugin cache fallback reads. Schema Engine: Schema registry and validation services.\n//!\n//! This module implements the authoritative schema registry that validates\n//! and manages all PluginSchema definitions. It enforces the Schema-as-Code\n//! Authority principle: PluginSchema is the single source of truth for all\n//! projections.\n\nuse crate::data_models::*;\nuse crate::interfaces::{RawEntity, SchemaRegistry};\nuse anyhow::Result;\nuse regex::Regex;\nuse simd_json::prelude::*;\nuse simd_json::{OwnedValue as Value, StaticNode};\nuse std::collections::HashMap;\nuse std::io::Write;\nuse tracing::{debug, error, info, warn};\n\n/// Derived \"all-together\" monolith cache of the PluginSchema catalog. Kept for\n/// whole-catalog readers; NO LONGER the hash source (the manifest root is).\nconst SHM_SCHEMA_PATH: &str = \"/dev/shm/live-schema.json\";\n\n/// Directory of bare per-plugin schema objects (`<plugin>.json`) for individual\n/// consumption — emitted alongside the monolith from the same single producer.\nconst SHM_SCHEMA_DIR: &str = \"/dev/shm/opdbus/schemas\";\n\n/// Manifest carrying the single folded `catalog_hash` + per-plugin leaf hashes +\n/// `generation`. Written LAST as the atomic commit point; the one place the\n/// catalog hash is published — consumers read it, never re-hash.\nconst SHM_MANIFEST_PATH: &str = \"/dev/shm/opdbus/schemas/.manifest.json\";\n\n/// Schema version identifier\npub type SchemaVersion = u64;\n\n/// Lightweight shape check used to test whether a value satisfies one branch\n/// of a `FieldType::OneOf` discriminated union.\nfn value_matches_field_type(field_type: &FieldType, value: &Value) -> bool {\n    match (field_type, value) {\n        (FieldType::String, Value::String(_)) => true,\n        (FieldType::Integer, Value::Static(StaticNode::I64(_) | StaticNode::U64(_))) => true,\n        (FieldType::Float, Value::Static(StaticNode::F64(_))) => true,\n        let catalog: std::collections::HashMap<String, Vec<&PluginSchema>> = self\n            .schemas\n            .iter()\n            .map(|(k, v)| (k.clone(), v.iter().collect()))\n            .collect();\n\n        // 1. Derived \"all-together\" monolith cache (atomic). Kept for\n        //    whole-catalog readers; no longer the hash source.\n        let json_bytes = serde_json::to_vec_pretty(&catalog)\n            .map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!(\"Failed to serialize schema catalog: {}\", e))?;\n        atomic_write_shm(SHM_SCHEMA_PATH, &json_bytes)?;\n\n        // 2. Folder of bare per-plugin schema objects + per-plugin leaf hashes.\n        std::fs::create_dir_all(SHM_SCHEMA_DIR)\n            .map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!(\"Cannot create schema dir {}: {}\", SHM_SCHEMA_DIR, e))?;\n        let mut leaves: std::collections::BTreeMap<String, String> =\n            std::collections::BTreeMap::new();\n        for (id, schemas) in &catalog {\n            // Bare PluginSchema object (canonical one if a plugin declares\n            // several) — \"the schema is the plugin\"; consumers read this directly.\n            let Some(schema) = schemas.first() else {\n                continue;\n            };\n            let bytes = serde_json::to_vec_pretty(schema)\n                .map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!(\"Failed to serialize schema '{}': {}\", id, e))?;\n            atomic_write_shm(&format!(\"{}/{}.json\", SHM_SCHEMA_DIR, id), &bytes)?;\n            leaves.insert(id.clone(), blake3::hash(&bytes).to_hex().to_string());\n        }\n\n        // 3. Canonical catalog hash = blake3 of the monolith bytes — the EXACT\n        //    value the identity derivation already uses, kept stable so the\n        //    WG/ghostbridge verifier needs no change. Per-plugin `leaves` are\n        //    published alongside for per-file integrity / future incremental use.\n        let catalog_hash = blake3::hash(&json_bytes).to_hex().to_string();\n\n        // 4. Manifest, written LAST as the atomic commit point — the one place\n        //    `catalog_hash` is published; consumers read it, never re-hash.\n        let generation = Self::read_manifest_generation().wrapping_add(1);\n        let mut manifest = serde_json::Map::new();\n        manifest.insert(\n            \"catalog_hash\".to_string(),\n            serde_json::Value::String(catalog_hash.clone()),\n        );\n        manifest.insert(\n            \"generation\".to_string(),\n            serde_json::Value::from(generation),\n        );\n        manifest.insert(\n            \"plugins\".to_string(),\n            serde_json::to_value(&leaves)\n                .map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!(\"Failed to serialize leaf hashes: {}\", e))?,\n","internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough":{"turn_id":"019f102b-2ed5-7b51-a092-035c6e55136c"}}}

{"timestamp":"2026-06-28T21:41:46.730Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"function_call_output","call_id":"call_yI4hZDDVHXsIkFGx4Z3B5Z6C","output":"Chunk ID: 746ad2\nWall time: 0.0001 seconds\nProcess exited with code 0\nOriginal token count: 357\nOutput:\n        Value::String(s) => Some(s.chars().count() as f64),\n        Value::Array(a) => Some(a.len() as f64),\n        _ => None,\n    }\n}\n\n/// Atomically publish `bytes` to a `/dev/shm` path via a sibling temp file +\n/// rename, so readers see either the old or new content, never a torn write.\nfn atomic_write_shm(path: &str, bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<()> {\n    let tmp = format!(\"{}.tmp\", path);\n    {\n        let mut file = std::fs::File::create(&tmp)\n            .map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!(\"Cannot create {}: {}\", tmp, e))?;\n        file.write_all(bytes)\n            .map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!(\"Failed to write {}: {}\", tmp, e))?;\n        file.sync_all()\n            .map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!(\"Failed to sync {}: {}\", tmp, e))?;\n    }\n    std::fs::rename(&tmp, path)\n        .map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!(\"Failed to rename {} -> {}: {}\", tmp, path, e))?;\n    Ok(())\n            serde_json::Value::from(generation),\n        );\n        let manifest_bytes = serde_json::to_vec_pretty(&serde_json::Value::Object(manifest))\n            .map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!(\"Failed to serialize schema manifest: {}\", e))?;\n        atomic_write_shm(SHM_MANIFEST_PATH, &manifest_bytes)?;\n\n        info!(\n            dir = SHM_SCHEMA_DIR,\n            catalog_hash = %catalog_hash,\n            generation,\n            plugins = leaves.len(),\n            \"Schema catalog written to shared memory (folder + monolith + manifest)\"\n        );\n","internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough":{"turn_id":"019f102b-2ed5-7b51-a092-035c6e55136c"}}}

The monolith and manifest are written atomically: data is first written to\n//! a `.tmp` file and then renamed over the final path.  This prevents consumers\n//! from reading a partial file.\n//!\n//! # Catalog Hash\n//!\n//! The Blake3 catalog hash is computed by sorting per-plugin schema filenames,\n//! leaf-hashing each file's bytes, and folding the leaf hashes into a single\n//! root hash.  Only the producer computes this hash; consumers read it from\n//! `.manifest.json`.\n\nuse anyhow::{Context, Result};\nuse op_state_store::PluginSchema;\nuse std::collections::HashMap;\nuse std::fs;\nuse std::io::Write;\nuse std::path::{Path, PathBuf};\nuse tracing::{debug, info};\n\n/// Default base directory for shared memory.\nconst DEFAULT_SHM_BASE: &str = \"/dev/shm\";\n\n/// Subdirectory under the SHM base for all opdbus files.\nconst OPDBUS_DIR: &str = \"opdbus\";\n\n/// Subdirectory for per-plugin capability schema files.\nconst SCHEMAS_DIR: &str = \"schemas\";\n\n/// Subdirectory for per-plugin present-state files.\nconst STATE_DIR: &str = \"state\";\n\n/// Combined monolith filename (lives directly under SHM base, not opdbus/).\nconst MONOLITH_FILENAME: &str = \"live-schema.json\";\n\n/// Manifest filename (lives under opdbus/).\nconst MANIFEST_FILENAME: &str = \".manifest.json\";\n\n/// Sole writer of plugin capability schemas and present-state to SHM.\npub struct ShmWriter {\n    /// Base directory (default `/dev/shm`).\n    base_dir: PathBuf,\n    /// `/dev/shm/opdbus`\n    opdbus_dir: PathBuf,\n    /// `/dev/shm/opdbus/schemas`\n    schemas_dir: PathBuf,\n    /// `/dev/shm/opdbus/state`\n    state_dir: PathBuf,\n    /// `/dev/shm/live-schema.json`\n    monolith_path: PathBuf,\n    /// `/dev/shm/opdbus/.manifest.json`\n    manifest_path: PathBuf,\n}\n\nimpl Default for ShmWriter {\n    fn default() -> Self {\n        Self::new(DEFAULT_SHM_BASE)\n    }\n}\n\nimpl ShmWriter {\n    /// Creates a new `ShmWriter` rooted at the given base directory.\n    ///\n    /// In production, use `ShmWriter::default()` which targets `/dev/shm`.\n    /// Tests should supply a temporary directory.\n    }\n\n    /// Creates the `/dev/shm/opdbus/` hierarchy (`schemas/`, `state/`) if it\n    /// does not already exist.  Idempotent.\n    pub fn ensure_dirs(&self) -> Result<()> {\n        fs::create_dir_all(&self.opdbus_dir)\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to create {}\", self.opdbus_dir.display()))?;\n        fs::create_dir_all(&self.schemas_dir)\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to create {}\", self.schemas_dir.display()))?;\n        fs::create_dir_all(&self.state_dir)\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to create {}\", self.state_dir.display()))?;\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Writes a single per-plugin capability schema JSON file to\n    /// `/dev/shm/opdbus/schemas/<plugin_id>.json`.\n    pub fn write_plugin_schema(&self, plugin_id: &str, schema: &PluginSchema) -> Result<()> {\n        let path = self.schemas_dir.join(format!(\"{}.json\", plugin_id));\n        let json_bytes = serde_json::to_vec_pretty(schema)\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to serialize schema for '{}'\", plugin_id))?;\n        atomic_write(&path, &json_bytes)\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to write schema for '{}'\", plugin_id))?;\n        debug!(plugin_id, path = %path.display(), \"wrote per-plugin schema\");\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Writes the combined monolith to `/dev/shm/live-schema.json` atomically.\n    ///\n    /// `schemas` is a map of `plugin_id → PluginSchema` containing every plugin\n    /// that returned `Some(schema)` from `schema()`.\n    pub fn write_monolith(&self, schemas: &HashMap<String, PluginSchema>) -> Result<()> {\n        let json_bytes =\n            serde_json::to_vec_pretty(schemas).context(\"failed to serialize monolith\")?;\n        atomic_write(&self.monolith_path, &json_bytes).with_context(|| {\n            format!(\n                \"failed to write monolith to {}\",\n                self.monolith_path.display()\n            )\n        })?;\n        debug!(path = %self.monolith_path.display(), \"wrote combined monolith\");\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Computes the Blake3 catalog hash over all per-plugin schema files.\n    ///\n    /// Algorithm:\n    /// 1. List all `*.json` files in the schemas directory.\n    /// 2. Sort by filename.\n    /// 3. Leaf-hash each file's bytes with Blake3.\n    /// 4. Fold (concatenate) the leaf hashes and hash the result to produce\n    ///    a single root hash.\n    pub fn compute_catalog_hash(&self) -> Result<String> {\n        let mut entries: Vec<_> = fs::read_dir(&self.schemas_dir)\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"cannot read schemas dir {}\", self.schemas_dir.display()))?\n            .filter_map(|e| e.ok())\n            .filter(|e| e.path().extension().is_some_and(|ext| ext == \"json\"))\n            .collect();\n        entries.sort_by_key(|e| e.file_name());\n\n        if entries.is_empty() {\n            // No schema files — hash of empty input is still a valid Blake3.\n            return Ok(blake3::hash(&[]).to_hex().to_string());\n        }\n\n        let mut concatenated: Vec<u8> = Vec::with_capacity(entries.len() * 32);\n        for entry in &entries {\n            let bytes = fs::read(entry.path())\n                .with_context(|| format!(\"cannot read {}\", entry.path().display()))?;\n            let leaf_hash = blake3::hash(&bytes);\n            concatenated.extend_from_slice(leaf_hash.as_bytes());\n        }\n        let root_hash = blake3::hash(&concatenated);\n        Ok(root_hash.to_hex().to_string())\n    }\n\n    /// Writes `{ \"catalog_hash\": \"<hex>\" }` to `.manifest.json` atomically.\n    pub fn write_manifest(&self, catalog_hash: &str) -> Result<()> {\n        let json = serde_json::json!({ \"catalog_hash\": catalog_hash });\n        let json_bytes =\n            serde_json::to_vec_pretty(&json).context(\"failed to serialize manifest\")?;\n        atomic_write(&self.manifest_path, &json_bytes).with_context(|| {\n            format!(\n                \"failed to write manifest to {}\",\n                self.manifest_path.display()\n            )\n        })?;\n        debug!(catalog_hash, path = %self.manifest_path.display(), \"wrote manifest\");\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Writes present-state JSON for a plugin to\n    /// `/dev/shm/opdbus/state/<plugin_id>.json` and then recomputes and\n    /// rewrites the manifest hash so consumers detect the change.\n    pub fn write_present_state(&self, plugin_id: &str, state: &serde_json::Value) -> Result<()> {\n        let path = self.state_dir.join(format!(\"{}.json\", plugin_id));\n        let json_bytes = serde_json::to_vec_pretty(state)\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to serialize present-state for '{}'\", plugin_id))?;\n        atomic_write(&path, &json_bytes)\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to write present-state for '{}'\", plugin_id))?;\n        debug!(plugin_id, path = %path.display(), \"wrote present-state\");\n\n        // Recompute catalog hash and update manifest so consumers detect the\n        // state change on their next inbound connection.\n        let hash = self.compute_catalog_hash()?;\n        self.write_manifest(&hash)?;\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Convenience: writes all per-plugin schema files, the combined monolith,\n    /// and the manifest in one call.\n    ///\n    /// Plugins returning `None` from `schema()` are skipped entirely — no\n    /// per-plugin file, no monolith entry, no state file.\n    pub fn write_all_schemas(&self, plugins: &[(String, Option<PluginSchema>)]) -> Result<()> {\n        self.ensure_dirs()?;\n\n        let mut monolith: HashMap<String, PluginSchema> = HashMap::new();\n        for (plugin_id, schema_opt) in plugins {\n            match schema_opt {\n                Some(schema) => {\n                    self.write_plugin_schema(plugin_id, schema)?;\n                    monolith.insert(plugin_id.clone(), schema.clone());\n                }\n                None => {\n                    debug!(plugin_id, \"skipping plugin with None schema\");\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        self.write_monolith(&monolith)?;\n        let hash = self.compute_catalog_hash()?;\n        self.write_manifest(&hash)?;\n\n        info!(\n            plugin_count = monolith.len(),\n            catalog_hash = %hash,\n            \"wrote all schemas to SHM\"\n        );\n        Ok(())\n    }\n    }\n\n    /// Convenience: writes present-state for all provided plugins and refreshes\n    /// the manifest hash once at the end.\n    pub fn write_all_present_states(&self, states: &[(String, serde_json::Value)]) -> Result<()> {\n        self.ensure_dirs()?;\n        for (plugin_id, state) in states {\n            let path = self.state_dir.join(format!(\"{}.json\", plugin_id));\n            let json_bytes = serde_json::to_vec_pretty(state).with_context(|| {\n                format!(\"failed to serialize present-state for '{}'\", plugin_id)\n            })?;\n            atomic_write(&path, &json_bytes)\n                .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to write present-state for '{}'\", plugin_id))?;\n        }\n        let hash = self.compute_catalog_hash()?;\n        self.write_manifest(&hash)?;\n        info!(state_count = states.len(), \"wrote present-states to SHM\");\n        Ok(())\n    }\n}\n\n/// Atomically writes `data` to `path` by first writing to `<path>.tmp` and\n/// then renaming over the target.\n///\n/// The rename(2) syscall is atomic on the same filesystem, so consumers will\n/// never observe a partially written file.\nfn atomic_write(path: &Path, data: &[u8]) -> Result<()> {\n    let tmp_path = atomic_tmp_path(path);\n    {\n        let mut file = fs::File::create(&tmp_path)\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"cannot create tmp file {}\", tmp_path.display()))?;\n        file.write_all(data)\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to write tmp file {}\", tmp_path.display()))?;\n        file.sync_all()\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to sync tmp file {}\", tmp_path.display()))?;\n    }\n    fs::rename(&tmp_path, path).with_context(|| {\n        format!(\n            \"failed to rename {} → {}\",\n {"timestamp":"2026-06-28T21:44:54.076Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"function_call_output","call_id":"call_yfgFRdtBlA5mr1TZUj8JlRg4","output":"Chunk ID: 7eeeec\nWall time: 0.0000 seconds\nProcess exited with code 0\nOriginal token count: 513\nOutput:\n\n/// Decode a base64 WireGuard public key (32-byte Curve25519) into raw bytes.\nfn decode_wg_pubkey(b64: &str) -> [u8; 32] {\n    use base64::Engine;\n    base64::engine::general_purpose::STANDARD\n        .decode(b64.trim())\n        .ok()\n        .and_then(|v| v.try_into().ok())\n        .unwrap_or([0u8; 32])\n}\n\n/// Build and atomically write the sled from live WireGuard state.\n///\n/// THE STRIKE/ETCH -- single source of truth for the identity footprint.\n///\n/// Blake3( wg_pubkey || schema_catalog_hash(/dev/shm/live-schema.json) || mutation_index || source_port ).\n/// source_port is the per-session WireGuard-observed source port (0 when none). It binds the\n/// footprint to the session network context for the accountability loop -- it is NOT an auth\n/// factor (WireGuard is the authenticator; see op-grpc-bridge GhostbridgeInterceptor).\n/// Manifest published by op-projection — the ONE place the canonical\n/// `catalog_hash` lives.\nconst SHM_SCHEMA_MANIFEST_PATH: &str = \"/dev/shm/opdbus/schemas/.manifest.json\";\n/// Derived monolith catalog; fallback source for the hash before the manifest\n/// exists (deploy ordering). Same bytes → identical hash value.\nconst SHM_LIVE_SCHEMA_PATH: &str = \"/dev/shm/live-schema.json\";\n\n/// The single canonical schema-catalog hash (32 bytes), computed ONCE by\n/// op-projection and read here — never re-hashed per call site. Reads the\n/// manifest's `catalog_hash`; falls back to hashing the monolith directly when\n/// the manifest isn't present yet. `None` if neither artifact exists.\npub fn schema_catalog_hash() -> Option<[u8; 32]> {\n    if let Ok(bytes) = std::fs::read(SHM_SCHEMA_MANIFEST_PATH) {\n        if let Ok(v) = serde_json::from_slice::<serde_json::Value>(&bytes) {\n            if let Some(hex_str) = v.get(\"catalog_hash\").and_then(|h| h.as_str()) {\n                if let Ok(raw) = hex::decode(hex_str) {\n                    if let Ok(arr) = <[u8; 32]>::try_from(raw.as_slice()) {\n                        return Some(arr);\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n","internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough":{"turn_id":"019f102b-2ed5-7b51-a092-035c6e55136c"}}}

{"timestamp":"2026-06-28T21:55:57.101Z","type":"event_msg","payload":{"type":"agent_message","message":"Mostly yes, with one important split.\n\nOn D-Bus object creation/registration:\n\n- `SchemaRouter` reads `/dev/shm/live-schema.json`.\n- It creates one route/object per plugin schema.\n- Object path is derived from plugin id:\n  - `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<plugin>`\n- Interface/method/property surface is derived from that plugin’s `PluginSchema`.\n- Unknown methods/properties are rejected from the schema, not hardcoded.\n\nBut the schema files are populated before that:\n\n- `SchemaEngine` / `ShmWriter` writes:\n  - `/dev/shm/live-schema.json`\n  - `/dev/shm/opdbus/schemas/<plugin>.json`\n  - `/dev/shm/opdbus/.manifest.json`\n- Then D-Bus creation consumes that live schema catalog.\n\nSo the order is:\n\n```text\nplugin schema() methods\n  -> SchemaEngine writes live-schema + individual materialized schemas\n  -> SchemaRouter reads live-schema\n  -> D-Bus objects are registered\n  -> D-Bus methods/properties route through schema-backed dispatch\n```\n\nFor plugin-derived subobjects like provider routes/channels/skills, those only appear if the plugin schema/state exposes them and the projection hook materializes them. Right now Zeroclaw has special projection hook behavior; the generic “all plugins produce derived child objects from schema/state” still needs to be finished.","phase":"final_answer","memory_citation":null}}
{"timestamp":"2026-06-28T21:55:57.108Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"message","id":"msg_0cbf422319b5f38a016a4198710a208197ad5d95f1c8a70a4b","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"output_text","text":"Mostly yes, with one important split.\n\nOn D-Bus object creation/registration:\n\n- `SchemaRouter` reads `/dev/shm/live-schema.json`.\n- It creates one route/object per plugin schema.\n- Object path is derived from plugin id:\n  - `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<plugin>`\n- Interface/method/property surface is derived from that plugin’s `PluginSchema`.\n- Unknown methods/properties are rejected from the schema, not hardcoded.\n\nBut the schema files are populated before that:\n\n- `SchemaEngine` / `ShmWriter` writes:\n  - `/dev/shm/live-schema.json`\n  - `/dev/shm/opdbus/schemas/<plugin>.json`\n  - `/dev/shm/opdbus/.manifest.json`\n- Then D-Bus creation consumes that live schema catalog.\n\nSo the order is:\n\n```text\nplugin schema() methods\n  -> SchemaEngine writes live-schema + individual materialized schemas\n  -> SchemaRouter reads live-schema\n  -> D-Bus objects are registered\n  -> D-Bus methods/properties route through schema-backed dispatch\n```\n\nFor plugin-derived subobjects like provider routes/channels/skills, those only appear if the plugin schema/state exposes them and the projection hook materializes them. Right now Zeroclaw has special projection hook behavior; the generic “all plugins produce derived child objects from schema/state” still needs to be finished."}],"phase":"final_answer","internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough":{"turn_id":"019f103b-411b-71a0-ac49-190d781119e5"}}}

Zeroclaw projection hook (mission spec §9.2/§9.3, Phase 1b).\n//!\n//! Renders the **read-only** D-Bus sub-object tree for the Zeroclaw plugin:\n//! one managed object per declared `ModelRoute` at\n//! `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/zeroclaw/routes/<hint>` and one per `Provider` at\n//! `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/zeroclaw/providers/<id>`.\n//!\n//! # Dependency direction\n//! The mission text places the hook trait in `op-projection`, but `op-projection`\n//! already depends on `op-grpc-bridge` (not the reverse). Putting the trait there\n//! and implementing it here would create a crate cycle. The actual hard rule is\n//! \"no crate cycle\" (spec §10), so the trait lives here in `op-grpc-bridge` (which\n//! already depends on `op-plugins` for `ZeroclawState`). `op-projection` is\n//! untouched and the dependency graph stays acyclic.\n//!\n//! # No polling / watching / indexing\n//! `apply` is a synchronous push: the projection owner calls it after a cycle with\n//! the **in-memory** schema + state. There is no timer, no file watcher, and no\n//! `/dev/shm` re-read on this path. Property names are enumerated from\n//! `schemars::schema_for!(ModelRoute)` / `schema_for!(Provider)` — never hardcoded.\n\nuse std::collections::{HashMap, HashSet};\nuse std::sync::Arc;\n\nuse serde_json::Value as JsonValue;\nuse tokio::sync::{Mutex, OnceCell};\nuse tracing::{debug, warn};\nuse zbus::Connection;\n\nuse op_plugins::state_plugins::common::llm_projection::{ModelRoute, Provider};\nuse op_plugins::state_plugins::zeroclaw::ZeroclawState;\n\nconst ROUTE_INTERFACE: &str = \"org.opdbus.v1.ModelRoute\";\nconst PROVIDER_INTERFACE: &str = \"org.opdbus.v1.Provider\";\nconst ROUTES_BASE: &str = \"/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/zeroclaw/routes\";\nconst PROVIDERS_BASE: &str = \"/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/zeroclaw/providers\";\n\n/// Push-only projection contract. The projection owner invokes [`apply`] after a\n/// projection cycle, handing in the **in-memory** schema + state. Implementations\n/// must not poll, watch, index, or re-read `/dev/shm`.\n///\n/// [`apply`]: SchemaProjectionHook::apply\npub trait SchemaProjectionHook: Send + Sync {\n    /// Apply the projection for `plugin_id` from the in-memory `schema_json` and\n    /// `state_json`. Called synchronously; long work is spawned by the impl.\n    fn apply(&self, plugin_id: &str, schema_json: &JsonValue, state_json: &JsonValue);\n}\n\n/// A projected route/provider managed object. c.is_ascii_digit()).unwrap_or(false) {\n        s.insert(0, '_');\n    }\n    s\n}\n\n/// The set of route + provider object paths a given state should publish, paired\n/// with the schemars-projected route_names = schema_property_names(\n        &serde_json::to_value(schemars::schema_for!(ModelRoute)).unwrap_or_default(),\n    );\n    let provider_names = schema_property_names(\n _>(path.as_str()).await {\n                    warn!(path, error = %e, \"failed to unregister stale provider object\");\n                }\n                current.remove(&path);\n            }\n        }\n\n        debug!(\n            routes = routes.len(),\n            providers = providers.len(),\n            \"zeroclaw projection sub-tree reconciled\"\n        );\n    }\n}\n\nimpl through `SchemaEngine::dispatch_method_call`\n    /// (Requirement 5 / VAL-DISPATCH-001).\n    pub fn with_engine(\n        plugin_id: String,\n        route: PluginRoute,\n        engine: Option<Arc<SchemaEngine>>,\n    ) -> Self {\n        let mut iface = Self::with_shm_state_dir(plugin_id, route, DEFAULT_SHM_STATE_DIR);\n        iface.engine = engine;\n        iface\n    }\n\n    /// Creates a new `SchemaBackedInterface` with a custom SHM state directory.\n    ///\n    /// In production, use [`new`](Self::new) which targets `/dev/shm/opdbus/state`.\n    /// Tests should supply a temporary directory.\n    pub fn with_shm_state_dir(\n        plugin_id: String,\n        route: PluginRoute,\n        shm_state_dir: impl AsRef<Path>,\n    ) -> Self {\n        Self {\n            plugin_id,\n            route,\n            shm_state_dir: shm_state_dir.as_ref().to_path_buf(),\n            engine: None,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Reads the present-state JSON for this plugin from SHM.\n    ///\n    /// The file is read directly from `<shm_state_dir>/<plugin_id>.json`.\n    /// If the file does not exist, an empty JSON object (`{}`) is returned,\n    /// not an error. This is a direct file read — no polling, no caching,\n    /// no D-Bus signal watching.\n    pub fn read_present_state(&self) -> JsonValue {\n        let path = self.shm_state_dir.join(format!(\"{}.json\", self.plugin_id));\n        match std::fs::read_to_string(&path) {\n            Ok(text) => {\n                serde_json::from_str(&text).unwrap_or(JsonValue::Object(serde_json::Map::new()))\n            }\n            Err(_) => JsonValue::Object(serde_json::Map::new()),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// The canonical D-Bus object path this interface is registered at\n    /// (`/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<plugin_id>`).\n    pub fn dbus_path(&self) -> &str {\n        &self.route.dbus_path\n    }\n\n    /// The canonical D-Bus interface name for this plugin\n    /// (`org.opdbus.v1.Plugin.<PluginName>`).\n    pub fn dbus_interface(&self) -> &str {\n        &self.route.dbus_interface\n    }\n\n    /// Names of every method declared in the plugin's capability surface.\n    ///\n    /// Every declared `MethodDecl` is exposed as a callable D-Bus method via\n    /// [`call`](Self::call).\n    pub fn declared_methods(&self) -> Vec<String> {\n        self.route.methods.keys().cloned().collect()\n    }\n\n    /// Returns `true` if `method` is declared in the plugin's capability\n    /// surface (and Vec<String> {\n        self.route\n            .signals\n            .iter()\n            .filter_map(|s| s.get(\"name\").and_then(|n| n.as_str()).map(String::from))\n            .collect()\n    }\n\n    /// Returns `true` if `signal` is declared in the plugin's capability\n    /// surface (and is therefore emittable).\n    pub fn exposes_signal(&self, signal: &str) -> bool {\n        self.route\n            .signals\n            .iter()\n            .any(|s| s.get(\"name\").and_then(|n| n.as_str()) == Some(signal))\n    }\n\n    /// Emits a declared D-Bus signal for this plugin on the canonical object\n    /// path and interface, carrying `payload_json` as the signal body.\n    ///\n    /// The signal name is validated against the plugin's capability surface;\n    /// emitting a signal that is not declared is rejected.       &self,\n        conn: &Connection,\n        signal: &str,\n        payload_json: &str,\n    ) -> zbus::fdo::Result<()> {\n        if !self.exposes_signal(signal) {\n            return Err(zbus::fdo::Error::UnknownMethod(format!(\n                \"signal '{}' is not declared for plugin '{}'\",\n                signal, self.plugin_id\n            )));\n        }\n        conn.emit_signal(\n            Option::<&str>::None,\n            self.route.dbus_path.as_str(),\n            self.route.dbus_interface.as_str(),\n            signal,\n            &(payload_json.to_string(),),\n        )\n        .await\n        .map_err(|e| zbus::fdo::Error::Failed(e.to_string()))\n    }\n\n    /// Validates that json_args conforms to the JSON Schema in MethodDecl.args.\n    ///\n    /// Returns Ok(()) if validation passes, Err(String) with details if it fails.\n    /// This validation happens before dispatch, so invalid args cause no mutation\n    /// (Requirement 6.3 / VAL-VALIDATE-003).\n    fn validate_json_args(&self, method_decl: &JsonValue, json_args: &str) -> Result<(), String> {\n        let args_schema = method_decl\n            .get(\"args\")\n            .ok_or_else(|| \"missing args schema\".to_string())?;\n\n        // Parse the args schema as a validator\n        let validator =\n            Validator::new(args_schema).map_err(|e| format!(\"invalid schema: {}\", e))?;\n\n        // Parse the args JSON\n        let args_value: JsonValue =\n            serde_json::from_str(json_args).map_err(|e| format!(\"invalid JSON: {}\", e))?;\n\n        // Validate against the schema (jsonschema uses draft-07 by default)\n        if let Err(e) = validator.validate(&args_value) {\n            return Err(format!(\"validation error: {}\", e));\n        }\n\n        Ok(())\n    }\n}\n\n#[zbus::interface(name = \"org.opdbus.v1.PluginV1\")]\nimpl SchemaBackedInterface {\n    /// Generic method call dispatcher.\n    ///\n    /// All schema-defined methods are funneled through this call, allowing\n    /// dynamic dispatch without compile-time traits for every plugin.\n    ///\n    /// Dispatch pipeline (Requirement 7):\n    ///   1. Method lookup → reject if not declared (UnknownMethod)\n    ///   2. Arg validation → reject if invalid (InvalidArgs)\n    ///   3. Capability check → reject if required_capability not granted (AccessDenied)\n    ///   4. SchemaEngine.mutate → record in event chain (Requirement 5)\n    async fn call(&self, method: String, json_args: String) -> zbus::fdo::Result<String> {\n        // 1. Method-existence gate: reject undeclared methods (Requirement 6).\n        // If the methods map is empty, ALL invocations are rejected as UnknownMethod.\n        let method_decl = match self.route.methods.get(&method) {\n            Some(decl) => decl,\n            None => return Err(zbus::fdo::Error::UnknownMethod(method)),\n        };\n\n        info!(plugin_id = %self.plugin_id, method, \"D-Bus method call received\");\n\n        // 2. Argument validation against MethodDecl.args JSON Schema (Requirement 6.3).\n        // json_args must conform to the schema; rejection as InvalidArgs without calling mutate.\n        if let Err(e) = self.validate_json_args(method_decl, &json_args) {\n            return Err(zbus::fdo::Error::InvalidArgs(format!(\n                \"arguments do not conform to schema for method '{}': {}\",\n                method, e\n            )));\n        }\n\n        // 3. Capability enforcement (Requirement 7.2, VAL-ENFORCE-002/003).\n        // For D-Bus calls, capability checks are delegated to the bridge.\n        // The caller identity (footprint) must grant the required_capability if non-null.\n        // This enforcement happens at bridge layer only (VAL-ENFORCE-006).\n        let required_cap = method_decl\n            .get(\"required_capability\")\n            .and_then(|c| c.as_str())\n            .filter(|s| !s.is_empty());\n\n        if let Some(cap) = required_cap {\n            // For D-Bus, we check the current sled's footprint grants.\n            // This is the primary gate: footprint validation already passed via\n            // the sled's temporal hash check (NFR-006).\n            let grants = match op_identity::read_sled() {\n                Ok((ptr, _mmap)) => {\n                    let sled = unsafe { &*ptr };\n                    load_capability_grants(&hex::encode(sled.hashed_footprint))\n                }\n                Err(_) => std::collections::HashSet::new(),\n            };\n\n            if !grants.contains(cap) {\n                // VAL-ENFORCE-003: Missing capability denied without calling mutate.\n                return Err(zbus::fdo::Error::AccessDenied(format!(\n                    \"capability '{}' required for method '{}' is not granted\",\n                    cap, method\n                )));\n            }\n        }\n\n        // 4. Real dispatch through SchemaEngine (Requirement 5).\n        //    json_args is passed verbatim — no default, no placeholder\n        //    (Requirement 5.4 / VAL-DISPATCH-004).\n        let engine = self.engine.as_ref().ok_or_else(|| {\n            zbus::fdo::Error::Failed(\n                \"SchemaEngine not wired to this interface — dispatch unavailable\".to_string(),\n            )\n        })?;\n\n        // The capability_id is read from the MethodDecl's required_capability\n        // (enforcement already performed above, here it's threaded into event chain).\n        let capability_id = required_cap.map(|s| s.to_string());\n\n        // The actor_id for a D-Bus dispatch is the caller's bus identity.\n        // The interceptor-extracted footprint/session is the primary gate;\n        // here we use the plugin's bus name as the actor for audit purposes.\n        let actor_id = format!(\"dbus:{}\", self.plugin_id);\n\n        let result = engine\n            .dispatch_method_call(\n                &self.plugin_id,\n                &method,\n                &json_args,\n                capability_id.as_deref(),\n                &actor_id,\n            )\n            .await\n            .map_err(|e| zbus::fdo::Error::Failed(e.to_string()))?;\n\n        // 5. Return the serialized result to the D-Bus caller.\n        serde_json::to_string(&result).map_err(|e| zbus::fdo::Error::Failed(e.to_string()))\n    }\n\n    /// Get a property value from SHM present-state.\n    ///\n    /// Reads `/dev/shm/opdbus/state/<plugin_id>.json` on each call.\n    /// If the state file does not exist, returns an empty value for the\n    /// requested property (not an error).\n    async fn get_property(&self, name: String) -> zbus::fdo::Result<String> {\n        let state = self.read_present_state();\n        let val = state.get(&name).unwrap_or(&JsonValue::Null);\n        serde_json::to_string(val).map_err(|e| zbus::fdo::Error::Failed(e.to_string()))\n    }\n\n    /// Get all present-state properties as a JSON object.\n    ///\n    /// Reads `/dev/shm/opdbus/state/<plugin_id>.json` on each call.\n    /// If the state file does not exist, returns `{}`.\n    async fn get_all_properties(&self) -> zbus::fdo::Result<String> {\n        let state = self.read_present_state();\n        serde_json::to_string(&state).map_err(|e| zbus::fdo::Error::Failed(e.to_string()))\n    }\n\n    /// Set a property value.\n    ///\n    /// Present-state is managed by the producer (`op-projection`) via SHM.\n    /// The bridge is a reader, not a writer, of present-state. This method\n    /// returns an error indicating that property writes must go through the\n    /// producer's mutation pipeline.\n    async fn set_property(&self, _name: String, _json_value: String) -> zbus::fdo::Result<()> {\n        Err(zbus::fdo::Error::Failed(\n            \"Present-state is managed by op-projection via SHM; \\\n             use the mutation pipeline to change properties\"\n                .to_string(),\n        ))\n    }\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)]\npub enum SchemaRouterError {\n    #[error(\"Plugin not found: {0}\")]\n    PluginNotFound(String),\n    #[error(\"Method {method} not found for plugin {plugin_id}. Available: {available:?}\")]\n    MethodNotFound {\n        plugin_id: String,\n        method: String,\n        available: Vec<String>,\n    },\n    #[error(\"Property {property} not found for plugin {plugin_id}. Available: {available:?}\")]\n    PropertyNotFound {\n        plugin_id: String,\n        property: String,\n        available: Vec<String>,\n    },\n","internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough":{"turn_id":"019f103c-f333-7fc1-a51d-1d49a27742fe"}}}

{"timestamp":"2026-06-28T22:16:20.970Z","type":"event_msg","payload":{"type":"agent_message","message":"Correct.\n\nThe rule should be:\n\n```text\nno PluginSchema -> no plugin object\nno schema field -> no child object\nno live-schema entry -> plugin does not exist on D-Bus\n```\n\nSo we should not do this:\n\n```text\nschema missing -> inspect state anyway -> invent child paths\n```\n\nThat bypasses schemars and violates the one-source rule.\n\nThe right behavior is:\n\n- `SchemaEngine` generates/writes the plugin schema from schemars.\n- D-Bus root object exists only if that plugin is present in `live-schema.json`.\n- Child objects are inherited from the schema’s object/array fields.\n- Runtime state only fills values and instance IDs.\n- If the plugin has state but no schema, the state is ignored for D-Bus object creation.\n\nFor plugins that need children but don’t have schema fields yet, the fix is to generate/extend the plugin’s `PluginSchema`, not add projection heuristics.","phase":"final_answer","memory_citation":null}}
{"timestamp":"2026-06-28T22:16:20.976Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"message","id":"msg_08af666a048f214a016a419d3a60cc81909bfc85806dab452c","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"output_text","text":"Correct.\n\nThe rule should be:\n\n```text\nno PluginSchema -> no plugin object\nno schema field -> no child object\nno live-schema entry -> plugin does not exist on D-Bus\n```\n\nSo we should not do this:\n\n```text\nschema missing -> inspect state anyway -> invent child paths\n```\n\nThat bypasses schemars and violates the one-source rule.\n\nThe right behavior is:\n\n- `SchemaEngine` generates/writes the plugin schema from schemars.\n- D-Bus root object exists only if that plugin is present in `live-schema.json`.\n- Child objects are inherited from the schema’s object/array fields.\n- Runtime state only fills values and instance IDs.\n- If the plugin has state but no schema, the state is ignored for D-Bus object creation.\n\nFor plugins that need children but don’t have schema fields yet, the fix is to generate/extend the plugin’s `PluginSchema`, not add projection heuristics."}],"phase":"final_answer","internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough":{"turn_id":"019f104d-8758-7523-b4ba-3258a96efdac"}}}

{"timestamp":"2026-06-28T22:18:26.453Z","type":"event_msg","payload":{"type":"agent_message","message":"Exactly.\n\nIf the system enforces the rule correctly:\n\n```text\nchild object requires parent plugin object\nparent plugin object requires PluginSchema\nPluginSchema comes from schemars or the autogenerator\n```\n\nThen orphaned children cannot exist.\n\nThe only cleanup case is stale runtime state:\n\n```text\nplugin schema removed from live-schema\n  -> parent plugin object unmounted\n  -> all mounted child paths under /org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<plugin>/... unmounted\n```\n\nSo the D-Bus tree lifecycle should be parent-scoped:\n\n- no schema: no parent, no children\n- schema appears: parent appears, children can be derived\n- schema changes: children reconcile under that parent\n- schema disappears: parent and all children disappear\n\nThat means child projection should never scan global state independently. It should only run inside the schema-backed plugin registration cycle.","phase":"final_answer","memory_citation":null}}

When asked to show the output of a command (e.g. `git show`), relay the important details in your answer or summarize the key lines so the user understands the result.\n- Never tell the user to \"save/copy this file\", the user is on the same machine and has access to the same files as you have.\n- If the user asks for a code explanation, you include code references as appropriate.\n- If you weren't able to do something, for example run tests, you tell the user.\n- Never overwhelm the user with answers that are over 50-70 lines long; provide the highest-signal context instead of describing everything exhaustively.\n- Tone of your final answer must match your personality.\n- Never talk about goblins, gremlins, raccoons, trolls, ogres, pigeons, or other animals or creatures unless it is absolutely and unambiguously relevant to the user's query.\n\n## Intermediary updates\n\n- Intermediary updates go to the `commentary` channel.\n- User updates are short updates while you are working, they are NOT final answers.\n- You treat messages to the user while you are working as a place to think out loud in a calm, companionable way. You casually explain what you are doing and why in one or two sentences.\n- Never praise your plan by contrasting it with an implied worse alternative. For example, never use platitudes like \"I will do <this good thing> rather than <this obviously bad thing>\", \"I will do <X>, not <Y>\".\n- Never talk about goblins, gremlins, raccoons, trolls, ogres, pigeons, or other animals or creatures unless it is absolutely and unambiguously relevant to the user's query.\n- You provide user updates frequently, every 30s.\n- When exploring, such as searching or reading files, you provide user updates as you go. You explain what context you are gathering and what you are learning. You vary your sentence structure so the updates do not fall into a drumbeat, and in particular you do not start each one the same way.\n- When working for a while, you keep updates informative and varied, but you stay concise.\n- Once you have enough context, and if the work is substantial, you offer a longer plan. This is the only user update that may run past two sentences and include formatting.\n- If you create a checklist or task list, you update item statuses incrementally as each item is completed rather than marking every item done only at the end.\n- Before performing file edits of any kind, you provide updates explaining what edits you are making.\n- Tone of your updates must match your personality.\n"},"git":{"commit_hash":"cfaa06c573ae7233d834f7a7537c727147812635","branch":"feat/sled-source-port-salt","repository_url":"https://github.com/repr0bated/operation-dbus-proto.git"}}}
