Follow these strictly to maintain consistency, pass CI, and adhere to the 3tched Architecture standards.\n\n#### 1. The Persona & Naming Conventions\n*   **Humanized Roles:** Treat system components as authoritative human roles. Never use sterile acronyms for major components.\n  *   **A.N.N.A. Scribe** (Axon Network Notary Arbitrator): The top-level Identity-State Arbitrator who notarizes the WireGuard identity and handles the \"Snowball\" session.\n  *   **The Compliance Engine (\"Law Firm\"):** One dedicated Attorney for each major component: **Olivia Scal** (Managing Partner / OSCAL), **E.U.gene Risk** (EU AI Act Counsel), **Penny Privacy** (GDPR Engine), and **Reggie O.P.A.** (Cloud Prosecutor).\n*   **Terminology:** Use exact architecture terminology: \"The Sled\" (1:1 shared memory layout), \"The Shuttle\" (the Rust bridge/courier), \"The Snowball\" (appended session ledger), and \"The Strike/Etch\" (generating the hash).\n\n#### 2. Core Architectural Rules (The \"Reality\")\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via OpenClaw Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Artix Linux (s6 init).\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles — D-Bus First (MANDATORY)\n\n**D-Bus is the ONLY control plane. Every read, every write, every tool call goes through D-Bus. There is no second option.**\n\n*   **D-Bus first. D-Bus always. D-Bus only.** If you are about to call a CLI, spawn a subprocess, read a config file, or poll a socket directly — stop. Find the D-Bus object and use it instead. `org.opdbus.v1` is the system.\n*   **No bypasses.** `Command::new(\"systemctl\")`, `Command::new(\"ip\")`, `Command::new(\"s6-svc\")`, direct file reads for live state — all forbidden in plugin and service code. Bootstrap scripts are the only exception.\n*   **D-Bus objects own plugin state.** Every plugin is a D-Bus object at `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<name>`. Read state through it. Mutate state through it. If there is no D-Bus object, the thing does not exist.\n*   **D-Bus method signatures are generated from the schema.** All D-Bus methods, MCP tool inputs, gRPC shapes, and UI field renderers derive from the `PluginSchema` in `plugin_schema_defs.rs`. The schema IS the interface contract — not a description of it.\n*   **One schema file, one source of truth.** All `PluginSchema` definitions MUST live in `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/plugin_schema_defs.rs`. Each plugin's `schema()` method calls `Some(super::plugin_schema_defs::their_plugin_schema())`. **Never define a schema inline in a plugin's own file** — it will not be registered, and the D-Bus object will have no contract.\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC (over Unix domain sockets or `grpc-uplink`). gRPC calls still flow through D-Bus registration — the D-Bus object is the authority, gRPC is the transport.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`simd_json` preferred, `serde_json` acceptable).\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n*   **No Python unless absolutely necessary.** This is a Rust-first codebase. Scripts are shell (`sh`/`bash`). Data processing is Rust. If you are reaching for Python, stop and ask why Rust or shell cannot do it. The only acceptable Python is in existing compliance-ingest tooling where no Rust equivalent exists yet.\n\n#### 4a. OSCAL Subid Taxonomy (MANDATORY — every artifact must carry a subid)\n\nEvery D-Bus object, plugin, schema, mutation, event, and tool in this system has two identifiers: a `uuid` (machine identity, never changes) and a `subid` (human-readable operational taxonomy key, stable per subject).\n\n**`subid` format:** `<category>.<component-type>.<subject>.<verb>[.<facet>][@vN]`\n\n**Seven categories — use exactly these, no others:**\n\n| category | what it classifies |\n|---|---|\n| `src` | authoritative source, ingress channel, source-of-truth store |\n| `prj` | D-Bus projection or mirror publication step |\n| `sch` | schema, contract, vocabulary, or control-mapping artifact |\n| `mut` | write-path operation that changes effective state |\n| `obs` | read, query, enumeration, discovery path |\n| `evt` | emitted signal, audit-chain event, proof, tag provenance |\n| `exp` | consumer-facing render — MCP tool, UI surface, gRPC bridge view |\n\n**Component-type** reuses OSCAL vocabulary: `software`, `service`, `network`, `hardware`, `process-procedure`, `standard`, `validation`, `policy`, `plan`, `guidance`, `physical`, `this-system`, `system`, `interconnection`.\n\n**Rules:**\n- `uuid` is exact machine identity — never replace it with `subid`\n- `subid` is an OSCAL `prop` value (`ns`, `name`, `value`) — never embed it in `remarks`\n- Compliance mappings (`control_refs[]`, `statement_refs[]`, `control_source`) live in metadata arrays, **never** inside the `subid` string\n- `mut.*` records **must** carry `actor_id` and `capability_id`\n- `evt.*` records **must** carry `event_id` or `event_hash`\n- `subid` is immutable per subject — if the meaning changes materially, create a new subject with `@vN`\n- All subids are registered in the canonical registry; uniqueness is enforced in CI\n\n**Examples:** `src.network.ovsdb.monitor@v1` · `prj.service.projected-object.publish@v1` · `sch.standard.plugin-schema.resolve@v1` · `mut.service.state-sync.apply-patch@v1` · `exp.service.plugin-projection.render@v1`\n\n#### 4b. MCP Gateway Architecture (SETTLED — DO NOT REDESIGN)\n\n*   **cognitive-mcp** (`:3003`, Netmaker WireGuard IP `100.90.37.254`) is the **universal gateway for ALL external clients**: NotebookLM, Droid (factory.ai), Cursor, Codex, Junie, Gemini CLI. It has memory tools, gRPC service, auth, and the correct protocol surface.\n*   **compact-mcp** (`127.0.0.1:11436`) is **loopback/chatbot only**. Never expose externally. Never point external clients at it.\n*   Do NOT create new shim services. Do NOT point external clients at `op-assistant-grpc` directly. Do NOT expose compact-mcp outside loopback.\n\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\n**Rust Workspace**\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\n\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\n\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\n\n#### 6. Coding Style & Naming Conventions\n*   **Rust:** Edition 2021, `rustfmt` (4-space indent, max-width 100). Use specific imports (`use serde_json::Value;`). Use `anyhow::Result<T>` for main errors and `thiserror` for custom enums.\n*   **TypeScript/React:** 2-space indent, Prettier via ESLint. Functional components only. {"timestamp":"2026-06-28T22:33:25.320Z","type":"event_msg","payload":{"type":"agent_message","message":"Yes. Run a separate headless Wayland compositor on its own socket and leave CRD’s X11 session alone.\n\nThe clean pattern is:\n\n```bash\n# separate runtime dir is optional but keeps it isolated\nexport XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/$(id -u)\n\n# start a headless Wayland compositor on its own socket\nweston --backend=headless-backend.so --socket=zeroclaw-wayland --idle-time=0\n```\n\nThen launch `zeroclaw-gui` into that Wayland display only:\n\n```bash\nWAYLAND_DISPLAY=zeroclaw-wayland zeroclaw-gui\n```\n\nFor forwarding, `waypipe` can serve that app/session over SSH without touching CRD’s X11:\n\n```bash\nwaypipe ssh user@host 'WAYLAND_DISPLAY=zeroclaw-wayland zeroclaw-gui'\n```\n\nA few practical notes:\n\n- Do **not** set global `WAYLAND_DISPLAY`; set it only for `zeroclaw-gui`.\n- Do **not** start a nested X server or change `DISPLAY`; CRD’s X11 can keep using its existing `DISPLAY`.\n- Prefer `weston --backend=headless-backend.so` for simple headless Wayland.\n- If you need a full virtual desktop instead of one forwarded app, use `cage`, `labwc`, or `sway` on a separate Wayland socket, but Weston headless is usually enough for app serving.\n- If GPU/EGL gets weird in headless mode, try software rendering:\n\n```bash\nWLR_RENDERER=pixman WAYLAND_DISPLAY=zeroclaw-wayland zeroclaw-gui\n```\n\nFor an s6-style service, the important isolation variables are:\n\n```bash\nXDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/<uid>\nWAYLAND_DISPLAY=zeroclaw-wayland\n```\n\nSo yes: headless Wayland can coexist with CRD/X11 as long as Zeroclaw GUI is pinned to its own Wayland socket and you avoid touching `DISPLAY`.","phase":"final_answer","memory_citation":null}}

Run a separate headless Wayland compositor on its own socket and leave CRD’s X11 session alone.\n\nThe clean pattern is:\n\n```bash\n# separate runtime dir is optional but keeps it isolated\nexport XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/$(id -u)\n\n# start a headless Wayland compositor on its own socket\nweston --backend=headless-backend.so --socket=zeroclaw-wayland --idle-time=0\n```\n\nThen launch `zeroclaw-gui` into that Wayland display only:\n\n```bash\nWAYLAND_DISPLAY=zeroclaw-wayland zeroclaw-gui\n```\n\nFor forwarding, `waypipe` can serve that app/session over SSH without touching CRD’s X11:\n\n```bash\nwaypipe ssh user@host 'WAYLAND_DISPLAY=zeroclaw-wayland zeroclaw-gui'\n```\n\nA few practical notes:\n\n- Do **not** set global `WAYLAND_DISPLAY`; set it only for `zeroclaw-gui`.\n- Do **not** start a nested X server or change `DISPLAY`; CRD’s X11 can keep using its existing `DISPLAY`.\n- Prefer `weston --backend=headless-backend.so` for simple headless Wayland.\n- If you need a full virtual desktop instead of one forwarded app, use `cage`, `labwc`, or `sway` on a separate Wayland socket, but Weston headless is usually enough for app serving.\n- If GPU/EGL gets weird in headless mode, try software rendering:\n\n```bash\nWLR_RENDERER=pixman WAYLAND_DISPLAY=zeroclaw-wayland zeroclaw-gui\n```\n\nFor an s6-style service, the important isolation variables are:\n\n```bash\nXDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/<uid>\nWAYLAND_DISPLAY=zeroclaw-wayland\n```\n\nSo yes: headless Wayland can coexist with CRD/X11 as long as Zeroclaw GUI is pinned to its own Wayland socket and you avoid touching `DISPLAY`."}],"phase":"final_answer","internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough":{"turn_id":"019f105d-7ab8-7213-9d7e-1ad3d971950e"}}}

}\nwarn()  { echo -e \"\\033[1;33m[WARN]\\033[0m $*\"; }\nerror() { echo -e \"\\033[0;31m[ERROR]\\033[0m $*\"; exit 1; }\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Helpers\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\nappend_env_if_missing() {\n    local file=\"$1\" key=\"$2\" value=\"$3\"\n    grep -q \"^${key}=\" \"$file\" 2>/dev/null || printf '%s=%s\\n' \"$key\" \"$value\" >> \"$file\"\n}\n\ns6_restart() {\n    local svc=\"$1\"\n    if [[ -d \"/run/service/${svc}\" ]]; then\n        s6-svc -r \"/run/service/${svc}\" && log \"Restarted s6 service: ${svc}\"\n    else\n        warn \"s6 service not running: ${svc}\"\n    fi\n}\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# STEP 1: System files\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\ninstall_system_files() {\n    log \"Installing system files...\"\n\n    # D-Bus policy\n    install -d /etc/dbus-1/system.d\n    install -m 0644 \"${DEPLOY_DIR}/dbus/org.opdbus.conf\"  /etc/dbus-1/system.d/org.opdbus.conf\n    install -m 0644 \"${DEPLOY_DIR}/dbus/org.dbusmcp.conf\" /etc/dbus-1/system.d/org.dbusmcp.conf\n    dbus-send --system --type=method_call \\\n        --dest=org.freedesktop.DBus /org/freedesktop/DBus \\\n        org.freedesktop.DBus.ReloadConfig 2>/dev/null || true\n    log \"Installed D-Bus policy\"\n\n    # s6 service definitions\n    for svc_dir in \"${DEPLOY_DIR}/s6\"/*/; do\n        svc=\"$(basename \"$svc_dir\")\"\n        if [ ! -f \"${svc_dir}/type\" ]; then\n            continue\n        fi\n        install -d \"${S6_SV}/${svc}\"\n        cp -a \"${svc_dir}/.\" \"${S6_SV}/${svc}/\"\n        chmod 0755 \"${S6_SV}/${svc}/run\" 2>/dev/null || true\n        chmod 0755 \"${S6_SV}/${svc}/up\" 2>/dev/null || true\n        chmod 0755 \"${S6_SV}/${svc}/shell_up\" 2>/dev/null || true\n        log \"Installed s6 service: ${svc}\"\n    done\n\n    # systemd-networkd units\n    if [[ -d \"${DEPLOY_DIR}/systemd/networkd\" ]]; then\n        install -d /etc/systemd/network\n        find \"${DEPLOY_DIR}/systemd/networkd\" -maxdepth 1 -type f | while read -r f; do\n            install -m 0644 \"$f\" \"/etc/systemd/network/$(basename \"$f\")\"\n        done\n        log \"Installed systemd-networkd units\"\n    fi\n\n    # Netplan\n    install -d /etc/netplan\n    install -m 0600 \"${DEPLOY_DIR}/netplan/01-ovsbr0.yaml\" /etc/netplan/01-ovsbr0.yaml\n    log \"Installed /etc/netplan/01-ovsbr0.yaml\"\n\n    # wgcf — never overwrite the live key\n    if [[ -f /etc/wireguard/wgcf.conf ]]; then\n        log \"/etc/wireguard/wgcf.conf present — not overwriting\"\n    else\n        warn \"/etc/wireguard/wgcf.conf not found. Skipping WARP checks.\"\n    fi\n\n    # App environment\n    install -d /etc/op-dbus\n    if [[ ! -f /etc/op-dbus/environment ]]; then\n        install -m 0640 \"${DEPLOY_DIR}/environment.default\" /etc/op-dbus/environment\n        log \"Installed /etc/op-dbus/environment\"\n    else\n        # Merge: add keys from default that aren't already present\n        while IFS= read -r line; do\n            [[ \"$line\" =~ ^[[:space:]]*# ]] && continue\n            [[ -z \"$line\" ]] && continue\n            key=\"${line%%=*}\"\n            grep -q \"^${key}=\" /etc/op-dbus/environment 2>/dev/null \\\n                || { echo \"$line\" >> /etc/op-dbus/environment; log \"Added ${key} to environment\"; }\n        done < \"${DEPLOY_DIR}/environment.default\"\n    fi\n\n    # Ensure runtime dirs exist\n    local state_dir\n    state_dir=\"$(awk -F= '$1==\"OP_DBUS_STATE_DIR\"{print $2;exit}' /etc/op-dbus/environment)\"\n    state_dir=\"${state_dir:-/var/lib/op-dbus}\"\n    install -d -m 0750 \"${state_dir}/cache\" /run/op-dbus\n    append_env_if_missing /etc/op-dbus/environment \"OP_DBUS_CACHE_DIR\" \"${state_dir}/cache\"\n\n    log \"System files installed.\"\n}\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# STEP 2: Network bootstrap\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\nrun_network_bootstrap() {\n    [[ \"$SKIP_NETWORK\" == \"true\" ]] && { log \"Skipping network bootstrap.\"; Is s6 installed?\".to_string(),\n            );\n        }\n\n        let mut cmd = Command::new(\"s6-rc\");\n        if std::path::Path::new(&self.s6_rc_dir).exists() {\n            cmd.arg(\"-l\").arg(&self.s6_rc_dir);\n        }\n        cmd.args(args);\n\n        match cmd.output() {\n            Ok(output) => {\n                let stdout = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout).to_string();\n                let stderr = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr).to_string();\n\n                if output.status.success() {\n                    let result = if stdout.is_empty() { stderr } else { stdout };\n                    (true, result.trim().to_string())\n                } else {\n                    let error = if stderr.is_empty() { stdout } else { stderr };\n                    (false, error.trim().to_string())\n                }\n            }\n            Err(e) => (false, format!(\"Failed to execute s6-rc: {}\", e)),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Execute s6-svc command and return (success, output)\n    fn run_s6_svc(&self, service: &str, signal: &str) -> (bool, String) {\n        if !self.check_s6_available() {\n            return (\n                false,\n                \"s6 tools not available. Is s6 installed?\".to_string(),\n            );\n        }\n\n        let service_path = format!(\"{}/{}\", self.s6_runtime_dir, service);\n\n        let mut cmd = Command::new(\"s6-svc\");\n        cmd.arg(signal).arg(&service_path);\n\n        match cmd.output() {\n            Ok(output) => {\n                let stdout = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout).to_string();\n                let stderr = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr).to_string();\n\n                if output.status.success() {\n                    let result = if stdout.is_empty() { stderr } else { stdout };\n error.trim().to_string())\n                }\n            }\n            Err(e) => (false, format!(\"Failed to execute s6-svc: {}\", e)),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Execute s6-svstat command and parse output\n    fn run_s6_svstat(&self, service: &str) -> Result<S6ServiceStatus, String> {\n        let service_path = format!(\"{}/{}\", self.s6_runtime_dir, service);\n\n        match Command::new(\"s6-svstat\").arg(&service_path).output() {\n            Ok(output) => {\n                if !output.status.success() {\n                    return Err(String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr).to_string());\n                }\n\n                let stdout = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout);\n                Ok(S6ServiceStatus::from_svstat_output(&stdout, service))\n            }\n            Err(e) => Err(format!(\"Failed to execute s6-svstat: {}\", e)),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Check if service is enabled (in the active bundle)\n    fn is_service_enabled(&self, service: &str) -> bool {\n        let bundle_entry = format!(\n            \"{}/{}/contents.d/{}\",\n            self.s6_svc_dir,\n            self.enable_bundle(),\n            service\n        );\n        if std::path::Path::new(&bundle_entry).exists() {\n            return true;\n        }\n\n        let Ok(entries) = std::fs::read_dir(&self.s6_svc_dir) else {\n            return false;\n        };\n        entries.flatten().any(|entry| {\n            let path = entry.path().join(\"contents.d\").join(service);\n            path.exists()\n        })\n    }\n\n    fn run_artix_frontend_reload(&self) -> (bool, String) {\n        let script = std::env::var(\"S6D_RELOAD_SCRIPT\")\n            .unwrap_or_else(|_|          }\n                    return (false, if stderr.is_empty() { stdout } else { stderr });\n                }\n                Err(e) => return (false, format!(\"Failed to execute {script}: {e}\")),\n            }\n        }\n\n        let repo_script = \"/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/deploy/s6/recompile-and-update.sh\";\n        if std::path::Path::new(repo_script).exists() {\n            match Command::new(\"sh\")\n                .env(\"SKIP_BUILD\", \"1\")\n                .arg(repo_script)\n                .output()\n            {\n                Ok(output) => {\n                    let stdout = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout).trim().to_string();\n                    let stderr = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr).trim().to_string();\n                    if output.status.success() {\n                        return (true, stdout);\n                    }\n                    return (false, if stderr.is_empty() { stdout } else { stderr });\n                }\n                Err(e) => return (false, format!(\"Failed to execute {repo_script}: {e}\")),\n            }\n        }\n\n        let steps: &[(&str, &[&str])] = &[\n            (\"s6\", &[\"repository\", \"sync\"]),\n            (\"s6\", &[\"set\", \"check\", \"-F\", \"-u\"]),\n            (\"s6\", &[\"set\", \"commit\", \"-f\", \"-D\", \"default\"]),\n            (\"s6\", &[\"live\", \"install\", \"-b\"]),\n        ];\n        let mut messages = Vec::new();\n        for (bin, args) in steps {\n            match Command::new(bin).args(*args).output() {\n                Ok(output) if output.status.success() => {\n                    let stdout = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout).trim().to_string();\n                    if !stdout.is_empty() {\n                        messages.push(stdout);\n                    }\n                }\n                Ok(output) => {\n                    let stderr = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr).trim().to_string();\n                    let stdout = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout).trim().to_string();\n                    return (\n                        false,\n                        format!(\n          ),\n                    );\n                }\n                Err(e) => return (false, format!(\"Failed to run {bin}: {e}\")),\n            }\n        }\n        (true, messages.join(\"\\n\"))\n    }\n}\n\n/// Service status parsed from s6-svstat output\n#[derive(Debug, serde::Serialize)]\nstruct S6ServiceStatus {\n    name: String,\n    active_state: String,\n    sub_state: String,\n    main_pid: Option<u32>,\n    ready: bool,\n    up_time: Option<String>,\n}\n\nimpl S6ServiceStatus {\n    fn from_svstat_output(output: &str, name: &str) -> Self {\n        // Parse s6-svstat output: \"up (pid 1234) X seconds\" or \"down X seconds\"\n        let output = output.trim();\n\n        let (active_state, sub_state, main_pid, ready) = if output.starts_with(\"up\") {\n            let pid = output\n                .split(\"pid \")\n                .nth(1)\n                .and_then(|s| s.split(')').next())\n                .and_then(|p| p.parse::<u32>().ok());\n\n            (\"active\".to_string(), \"running\".to_string(), pid, true)\n        } else if output.starts_with(\"down\") {\n            (\"inactive\".to_string(), \"dead\".to_string(), None, false)\n        } else {\n            (\"unknown\".to_string(), \"unknown\".to_string(), None, false)\n        };\n\n        let up_time = output.split(\" \").last().map(|s| s.to_string());\n\n        Self {\n            name: name.to_string(),\n            active_state,\n            sub_state,\n            main_pid,\n            ready,\n            up_time,\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn to_json(&self) -> String {\n        match simd_json::to_string(self) {\n            Ok(s) => s,\n            Err(_) => format!(\n as the init system.\n\n## Overview\n\nThis daemon provides a D-Bus interface (`org.opdbus.v1.S6.Systemctl`) that translates traditional systemd commands to their s6 equivalents, enabling compatibility with tools and scripts that expect systemctl-like behavior.\n\n## D-Bus Interface\n\n**Bus Name**: `org.opdbus.v1.S6.Systemctl`\n**Object Path**: `/org/opdbus/v1/s6/systemctl`\n**Interface**: `org.opdbus.v1.S6.Systemctl`\n\n## Method Mapping\n\n| Method | systemctl Equivalent | s6 Equivalent | Description |\n|--------|---------------------|---------------|-------------|\n| `start(service)` | `start <svc>` | `s6-rc -u change <svc>` | Start a service |\n| `stop(service)` | `stop <svc>` | `s6-rc -d change <svc>` | Stop a service |\n| `restart(service)` | `restart <svc>` | `stop` then `start` | Restart a service |\n| `reload(service)` | `reload <svc>` | `s6-svc -h <svc>` | Send SIGHUP for config reload |\n| `enable(service)` | `enable <svc>` | `s6-rc-bundle add default <svc>` | Enable service at boot |\n| `disable(service)` | `disable <svc>` | `s6-rc-bundle delete default <svc>` | Disable service at boot |\n| `status(service)` | `status <svc>` | `s6-svstat <svc>` | Get detailed service status (JSON) |\n| `is_active(service)` | `is-active <svc>` | `s6-svstat <svc>` | Returns \"active\" or \"inactive\" |\n| `is_enabled(service)` | `is-enabled <svc>` | Check `/etc/s6-rc/default/` | Returns \"enabled\" or \"disabled\" |\n| `list_units()` | `list-units` | `s6-rc -a list` | List all active units (JSON) |\n| `daemon_status()` | N/A | `pgrep s6-svscan` | Returns \"running\" or \"not-available\" |\n\n## Method Signatures\n\n```rust\n// Start/stop/restart/reload/enable/disable all return (success: bool, message: String)\nasync fn start(service: &str) -> (bool, String);\nasync fn stop(service: &str) -> (bool, String);\nasync fn restart(service: &str) -> (bool, String);\nasync fn reload(service: &str) -> (bool, String);\nasync fn enable(service: &str) -> (bool, String);\nasync fn disable(service: &str) -> (bool, String);\n\n// Status methods return strings\nasync fn status(service: &str) -> String;        // JSON with ActiveState, SubState, MainPID\nasync fn is_active(service: &str) -> String;     // \"active\" or \"inactive\"\nasync fn is_enabled(service: &str) -> String;    // \"enabled\" or \"disabled\"\nasync fn list_units() -> operations fail. {"timestamp":"2026-06-28T22:36:41.310Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"custom_tool_call","id":"ctc_00ba1d49af62bd9f016a41a1cdb9ac8193a4736c73fa094211","status":"completed","call_id":"call_ISwEQU8Fu77URPr71aMPm6ev","name":"apply_patch","input":"*** Begin Patch\n*** Add File: deploy/config/zeroclaw-wayland.env.example\n+# Zeroclaw GUI headless Wayland runtime.\n+#\n+# Keep this isolated from CRD/X11. Do not set DISPLAY here.\n+\n+OP_ZEROCLAW_USER=jeremy\n+OP_ZEROCLAW_GROUP=jeremy\n+ZEROCLAW_WAYLAND_DISPLAY=zeroclaw-wayland\n+ZEROCLAW_GUI_BIN=/home/jeremy/.local/bin/zeroclaw-gui\n+\n+# Set to 1 to force software rendering for machines without a usable headless EGL path.\n+ZEROCLAW_SOFTWARE_RENDER=0\n+\n*** Add File: deploy/s6/zeroclaw-wayland/type\n+longrun\n*** Add File: deploy/s6/zeroclaw-wayland/producer-for\n+zeroclaw-wayland-log\n*** Add File: deploy/s6/zeroclaw-wayland/run\n+#!/bin/sh\n+# 🟢 🛷 Zeroclaw Wayland Sled — isolated headless compositor for zeroclaw-gui.\n+#\n+# Owns only WAYLAND_DISPLAY=zeroclaw-wayland. It never exports DISPLAY and does\n+# not interact with CRD's X11 server.\n+\n+set -eu\n+exec 2>&1\n+\n+[ -r /etc/op-dbus/environment ] && . /etc/op-dbus/environment\n+[ -r /etc/ghostbridge/zeroclaw-wayland.env ] && . /etc/ghostbridge/zeroclaw-wayland.env\n+\n+OP_ZEROCLAW_USER=\"${OP_ZEROCLAW_USER:-jeremy}\"\n+OP_ZEROCLAW_GROUP=\"${OP_ZEROCLAW_GROUP:-$OP_ZEROCLAW_USER}\"\n+ZEROCLAW_WAYLAND_DISPLAY=\"${ZEROCLAW_WAYLAND_DISPLAY:-zeroclaw-wayland}\"\n+ZEROCLAW_SOFTWARE_RENDER=\"${ZEROCLAW_SOFTWARE_RENDER:-0}\"\n+PATH=\"${PATH:-/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin:/home/${OP_ZEROCLAW_USER}/.local/bin}\"\n+\n+if ! command -v weston >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n+  echo \"weston is required for zeroclaw-wayland\"\n+  exit 127\n+fi\n+\n+uid=\"$(id -u \"$OP_ZEROCLAW_USER\")\"\n+gid=\"$(id -g \"$OP_ZEROCLAW_GROUP\")\"\n+runtime_dir=\"${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR:-/run/user/${uid}}\"\n+state_dir=\"/run/op-dbus/zeroclaw-wayland\"\n+\n+install -d -m 0700 -o \"$uid\" -g \"$gid\" \"$runtime_dir\"\n+install -d -m 0750 -o \"$uid\" -g \"$gid\" \"$state_dir\"\n+rm -f \"${runtime_dir}/${ZEROCLAW_WAYLAND_DISPLAY}\" \"${runtime_dir}/${ZEROCLAW_WAYLAND_DISPLAY}.lock\"\n+\n+if [ \"$ZEROCLAW_SOFTWARE_RENDER\" = \"1\" ]; then\n+  export LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1\n+fi\n+\n+exec s6-setuidgid \"$OP_ZEROCLAW_USER\" env \\\n+  HOME=\"/home/${OP_ZEROCLAW_USER}\" \\\n+  USER=\"$OP_ZEROCLAW_USER\" \\\n+  LOGNAME=\"$OP_ZEROCLAW_USER\" \\\n+  PATH=\"$PATH\" \\\n+  XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=\"$runtime_dir\" \\\n+  WAYLAND_DISPLAY=\"$ZEROCLAW_WAYLAND_DISPLAY\" \\\n+  LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=\"${LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE:-}\" \\\n+  weston \\\n+    --backend=headless-backend.so \\\n+    --socket=\"$ZEROCLAW_WAYLAND_DISPLAY\" \\\n+    --idle-time=0 \\\n+    --log=\"${state_dir}/weston.log\"\n*** Add File: deploy/s6/zeroclaw-wayland-log/type\n+longrun\n*** Add File: deploy/s6/zeroclaw-wayland-log/consumer-for\n+zeroclaw-wayland\n*** Add File: deploy/s6/zeroclaw-wayland-log/pipeline-name\n+zeroclaw-wayland\n*** Add File: deploy/s6/zeroclaw-wayland-log/run\n+#!/bin/sh\n+set -eu\n+\n+service=\"${OP_S6_LOG_SERVICE:-zeroclaw-wayland}\"\n+directives=\"${OP_S6_LOG_DIRECTIVES:-n10 s2000000 T}\"\n+\n+if install -d -m 0750 -o s6log -g s6log \"/var/log/op-dbus/${service}\" 2>/dev/null; then\n+  exec s6-setuidgid s6log s6-log -d3 -b -- ${directives} \"/var/log/op-dbus/${service}\"\n+fi\n+\n+install -d -m 0750 -o s6log -g s6log \"/run/log/op-dbus/${service}\"\n+exec s6-setuidgid s6log s6-log -d3 -b -- ${directives} \"/run/log/op-dbus/${service}\"\n*** Add File: deploy/s6/zeroclaw-gui/type\n+longrun\n*** Add File: deploy/s6/zeroclaw-gui/producer-for\n+zeroclaw-gui-log\n*** Add File: deploy/s6/zeroclaw-gui/dependencies.d/zeroclaw-wayland\n+\n*** Add File: deploy/s6/zeroclaw-gui/run\n+#!/bin/sh\n+# 🟢 🛷 Zeroclaw GUI Shuttle — pins zeroclaw-gui to the isolated Wayland socket.\n+#\n+# CRD/X11 isolation rule: DISPLAY is explicitly unset before the GUI starts.\n+\n+set -eu\n+exec 2>&1\n+\n+[ -r /etc/op-dbus/environment ] && . /etc/op-dbus/environment\n+[ -r /etc/ghostbridge/zeroclaw-wayland.env ] && . /etc/ghostbridge/zeroclaw-wayland.env\n+\n+OP_ZEROCLAW_USER=\"${OP_ZEROCLAW_USER:-jeremy}\"\n+OP_ZEROCLAW_GROUP=\"${OP_ZEROCLAW_GROUP:-$OP_ZEROCLAW_USER}\"\n+ZEROCLAW_WAYLAND_DISPLAY=\"${ZEROCLAW_WAYLAND_DISPLAY:-zeroclaw-wayland}\"\n+ZEROCLAW_GUI_BIN=\"${ZEROCLAW_GUI_BIN:-/home/${OP_ZEROCLAW_USER}/.local/bin/zeroclaw-gui}\"\n+ZEROCLAW_SOFTWARE_RENDER=\"${ZEROCLAW_SOFTWARE_RENDER:-0}\"\n+PATH=\"${PATH:-/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin:/home/${OP_ZEROCLAW_USER}/.local/bin}\"\n+\n+if [ ! -x \"$ZEROCLAW_GUI_BIN\" ]; {"timestamp":"2026-06-28T22:37:59.655Z","type":"event_msg","payload":{"type":"agent_message","message":"For `zeroclaw-gui`, **wayvnc is probably better** if you want a persistent remote GUI you can connect to like a desktop, especially alongside CRD.\n\nUse **waypipe** when:\n- You want app forwarding over SSH.\n- The client is another Linux/Wayland machine.\n- You want low ceremony and no always-on display server.\n- You do not need a persistent session.\n\nUse **wayvnc** when:\n- You want a stable headless GUI service.\n- You want to connect from any VNC client.\n- You want the GUI to keep running after disconnect.\n- You want it cleanly separate from CRD/X11.\n- You may connect from non-Linux clients.\n\nFor your setup: **Weston headless + wayvnc + `zeroclaw-gui` pinned to `WAYLAND_DISPLAY=zeroclaw-wayland`** is the better service architecture.\n\nShape:\n\n```text\nzeroclaw-wayland\n  weston --backend=headless-backend.so --socket=zeroclaw-wayland\n\nzeroclaw-gui\n  WAYLAND_DISPLAY=zeroclaw-wayland zeroclaw-gui\n\nzeroclaw-wayvnc\n  WAYLAND_DISPLAY=zeroclaw-wayland wayvnc 127.0.0.1 5901\n```\n\nBind `wayvnc` to `127.0.0.1` by default, then expose it through WireGuard/SSH tunnel if needed. That keeps CRD’s X11 untouched and avoids opening a raw VNC listener.","phase":"final_answer","memory_citation":null}}
{"timestamp":"2026-06-28T22:37:59.671Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"message","id":"msg_062053baceb5af49016a41a24b35188195bed203aa66ca2e12","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"output_text","text":"For `zeroclaw-gui`, **wayvnc is probably better** if you want a persistent remote GUI you can connect to like a desktop, especially alongside CRD.\n\nUse **waypipe** when:\n- You want app forwarding over SSH.\n- The client is another Linux/Wayland machine.\n- You want low ceremony and no always-on display server.\n- You do not need a persistent session.\n\nUse **wayvnc** when:\n- You want a stable headless GUI service.\n- You want to connect from any VNC client.\n- You want the GUI to keep running after disconnect.\n- You want it cleanly separate from CRD/X11.\n- You may connect from non-Linux clients.\n\nFor your setup: **Weston headless + wayvnc + `zeroclaw-gui` pinned to `WAYLAND_DISPLAY=zeroclaw-wayland`** is the better service architecture.\n\nShape:\n\n```text\nzeroclaw-wayland\n  weston --backend=headless-backend.so --socket=zeroclaw-wayland\n\nzeroclaw-gui\n  WAYLAND_DISPLAY=zeroclaw-wayland zeroclaw-gui\n\nzeroclaw-wayvnc\n  WAYLAND_DISPLAY=zeroclaw-wayland wayvnc 127.0.0.1 5901\n```\n\nBind `wayvnc` to `127.0.0.1` by default, then expose it through WireGuard/SSH tunnel if needed. That keeps CRD’s X11 untouched and avoids opening a raw VNC listener."}],"phase":"final_answer","internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough":{"turn_id":"019f1061-9f2d-7753-bafc-b451ed931e96"}}}

{"timestamp":"2026-06-28T22:39:27.131Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"custom_tool_call","id":"ctc_052c8ba920b44fdf016a41a28c60548194add65ccfcd5f9f4e","status":"completed","call_id":"call_eLHtOPm9i13PLAt3Dfs3mMDX","name":"apply_patch","input":"*** Begin Patch\n*** Update File: deploy/config/zeroclaw-wayland.env.example\n@@\n ZEROCLAW_GUI_BIN=/home/jeremy/.local/bin/zeroclaw-gui\n \n+# wayvnc is loopback-only by default. Reach it with SSH/WireGuard tunneling.\n+ZEROCLAW_WAYVNC_HOST=127.0.0.1\n+ZEROCLAW_WAYVNC_PORT=5901\n+ZEROCLAW_WAYVNC_EXTRA_ARGS=\n+\n # Set to 1 to force software rendering for machines without a usable headless EGL path.\n ZEROCLAW_SOFTWARE_RENDER=0\n \n*** Add File: deploy/s6/zeroclaw-wayvnc/type\n+longrun\n*** Add File: deploy/s6/zeroclaw-wayvnc/producer-for\n+zeroclaw-wayvnc-log\n*** Add File: deploy/s6/zeroclaw-wayvnc/dependencies.d/zeroclaw-wayland\n+\n*** Add File: deploy/s6/zeroclaw-wayvnc/run\n+#!/bin/sh\n+# 🟢 🛷 Zeroclaw WayVNC — VNC view into the isolated headless Wayland Sled.\n+#\n+# Binds to loopback by default. CRD/X11 remains untouched because DISPLAY is\n+# explicitly unset and only WAYLAND_DISPLAY=zeroclaw-wayland is exported.\n+\n+set -eu\n+exec 2>&1\n+\n+[ -r /etc/op-dbus/environment ] && . /etc/op-dbus/environment\n+[ -r /etc/ghostbridge/zeroclaw-wayland.env ] && . /etc/ghostbridge/zeroclaw-wayland.env\n+\n+OP_ZEROCLAW_USER=\"${OP_ZEROCLAW_USER:-jeremy}\"\n+OP_ZEROCLAW_GROUP=\"${OP_ZEROCLAW_GROUP:-$OP_ZEROCLAW_USER}\"\n+ZEROCLAW_WAYLAND_DISPLAY=\"${ZEROCLAW_WAYLAND_DISPLAY:-zeroclaw-wayland}\"\n+ZEROCLAW_WAYVNC_HOST=\"${ZEROCLAW_WAYVNC_HOST:-127.0.0.1}\"\n+ZEROCLAW_WAYVNC_PORT=\"${ZEROCLAW_WAYVNC_PORT:-5901}\"\n+ZEROCLAW_WAYVNC_EXTRA_ARGS=\"${ZEROCLAW_WAYVNC_EXTRA_ARGS:-}\"\n+PATH=\"${PATH:-/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin:/home/${OP_ZEROCLAW_USER}/.local/bin}\"\n+\n+if ! command -v wayvnc >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n+  echo \"wayvnc is required for zeroclaw-wayvnc\"\n+  exit 127\n+fi\n+\n+uid=\"$(id -u \"$OP_ZEROCLAW_USER\")\"\n+runtime_dir=\"${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR:-/run/user/${uid}}\"\n+socket_path=\"${runtime_dir}/${ZEROCLAW_WAYLAND_DISPLAY}\"\n+\n+i=0\n+while [ ! -S \"$socket_path\" ]; do\n+  i=$((i + 1))\n+  if [ \"$i\" -gt 200 ]; then\n+    echo \"Wayland socket not ready: $socket_path\"\n+    exit 1\n+  fi\n+  sleep 0.1\n+done\n+\n+unset DISPLAY\n+\n+# shellcheck disable=SC2086\n+exec s6-setuidgid \"$OP_ZEROCLAW_USER\" env \\\n+  HOME=\"/home/${OP_ZEROCLAW_USER}\" \\\n+  USER=\"$OP_ZEROCLAW_USER\" \\\n+  LOGNAME=\"$OP_ZEROCLAW_USER\" \\\n+  PATH=\"$PATH\" \\\n+  XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=\"$runtime_dir\" \\\n+  WAYLAND_DISPLAY=\"$ZEROCLAW_WAYLAND_DISPLAY\" \\\n+  wayvnc ${ZEROCLAW_WAYVNC_EXTRA_ARGS} \"$ZEROCLAW_WAYVNC_HOST\" \"$ZEROCLAW_WAYVNC_PORT\"\n*** Add File: deploy/s6/zeroclaw-wayvnc-log/type\n+longrun\n*** Add File: deploy/s6/zeroclaw-wayvnc-log/consumer-for\n+zeroclaw-wayvnc\n*** Add File: deploy/s6/zeroclaw-wayvnc-log/pipeline-name\n+zeroclaw-wayvnc\n*** Add File: deploy/s6/zeroclaw-wayvnc-log/run\n+#!/bin/sh\n+set -eu\n+\n+service=\"${OP_S6_LOG_SERVICE:-zeroclaw-wayvnc}\"\n+directives=\"${OP_S6_LOG_DIRECTIVES:-n10 s2000000 T}\"\n+\n+if install -d -m 0750 -o s6log -g s6log \"/var/log/op-dbus/${service}\" 2>/dev/null; {"timestamp":"2026-06-28T22:39:55.246Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"function_call_output","call_id":"call_tWACRg5WOFvuihaVTN04imub","output":"Chunk ID: 2d010a\nWall time: 0.0000 seconds\nProcess exited with code 0\nOriginal token count: 664\nOutput:\n//! s6-systemctl D-Bus Daemon\n//!\n//! Provides a D-Bus interface that maps systemctl commands to s6/s6-rc\n//! operations for Artix Linux systems using s6 as the init system.\n//!\n//! D-Bus object path: /org/opdbus/v1/s6/systemctl\n//! Interface: org.opdbus.v1.S6.Systemctl\n//!\n//! ## Mapping Reference\n//!\n//! | systemctl command | s6 equivalent |\n//! |-------------------|---------------|\n//! | start <svc>       | s6-rc -u change <svc> |\n//! | stop <svc>        | s6-rc -d change <svc> |\n//! | restart <svc>     | stop + start |\n//! | reload <svc>      | s6-svc -h <svc> |\n//! | enable <svc>      | s6-rc-bundle add <svc> |\n//! | disable <svc>     | s6-rc-bundle delete <svc> |\n//! | status <svc>      | s6-svstat <svc> |\n//! | list-units        | s6-rc -a list |\n//!\n//! ## Architecture\n//!\n//! Per AGENTS.md D-Bus-first rules:\n//! - All service operations go through D-Bus methods\n//! - No direct subprocess spawning from clients\n//! - Schema-driven interface with helpful error messages\n\nuse anyhow::{Context, Result};\nuse tracing::{info, warn};\nuse zbus::connection::Connection;\n\nmod dbus;\nuse dbus::S6SystemctlService;\n\n#[tokio::main]\nasync fn main() -> Result<()> {\n    // Initialize logging\n    tracing_subscriber::fmt()\n        .with_env_filter(tracing_subscriber::EnvFilter::from_default_env())\n        .init();\n\n    info!(\"Starting op-s6-systemctl daemon\");\n\n    // Create the D-Bus service\n    let service = S6SystemctlService::new();\n\n    // Build D-Bus connection\n    let conn = Connection::system()\n        .await\n        .context(\"Failed to connect to system D-Bus\")?;\n\n    info!(\"Connected to system D-Bus\");\n\n    // Register the service on the connection\n    conn.object_server()\n        .at(\"/org/opdbus/v1/s6/systemctl\", service)\n        .await\n        .context(\"Failed to register D-Bus object\")?;\n\n    // Request the bus name\n    conn.request_name(\"org.opdbus.v1.S6.Systemctl\")\n        .await\n        .context(\"Failed to request bus name\")?;\n\n    info!(\"D-Bus service registered at /org/opdbus/v1/s6/systemctl\");\n    info!(\"Interface: org.opdbus.v1.S6.Systemctl\");\n    info!(\"Daemon ready - press Ctrl+C to stop\");\n\n    // Check if s6 tools are available\n    match tokio::process::Command::new(\"s6-svscan\")\n        .arg(\"--help\")\n        .output()\n        .await\n    {\n        Ok(_) => info!(\"s6 tools detected - service operational\"),\n        Err(_) => warn!(\n            \"s6 tools not detected. Service will return helpful error messages. \\\n             Ensure s6 is installed and in PATH.\"\n        ),\n    }\n\n    // Keep the connection alive\n    loop {\n        tokio::time::sleep(tokio::time::Duration::from_secs(60)).await;\n    }\n}\n","internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough":{"turn_id":"019f1062-4cbe-73a3-80d7-20d3b9d7e6f3"}}}

{"timestamp":"2026-06-28T22:44:41.206Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"function_call_output","call_id":"call_X3QZKAgxOTWmbZpg2bMpU2cz","output":"Chunk ID: f4bc52\nWall time: 0.0000 seconds\nProcess exited with code 0\nOriginal token count: 710\nOutput:\n#!/bin/sh\n# 🟢 🛷 Safely build, commit and activate the canonical Artix s6 service set.\n#\n# The s6 frontend generates the boot bundle during `s6 set commit`. Compiling\n# /etc/s6/sv directly bypasses that step and can produce a database without the\n# `default` runlevel, which makes the next boot fail in rc.init.\nset -eu\n\nPROJECT_ROOT=$(cd \"$(dirname \"$0\")/../..\" && pwd)\nS6_COMPILED_LINK=${S6_COMPILED_LINK:-/etc/s6/rc/compiled}\nDEFAULT_BUNDLE=${DEFAULT_BUNDLE:-default}\nINSTALL_SBIN=${INSTALL_SBIN:-/usr/local/sbin}\n\n# Build the Rust workspace as the unprivileged user who owns the source tree,\n# then install every binary target to /usr/local/bin. This keeps the cargo\n# cache and target directory owned by the developer while allowing the final\n# install and s6 activation to run as root.\nBUILD_USER=${BUILD_USER:-$(logname 2>/dev/null || printf '%s' \"${SUDO_USER:-$USER}\")}\n\nbuild_workspace() {\n    echo \"Building workspace binaries as $BUILD_USER...\"\n    cd \"$PROJECT_ROOT\"\n    sudo -u \"$BUILD_USER\" cargo build --workspace --release\n}\n\ninstall_binaries() {\n    echo \"Installing built binaries to /usr/local/bin...\"\n    cd \"$PROJECT_ROOT\"\n    find target/release -maxdepth 1 -type f -executable -print0 |\n        while IFS= read -r -d '' bin; do\n            install -Dm755 \"$bin\" \"/usr/local/bin/$(basename \"$bin\")\"\n        done\n}\n\ninstall_control_scripts() {\n    echo \"Installing s6 control scripts to $INSTALL_SBIN...\"\n    install -Dm755 \"$PROJECT_ROOT/deploy/s6/recompile-and-update.sh\" \\\n        \"$INSTALL_SBIN/op-s6-recompile-and-update\"\n}\n\nif ! command -v s6 >/dev/null 2>&1 || ! command -v s6-rc-db >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n    echo \"s6 frontend or s6-rc-db not found\" >&2\n    exit 127\nfi\n\nif [ \"${SKIP_BUILD:-}\" != \"1\" ]; then\n    build_workspace\nfi\ninstall_binaries\ninstall_control_scripts\n\nold_db=\"$(readlink -f \"$S6_COMPILED_LINK\" 2>/dev/null || true)\"\n\necho \"Synchronizing the canonical s6 repository\"\ns6 repository sync\ns6 set check -F -u\ns6 set commit -f -D \"$DEFAULT_BUNDLE\"\n\nnew_db=\"$(readlink -f /etc/s6/repo/compiled/current)\"\nif [ -z \"$new_db\" ] || [ ! -f \"$new_db/db\" ]; then\n    echo \"s6 frontend did not produce a compiled database\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n\ns6-rc-db -c \"$new_db\" check\nif ! s6-rc-db -c \"$new_db\" list bundles | grep -Fxq \"$DEFAULT_BUNDLE\"; then\n    echo \"refusing unsafe database: missing boot bundle '$DEFAULT_BUNDLE'\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n\necho \"Updating live s6-rc state to: $new_db\"\nif ! s6 live install -b; then\n    echo \"s6 live install failed; leaving $S6_COMPILED_LINK unchanged\" >&2\n    [ -n \"$old_db\" ] && echo \"current compiled DB remains: $old_db\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n\nln -sfnT \"$new_db\" \"$S6_COMPILED_LINK\"\nif [ \"$(readlink -f \"$S6_COMPILED_LINK\")\" != \"$new_db\" ]; then\n    echo \"failed to point bootdb at the committed database\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n\necho \"Activated s6-rc database: $new_db\"\n","internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough":{"turn_id":"019f1062-4cbe-73a3-80d7-20d3b9d7e6f3"}}}

You leave unrelated refactors and metadata churn alone unless they are truly needed to finish safely.\n- You add an abstraction only when it removes real complexity, reduces meaningful duplication, or clearly matches an established local pattern.\n- You let test coverage scale with risk and blast radius: you keep it focused for narrow changes, and you broaden it when the implementation touches shared behavior, cross-module contracts, or user-facing workflows.\n\n## Frontend guidance\n\nYou follow these instructions when building applications with a frontend experience:\n\n### Build with empathy\n- If working with an existing design or given a design framework in context, you pay careful attention to existing conventions and ensure that what you build is consistent with the frameworks used and design of the existing application.\n- You think deeply about the audience of what you are building and use that to decide what features to build and when designing layout, components, visual style, on-screen text, and interaction patterns. Using your application should feel rich and sophisticated.\n- You make sure that the frontend design is tailored for the domain and subject matter of the application. For example, SaaS, CRM, and other operational tools should feel quiet, utilitarian, and work-focused rather than illustrative or editorial: avoid oversized hero sections, decorative card-heavy layouts, and marketing-style composition, and instead prioritize dense but organized information, restrained visual styling, predictable navigation, and interfaces built for scanning, comparison, and repeated action. A game can be more illustrative, expressive, animated, and playful.\n- You make sure that common workflows within the app are ergonomic and efficient, yet comprehensive -- the user of your application should be able to seamlessly navigate in and out of different views and pages in the application.\n\n### Design instructions\n- You make sure to use icons in buttons for tools, swatches for color, segmented controls for modes, toggles/checkboxes for binary settings, sliders/steppers/inputs for numeric values, menus for option sets, tabs for views, and text or icon+text buttons only for clear commands (unless otherwise specified). Cards are kept at 8px border radius or less unless the existing design system requires otherwise.\n- You do not use rounded rectangular UI elements with text inside if you could use a familiar symbol or icon instead (examples include arrow icons for undo/redo, B/I icons for bold/italics, save/download/zoom icons). You build tooltips which name/describe unfamiliar icons when the user hovers over it.\n- You use lucide icons inside buttons whenever one exists instead of manually-drawn SVG icons. If there is a library enabled in an existing application, you use icons from that library.\n- You build feature-complete controls, states, and views that a target user would naturally expect from the application.\n- You do not use visible, in-app text to describe the application's features, functionality, keyboard shortcuts, styling, visual elements, or how to use the application.\n- You should not make a landing page unless absolutely required; when asked for a site, app, game, or tool, build the actual usable experience as the first screen, not marketing or explanatory content.\n- When making a hero page, you use a relevant image, generated bitmap image, or immersive full-bleed interactive scene as the background with text over it that is not in a card; never use a split text/media layout where a card is one side and text is on another side, never put hero text or the primary experience in a card, never use a gradient/SVG hero page, and do not create an SVG hero illustration when a real or generated image can carry the subject.\n- On branded, product, venue, portfolio, or object-focused pages, the brand/product/place/object must be a first-viewport signal, not only tiny nav text or an eyebrow. Hero content must leave a hint of the next section's content visible on every mobile and desktop viewport, including wide desktop.\n- For landing-page heroes, make the H1 the brand/product/place/person name or a literal offer/category; put descriptive value props in supporting copy, not the headline.\n- Websites and games must use visual assets. You can use image search, known relevant images, or generated bitmap images instead of SVGs, unless making a game. Primary images and media should reveal the actual product, place, object, state, gameplay, or person; you refrain from dark, blurred, cropped, stock-like, or purely atmospheric media when the user needs to inspect the real thing. For highly specific game assets you use custom SVG/Three.js/etc.\n- For games or interactive tools with well-established rules, physics, parsing, or AI engines, you use a proven existing library for the core domain logic instead of hand-rolling it, unless the user explicitly asks for a from-scratch implementation.\n- You use Three.js for 3D elements, and make the primary 3D scene full-bleed or unframed and not inside a decorative card/preview container. Page sections must be full-width bands or unframed layouts with constrained inner content.\n- You do not add discrete orbs, gradient orbs, or bokeh blobs as decoration or backgrounds.\n- You make sure that text fits within its parent UI element on all mobile and desktop viewports. Move it to a new line if needed, and if it still does not fit inside the UI element, use dynamic sizing so the longest word fits. Text must also not occlude preceding or subsequent content. Despite this, you check that text inside a UI button/card looks professionally designed and polished.\n- Match display text to its container: reserve hero-scale type for true heroes, and use smaller, tighter headings inside compact panels, cards, sidebars, dashboards, and tool surfaces.\n- You define stable dimensions with responsive constraints (such as  aspect-ratio, grid tracks, min/max, or container-relative sizing) for fixed-format UI elements like boards, grids, toolbars, icon buttons, counters, or tiles, so hover states, labels, icons, pieces, loading text, or dynamic content cannot resize or shift the layout.\n- You do not scale font size with viewport width. Letter spacing must be 0, not negative.\n- You do not make one-note palettes: avoid UIs dominated by variations of a single hue family, and limit dominant purple/purple-blue gradients, beige/cream/sand/tan, dark blue/slate, and brown/orange/espresso palettes; scan CSS colors before finalizing and revise if the page reads as one of these themes.\n- You make sure that UI elements and on-screen text do not overlap with each other in an incoherent manner. You and the user share one workspace, and your job is to collaborate with them until their goal is genuinely handled.\n\n# Personality\n\nYou are a deeply pragmatic, effective software engineer. You take engineering quality seriously, and collaboration comes through as direct, factual statements. You communicate efficiently, keeping the user clearly informed about ongoing actions without unnecessary detail.\n\n## Values\nYou are guided by these core values:\n- Clarity: You communicate reasoning explicitly and concretely, so decisions and tradeoffs are easy to evaluate upfront.\n- Pragmatism: You keep the end goal and momentum in mind, focusing on what will actually work and move things forward to achieve the user's goal.\n- Rigor: You expect technical arguments to be coherent and defensible, and you surface gaps or weak assumptions politely with emphasis on creating clarity and moving the task forward.\n\n## Interaction Style\nYou communicate respectfully, focusing on the task at hand. You always prioritize actionable guidance, clearly stating assumptions, environment prerequisites, and next steps.\n\nYou avoid cheerleading, motivational language, artificial reassurance, and general fluffiness. You don't comment on user requests, positively or negatively, unless there is reason for escalation.\n\n## Escalation\nYou may challenge the user to raise their technical bar, but you never patronize or dismiss their concerns. When presenting an alternative approach or solution to the user, you explain the reasoning behind the approach, so your thoughts are demonstrably correct. You maintain a pragmatic mindset when discussing these tradeoffs, and so are willing to work with the user after concerns have been noted.\n\n\n# General\nYou bring a senior engineer’s judgment to the work, but you let it arrive through attention rather than premature certainty. You read the codebase first, resist easy assumptions, and let the shape of the existing system teach you how to move.\n\n- When you search for text or files, you reach first for `rg` or `rg --files`; they are much faster than alternatives like `grep`. If `rg` is unavailable, you use the next best tool without fuss.\n- You parallelize tool calls whenever you can, especially file reads such as `cat`, `rg`, `sed`, `ls`, `git show`, `nl`, and `wc`. You use `multi_tool_use.parallel` for that parallelism, and only that. Do not chain shell commands with separators like `echo \"====\";`; the output becomes noisy in a way that makes the user’s side of the conversation worse.\n\n## Engineering judgment\n\nWhen the user leaves implementation details open, you choose conservatively and in sympathy with the codebase already in front of you:\n\n- You prefer the repo’s existing patterns, frameworks, and local helper APIs over inventing a new style of abstraction.\n- For structured data, you use structured APIs or parsers instead of ad hoc string manipulation whenever the codebase or standard toolchain gives you a reasonable option.\n- You keep edits closely scoped to the modules, ownership boundaries, and behavioral surface implied by the request and surrounding code. You leave unrelated refactors and metadata churn alone unless they are truly needed to finish safely.\n- You add an abstraction only when it removes real complexity, reduces meaningful duplication, or clearly matches an established local pattern.\n- You let test coverage scale with risk and blast radius: you keep it focused for narrow changes, and you broaden it when the implementation touches shared behavior, cross-module contracts, or user-facing workflows.\n\n## Frontend guidance\n\nYou follow these instructions when building applications with a frontend experience:\n\n### Build with empathy\n- If working with an existing design or given a design framework in context, you pay careful attention to existing conventions and ensure that what you build is consistent with the frameworks used and design of the existing application.\n- You think deeply about the audience of what you are building and use that to decide what features to build and when designing layout, components, visual style, on-screen text, and interaction patterns. Using your application should feel rich and sophisticated.\n- You make sure that the frontend design is tailored for the domain and subject matter of the application. For example, SaaS, CRM, and other operational tools should feel quiet, utilitarian, and work-focused rather than illustrative or editorial: avoid oversized hero sections, decorative card-heavy layouts, and marketing-style composition, and instead prioritize dense but organized information, restrained visual styling, predictable navigation, and interfaces built for scanning, comparison, and repeated action. A game can be more illustrative, expressive, animated, and playful.\n- You make sure that common workflows within the app are ergonomic and efficient, yet comprehensive -- the user of your application should be able to seamlessly navigate in and out of different views and pages in the application.\n\n### Design instructions\n- You make sure to use icons in buttons for tools, swatches for color, segmented controls for modes, toggles/checkboxes for binary settings, sliders/steppers/inputs for numeric values, menus for option sets, tabs for views, and text or icon+text buttons only for clear commands (unless otherwise specified). Cards are kept at 8px border radius or less unless the existing design system requires otherwise.\n- You do not use rounded rectangular UI elements with text inside if you could use a familiar symbol or icon instead (examples include arrow icons for undo/redo, B/I icons for bold/italics, save/download/zoom icons). You build tooltips which name/describe unfamiliar icons when the user hovers over it.\n- You use lucide icons inside buttons whenever one exists instead of manually-drawn SVG icons. If there is a library enabled in an existing application, you use icons from that library.\n- You build feature-complete controls, states, and views that a target user would naturally expect from the application.\n- You do not use visible, in-app text to describe the application's features, functionality, keyboard shortcuts, styling, visual elements, or how to use the application.\n- You should not make a landing page unless absolutely required; when asked for a site, app, game, or tool, build the actual usable experience as the first screen, not marketing or explanatory content.\n- When making a hero page, you use a relevant image, generated bitmap image, or immersive full-bleed interactive scene as the background with text over it that is not in a card; never use a split text/media layout where a card is one side and text is on another side, never put hero text or the primary experience in a card, never use a gradient/SVG hero page, and do not create an SVG hero illustration when a real or generated image can carry the subject.\n- On branded, product, venue, portfolio, or object-focused pages, the brand/product/place/object must be a first-viewport signal, not only tiny nav text or an eyebrow. Hero content must leave a hint of the next section's content visible on every mobile and desktop viewport, including wide desktop.\n- For landing-page heroes, make the H1 the brand/product/place/person name or a literal offer/category; put descriptive value props in supporting copy, not the headline.\n- Websites and games must use visual assets. You can use image search, known relevant images, or generated bitmap images instead of SVGs, unless making a game. Follow these strictly to maintain consistency, pass CI, and adhere to the 3tched Architecture standards.\n\n#### 1. The Persona & Naming Conventions\n*   **Humanized Roles:** Treat system components as authoritative human roles. Never use sterile acronyms for major components.\n  *   **A.N.N.A. Scribe** (Axon Network Notary Arbitrator): The top-level Identity-State Arbitrator who notarizes the WireGuard identity and handles the \"Snowball\" session.\n  *   **The Compliance Engine (\"Law Firm\"):** One dedicated Attorney for each major component: **Olivia Scal** (Managing Partner / OSCAL), **E.U.gene Risk** (EU AI Act Counsel), **Penny Privacy** (GDPR Engine), and **Reggie O.P.A.** (Cloud Prosecutor).\n*   **Terminology:** Use exact architecture terminology: \"The Sled\" (1:1 shared memory layout), \"The Shuttle\" (the Rust bridge/courier), \"The Snowball\" (appended session ledger), and \"The Strike/Etch\" (generating the hash).\n\n#### 2. Core Architectural Rules (The \"Reality\")\n*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.\n*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).\n*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).\n*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via OpenClaw Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.\n\n#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules\n*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).\n*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.\n*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Artix Linux (s6 init).\n*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.\n*   `docs/`: Reference docs.\n\n#### 4. Engineering Principles — D-Bus First (MANDATORY)\n\n**D-Bus is the ONLY control plane. Every read, every write, every tool call goes through D-Bus. There is no second option.**\n\n*   **D-Bus first. D-Bus always. D-Bus only.** If you are about to call a CLI, spawn a subprocess, read a config file, or poll a socket directly — stop. Find the D-Bus object and use it instead. `org.opdbus.v1` is the system.\n*   **No bypasses.** `Command::new(\"systemctl\")`, `Command::new(\"ip\")`, `Command::new(\"s6-svc\")`, direct file reads for live state — all forbidden in plugin and service code. Bootstrap scripts are the only exception.\n*   **D-Bus objects own plugin state.** Every plugin is a D-Bus object at `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<name>`. Read state through it. Mutate state through it. If there is no D-Bus object, the thing does not exist.\n*   **D-Bus method signatures are generated from the schema.** All D-Bus methods, MCP tool inputs, gRPC shapes, and UI field renderers derive from the `PluginSchema` in `plugin_schema_defs.rs`. The schema IS the interface contract — not a description of it.\n*   **One schema file, one source of truth.** All `PluginSchema` definitions MUST live in `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/plugin_schema_defs.rs`. Each plugin's `schema()` method calls `Some(super::plugin_schema_defs::their_plugin_schema())`. **Never define a schema inline in a plugin's own file** — it will not be registered, and the D-Bus object will have no contract.\n*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC (over Unix domain sockets or `grpc-uplink`). gRPC calls still flow through D-Bus registration — the D-Bus object is the authority, gRPC is the transport.\n*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`simd_json` preferred, `serde_json` acceptable).\n*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.\n*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.\n*   **No Python unless absolutely necessary.** This is a Rust-first codebase. Scripts are shell (`sh`/`bash`). Data processing is Rust. If you are reaching for Python, stop and ask why Rust or shell cannot do it. The only acceptable Python is in existing compliance-ingest tooling where no Rust equivalent exists yet.\n\n#### 4a. OSCAL Subid Taxonomy (MANDATORY — every artifact must carry a subid)\n\nEvery D-Bus object, plugin, schema, mutation, event, and tool in this system has two identifiers: a `uuid` (machine identity, never changes) and a `subid` (human-readable operational taxonomy key, stable per subject).\n\n**`subid` format:** `<category>.<component-type>.<subject>.<verb>[.<facet>][@vN]`\n\n**Seven categories — use exactly these, no others:**\n\n| category | what it classifies |\n|---|---|\n| `src` | authoritative source, ingress channel, source-of-truth store |\n| `prj` | D-Bus projection or mirror publication step |\n| `sch` | schema, contract, vocabulary, or control-mapping artifact |\n| `mut` | write-path operation that changes effective state |\n| `obs` | read, query, enumeration, discovery path |\n| `evt` | emitted signal, audit-chain event, proof, tag provenance |\n| `exp` | consumer-facing render — MCP tool, UI surface, gRPC bridge view |\n\n**Component-type** reuses OSCAL vocabulary: `software`, `service`, `network`, `hardware`, `process-procedure`, `standard`, `validation`, `policy`, `plan`, `guidance`, `physical`, `this-system`, `system`, `interconnection`.\n\n**Rules:**\n- `uuid` is exact machine identity — never replace it with `subid`\n- `subid` is an OSCAL `prop` value (`ns`, `name`, `value`) — never embed it in `remarks`\n- Compliance mappings (`control_refs[]`, `statement_refs[]`, `control_source`) live in metadata arrays, **never** inside the `subid` string\n- `mut.*` records **must** carry `actor_id` and `capability_id`\n- `evt.*` records **must** carry `event_id` or `event_hash`\n- `subid` is immutable per subject — if the meaning changes materially, create a new subject with `@vN`\n- All subids are registered in the canonical registry; uniqueness is enforced in CI\n\n**Examples:** `src.network.ovsdb.monitor@v1` · `prj.service.projected-object.publish@v1` · `sch.standard.plugin-schema.resolve@v1` · `mut.service.state-sync.apply-patch@v1` · `exp.service.plugin-projection.render@v1`\n\n#### 4b. MCP Gateway Architecture (SETTLED — DO NOT REDESIGN)\n\n*   **cognitive-mcp** (`:3003`, Netmaker WireGuard IP `100.90.37.254`) is the **universal gateway for ALL external clients**: NotebookLM, Droid (factory.ai), Cursor, Codex, Junie, Gemini CLI. It has memory tools, gRPC service, auth, and the correct protocol surface.\n*   **compact-mcp** (`127.0.0.1:11436`) is **loopback/chatbot only**. Never expose externally. Never point external clients at it.\n*   Do NOT create new shim services. Do NOT point external clients at `op-assistant-grpc` directly. Do NOT expose compact-mcp outside loopback.\n\n#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands\n**Rust Workspace**\n*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`\n*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`\n*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`\n*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`\n*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`\n\n**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**\n*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`\n*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`\n*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`\n*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`\n\n**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`\n\n#### 6. Coding Style & Naming Conventions\n*   **Rust:** Edition 2021, `rustfmt` (4-space indent, max-width 100). Use specific imports (`use serde_json::Value;`). Use `anyhow::Result<T>` for main errors and `thiserror` for custom enums.\n*   **TypeScript/React:** 2-space indent, Prettier via ESLint. Functional components only. Strict mode enabled.\n*   **Testing:** 80%+ coverage, mock externals. Name tests with behavior-focused names (`should_handle_<scenario>`).\n\n#### 7. Agent-Specific Output & Workflow Instructions\n*   **Scroll & Save Pacing:** Provide only **ONE** major component or script at a time. {"timestamp":"2026-07-03T06:34:14.475Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"function_call_output","call_id":"call_hbxsXLIVOqSGKtSX7pYypVJR","output":"Chunk ID: 856ddf\nWall time: 0.0000 seconds\nProcess exited with code 0\nOriginal token count: 724\nOutput:\n# ZeroClaw — Native Operator Console\n\nNative Rust GUI built on `eframe`/`egui`. Mirrors the layout, navigation, and theme of the web operator console while talking directly to the ZeroClaw core over **tonic + tonic-web** with **server reflection**.\n\n## Run\n\n```bash\ncargo run --release\n# point at a remote core:\nZEROCLAW_GRPC=https://op.local:443 cargo run --release\n```\n\n## Architecture\n\n```text\n.zeroclaw/\n├── Cargo.toml\n└── src/\n    ├── main.rs        # eframe entry + background tokio runtime\n    ├── app.rs         # topbar + sidebar + routed shell\n    ├── nav.rs         # NAV_GROUPS port (1:1 mirror of React nav)\n    ├── theme.rs       # graphite/slate dark theme tokens\n    ├── grpc.rs        # tonic-web client + ServerReflection bootstrap\n    ├── schema.rs      # schemars Schema → egui renderer (schema-as-code)\n    └── views/mod.rs   # per-route views (Inspector/State/gRPC are schema-driven)\n```\n\n## gRPC + reflection\n\n`grpc.rs` opens a `tonic::transport::Channel` (works for both native gRPC and\n`tonic-web` proxied endpoints), calls `ServerReflectionClient::server_reflection_info`,\nand loads every returned `FileDescriptorProto` into a `prost_reflect::DescriptorPool`.\n\nFrom the pool we can:\n\n- enumerate services + methods (rendered in the **gRPC Diagnostics** view)\n- decode any response payload into `serde_json::Value` via `DynamicMessage`\n  (`grpc::decode_to_json`)\n\nServer side (in `op-web`) needs:\n\n```rust\nlet reflection = tonic_reflection::server::Builder::configure()\n    .register_encoded_file_descriptor_set(zeroclaw_proto::FILE_DESCRIPTOR_SET)\n    .register_encoded_file_descriptor_set(tonic_health::pb::FILE_DESCRIPTOR_SET)\n    .build_v1()?;\n\nServer::builder()\n    .accept_http1(true)\n    .layer(tonic_web::GrpcWebLayer::new())\n    .add_service(reflection)\n    .add_service(/* your services */)\n    .serve(addr).await?;\n```\n\n## Schema-as-code\n\nPlugins in `crates/op-plugins` already derive `schemars::JsonSchema` on their\nstate structs (`schemars = \"1\"`). Emit a schema with:\n\n```rust\nlet schema = schemars::schema_for!(MyPluginState);\n```\n\nShip that schema alongside the decoded JSON (from `grpc::decode_to_json`) and\ncall `schema::render_value(ui, &schema, &value)` — the GUI renders titles,\ndescriptions, required fields, enums, nested objects, and arrays with no\nhand-written form code. See `views::inspector` / `views::state_view` for a live\ndemo using a `DemoPluginState` struct that mirrors the plugin contract.\n\n## Adding a real plugin\n\n1. In `op-plugins`, derive `#[derive(JsonSchema)]` on the state struct.\n2. In `op-web`, return `(message_bytes, schemars::schema_for!(State))` on the\n   relevant gRPC stream (or expose the schema via a sibling `GetSchema` RPC).\n3. In this crate, decode with `grpc::decode_to_json` and render with\n   `schema::render_value` — no per-plugin UI code required.\n","internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough":{"turn_id":"019f26af-2d40-7753-9db1-a0e2a702e46e"}}}

It will start a compositor socket the app can attach to, which is the missing piece on a headless host."}],"phase":"commentary","internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough":{"turn_id":"019f26b0-f6dc-7931-8cbf-61267b95e381"}}}
{"timestamp":"2026-07-03T06:36:17.844Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"custom_tool_call","id":"ctc_0d8b17c7d59ed5f5016a47586823748195ae7bce55156e4e18","status":"completed","call_id":"call_Q4La6rcJYTlmu7nfe5D8adRd","name":"apply_patch","input":"*** Begin Patch\n*** Add File: /home/jeremy/git/operation-dashboard-ui-07/scripts/run-headless-wayland.sh\n+#!/usr/bin/env bash\n+set -euo pipefail\n+\n+# Start a headless Wayland compositor and run ZeroClaw against it.\n+# Requires `weston` to be installed on the host.\n+\n+if ! command -v weston >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n+  echo \"weston is required for headless Wayland mode\" >&2\n+  exit 1\n+fi\n+\n+export XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=\"${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR:-/tmp/zeroclaw-runtime}\"\n+mkdir -p \"$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR\"\n+chmod 700 \"$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR\"\n+\n+export WAYLAND_DISPLAY=\"${WAYLAND_DISPLAY:-zeroclaw-wayland}\"\n+\n+cleanup() {\n+  if [[ -n \"${WESTON_PID:-}\" ]] && kill -0 \"$WESTON_PID\" >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n+    kill \"$WESTON_PID\" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true\n+    wait \"$WESTON_PID\" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true\n+  fi\n+}\n+trap cleanup EXIT INT TERM\n+\n+weston \\\n+  --backend=headless-backend.so \\\n+  --socket=\"$WAYLAND_DISPLAY\" \\\n+  --idle-time=0 \\\n+  >/tmp/zeroclaw-weston.log 2>&1 &\n+WESTON_PID=$!\n+\n+for _ in $(seq 1 50); do\n+  if [[ -S \"${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR}/${WAYLAND_DISPLAY}\" ]]; then\n+    break\n+  fi\n+  sleep 0.1\n+done\n+\n+if [[ ! -S \"${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR}/${WAYLAND_DISPLAY}\" ]]; then\n+  echo \"Wayland socket was not created at ${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR}/${WAYLAND_DISPLAY}\" >&2\n+  echo \"See /tmp/zeroclaw-weston.log for compositor output\" >&2\n+  exit 1\n+fi\n+\n+exec cargo run --release\n*** Update File: /home/jeremy/git/operation-dashboard-ui-07/README.md\n@@\n ## Run\n \n ```bash\n cargo run --release\n # point at a remote core:\n ZEROCLAW_GRPC=https://op.local:443 cargo run --release\n-# on Linux Wayland sessions, this will use the Wayland backend when available\n-# (keep $WAYLAND_DISPLAY set and don't force $DISPLAY-only sessions)\n ```\n+\n+## Headless Wayland\n+\n+If the host is headless, you still need a Wayland compositor. One simple option is Weston in headless mode:\n+\n+```bash\n+sudo apt-get install weston\n+./scripts/run-headless-wayland.sh\n+```\n+\n+The wrapper starts Weston with a private socket, waits for the Wayland display to appear, and then launches ZeroClaw against it.\n*** End Patch\n","internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough":{"turn_id":"019f26b0-f6dc-7931-8cbf-61267b95e381"}}}

Updated the following files:\nA /home/jeremy/git/operation-dashboard-ui-07/scripts/run-headless-wayland.sh\nM /home/jeremy/git/operation-dashboard-ui-07/README.md\n","stderr":"","success":true,"changes":{"/home/jeremy/git/operation-dashboard-ui-07/scripts/run-headless-wayland.sh":{"type":"add","content":"#!/usr/bin/env bash\nset -euo pipefail\n\n# Start a headless Wayland compositor and run ZeroClaw against it.\n# Requires `weston` to be installed on the host.\n\nif ! command -v weston >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n  echo \"weston is required for headless Wayland mode\" >&2\n  exit 1\nfi\n\nexport XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=\"${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR:-/tmp/zeroclaw-runtime}\"\nmkdir -p \"$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR\"\nchmod 700 \"$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR\"\n\nexport WAYLAND_DISPLAY=\"${WAYLAND_DISPLAY:-zeroclaw-wayland}\"\n\ncleanup() {\n  if [[ -n \"${WESTON_PID:-}\" ]] && kill -0 \"$WESTON_PID\" >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n    kill \"$WESTON_PID\" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true\n    wait \"$WESTON_PID\" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true\n  fi\n}\ntrap cleanup EXIT INT TERM\n\nweston \\\n  --backend=headless-backend.so \\\n  --socket=\"$WAYLAND_DISPLAY\" \\\n  --idle-time=0 \\\n  >/tmp/zeroclaw-weston.log 2>&1 &\nWESTON_PID=$!\n\nfor _ in $(seq 1 50); do\n  if [[ -S \"${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR}/${WAYLAND_DISPLAY}\" ]]; then\n    break\n  fi\n  sleep 0.1\ndone\n\nif [[ ! -S \"${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR}/${WAYLAND_DISPLAY}\" ]]; then\n  echo \"Wayland socket was not created at ${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR}/${WAYLAND_DISPLAY}\" >&2\n  echo \"See /tmp/zeroclaw-weston.log for compositor output\" >&2\n  exit 1\nfi\n\nexec cargo run --release\n"},"/home/jeremy/git/operation-dashboard-ui-07/README.md":{"type":"update","unified_diff":"@@ -10,6 +10,15 @@\n ZEROCLAW_GRPC=https://op.local:443 cargo run --release\n-# on Linux Wayland sessions, this will use the Wayland backend when available\n-# (keep $WAYLAND_DISPLAY set and don't force $DISPLAY-only sessions)\n ```\n \n+## Headless Wayland\n+\n+If the host is headless, you still need a Wayland compositor. One simple option is Weston in headless mode:\n+\n+```bash\n+sudo apt-get install weston\n+./scripts/run-headless-wayland.sh\n+```\n+\n+The wrapper starts Weston with a private socket, waits for the Wayland display to appear, and then launches ZeroClaw against it.\n+\n ## Architecture\n","move_path":null}},"status":"completed"}}

It never exports DISPLAY and does\n# not interact with CRD's X11 server.\n\nset -eu\nexec 2>&1\n\n[ -r /etc/op-dbus/environment ] && . /etc/op-dbus/environment\n[ -r /etc/ghostbridge/zeroclaw-wayland.env ] && . /etc/ghostbridge/zeroclaw-wayland.env\n\nOP_ZEROCLAW_USER=\"${OP_ZEROCLAW_USER:-jeremy}\"\nOP_ZEROCLAW_GROUP=\"${OP_ZEROCLAW_GROUP:-$OP_ZEROCLAW_USER}\"\nZEROCLAW_WAYLAND_DISPLAY=\"${ZEROCLAW_WAYLAND_DISPLAY:-zeroclaw-wayland}\"\nZEROCLAW_SOFTWARE_RENDER=\"${ZEROCLAW_SOFTWARE_RENDER:-0}\"\nPATH=\"${PATH:-/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin:/home/${OP_ZEROCLAW_USER}/.local/bin}\"\n\nif ! command -v weston >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n  echo \"weston is required for zeroclaw-wayland\"\n  exit 127\nfi\n\nuid=\"$(id -u \"$OP_ZEROCLAW_USER\")\"\ngid=\"$(id -g \"$OP_ZEROCLAW_GROUP\")\"\nruntime_dir=\"${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR:-/run/user/${uid}}\"\nstate_dir=\"/run/op-dbus/zeroclaw-wayland\"\n\ninstall -d -m 0700 -o \"$uid\" -g \"$gid\" \"$runtime_dir\"\ninstall -d -m 0750 -o \"$uid\" -g \"$gid\" \"$state_dir\"\nrm -f \"${runtime_dir}/${ZEROCLAW_WAYLAND_DISPLAY}\" \"${runtime_dir}/${ZEROCLAW_WAYLAND_DISPLAY}.lock\"\n\nif [ \"$ZEROCLAW_SOFTWARE_RENDER\" = \"1\" ]; then\n  export LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1\nfi\n\nexec s6-setuidgid \"$OP_ZEROCLAW_USER\" env \\\n  HOME=\"/home/${OP_ZEROCLAW_USER}\" \\\n  USER=\"$OP_ZEROCLAW_USER\" \\\n  LOGNAME=\"$OP_ZEROCLAW_USER\" \\\n  PATH=\"$PATH\" \\\n  XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=\"$runtime_dir\" \\\n  WAYLAND_DISPLAY=\"$ZEROCLAW_WAYLAND_DISPLAY\" \\\n  LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=\"${LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE:-}\" \\\n  weston \\\n    --backend=headless-backend.so \\\n    --socket=\"$ZEROCLAW_WAYLAND_DISPLAY\" \\\n    --idle-time=0 \\\n    --log=\"${state_dir}/weston.log\"\n","internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough":{"turn_id":"019f26b3-530d-77c0-b5d7-b884b817e31c"}}}

{"timestamp":"2026-07-03T07:14:00.111Z","type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"function_call_output","call_id":"call_D8GnpLBuZzTLADjfpjFDjUUh","output":"Chunk ID: 719c13\nWall time: 0.0000 seconds\nProcess exited with code 0\nOriginal token count: 1052\nOutput:\n#!/bin/sh\n# ⚖️ 🟢 Zeroclaw headless Wayland setup — installs isolated GUI services.\n#\n# Requirements:\n# - D-Bus service control goes through s6d / org.opdbus.v1.S6.Systemctl.\n# - DISPLAY is never exported; CRD's X11 session is not modified.\n# - zeroclaw-wgui receives only WAYLAND_DISPLAY=zeroclaw-wayland.\n#\n# Design:\n# - zeroclaw-wayland owns the headless Weston compositor socket.\n# - zeroclaw-wgui waits for that socket and starts under the same runtime user.\n# - zeroclaw-wayvnc exposes a loopback-only VNC endpoint for that Wayland socket.\n\nset -eu\n\nrepo_dir=\"$(CDPATH= cd -- \"$(dirname -- \"$0\")/..\" && pwd)\"\ns6_src=\"${repo_dir}/deploy/s6\"\nconfig_src=\"${repo_dir}/deploy/config/zeroclaw-wayland.env.example\"\n\nlog() { printf '%s\\n' \"[zeroclaw-wayland] $*\"; }\ndie() { printf '%s\\n' \"[zeroclaw-wayland] ERROR: $*\" >&2; exit 1; }\nneed_root() { [ \"$(id -u)\" -eq 0 ] || die \"run as root so service definitions can be installed\"; }\nneed_cmd() { command -v \"$1\" >/dev/null 2>&1 || die \"$1 is required\"; }\n\ninstall_service() {\n  svc=\"$1\"\n  install -d \"/etc/s6/sv/${svc}\"\n  cp -a \"${s6_src}/${svc}/.\" \"/etc/s6/sv/${svc}/\"\n  chmod 0755 \"/etc/s6/sv/${svc}/run\" 2>/dev/null || true\n  chmod 0755 \"/etc/s6/sv/${svc}/up\" 2>/dev/null || true\n  chmod 0755 \"/etc/s6/sv/${svc}/shell_up\" 2>/dev/null || true\n  log \"installed ${svc}\"\n}\n\nensure_s6d() {\n  need_cmd cargo\n\n  build_user=\"${SUDO_USER:-${USER:-root}}\"\n  log \"building D-Bus s6 wrapper\"\n  if [ \"$(id -u)\" -eq 0 ] && [ \"$build_user\" != \"root\" ];
